## Executive Summary

Enterprise Trials is delivering a standardized enterprise trial capability across products, markets, and channels so sales, product, and customer success teams can offer consistent, controlled trial experiences that increase trial-to-paid conversion and reduce operational friction. The program aligns product readiness, sales enablement, provisioning, onboarding, usage tracking, support, legal controls, and conversion reporting to improve trial setup speed, activation, engagement, and visibility.

To date, 4 of 11 defined milestones are complete, including the unified trial journey dashboard removal, the revamped Tableau reporting solution, AEM expansion MVP 1.0, and Westlaw Advantage Canada enablement. Five milestones are in progress and two are not yet started, with critical-path builds for CoCounsel Tax access-based trials and GLLF/MLF Salesforce-based enterprise trials due in the July to August 2026 window.

Overall status is AMBER, driven by critical GLLF/MLF and CoCounsel Tax capabilities still in build and dependent on open Eloqua, React, and AEM integrations targeted for closure in June 2026.

#### **Key Highlights**

-   **GLLF/MLF** initiatives progressing with **HLD completed** on **May 18, 2026** to technical teams for solutioning.
    
-   Near-term focus on **GLLF/MLF Calendar-Based Trial End Date Selection** and **Adding Products to an Active Trial**.
    
-   Most capabilities within **GLLF/MLF** features planned for AUG-SEMIMONTHLY release. Early delivery through Sprints discussion started with Release Management (In progress and pending approval)
    
-   Delivery plan for other features for **GLLF/MLF** timelines are under weekly review with all teams involved: GSI, Eloqua, TFMS, Boomi, OLC and SAP
    
-   CoCounsel Tax feature in QA Testing is in progress
    
-   Late SAP requirements discovered to enable GLLF/MLF multi-location feature to convert from trial to paid subscriptions. SAP team does not have capacity to work on this until sprint 15
    
-   RepLed Team Full allocation to GLLF/MLF through SP16 limits bandwidth for any additional priorities (deferred to SP17+). Any additional workload requires prioritization
    

#### Next Steps

1.  Maintain Scrum of Scrums call among all teams involved in GLLF/MLF to identify risks, blockers and/or dependencies so they are addressed according to the delivery and testing plans
    
2.  Start Early deployment request and discussion with Release management involving Commercial Engineering Management and Tech Team for GLLF/MLF work - AUG SEMI Release
    
3.  Address CoCounsel Tax REACT dependency with Commercial Engineering and React developer to complete QA Testing in Sprint 12
    

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on de-risking the July release window by completing CoCounsel Tax QA and UAT by 12 Jun 2026, securing React and AEM changes by 16 Jun 2026, and locking the Eloqua email dependency for “add products to active trial” by 30 Jun 2026 so notification flows are in place before GLLF/MLF capabilities go live. In parallel, GLLF/MLF nurture email changes and duration/extension rules will be sequenced behind these dependencies to ensure policy enforcement and communications remain aligned once all segments are fully on the Salesforce-based Enterprise Trial system.

## Milestones

-   Complete CoCounsel Tax access-based enterprise trial foundation and lower-environment readiness by 13 Jul 2026.
    
-   Deliver GLLF/MLF enterprise trial product onboarding and calendar-based trial end-date selection in Salesforce by 13 Jul 2026.
    
-   Enable global customer support numbers in Eloqua emails and AEM trial journey error messages by 11 Jul 2026.
    
-   Implement “add products to an active trial” for GLLF/MLF, including Eloqua notification support, by 22 Aug 2026.

Its purpose is to enable digitally initiated and configurable trials, support a seamless trial-to-paid conversion with no service interruption, and establish a standardized onboarding model that reduces manual processes and prepares product teams for future integration.

milestones.name: Calendar-Based Trial End Date Selection with Segment-Specific Creation Limits for GLLF/MLF
milestones.description:
This feature replaces the manual day-count input with a calendar-based end date picker in the Salesforce trial creation UI. Reps will select a specific end date directly from a calendar, giving them precise, intuitive control over when the trial ends.

For GLLF and MLF accounts, the calendar picker must enforce a maximum initial trial period of 60 days from the trial start date. Reps may select any end date within the 1–60 day window, but the system must prevent selection or saving of any date that exceeds this limit. This enforcement must be segment-aware — other segments must not be affected by GLLF/MLF-specific rules.

The calendar-based date picker also applies at every extension event, replacing any manual day-count input at the point of extension

milestones.name: GLLF/MLF | Enterprise Trial Product Onboarding for GLLF & MLF
milestones.description:
The objective is to transition all segments to the Salesforce‑based Enterprise Trial system as the primary solution. Trial strategists will continue to support complex, high‑touch scenarios.
Operational Mechanics: Bulk contact upload is available (limits still to be confirmed). Multi‑location trials remain a per‑account manual process. Usage reporting in Salesforce is now active and sharable.
Volume Benchmark: MLF executed ~1,800 managed trials last year, with ~574 extensions—highlighting the operational scale this migration must support.

milestones.name: Global customer support number in the Eloqua emails & AEM pages for Trial journey
milestones.description: Add the Technical Support phone number for West, UK, CARS and AEM region to the existing support contact information so customers have a direct phone option for urgent technical issues. The phone contact should display the below numbers for the regions: US, UK, Canada, AEM

milestones.name: GLLF/MLF | Adding Products to an Active Trial
milestones.description:
This feature enables sales reps to add one or more eligible products to an already-active GLLF or MLF Enterprise Trial directly from the trial record in Salesforce. When a product is added mid-trial, entitlements must be provisioned seamlessly via TFMS for all users on the trial — both those who have already activated and those who have been invited but not yet activated.

Eligible products in scope are existing bundle offerings used by the GLLF and MLF segments: Westlaw, Practical Law, and Co-Counsel. Simplicity with Deadline Assistant is explicitly out of scope for this phase as it is not onboarded onto the Enterprise Trial system.

Adding a product mid-trial must not trigger duplicate or re-triggered welcome emails to existing trial users via Eloqua.

## Executive Summary

Special Offers – Migration to OC is replacing bespoke Special Offers handling with standard Order Capture (OC) processes for Enterprise Access / Future Start & Lapse and Flexible Contract Terms / Mid-Contract Modifications, underpinned by SAP, Conga, pricing, and material code changes. This matters because it shifts ~\$1.54B ACV of orders to scalable, controlled workflows, reducing manual handling and improving sales and fulfillment efficiency.

F1 SAP Discovery and Interlock is 80% complete against a planned finish of 05 Jun 2026 and is gating downstream design and build, while F1 Business Refinement is 20% complete ahead of its 12 Jun 2026 baseline. Most downstream milestones (Conga design, development, SIT, UAT, PPE, and ELS go-lives for both F1 and F2) remain on paper only, and several critical technical and data dependencies, including L4 setup, material masters, product lists, sample data, and EPM data readiness, are still open with June and July target dates.

Overall status is Red, driven by unresolved compensation and finance pushback on opening up future start, which directly threatens approvals and the September 2026 Enterprise Access / Future Start & Lapse release.

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on closing the compensation and finance risk by completing the targeted working group and securing a decision on future start controls by 12 Jun 2026, while in parallel clearing critical data and product setup dependencies (L4/L5 codes, initial product list, material masters, and sample data) by their June and July target dates to protect the downstream SIT and go-live windows.

## Milestones

- Complete F1.1 SAP Discovery and Interlock sessions by 05 Jun 2026.  
- Complete F1.2 Business Refinement for Enterprise Access / Future Start and Lapse by 12 Jun 2026.  
- Finalize the first-wave product list (10–25 products) and provide sample data to enable development and testing by 11 Jun 2026.  
- Resolve compensation and finance concerns on opening up future start and confirm the control approach by 12 Jun 2026.  
- Deliver F2 ELS Go-Live for Flexible Contract Terms / Mid-Contract Modifications and complete the overall Special Offers – Migration to OC programme by 22 Oct 2026, ahead of project closure on 30 Oct 2026.

risks.impact_description: If compensation and finance do not support opening up future start, approvals for the September enhancements may be delayed or withheld, requiring design changes or additional controls to prevent overpayments. This could delay the September release for Enterprise Access and Future Start & Lapse, impact the ability to migrate orders off Special Offers on schedule, and erode stakeholder confidence in the solution.
risks.mitigation: Form a focused working group including compensation, finance, and the feature leads (Julie and Ryan) to study the detailed implications of opening up future start and to align on controls to prevent overpayments, then reconvene later in June 2026 to confirm the path forward.

## Executive Summary

The IFRS 18 project will deliver the scoped changes required to comply with the IFRS 18 accounting standard. This matters to ensure financial reporting remains compliant with evolving regulatory expectations and supports the finance function.

No delivery progress has been made yet, as the project is scheduled to start on 15 Jun 2026 and the first milestone "Finalize & Scoping" is currently Not Started. The latest estimate for "Finalize & Scoping" completes on 30 Jun 2026, which is 15 days earlier than the original planned end date of 15 Jul 2026.

Overall status is Green, driven by the project being in pre-start with a defined schedule and no recorded risks or issues.

## Path to Green

To maintain Green status, the team will closely track initiation and completion of the "Finalize & Scoping" work against its 15 Jun 2026 start and 30 Jun 2026 latest estimated completion dates.

## Milestones

- Start the "Finalize & Scoping" phase by 15 Jun 2026.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) is delivering a single enterprise platform (Icertis) for commercial and procurement contracts, providing a global contract repository, standardized terms, and obligation management to reduce financial, compliance, and operational risk. The program underpins enterprise risk reduction for an identified Top Risk area and is a core enabler for lead-to-cash, data, and AI-driven governance outcomes.

Release 1 Commercial pilot went live on 13 Apr 2026 with all planned pilot scope in production and no Sev1/Sev2 incidents, and Release 2 has moved its business rollout for Government and Legal Professionals from 31 Jul 2026 to 10 Aug 2026 to accommodate build and UAT timelines. R1a Procurement is targeting 29 Aug 2026 for Buy-Side Master Agreement go-live with 5–10 users, while 32 R1 pilot enhancements (5 already resolved) and the H2 data and obligation pilots are scheduled to land by 10 Aug 2026 and through H2.

Overall status is Red, driven by unresolved data access and migration-readiness dependencies that threaten timely data migration and alignment with the 10 Aug 2026 Release 2 rollout.

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on unblocking the data workstream by securing data access, completing template deployment, and finalizing the AI extraction approach so that migration can start on time and support the August rollout and data pilot targets. In parallel, the team will lock MSA and Modification requirements by 30 Jun 2026, define a single accountable owner and governance model for Obligation Management, and maintain scope discipline on R1a Procurement so that the 10 Aug and 29 Aug milestones are met without further slippage.

## Milestones

- Complete R1 pilot enhancement backlog, resolving the remaining 27 of 32 enhancements, and align changes with the enterprise rollout by 10 Aug 2026.  
- Deliver Release 2 business rollout for Government and Legal Professionals (US, UK, EU), expanding CLM to NDA, Termination Letter, GPV and Special Offer contract types, and maintaining zero P1/P2 defects at go-live by 10 Aug 2026.  
- Go-live R1a Procurement with Buy-Side Master Agreement CLM MVP and light-touch Contract Express–Icertis integration for an initial cohort of 5–10 users by 29 Aug 2026.  
- Complete the H2 Data Pilot with at least 80% migration coverage across prioritized sell-side and buy-side contracts and close out August data migration activities by 31 Aug 2026.  
- Complete R3 enterprise-scale rollout and advanced capability enablement, then transition the CLM platform to steady-state operations by the overall program end date of 31 Dec 2026.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

**Summary: (Tooling Update)** For clarity, this summary relates to the Pagero Program, not the S3NS project. All PLE activities for this project are complete; ongoing updates are being maintained only for any remaining tooling items or issues to ensure centralized visibility and a consistent point of reference for stakeholders.

**Pagero Program:** Overall integration status has reverted to **RED** due to a critical blocker impacting Sentinel One installation. Europe 1 and 2 will not complete the GKE 1.34 upgrade by 12 June, which is a prerequisite for deployment. All teams are evaluating alternative tools compatible with the S3NS environment. Despite this issue, production delivery remains on track for 12 June, with current efforts focused on enabling tier 1 customer requirements, including account creation and connectivity.

Tooling migration has reached 80% completion against a 100% target by 2026-12-31, with the remaining 20% attributable to clearly defined outstanding items. Several foundational controls are already implemented, including container security, data loss prevention, secrets management, and data in transit encryption, while key remaining integrations focus on endpoint protection, cloud security monitoring, centralized logging, and WAF.

Overall status is AMBER, driven primarily by SentinelOne installation and GKE upgrade dependencies that risk delaying full endpoint protection coverage in the S3NS environment.

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on clearing endpoint and platform dependencies by 30 Jun 2026, completing the GKE upgrade to version 1.34, enabling the required allow list, and validating SentinelOne installation through joint troubleshooting with platform and vendor teams. In parallel, we will close remaining cloud security integrations by securing Wiz licensing, progressing WAF implementation, and enabling Splunk based centralized logging so the final 20% of tools can be deployed ahead of the 01 Sep 2026 mandate date.

## Milestones

-   Complete SentinelOne installation for Pagero workloads and finish the GKE 1.34 upgrade required for stable agent deployment by 30 Jun 2026.
    
-   Finalize the eSSO solution build and configuration for the S3NS environment by 30 Jun 2026.
    
-   Implement Wiz cloud security monitoring, Truccr manual data loads into TRUCCR, Cloud ARM and WAF protection, and Splunk or PLE based centralized logging for Pagero by 30 Sep 2026.
    
-   Complete creation, formal approval, and implementation of all ISRM tools required for Pagero, reaching 100% tooling migration, by 2026-12-31.
    
-   Deliver the full eSSO and MFA solution and complete the security technology migration required to support the French e-invoicing and e-reporting mandate by 01 Sep 2026.

## Executive Summary

Pagero Cloud Migration (Public) and Office Networking is delivering TR-standard public cloud environments and integrating six European offices into TR’s network, including routers, switches, wireless access points, ISP migration, and final handover to TechM support. This work underpins the Pagero acquisition by providing secure, reliable connectivity and a consistent tooling platform for Pagero teams.

Office integration is 50% complete across six sites against a plan to finish by 30 Sep 2026, with Ostersund and Skovde at 75%, Espoo at 60%, Stockholm at 70%, Langenfeld at 50%, and Gothenburg planned but not yet started. Despite ISP-related delays pushing individual site dates into late June and July, the aggregate milestone for completing all six offices by 30 Sep 2026 remains intact.

Overall status is Green, driven by office integration staying on track for 30 Sep 2026 completion while ISP delays are managed within contingency.

## Path to Green

The top risk remains ISP connectivity delivery delays, which we are mitigating through close ISP tracking, landlord coordination, and applying lessons learned on cabling and vendor control before handing sites over to TechM support.

## Milestones

- Complete office integrations for Ostersund and Skovde by 26 Jun 2026.  
- Complete office integrations for Espoo and Stockholm by 30 Jun 2026.  
- Complete office integration for Langenfeld by 30 Jul 2026.  
- Complete office integration across all six European offices by 30 Sep 2026.  
- Close out remaining cloud setup and migration activities and transition the program to steady-state by 17 Dec 2027.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Product Engineering & Platform Readiness is delivering S3NS-based pre-production and production environments, replicating Pagero’s current platform and enabling France e-invoicing and e-reporting in line with French PA and audit requirements. This work underpins France customer and supplier onboarding by ensuring the underlying platform, microservices, and controls are production-ready.  

Pre-production build in S3NS completed on 19 May 2026, four days later than planned, with the S3NS production environment now forecast to complete by 12 Jun 2026 versus the original 31 May 2026 plan, and internal pre-production testing is 50% complete against a revised 11 Jun 2026 target (beyond the original 31 May KPI date). Linux developer laptop compliance has reached 80% toward full Intune remediation by 30 Jun 2026, reducing but not yet closing the associated audit risk.  

Overall status is AMBER, driven primarily by the remaining Linux laptop Intune compliance gap, which keeps audit and security risk elevated despite a 30 Jun 2026 remediation target.  

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on closing the Linux Intune compliance gap by 30 Jun 2026 through escalated ETS support, dedicated re-enrollment sprints, and tight tracking against Cyber Essentials, ISO, and SOC 2 audit needs. In parallel, the team will hold the 12 Jun 2026 S3NS production readiness and 11 Jun 2026 internal testing completion as gates before declaring the platform fully ready for France e-invoicing and e-reporting.  

## Milestones

- Complete platform microservices readiness and internal functional testing in pre-production by 11 Jun 2026.  
- Complete S3NS production environment readiness for Pagero Online by 12 Jun 2026.  
- Complete the mid-year audit for the Pagero environment and achieve full Linux laptop Intune compliance by 30 Jun 2026, with Linux devices currently 80% compliant.  
- Close the Product Engineering & Platform Readiness program and transition to steady-state operations by 18 Dec 2026.

risks.title: Linux developer laptops not compliant in Intune may cause audit failures and security exposure
risks.description: A large number of Linux laptops used by Pagero developers dropped out of Intune because users did not log into the Intune app at least monthly. Re‑enrolling these devices into Intune is encountering errors and progressing very slowly, with different issues occurring on each laptop. Approximately 100 Linux laptops are currently not Intune‑managed, and there is poor visibility into the exact number because Intune is not functioning correctly for them. While day‑to‑day end‑user work is not currently impacted, this creates a compliance gap and a risk that non‑managed or even private Linux devices could be used to access customer data.
risks.impact_description: If Linux laptops remain unmanaged in Intune, the organization cannot demonstrate control over which devices exist within TR or whether they are compliant. This may cause failures or findings in Cyber Essentials, ISO, and SOC 2 audits, particularly the mid‑year (Q3) and Q4 audits. Lack of device control increases the risk that private, non‑company Linux devices are used to access customer data, potentially breaching internal security standards and regulatory obligations. Future activation of conditional access for single sign‑on may lock out developers with non‑compliant devices, causing disruption to development activities.

risk_owner.name: Bhamidipati Kanaka Durga, Phani Venkata Sai (TR Technology)

mitigation_plan_owner.name: Bhamidipati Kanaka Durga, Phani Venkata Sai (TR Technology)

risks.mitigation: Ola Nilsson continues to work directly with the ETS team to troubleshoot and resolve Intune re‑enrollment issues affecting Linux laptops and to support engineering teams with testing. Christer Wejke will keep actively chasing, monitoring progress, and escalating within ETS leadership (potentially via Cherie and above Mayank) to raise the priority of this work, emphasizing the compliance and audit impact. The goal is to re‑enroll all Linux laptops into Intune, restore full visibility of devices, and ensure they comply with TR standards before upcoming Cyber Essentials, ISO, and SOC 2 audits, particularly the Q3 audit.
risks.source_file_name: Pagero Integration - progress update ProdEng April 30 .docx

risks.title: Lack of Wiz support in SANS may delay required cloud security coverage for S3NS
risks.description: The Wiz security solution is currently not supported by SANS in the targeted environment. Bill communicated that there is no firm plan yet for how this will be addressed, despite a policy requirement to have this resolved by 2026. Recent discussions with Google (around 22 April) did not yield a clear delivery timeline for support. If support is significantly delayed, the project may lack the desired level of cloud security visibility and control, and compensating controls may be required.
risks.impact_description: If Wiz remains unsupported in SANS for an extended period, the S3NS platform will not have the intended Wiz-based visibility and protections. This may leave gaps in cloud security monitoring and vulnerability management, and could lead to deviations from TR security policy, which expects this to be in place by 2026. If auditors or internal security governance identify this gap, additional scrutiny or corrective actions may be imposed. Implementing compensating controls later under time pressure could consume significant time and resources and potentially delay other security and platform readiness activities.
risks.mitigation: Bill will obtain a more definitive timeline from SANS/Google regarding when Wiz will be supported and use that to decide on the strategy. If support can be delivered within 2026 (for example by Q4), the project may accept the delay with careful monitoring. If the timeline extends significantly (e.g., into 2027), Bill and the security team will design and implement compensating controls that provide a similar level of visibility and protection, balancing the effort and resources required against the expected duration until Wiz support becomes available.

assumptions.description: Service management process approvals, originally targeted for 30 April, have been extended to 30 June at the request of Lalit to allow more time for discussions and approvals with Kristine. Christer and Lorna agreed that this schedule shift does not currently create additional risk because BAU operations continue under the existing setup and there is already a functioning process in place.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The existing service management process is already functioning, and BAU operations are continuing without issue under the current arrangements. The change is only to the formal approval date, not to day‑to‑day operations.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Christer explicitly stated that there is currently 'no extra risk' from shifting the process approval date and that this new date is more realistic. The team continues to operate under a known, tested process, meaning the extension is largely administrative. BAU has not shown any deterioration due to the delay, supporting the assumption that operations remain safe until formal approval is granted.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If issues surface before approval (e.g., incidents tied to process weaknesses), the team will prioritize completion and approval of the service management process earlier than 30 June and introduce interim work instructions or temporary controls to stabilize BAU operations. They can also escalate to governance to secure expedited approvals.
assumptions.validation_method: Monitor BAU performance and incident handling between April and June; confirm with Kristine and governance stakeholders that no negative impacts or audit concerns arise from the extended approval date and that approvals are completed by 30 June.

issues.title: Linux laptops not managed in Intune, creating compliance and audit risk
issues.description: A significant number of Linux laptops used by Pagero developers have dropped out of Intune because users did not regularly log into the Intune app, and attempts to re-enroll them are encountering varied errors on different devices. Approximately 100 Linux laptops are currently not Intune-managed, which prevents TR from demonstrating full control over devices accessing customer data and may cause issues with conditional access and compliance audits (Cyber Essentials, ISO, SOC 2).
issues.impact_assessment: Without Intune management for all Linux laptops, TR lacks an accurate inventory and compliance status for devices accessing internal systems and customer data. This undermines the ability to enforce conditional access policies for single sign-on and creates a major gap for Cyber Essential, ISO, and SOC 2 audits, where auditors require evidence that all in-scope devices are known and compliant. There is also a risk that private, non-TR Linux devices could be used to access customer data, breaching internal standards.
issues.dependencies_affecting: ETS (Intune and device management), Pagero engineering teams using Linux laptops, Cyber Essential audits, ISO certification, SOC 2 audits, conditional access policies for SSO.
issues.resolution: Re-enroll all Pagero Linux laptops into Intune, resolve the device-specific errors currently blocking re-enrollment, and ensure ongoing processes so developers regularly log into the Intune app to remain active. ETS will provide L3 support while developers perform first-line activities.

## Executive Summary

Pagero – Legal Entity Migrations is delivering the migration of Belgium, Italy, and Poland from legacy IFS legal entities into new Thomson Reuters legal entities, enabling compliant billing, renewals, and notifications aligned to the broader Legal Entity Migration Strategy. This ensures regional customers are served under the correct legal, tax, and contract structures while standardizing commercial policy execution.

To date, 8 of 11 defined milestones are complete, including Sales Org creation in WRP, GSI updates, Eloqua/Temails code releases, and IFS/Pagero information collection, with all completed items delivered on their planned dates. Three milestones remain in progress, covering Conga order form enhancements through 30 Jun 2026, UAT sign-off targeted for 11 Jun 2026, and the Belgium/Italy and Poland business launches on 30 Jun 2026 and 01 Jul 2026 respectively.

Overall status is Green, driven by on-plan completion of all foundational system changes and testing preparation, with remaining work focused on final UAT closure and country go-lives.

## Path to Green

The primary mitigation focus is managing dependencies around IFS and Pagero Online updates on the 30 Jun 2026 and 01 Jul 2026 go-live dates so that final configuration changes avoid any finance blackout or billing disruption.

## Milestones

- Achieve UAT Sign-Off, with critical test scenarios passed and defects resolved or accepted, by 11 Jun 2026.  
- Complete Conga / Order Capture order form enhancements to support the new legal entities by 30 Jun 2026.  
- Complete Business Launch for Belgium and Italy by 30 Jun 2026.  
- Complete Business Launch for Poland by 01 Jul 2026.  
- Close out the Pagero Legal Entity migrations program, including post-go-live stabilization, by 10 Jul 2026.

## Executive Summary

Plat Eng AI Reimagine is deploying AI and automation across infrastructure services, platform operations, and software development to shift teams from manual execution to exception management and unlock measurable productivity and scale benefits. The program focuses on agentic infrastructure services, AI coding agents, and service management agents as the primary levers for value.

A high-level benefits delivery plan exists, but the phased, period-level plan remains in development.

Overall status is AMBER, driven by the absence of a detailed phased benefits delivery plan that provides period-level visibility to the 2026 financial targets.

## Path to Green

The path to Green centres on completing the phased benefits delivery plan by 15 Jun 2026, including quarterly and period-level benefit phasing, and using this as the baseline for monitoring realized benefits against the PLE financial targets. HR and Finance will continue partnering with Platform Engineering to confirm funding, legal dependencies, and benefit capture mechanisms so that realized savings can be tracked and reported consistently.

## Milestones

-   Complete the phased, period-level PLE benefits realization plan by 15 Jun 2026.
    
-   Achieve initial confirmed benefits realization for the PLE AI Reimagine portfolio by 30 Jan 2026.
    
-   Complete Agentic Infrastructure Services, AI Coding Agents Efficiency, and PLE Service Management Agents milestones by 31 Dec 2026.

risks.title: [PE14] Agentic CD Pipeline Generation Automation: AI Model context window limitation impacts Cumulus Agent scalability
risks.description: The current AI model used for the AI‑assisted Cumulus pipeline creation tool has a 1,000‑file context window limitation, which may restrict its ability to accurately process and validate large or complex repositories. This constraint presents a risk to the reliability, scalability, and completeness of pipeline generation and validation as the solution evolves beyond the current POC scope.
risks.impact_description: If the context window limitation is not addressed, the AI‑assisted pipeline creation tool may fail to fully analyze larger codebases or complex repository structures, produce incomplete or inaccurate pipeline definitions, require increased manual intervention (reducing expected productivity gains), and limit the solution’s ability to scale for broader enterprise adoption. This would delay progression beyond POC and weaken the business value case for MVP and Scale phases.
risks.mitigation: Engage the Tiger Team to assess architectural or design patterns that mitigate context size constraints (e.g., repository chunking, staged analysis, or selective context loading).

risks.title: Discover additional opportunities to close financial gap
risks.description: The current set of identified PLE Point Solutions (e.g., ADO Assist) may be insufficient to close the remaining gap to PLE financial targets, with limited additional use cases identified to date.
risks.impact_description: If additional opportunities are not discovered in a timely manner, PLE may fall short of committed financial targets, requiring re‑baselining or reliance on higher‑risk assumptions.
risks.mitigation: Initiate a structured discovery effort across PLE teams to identify incremental, high‑impact point solutions; prioritize use cases with short time‑to‑value and clear benefit attribution.

risks.title: Market‑Benchmarked Coding Efficiency Limits
risks.description: Coding efficiency improvements are market‑benchmarked at approximately 8–10%, making benefits planning and realization complex. Gains are incremental, distributed across multiple teams and tools, and not concentrated in a single measurable outcome, which complicates planning and value realization for the AI coding agents efficiency initiative.
risks.impact_description: Difficulty in quantifying, attributing, and realizing savings from coding efficiency improvements. Benefits may remain theoretical or be absorbed as additional delivery capacity rather than converted to measurable financial value. This will increase the challenge of demonstrating clear ROI to leadership and could erode confidence in coding efficiency as a defensible value lever for the PLE AI Reimagine program.
risks.mitigation: Shift success metrics from pure efficiency percentage improvements to capacity redeployment or avoided cost. Define clear benefit capture mechanisms (for example, reduced backlog growth and reduced contractor usage). Bundle incremental gains into aggregated benefit stories instead of reporting per use case. Apply risk‑adjusted benefit forecasting for coding efficiency use cases.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Service Mgmt AI Reimagine is delivering AI-driven L0/L1 operations, SRE recovery agents, standardized DevOps pipelines, and automated ITIL workflows so that service teams can shift from manual execution to exception management and higher-value product delivery. This matters because current incident handling, deployment, and change processes scale only with additional headcount, which is not economically sustainable.

Against 2026 targets of 23 SRE agents live in production by 31 Dec 2026, the roadmap calls for 15 agents by November and an AWS proof-of-concept for 4 agents that remains in progress past its 22 May 2026 target. Diamond Lane readiness is still constrained, with 4 of 11 core automation and criteria milestones cited as incomplete ahead of the 30 Jun 2026 framework-completeness target and key DevOps and ITIL value-realization roadmaps missing their May 2026 target dates.

Overall status is Amber, driven primarily by dependence on an unproven SRE agent technology stack whose delayed AWS proof-of-concept is pushing out validation of productivity and reliability benefits.

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on completing the AWS-based SRE agent proof-of-concept with clear pass or fail criteria, including parallel manual and automated runbook execution, by 31 Aug 2026 so that reliability and MTTR improvements are validated before scaling to the full 23-agent target. In parallel, the team will close the DevOps and ITIL value-realization roadmaps and finalize Diamond Lane CI criteria, product contracts, scorecard v1, and pipeline automation by 30 Jun 2026, using these as gating criteria for any further application or workflow onboarding.

## Milestones

- Stabilize Diamond Lane CI criteria, product contracts, scorecard v1, and pipeline-driven change automation by 30 Jun 2026.  
- Complete deployment of Change Enablement enhancements for ITIL by 31 Jul 2026.  
- Close SRE agent technology validation and associated risk mitigations, including the AWS proof-of-concept, by 31 Aug 2026.  
- Deliver the planned 23 production SRE agents and complete the Deployment of SRE Agents milestone by 31 Dec 2026.  
- Complete DevOps Acceleration, Deployment of TRT (ITIL), and overall Service Mgmt AI Reimagine program close-out by 31 Dec 2026.

risks.title: SRE Agent: Unproven technology dependency
risks.description: The workstream places a strategic "big-bet" on AI agent technology that has not yet been validated in production SRE environments. The core automated remediation and runbook execution capabilities depend on cloud-native AI services (AWS) whose reliability, accuracy, and performance at scale remain unproven within the organization.
risks.impact_description: Failure to prove out the technology delays or eliminates SRE productivity gains, exposing the portfolio to material concentration risk. Teams continue operating at current capacity, preventing each SRE from supporting additional Product Engineering teams and eroding the business case for the investment.
risks.mitigation: Accelerate validation through a time-boxed proof-of-concept using AWS infrastructure with the embedded AI Squad on a long-term basis. Define clear technical pass/fail criteria up front. Run parallel runbook execution (manual and automated) during the trial to measure accuracy and reduction in mean time to recovery (MTTR) before full commitment.

risks.title: SRE Agent: Unclear path to scaled benefits beyond initial scope
risks.description: The aggregate business value of the SRE Agent workstream is predicated on scaling beyond the initial product suite (LPP). There is currently no confirmed product roadmap or suitability assessment that provides a clear, sequenced line-of-sight into which additional products will benefit from automation, or when.
risks.impact_description: Without a defined scaling path, benefits remain constrained to a narrow initial scope, significantly reducing ROI and undermining stakeholder confidence. The workstream may be deprioritized before reaching the scale at which SRE-to-team coverage ratios improve materially across the portfolio.
risks.mitigation: Pillar LT to confirm the short-list of candidate products for the initial roadmap (noted as complete). Develop a detailed scaling plan that documents: (1) prioritization criteria for product suitability, (2) the sequencing logic that maximizes early benefit realization, and (3) a governance checkpoint at the end of each phase to validate the next tranche of candidates before expanding scope.

risks.title: DevOps: Diamond Lane Scale Readiness Risk – Incomplete Automation and Criteria Frameworks
risks.description: With 4 of 11 core milestones still in progress and ServiceNow policy integration intentionally deferred, there is a risk that Diamond Lane's CI criteria, product contracts, scorecard v1, and pipeline-driven change automation will not reach sufficient maturity by the 30 Jun 2026 target. This could prevent the program from enforcing eligibility and routing decisions in an auditable, repeatable way before broader application onboarding begins.
risks.impact_description: If the pipeline automation, rollback patterns, and scorecard frameworks are not stabilized before expansion, Diamond Lane risks scaling ahead of proven templates and controls. This could result in ungoverned production changes, audit exposure, and potential rollback failures for onboarded applications — undermining the program's core value proposition of faster, compliant delivery.
risks.mitigation: Gate all new application onboarding behind defined readiness criteria tied to scorecard v1 and crawl-stage rollback completion. Prioritize the 30 Jun 2026 milestone for CI criteria, contracts, and pipeline automation. Maintain the deferral of ServiceNow policy integration to avoid scope creep. Conduct bi-weekly checkpoint reviews against the path-to-green plan to surface blockers early and allow resource reallocation if needed.

risks.title: DevOps Diamond Lane – Limited '26 Product Coverage and VC Benefit Realization
risks.impact_description: Without a product in the 2026 plan that delivers meaningful VC benefits, the Diamond Lane program risks being perceived as a capability buildout rather than a value driver. This could affect stakeholder confidence, funding continuity, and prioritization decisions heading into 2027 planning cycles — particularly if leadership expects demonstrable ROI from the DevOps Acceleration investment within the year.
risks.mitigation: Identify and evaluate whether any current or near-term candidate products could be onboarded to Diamond Lane in a way that surfaces measurable VC benefits without compromising pilot integrity. In parallel, develop a clear narrative that frames the 2026 crawl-stage work as the prerequisite to VC realization in 2027, with defined benefit milestones tied to the expansion and enablement phase. Establish leading indicators (e.g., deployment frequency, change failure rate, manual effort reduction) that can serve as proxy VC metrics while the full model matures.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Comm Eng AI Reimagine is scaling AI-assisted development, testing, and service management across Commercial Engineering to improve productivity, reduce manual effort, and maintain service reliability while delivering ($3.3M+.8M ) of verified efficiency savings. The scope includes standardized IDE-based AI coding assistants, AI QA agents and AIOps and SRE agents for CE service management. The program also establishes a reusable AI skills library and operating model. Also, discovery efforts are currently underway within the Release Management and Technology Architecture domains to identify new opportunities.

Salesforce Coding Assistant adoption is currently about 38% of the production scope versus a 70% target, with 95% of eligible scope enabled but ~84 user stories still untagged. SAP GitHub Copilot coverage for target developers is at roughly 100% with governance in place, yet the adoption metrics are awaited. Overall use case–level plan still falls short of the committed savings and AI adoption dashboards remain partially incomplete, leaving productivity and savings trends directional rather than fully evidenced.

Overall status is Amber, driven primarily by the current shortfall against the benefits commitment, which is compounded by Salesforce tool/adoption gaps, SAP metrics measurement gap and incomplete AI adoption measurement.

## Path to Green

The path to Green centres on raising Salesforce Coding Assistant adoption toward the 70% target, and completing SAP GitHub Copilot metrics measurement execution so its contribution to the commitment is evidenced. In parallel, the team will resolve AI adoption dashboard data issues and progress the Core test-tool decision so that AI-driven QA coverage expands beyond the current non-Worksoft subset so productivity and efficiency gains can be measured reliably across all CE workstreams.

## Milestones

-   Complete the CE Service Management AI “plan on a page” and confirm any changes to TFMS and other AIOps onboarding dates by 12 Jun 2026.
    
-   Complete mitigation actions for Salesforce Coding Assistant adoption, AI adoption dashboard data quality, and delayed Playwright agent rollout by 15 Jun 2026.
    
-   Stabilize the AI Dashboard by resolving data quality issues and mitigating team availability gaps by 15th June.
    
-   Close the shortfall against the efficiency-savings plan by identifying and onboarding additional AI use cases by 30 Jun 2026.
    
-   Execute the finance-backed quarterly savings plan for SAP GitHub Copilot adoption and evidence associated benefits by 31 Jul 2026.
    
-   Complete the Comm Eng AI Reimagine program, including CE Service Management Agents, CE AI Coding Agents, CE QA Agents, Release Management, and Technology Architecture workstreams, by 31 Dec 2027.

risks.title: SAP Coding Assistant - Productivity/Benefits realization
risks.impact_description: If the native SAP Coding Assistant remains unavailable for on‑prem deployment and teams must rely on GitHub Copilot, overall SAP development productivity gains may be lower than planned. This could result in missed Q1 adoption and usage targets, reduced benefits realisation, and potential gaps against the finance-backed quarterly savings plan for the CE AI Coding Agents Efficiency project.
risks.mitigation: Adopt GitHub Copilot for SAP development with strong governance for both vendor and FTE teams to drive deeper usage. Implement an enablement plan to provide access to the majority of target users (aiming for 95–98% coverage) and configure an AI usage dashboard for tracking usage percentages and benefits. Revise Q1 targets as needed while agreeing critical actions with the VP to improve the baseline adoption and ensure alignment with the finance-backed quarterly savings plan.

risks.title: Benefit Mechanism
risks.description: Comm Eng benefits assumptions are tied to a contract model change (T&M → SOW + AI clauses) - outside the program’s direct control and may face attribution challenges
risks.mitigation: Ongoing engagement with Pillar VP and Finance to ensure savings attribution to AI are fair and accurate

risks.title: Salesforce Coding Assistant - low adoption (CE AI Coding Agents Efficiency)
risks.description: Usage reports indicate low adoption of the Salesforce Coding Assistant despite rollout and completion of training. Recent discussions highlight that Agentforce (Salesforce AI assistant) is moving to a licensed model with unclear licensing and/or alternative tool strategy, which may further depress adoption and complicate measurement.
risks.impact_description: If adoption of the Salesforce Coding Assistant remains low and the Agentforce tool becomes license-restricted without a clear procurement or alternative-tool decision, expected benefits will not be realised. Engineers may lose access to the current tool, continue to rely on manual coding, and anticipated productivity improvements will not be achieved. This may necessitate additional change management, training, and potentially tool migration investment, and could delay overall productivity and efficiency goals for the CE AI Coding Agents Efficiency project.
risks.mitigation: Continue targeted training and engagement to address resistance and increase adoption, supported by weekly checkpoints and adoption monitoring (current production-scope adoption is ~38% with 95% of scope enabled and 84 user stories still untagged). Work with Peer’s team and Salesforce to clarify the Agentforce licensing model and evaluate alternative tools (including GitHub Copilot) so that developers retain access to effective AI assistance. Escalate licensing/tool decisions to leadership (e.g., Linki and Peer) if needed, and consider revising adoption targets and timelines once the tool strategy is confirmed.

risks.title: Worksoft-based Core regression testing cannot leverage external AI/LLMs
risks.description: In Core, approximately 85% of the regression test bed relies on Worksoft, a third-party tool that currently does not allow integration with external LLMs such as Claude or GPT. Worksoft’s own AI capabilities are limited, and any AI agent would have to be built within Worksoft itself. A replacement tool (e.g., Tosca) is now being actively considered to address this constraint.
risks.impact_description: If Worksoft continues to block third-party LLM integration and no viable replacement tool is selected and implemented, the majority of Core regression tests (~85%) will remain unable to benefit from AI agents. This would significantly constrain AI-driven test automation and productivity gains in Core, leaving only the ~15% of tests using Selenium and Playwright able to leverage AI. The CE5 Testing Tools use case may fall short of adoption and efficiency targets, and the overall CE AI Reimagine benefits could be materially reduced. If a replacement such as Tosca is chosen and implemented, the risk could be reduced for all QE practices except the contact center, which would remain an exception.
risks.mitigation: Maintain an active dialogue with Worksoft, sharing the business case and exploring their roadmap and any options to expose AI/LLM capabilities or APIs. In parallel, progress evaluation of replacement tools: Sumathi is currently assessing Tosca as the primary contender for a Worksoft replacement and has committed to return with findings by mid-June (Tuesday/Wednesday of next week). Ensure her assessment explicitly considers AI advancements and coverage for QE practices so that any replacement supports AI agents. If a viable replacement is confirmed, move forward with a migration plan that transitions Core regression suites off Worksoft (with the only exception likely being the contact center), quantify the cost/risk/timeline, and track adoption in the AI testing dashboard once implemented. Escalate outcomes and recommendations to leadership to support a broader Core regression test tool strategy.

risks.title: Delivery Quality measurement using AI Adoption Dashboard
risks.description: Until all platforms have consistent adoption reporting and data feeds (including GitHub, Claude, and other LLMs), delivery quality and efficiency tracking remains partially mixed and directional rather than definitive. Recent changes in data pipelines and data stores (e.g., decommissioning of the LLM data store and incorrect mapping of GitHub pull requests) introduce additional risk to the accuracy and completeness of AI adoption metrics.
risks.impact_description: If key data sources for the AI adoption dashboard (such as Claude metrics, GitHub pull request counts and review comments, and other LLM usage metrics) remain inaccessible, decommissioned, or incorrectly mapped, the dashboard will under-report or misrepresent AI adoption and efficiency across Digital, GTM/KTLO, Core, and SAP. For example, decommissioning the LLM data store will remove Claude usage from future metrics, causing apparent drops in adoption percentages that are purely artefacts, while the GitHub pull request mapping issue prevents accurate reporting on Jason’s expectation that 100% of pull requests be AI-reviewed. This will erode confidence in reported KPIs, hinder evidence-based decision-making for leadership (including CIO-level reporting), and may delay benefit attribution and prioritisation of AI investments.
risks.mitigation: Continue onboarding all platforms to the AI adoption dashboard, but explicitly address the emerging data access issues: (1) Work with product engineering (e.g., Heema ) to identify and gain access to the new data store that will host Claude-related metrics now that the LLM data store is being decommissioned, and document the decommission date and pre-decommission Claude usage levels so that any apparent adoption drops can be correctly attributed. (2) Coordinate with the GitHub team, TR Data Factory team, and EDL support to correct the mapping of GitHub pull requests and review comments, ensuring PRs are attributed to the right users/teams instead of a single Thomson Reuters user; escalate via Angela and mark the request as a CIO-driven priority if responses stall. (3) For SAP, continue UAT and plan production deployment of the adoption widget around June 10, while working with SAP teams (e.g., Gojer and colleagues) to define how efficiency metrics can be captured from SAP’s separate repositories (potentially via ADO tasks) even if a direct automated feed is not yet available. Once these fixes are implemented, re-baseline adoption and efficiency metrics and clearly annotate any historical data gaps or step-changes in the dashboard.

entities.okrs: 1.1 Product stability

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

CIO Co-Counsel Next Next Rollout is delivering operational readiness for CoCounsel Next beta and general availability. Work in this project will form the basis of the new operating model for future catalyst launches.

Overall status is GREEN, the project remains on track for the 24 June beta, with all critical items identified and progressing, including incident management, ServiceNow integration, and capacity readiness.  
Key delivery risks are concentrated around rollback readiness and support model maturity, where complexity and incomplete coverage require interim operational arrangements ahead of GA.  
To mitigate this, the team is defining a simplified interim support model and escalation flow, ensuring operational continuity while full end-state processes are completed.  
Metrics and monitoring are largely in place via synthetics, with follow-on work planned to enable real user performance reporting and dashboards post-beta.  
Overall, the programme is tracking to beta with managed risk, strong cross-team alignment, and clear prioritisation on immediate deliverables.

## Path to Green

Not required.

## Milestones

-   Achieve beta release readiness, with all identified June beta requirements completed, by 19 Jun 2026.
    
-   Deliver Service Management readiness across Change/Release, Incident Management, Monitoring/Alerting, Ownership & Support, and Scale & Stability by 31 Jul 2026.
    
-   Complete ISRM production and launch readiness guardrails for AI capabilities by 14 Aug 2026 and achieve CoCounsel compliance readiness across key frameworks by 31 Aug 2026.
    
-   Close out the CIO Co-Counsel Next Rollout program and baseline framework for future catalyst launches by 31 Dec 2026.

risks.title: Unsecured HTTP connections between internal systems not remediated by GA
risks.description: Some internal systems in the CoCounsel Next architecture are communicating over HTTP instead of HTTPS. ISRM accepted this configuration for beta but explicitly stated it is not acceptable for GA. There is a risk that the required security changes may not be completed before GA.
risks.impact_description: If HTTP communication between internal components remains in place at GA, CoCounsel Next may be non-compliant with ISRM security requirements. This could delay or block GA approval, create security vulnerabilities, increase audit findings, and require emergency remediation work close to or after launch.

mitigation_plan_owner.name: Product engineering team for CoCounsel Next (e.g., delivery manager Chetan Singh and architect Josh Schmidt)

risks.mitigation: Track the HTTP-to-HTTPS remediation as a required GA guardrail item and ensure it is included in the operational readiness tracker. Coordinate with product engineering (delivery manager Chetan Singh and architect Josh Schmidt) to plan and implement secure HTTPS communication between all relevant internal systems before GA. Confirm with ISRM that the final configuration meets GA security expectations. As of 13 May 2026, ISRM has indicated that a solution exists, but service management has verified that the production load balancer is still accepting port 80/8080 traffic and routing to port 80 targets. Service management will re-check lower environments and production configuration after the target closure date to confirm that HTTPS has been fully deployed end-to-end.

milestones.name: First iteration of operational readiness framework ready for alignment with Product Engineering leadership

risks.source_file_name: Operational Readiness — CoCounsel Next Product Launch - Scope & requirements.docx

risks.title: Potential impact of CoCounsel Next on shared infrastructure capacity
risks.description: CoCounsel Next (an AI ESE project) may place significant additional load on shared infrastructure. Service management has identified a continuing risk that the traffic generated during multi-wave beta and upcoming GA could negatively impact shared systems, leading to degraded performance or instability for CoCounsel Next and other services sharing the same infrastructure.
risks.impact_description: If CoCounsel Next's usage exceeds the capacity of shared infrastructure, it could cause performance degradation, timeouts, or outages for CoCounsel Next and other shared services. This may jeopardize the GA launch, harm customer experience, and require emergency remediation effort across SRE, GCC, and product engineering teams.
risks.mitigation: Coordinate with the product engineering team and the service management scale program to ensure infrastructure scale testing adequately covers CoCounsel Next's expected and peak loads before GA. Review scale and load test results regularly, and ensure tests are run in pre-prod at higher levels than expected in production. Track this as a formal guardrail requirement for GA and ensure it is included in the operational readiness checklist. As of 13 May 2026, the team has improved visibility into scale testing and is confident in the current trajectory, but recognizes that scale and capacity validation must remain an ongoing activity throughout beta and post-GA rather than a one-time exercise.
risks.source_file_name: Operational Readiness — CoCounsel Next Product Launch - Scope & requirements.docx

risks.title: Lack of defined operational guardrails for AI ESE launches
risks.description: Service management does not yet have an agreed list of minimum operational readiness requirements (“guardrails”) for AI ESE projects like CoCounsel Next. ESE projects are intentionally doing things differently to enable speed, which changes the typical division of accountability and processes (e.g., change management, incident management, scale testing). Without defined guardrails, CoCounsel Next could proceed to GA without essential operational controls in place.
risks.impact_description: If the minimum operational requirements for ESE launches are not defined and agreed with product engineering before CoCounsel Next GA, the product may launch with inconsistent or insufficient processes for change, incident, and scale management. This could lead to operational instability, unclear responsibilities, and reduced ability for service management to protect production, potentially impacting customer experience and setting a problematic precedent for future ESE launches.
risks.mitigation:
Service management (including Kathy Holtzleiter and Justin Jenkins) will compile a list of critical guardrails and requirements needed for operational readiness in the ESE model, including scale testing expectations, use of ServiceNow (or alternative tools) for changes and incidents, and pre‑prod testing thresholds. Present this list to Wil LeBlanc for review and refinement, then align with ESE program leadership (e.g., via Wil’s discussions with Viola Matisse and Jason) to agree on a minimum set of requirements that must be met before GA.

 Once confirmed these requirements will form the scope of the project from a Service Management perspective.  Requirements will be used to create ADO work items and be tracked to completion.  This risk will be closed at that time.

milestones.name: First iteration of operational readiness framework ready for alignment with Product Engineering leadership

risks.source_file_name: Operational Readiness — CoCounsel Next Product Launch - Scope & requirements.docx

risks.title: Potential fragmentation of tooling and processes for incidents and changes under ESE
risks.description: In the ESE model, there is active discussion of using alternatives to ServiceNow for incident and change management. Some stakeholders view traditional tools as inconvenient or not “easy.” Service management relies on consistent tools like ServiceNow to operate effectively and ensure consistent processes for GCC staff and SRE teams. There is a risk that CoCounsel Next might adopt different tooling, fragmenting processes.
risks.impact_description: If CoCounsel Next uses alternative tools instead of ServiceNow for incident and change management, service management could lose centralized visibility and control. This may lead to inconsistent processes, reduced ability to coordinate responses across products, data gaps for reporting and governance, and difficulty enforcing standard practices for GCC and SRE teams.
risks.mitigation: Include use of standard service management tooling (e.g., ServiceNow for incident and change management) as a proposed guardrail in the ESE operational readiness requirements. Work with service management leadership and ESE leadership to determine where flexibility is acceptable and where consistency is required, and ensure CoCounsel Next’s chosen tools/approach are aligned with this decision before GA.
risks.source_file_name: Operational Readiness — CoCounsel Next Product Launch - Scope & requirements.docx

risks.title: Unclear production support ownership model for CoCounsel Next post‑GA
risks.description: There is no agreed model on who will own and provide production support for CoCounsel Next after GA. For non‑ESE products, service management typically owns production support. However, ESE messaging emphasizes that product engineering “builds it, deploys it, supports it.” Individual engineers, however, have expressed assumptions that service management might take over after beta. This misalignment means operational responsibilities are not defined.
risks.impact_description: If production support responsibilities remain unclear at GA, there may be gaps or overlaps in incident response, on‑call coverage, and problem management. This can lead to delayed incident handling, finger‑pointing, and poor customer experience, as well as burnout of teams unintentionally bearing unsupported workloads.
risks.mitigation:
Drive a discussion between service management leadership (Wil LeBlanc), CoCounsel product engineering leadership (e.g., Viola Matisse), and relevant stakeholders to explicitly define the production support model for CoCounsel Next (who owns support during beta, GA, and beyond). Document the agreed model, including escalation paths and hand‑offs, and incorporate it into the operational readiness criteria for GA.

Once operational readiness criteria are confirmed these will be moved into ADO as work items to track until project completion.

milestones.name: First iteration of operational readiness framework ready for alignment with Product Engineering leadership

risks.description: There is no agreed model on who will own and provide production support for CoCounsel Next after GA. For non-ESE products, service management typically owns production support. However, ESE messaging emphasizes that product engineering builds it, deploys it, supports it. Individual engineers, however, have expressed assumptions that service management might take over after beta. This misalignment means operational responsibilities are not defined.
risks.impact_description: If production support responsibilities remain unclear at GA, there may be gaps or overlaps in incident response, on-call coverage, and problem management. This can lead to delayed incident handling, finger-pointing, and poor customer experience, as well as burnout of teams unintentionally bearing unsupported workloads. In addition, misalignment with the EASY objective of keeping product engineering close to the impact of their deployments could cause friction with leadership expectations.
risks.mitigation:
Drive a discussion between service management leadership (Wil LeBlanc), CoCounsel product engineering leadership (e.g., Viola Matisse), and relevant stakeholders to explicitly define the production support model for CoCounsel Next (who owns support during beta, GA, and beyond). Document the agreed model, including escalation paths and hand-offs, and incorporate it into the operational readiness criteria for GA. 

As of 13 May 2026, the team has confirmed that the production support model is not part of the current guardrails list and must be managed as a separate deliverable (the support flow), with potentially significant staffing and training implications depending on the model chosen.
