latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

LHR3 DC Exit is migrating all business applications out of the LHR3 colo data center to cloud platforms and then completing dilapidation and closure of the facility. This enables full site exit and removal of ongoing run costs for the LHR3 data center.

Application migrations are structured around two key workstreams: Abacus/Barossa to Azure/AVD, which will account for 50% of migrations by 31 Dec 2026, and OTP to a NextGen AWS offering, which will bring the program to 100% of application migrations by 30 Jun 2027. Dilapidation and colo closure activities are planned to reach 100% completion by 31 Jul 2027, aligned with the overall data center exit.

Overall status is Green, driven by Abacus/Barossa and OTP migration milestones both in progress and currently aligned to their planned completion dates that deliver 50% and 100% of migrations respectively.

## Path to Green

The top RAID focus is resolving the Globalscape TAXONE geo-restricted SFTP dependency by delivering the AWS Transfer Family replacement solution by 31 Jul 2026 and migrating affected clients ahead of Globalscape license expiry at the end of 2026 to avoid blocking LHR3 shutdown.

## Milestones

- Complete Abacus/Barossa migration to Azure/AVD, delivering 50% of total application migrations, by 31 Dec 2026.
- Complete OTP client migration to the NextGen AWS offering and submit decommission requests for remaining LHR3 infrastructure, bringing application migrations to 100%, by 30 Jun 2027.
- Complete 100% of dilapidation and colo closure activities for LHR3 by 31 Jul 2027.
- Achieve full LHR3 data center exit program completion by 20 Sep 2027.

assumptions.title: SPLA licensing remains valid for on-prem LHR3/MSP workloads beyond November 2026 while Abacus/Barossa migration completes
assumptions.description: Project planning assumes that SPLA licensing for Microsoft components currently used by Abacus/Barossa in on-prem data centers (e.g., LHR3 or MSP) will remain valid beyond November 2026 as long as workloads stay in Thomson Reuters–owned data centers and are not run on hyperscalers (Azure, AWS, GCP, Alibaba). This allows the project to accommodate potential schedule slips into December 2026 or January 2027 without losing licensing coverage for the current Excel/Office-dependent solution during migration.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Software Asset Management has communicated that SPLA will not be available/applicable beyond November 2026, raising concerns that licensing might block or constrain the migration schedule. During the meeting, Bill Richardson clarified that recent SPLA terms and conditions changes primarily affect use on major cloud providers (Azure, AWS, GCP, Alibaba), and do not prevent Thomson Reuters from using SPLA in its own data centers. The project is therefore assuming SPLA remains usable on-prem while migration completes.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Bill Richardson stated that SPLA restrictions apply to workloads on certain hyperscalers (Azure, AWS, GCP, Alibaba) and do not prohibit SPLA use in Thomson Reuters–owned data centers. As long as Abacus/Barossa workloads remain in LHR3/MSP and not on those hyperscalers before migration cutover, SPLA can continue to be reported and paid for, keeping the project compliant even if dates slip slightly past November 2026. In the 2026-06-08 meeting, Lalit Pathak further indicated that based on discussions with Jason and Bill, the team believes they should be covered even if the schedule extends by a couple of months into 2027, though formal written confirmation is still required.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If validation shows SPLA cannot be used beyond November 2026 for on-prem workloads, or if Software Asset Management enforces an earlier stop: (1) renegotiate or seek explicit relaxation/extension from Microsoft; (2) accelerate removal of Excel/Office dependencies and migration to Azure/AVD; (3) evaluate and procure alternative licensing models that cover the interim period; and (4) adjust the migration and LHR3 exit schedule to ensure no unlicensed production use.
assumptions.validation_method: Coordinate with Software Asset Management and Microsoft licensing contacts to confirm written interpretation of SPLA terms (specifically around on-prem vs hyperscalers) and explicitly document that on-prem LHR3/MSP workloads remain in scope for SPLA beyond November 2026 while migration is underway.
assumptions.source_file_name: Colo Exit LHR3 - Abacus_Barossa Cloud migration for legacy app_clients to Azure_AVD (plus remove excel plug in) (1).docx

## Executive Summary

Disaster Recovery Optimization is delivering centralized, reusable cross-region infrastructure templates and failover automation for shared backend services and Auth0/CIAM, covering top-revenue products such as Westlaw and CoCounsel. This matters because a single AWS region outage today would simultaneously take down the company’s highest-revenue products.

As of 09 Jun 2026, 0 of 6 major milestones are complete, with 1 in progress and 5 planned against the 31 Dec 2026 program end date. Current work is concentrated on completing target-state DR architecture designs by 19 Jun 2026, which will enable remediation planning and subsequent AI-assisted DR assessments for Tier 1 applications.

Overall status is Green, driven by all planned milestones tracking to their baseline dates with no reported schedule variance.

## Path to Green

The primary mitigation focus is cleansing and reconciling DR application data in Fusion, Asset Insights and Service Health Dashboards so that architecture designs, compliance gap remediation and AI-assisted assessments are based on accurate Tier 1 system inventories.

## Milestones

- Complete target state DR architecture designs for prioritized Tier 1 applications by 19 Jun 2026.
- Jointly approve remediation plans for identified Tier 1 disaster recovery compliance gaps by 30 Jun 2026.
- Initiate AI-assisted disaster recovery assessments for remaining Tier 1 applications by 31 Jul 2026.
- Define and publish standard enterprise resilience patterns and ensure at least five standard resilience patterns are adopted by multiple Tier 1 applications by 30 Sep 2026.
- Implement approved remediation plans for Tier 1 applications identified in Q1 and Q2 and close the program by 31 Dec 2026.

## Executive Summary

**Scope:** The NYNJ Port Authority Compliance Program is delivering compliant government environments for HighQ, Contract Express, the CoCounsel Outlook Add-In HighQ integration and CoCounsel US. The new government environment meets the TR Government Compliance baseline and will reduce regulatory and contractual risk while strengthening Thomson Reuters’ position with government customers.

**Current Status:** Overall status is AMBER; HighQ Pen testing and FARB approval for the Sophos anti-virus remain open. The CoCounsel HIPAA and Privacy & Security Control funding is pending EPC decision on 18 Jun 2026.

HighQ and Contract Express are on target for the 30 Jun 2026 customer deliverable. HighQ Pen Testing may spill into the first week in July since DR work has been prioritized first. Contract Express received the final HIPAA assessment with no additional development work required. CoCounsel remains on target for 30 Sep FedRAMP deliverable. An EPC ask for funding to accelerate CoCounsel HIPAA remediation and Privacy & Security Control implementation is scheduled for 18 Jun. Funding is critical to meeting Q3 customer deliverable.

Top RAID Items:

-   Risk: Antivirus solution and cryptographic controls not finalized. FARB approval pending. Target resolution 12 Jun 2026
    
-   Risk: CoCounsel additional EPC ask approval pending. Target resolution 18 Jun 2026.
    
-   Risk: CoCounsel final HIPAA assessment. Target resolution 12 Jun 2026.
    
-   Dependency: EPC approval required for off-schedule 2026 CoCounsel US Privacy & Security Control and HIPAA Remediation funding; EPC meeting scheduled 18 Jun 2026. Delay puts 30 Sep 2026 deadline at risk.
    

## Path to Green

The path to green focuses on:

-   FARB approval for Sophos antivirus solution (12 Jun 2026)
    
-   HighQ Pen testing complete (30 Jun 2026)
    
-   EPC funding approval for CoCounsel HIPAA & Privacy Controls (18 Jun 2026)
    
-   DevOps capacity shift to CoCounsel Outlook Add-In (1 Jul 2026)
    

## Milestones

-   12 Jun 2026 – CoCounsel HIPAA assessment complete
    
-   12 Jun 2026 - HighQ antivirus solution approved by FARB.
    
-   30 Jun 2026 - HighQ and Contract Express government environments live in Production; Port Authority onboarding begins.
    
-   30 Sep 2026 - CoCounsel FedRAMP, HIPAA/Privacy Controls and Outlook Add-In (HighQ integration) available in Production.
    
-   01 Apr 2027 - NYNJ Port Authority compliance program complete; transition to steady-state operations.

risks.title: Service Management competing priorities may delay Port Authority work
risks.description: Competing priorities for Service Management work create a risk: Service Management needs prioritization away from the company‑wide migration to Azure and onto Port Authority work. If this does not happen, the Port Authority deadline may not be met.
risks.impact_description: If Service Management cannot reprioritize from the company‑wide Azure migration to Port Authority work, key service management deliverables for Port Authority may be delayed, risking missed contractual deadlines and impacting go‑live readiness.
risks.mitigation: Secure additional capacity so Service Management can continue the Azure migration while also supporting Port Authority work; Noah has approved $500K in CapEx for Service Management to bring in additional resources for the Azure migration.

risks.title: HighQ: Pen testing may exceed QA testing dates
risks.description: The full Pen testing completion dates will fall outside of the QA testing date window. This could put timelines at risk.
risks.mitigation: To meet the timelines, the team will create a delta report from the HighQ Commercial instance and the HighQ Gov instance to run Pen testing on, which brings the pen testing date back down before the QA testing window dates.

risks.title: HighQ Transparent File Encryption (TFE) implementation for HIPAA within FedRAMP boundary
risks.description: TFE for HIPAA must be defined and implemented appropriately while on the FedRAMP boundary. Developments may be required and were not estimated; documentation and mitigating controls need to be evaluated.
risks.impact_description: If TFE is not properly defined and implemented for HIPAA within the FedRAMP boundary, HighQ may not meet HIPAA expectations or internal risk posture, potentially delaying compliance, increasing audit findings, or requiring unplanned remediation work.
risks.mitigation: Evaluate and document appropriate TFE implementation and mitigating controls for HIPAA on the FedRAMP boundary; plan and perform any required development work and update documentation accordingly.

risks.title: WL/PL privacy control requirements and impact not yet understood
risks.description: For WL/PL, the team needs to understand what the requirements are for the 24 privacy controls that have now been approved. This could impact timelines but direction is not yet clear and estimates are still needed.
risks.impact_description: If WL/PL teams do not gain clarity on the 24 approved privacy controls and complete estimates, privacy‑related work may be delayed, potentially impacting WL/PL compliance posture and any Port Authority dependencies on these products.
risks.mitigation: Meet with Jenna to review the 24 required privacy controls for WL/PL, clarify expectations, and then complete effort estimates to inform planning and resourcing.

risks.title: Cloudflare setup on CARI commercial side may be delayed due to Ops team inexperience
risks.description: Cloudflare setup on the CARI commercial side is being performed by the Ops team for the first time. Because the team has not done this work before, there is a learning curve that may impact delivery timelines for the dual-region CARI commercial environment that underpins CoCounsel services.
risks.impact_description: If the Ops team requires more time than planned to complete Cloudflare setup due to inexperience, the schedule for standing up CARI APIs in USE2 (Pre Prod and Prod) and completing Cloudflare work for APIs and MFEs may slip, which could delay broader CoCounsel readiness and associated Port Authority and FedRAMP activities.
risks.mitigation: Schedule knowledge transitions for the Ops team and engage the DOE team, which previously supported FedRAMP, for additional assistance if required. Use this support to accelerate learning and reduce schedule impact while Cloudflare work is completed.

risks.title: CIAM orchestration token correctness may delay CARI integration and customer onboarding
risks.description: Previously, CIAM integration and customer onboarding for Port Authority products were blocked not by architecture but by token correctness. An authentication gap in CIAM orchestration tokens required for CARI integration prevented completion of integration with the new legacy token service.
risks.impact_description: If CIAM orchestration token issues are not resolved, CARI's integration with the new legacy token service would be delayed, slowing customer onboarding for Port Authority and potentially impacting downstream timelines for product enablement and compliance validation across HighQ, CoCounsel, and other in-scope products.
risks.mitigation: Continue technical validation of CIAM orchestration tokens; work closely with CARI/RAS on cutover activities, obtain and verify correct CIAM tokens, and complete integration with the new legacy token service so that CIAM is no longer a blocker for customer onboarding.

risks.title: IAM/CoCounsel tight coupling with HighQ limits failover and failback options
risks.description: If IAM/CoCounsel remains tightly coupled with HighQ under the chosen hosting model, single‑component failover/failback will be limited, which is acknowledged as a constraint of the chosen hosting model.
risks.impact_description: Limited ability to fail over or fail back IAM/CoCounsel independently of HighQ could reduce system resilience and increase recovery times during incidents, potentially impacting availability commitments for the Port Authority environment.
risks.mitigation: Accept the architectural constraint for the Port Authority timeline and manage operational risk through monitoring and incident response; consider decoupling or additional resiliency improvements in future post‑Port Authority enhancements.

milestones.name: NYNJ PA - HighQ available in Production

risks.title: FIPS cryptography requirements may cause microservice startup issues
risks.description: FIPS cryptography requirements may cause application startup issues, requiring additional joint troubleshooting; this is a current technical challenge for the microservices.
risks.impact_description: If FIPS cryptography requirements cause persistent startup issues, microservices may be unstable or unavailable in the FedRAMP/HIPAA environment, delaying deployment, increasing engineering effort, and potentially impacting Port Authority go‑live timelines.
risks.mitigation: Conduct joint troubleshooting of FIPS‑related startup issues for affected microservices, adjusting configurations or components as needed to ensure stable operation under FIPS requirements.

risks.title: HighQ and Contract Express resourcing at risk due to incomplete effort estimation

risks.impact_description: If the effort to meet the Port Authority contract is not accurately estimated, HighQ and Contract Express may be under‑resourced, causing schedule slippage, scope cuts, or quality issues in meeting contract requirements.
risks.mitigation: Complete detailed estimation for HighQ and Contract Express Port Authority work and request additional resources as needed following completion of estimation.

risks.title: HighQ antivirus tool Sophos may not meet FedRAMP FIPS 140‑2/3 requirements
risks.description: Sophos, an antivirus/security tool currently used by HighQ, has not been confirmed as compliant with FedRAMP requirements, specifically around FIPS 140‑2/3 encryption compliance. A similar issue previously required another internal team to abandon ClamAV and switch tools. If Sophos cannot prove compliance, HighQ may need to replace it with a different tool such as SentinelOne or Azure Defender, which could impact the engineering timeline.
risks.impact_description: If Sophos cannot demonstrate FIPS 140‑2/3 compliance and must be replaced, HighQ will face additional engineering work to select, integrate, configure, and validate a new antivirus tool, potentially delaying the Port Authority compliance schedule and introducing operational risk during the transition.
risks.mitigation: Evaluate Sophos for FIPS 140‑2/3 and FedRAMP compliance; if it cannot meet requirements, plan and execute a transition to a compliant tool such as SentinelOne or Azure Defender, including necessary engineering and testing.

milestones.name: NYNJ PA - HighQ available in Production

risks.title: HighQ antivirus scanning tool selection (Sophos / SentinelOne / Defender) remains unresolved
risks.description: For HighQ (and related CoCounsel integrations), identifying and validating a compliant antivirus/malware scanning tool is still in progress. Options under evaluation include Sophos, SentinelOne, and Microsoft Defender. License procurement has been completed, but verification of the selected solution against FedRAMP FIPS 140‑2/3 and Port Authority requirements is ongoing, including a planned FARB discussion on the Sophos solution.
risks.impact_description: If a compliant antivirus solution is not fully verified and approved in time, HighQ and dependent CoCounsel integrations may face delays achieving FedRAMP/HIPAA and Port Authority security requirements. Late changes to the selected tool (e.g., replacing Sophos if it fails FIPS validation) would introduce additional engineering, configuration, and testing effort, potentially impacting the June 30, 2026 compliance milestones and increasing operational security risk.
risks.mitigation: Continue evaluation of Sophos, SentinelOne, and Microsoft Defender with a specific focus on FedRAMP FIPS 140‑2/3 compliance and Port Authority requirements. Use the completed license procurement to accelerate hands‑on verification in the HighQ/FedRAMP environment. Engage FARB and ISRM to review the proposed Sophos solution and confirm acceptability; if Sophos cannot meet requirements, pivot to a verified alternative (e.g., SentinelOne or Defender) with minimal delay.

risks.title: Cloudflare setup on the CARI commercial side may be delayed due to Ops team inexperience
risks.description: Cloudflare setup on the CARI commercial side is being performed by the Ops team for the first time. Because the team has not done this work before, there is a learning curve that may impact delivery timelines for the dual‑region CARI commercial environment that underpins CoCounsel services.
risks.impact_description: If the Ops team requires more time than planned to complete Cloudflare setup due to inexperience, the schedule for standing up CARI APIs in USE2 (Pre Prod and Prod) and completing Cloudflare work for APIs and MFEs may slip. This could delay broader CoCounsel readiness, dual‑region resilience, and associated Port Authority and FedRAMP activities that depend on these services.
risks.mitigation: Schedule and execute knowledge transitions for the Ops team, and reach out to the DOE team (which previously supported FedRAMP) for additional assistance as needed. Use DOE support to accelerate learning and unblock Cloudflare configuration for APIs and MFEs so that USE2 Pre Prod and Prod timelines can be met.

risks.title: RAS Dual Region team bandwidth constraints may delay dual-region delivery
risks.description: The RAS Dual Region workstream is constrained by insufficient team bandwidth due to org-level resource changes. Team members were moved to other projects (e.g., Catalyst and AIESE), and remaining staff are spread thin across multiple initiatives.
risks.impact_description: If bandwidth issues persist, migration waves (especially Waves 1–4, including core services, RAS Search, and Notifications) may be delayed beyond planned dates, pushing out completion of RAS Dual Region work. This would in turn impact dependent CoCounsel and CARI dual-region and FedRAMP activities, as well as failover testing and resilience commitments required for Port Authority and other government customers.

mitigation_plan_owner.name: RAS Dual Region leadership (Karen McInrue and Tim Masso)

risks.mitigation: Conduct resourcing adjustment discussions to obtain clearer time commitments and add capacity; prioritize high-priority repos and dependency chains first. As of late May 2026, five additional resources have been added to the project. Continue progressing Waves 1–4 (core services, RAS Content Display and Search repos, Notifications, and remaining repos) with close tracking to complete migrations by end of June 2026, and prepare for scale and failover testing thereafter.

risks.title: FedRAMP vulnerability remediation may not achieve significant progress by end of June 2026
risks.description: Legal Research/Risk & Fraud (WL/PL) and CoCounsel FedRAMP environments still have thousands of outstanding vulnerabilities across FedRAMP and RAS-FedRAMP Plexus Service Mesh. Although overall trends are improving, recent sprints showed increases in remaining vulnerabilities, and teams note that achieving consistent sprint-cadence container refreshes and vulnerability reduction will be a struggle until a stable process is in place. There is a risk that the program will not achieve the targeted 'significant progress' in vulnerability reduction by the end of June 2026 needed for HHS FedRAMP ATO.
risks.impact_description: If significant vulnerability reduction is not achieved by the end of June 2026, HHS FedRAMP ATO could be delayed due to unresolved SAR discrepancies and non-compliance reports, and Port Authority's reliance on these FedRAMP environments may be impacted. This could extend timelines for container hardening, dual-region readiness (including US East2 builds), and overall government compliance.

risk_owner.name: Legal Research/Risk & Fraud and CoCounsel FedRAMP engineering leads

risks.mitigation: Continue to adjust Plexus and RAS container refreshes from monthly or longer to monthly or every 2 weeks (aligned to sprint cadence), make this cadence business-as-usual (BAU), and implement ConMon monitoring. Focus sprint work on reducing outstanding vulnerabilities in WL/PL and CoCounsel FedRAMP environments to achieve the defined 'significant progress' by end of June. Proceed with building out US East2 region RAS/CARI containers behind the FedRAMP change request while monitoring their impact on non-compliance reports, and ensure vulnerabilities introduced by new builds are promptly remediated.

risks.title: HighQ: CSPP – Microsoft program requirement for WOPI (8 week expected time) – request submitted
risks.description:
For continuity of service within the new HighQ Azure Gov environment of our Open-in-Office-for-the-Web/WOPI integration, we are required to submit a CSPP environment change request to Microsoft. 
 
This request has been submitted and normally this process should take 4-5 weeks for Microsoft to complete, however, they informed us May 22 that, due to issues on their side with Office deployment via CSPP, this could now take up to 8 weeks. 
 
Despite detailed conversations with Microsoft over the last 3 months in relation to this service, we weren't previously informed of this requirement, however, we are doing all we can to expedite execution via Microsoft as quickly as possible.  
 
As a result, it is likely the Open-in-Office-for-the-Web capability will not be available immediately upon release of the HighQ instance to PANYNJ and work-arounds may need to be employed (e.g. download documents, then edit locally) in the interim period.
risks.impact_description: No impact to delivery, but it will limit functionality delivered on June 30 if Microsoft cannot accelerate their work.
risks.mitigation:
1. Noah will escalate to Microsoft for a faster turn around, closer to the 4 week promised timeframe.
2. As a workaround, the customer can download the file to their local machine, open in Microsoft products, edit and then reupload. This would be stated on the Customer Responsibility Matrix, such that the customer will need to take responsibility once data leaves the HighQ domain (i.e. they open a file in Office)

risks.title: DevOps bandwidth constraints may delay CoCounsel Outlook Add-In and CoCounsel US compliance work
risks.description: The DevOps team supporting CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add-In and CoCounsel US HIPAA/privacy work is very resource constrained until the end of Q2 2026. While application teams are progressing sprint plans (sprints 11–15 for both the Outlook Add-In privacy/security controls and CoCounsel HIPAA documentation and control-evidence work), they report very limited DevOps engagement.
risks.impact_description: If DevOps bandwidth remains constrained, key technical and operational tasks—such as Azure App registrations, CI/CD compliance gates, deployment of AKS/FIPS configurations, K8s pod security settings, and infrastructure changes in Azure Gov—may not be completed in sync with application sprints. This could delay E2E testing across Azure Gov and M365, postpone achieving compliant runtime environments for the Outlook Add-In and CoCounsel US, and ultimately push out Q3 2026 delivery of HIPAA and privacy controls required for Port Authority.
risks.mitigation: Prioritize DevOps support for CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add-In and CoCounsel US workstreams through Q2 2026 by explicitly reserving capacity for Azure App registrations, CI/CD pipeline changes, and AKS/FIPS configuration work. Coordinate sprint planning between application teams and DevOps so that critical infrastructure tasks are scheduled early in sprints 11–15. Consider temporary reallocation of additional DevOps engineers or engaging shared services to cover the Q2 peak demand.

assumptions.title: Azure Gov environment will be available in early June 2026 for Add-In and CoCounsel testing
assumptions.description: Planning for the CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add-In and related HighQ integration assumes that the Azure Gov environment will be available in early June 2026, enabling early infrastructure testing and resolution of compatibility gaps.

owner.name: CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add-in team

assumptions.rationale_basis: The path-to-green narrative and earlier weekly status reports stated that teams expected to move to Green in early June once Azure Gov was available, so they could surface infrastructure issues and resolve compatibility gaps before HighQ integration in Q3 2026.
assumptions.validity_explanation: As of the 2026-05-28 Weekly Status, sprint plans for CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add-In and CoCounsel US HIPAA/privacy work continue to assume Azure Gov availability in time to support infrastructure testing and E2E validation, but the path-to-green expectation has shifted to July 2026 ("Hope to be Green in July once Azure Gov is available to Add-In team and we have full DevOps capacity"). This indicates continued confidence that Azure Gov will be available in early summer, while acknowledging that integration and testing activities may extend into July rather than concluding in June.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If Azure Gov is not available by early June, adjust sprint timelines by extending or intensifying E2E testing once the environment becomes ready, consider using interim non-Gov environments for limited functional validation where compliant, resequence lower-priority backlog items, and coordinate with stakeholders to protect critical Q3 2026 HighQ integration milestones.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm Azure Gov environment readiness via environment build status from infrastructure teams and successful execution of initial pre-production compliance tests using the HighQ-managed environment in Azure Gov.

dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Without a consistent PII definition, teams may mis‑scope or inconsistently implement privacy controls, risking non‑compliance with Port Authority and internal standards.
dependencies.mitigation: Use the TR Data Classification Standard as the basis; treat all 'Strictly Confidential' data and specified 'Confidential' items as PII, as documented in the referenced PII definition document.

dependencies.title: Obtain government authorization of CoCounsel FedRAMP legal research packet
dependencies.description: CoCounsel FedRAMP onboarding is dependent on government authorization of the legal research packet.
dependencies.dependent_on: Government authorization of CoCounsel legal research packet
dependencies.consumer: CoCounsel FedRAMP authorization and Port Authority onboarding
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If authorization is delayed, CoCounsel FedRAMP and subsequent Port Authority onboarding could be pushed back, impacting the program’s overall timeline.
dependencies.mitigation: Actively monitor for approval and raise awareness and planning activities early if delays appear likely.

dependencies.title: Review Contract Express HIPAA gap analysis and share identified gaps
dependencies.description: The Contract Express HIPAA gap analysis must be reviewed and any identified gaps communicated to the team so that estimation and remediation work can be completed.
dependencies.dependent_on: Maria & Jenna (Privacy workstream leads) completing HIPAA assessment for Contract Express
dependencies.consumer: Contract Express Port Authority HIPAA compliance workstream
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Without clarity on HIPAA gaps, Contract Express cannot be accurately estimated or remediated, putting HIPAA compliance for the Port Authority at risk.
dependencies.mitigation: Maria and Jenna, as privacy workstream leads, will complete the assessment and share detailed findings with the team.

dependencies.title: Review HighQ HIPAA gap analysis and share identified gaps
dependencies.description: The HighQ HIPAA gap analysis must be reviewed and any identified gaps communicated to the team so that estimation and remediation work can be completed.
dependencies.dependent_on: Maria & Jenna (Privacy workstream leads) completing HIPAA assessment for HighQ
dependencies.consumer: HighQ Port Authority HIPAA compliance workstream
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Without clarity on HIPAA gaps, HighQ cannot be accurately estimated or remediated, putting HIPAA compliance for the Port Authority at risk.
dependencies.mitigation: Maria and Jenna, as privacy workstream leads, will complete the assessment and share detailed findings with the team.

dependencies.title: Review CoCounsel HIPAA gap analysis and share identified gaps
dependencies.description: The CoCounsel HIPAA gap analysis (covering FedRAMP and commercial environments) must be reviewed and any identified gaps communicated to the team for estimation and remediation. It appears commercial CoCounsel is already suitable for HIPAA; the FedRAMP environment must adhere to the same HIPAA control implementations.
dependencies.dependent_on: Maria & Jenna (Privacy workstream leads) completing HIPAA assessment for CoCounsel
dependencies.consumer: CoCounsel Port Authority HIPAA compliance workstream
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Without clarity on HIPAA gaps, CoCounsel cannot be accurately estimated or remediated, risking HIPAA compliance for Port Authority.
dependencies.mitigation: Maria and Jenna will complete the HIPAA assessment and share detailed findings with the team.

dependencies.title: Collect Port Authority CIAM requirements for potential separate workstream
dependencies.description: Government will collect any Port Authority CIAM requirements and relay them to Harvarinder Batth. Any resulting work from this effort will be treated as its own workstream and not handled under security or privacy.
dependencies.dependent_on: Government (Port Authority) customer requirement gathering
dependencies.consumer: Potential future CIAM workstream for Port Authority
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Delay in collecting customer requirements could postpone planning and initiation of any necessary CIAM work but does not directly block the core security/privacy workstreams.
dependencies.mitigation: Paul McClaughry to proactively collect requirements from the customer and provide them to the relevant CIAM owner.

dependencies.title: Ensure FedRAMP is fully operational before CoCounsel Port Authority onboarding
dependencies.description: CoCounsel Port Authority onboarding cannot begin until the FedRAMP environment is fully operational.
dependencies.dependent_on: Completion and operational readiness of CoCounsel FedRAMP environment
dependencies.consumer: CoCounsel Port Authority onboarding
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If FedRAMP is not operational, CoCounsel cannot be onboarded for Port Authority, pushing back delivery for CoCounsel in the program timeline.
dependencies.mitigation: Plan CoCounsel Port Authority onboarding only after FedRAMP is live; sequence Port Authority work post‑FedRAMP go‑live.

dependencies.title: Resolve cryptography/encryption-decryption approach with FARB and ISRM
dependencies.description: HighQ, Contract Express, and the CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add‑in require clarity and approval on the cryptography/encryption‑decryption approach, requiring a FARB outcome and ISRM input.
dependencies.dependent_on: FARB decision and ISRM guidance on cryptography/encryption
dependencies.consumer: HighQ, Contract Express, and CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add‑in security implementations
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Without agreed cryptography and encryption‑decryption guidance, implementation and compliance with FedRAMP and HIPAA could be delayed, impacting timelines.
dependencies.mitigation: Engage FARB and ISRM to obtain an outcome and formal input for cryptographic standards and ensure implementation across products.

dependencies.title: Review HighQ integrations for HIPAA compliance
dependencies.description: HighQ’s integrations with third‑party and Thomson Reuters products (e.g., Microsoft Teams, Contract Express, Microsoft Office, DocuSign, Office 365 Gov/WOPI, and others) must be reviewed to confirm HIPAA compliance under the revised scope.
dependencies.dependent_on: Assessment of over 20 integration components including Mail Server, DocuSign, Office 365 Gov (WOPI), Teams, and others
dependencies.consumer: HighQ Port Authority HIPAA compliance workstream
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If integration components are not reviewed and remediated as needed, HighQ may fail to meet HIPAA expectations for Port Authority, risking compliance and go‑live timelines.
dependencies.mitigation: Review each integration component against HIPAA requirements under the new scope and track high‑risk items such as mail server, DocuSign, and Office 365 Gov (WOPI).

dependencies.title: Build HighQ FedRAMP/HIPAA environment within buffer to protect dependent activities
dependencies.description: The HighQ environment build has exhausted its schedule buffer; any delays will impact a range of dependent activities.
dependencies.dependent_on: HighQ engineering and infrastructure teams completing environment build
dependencies.consumer: All downstream HighQ Port Authority workstreams and integrations
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Delays in environment build will directly push out all dependent testing, integration, and compliance activities, jeopardizing delivery timelines.
dependencies.mitigation: Actively track and manage this as a risk even though it is currently on track, ensuring rapid response to emerging delays.

dependencies.title: Select compliant antivirus scanning tool for HighQ (Sophos/SentinelOne/Defender)
dependencies.description: HighQ must identify an antivirus/malware scanning tool that meets FedRAMP FIPS 140-2/3 cryptographic requirements, evaluating options such as Sophos, SentinelOne, and Microsoft Defender. License procurement has been completed and verification of the selected option is in progress.
dependencies.dependent_on: Tool evaluation and compliance verification for Sophos, SentinelOne, and Defender
dependencies.consumer: HighQ FedRAMP/HIPAA environment security posture
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If a compliant antivirus solution is not selected and verified in time, HighQ may need to make late changes to security tooling, impacting the engineering timeline and potentially delaying FedRAMP/HIPAA readiness and Port Authority commitments.
dependencies.mitigation: Continue evaluation and compliance verification of Sophos, SentinelOne, and Defender; license procurement has been completed and verification is in progress for the selected option(s). If no single tool meets requirements, explore alternate strategies based on Fortreum and security team guidance.

decisions.title: Host HighQ and Contract Express in Azure GovCloud
decisions.description: The HighQ and Contract Express environments for the Port Authority program will be hosted in Azure GovCloud rather than commercial Azure.
decisions.rationale: Using Azure GovCloud aligns with FedRAMP requirements and government customer expectations for data residency and security.
decisions.options_considered: Commercial Azure versus Azure GovCloud for HighQ and Contract Express environments.

decisions.title: Use CoCounsel FedRAMP Moderate for Port Authority security requirements
decisions.description: To meet Port Authority contractual security requirements, CoCounsel will satisfy all security obligations by achieving FedRAMP Moderate authorization (anticipated completion in Q3 2026), without separate additional security work specifically for Port Authority.
decisions.rationale: Leveraging the existing FedRAMP Moderate program avoids duplicative work and ensures a standardized security posture that meets Port Authority expectations.
decisions.options_considered: Performing separate Port Authority‑specific security enhancements for CoCounsel versus relying on the broader FedRAMP Moderate authorization.

decisions.title: Layer privacy and HIPAA controls onto CoCounsel FedRAMP environment
decisions.description: CoCounsel will implement required privacy and HIPAA controls on top of its FedRAMP version to meet full Port Authority requirements, rather than maintaining separate implementations.
decisions.rationale: Extending the FedRAMP environment with privacy and HIPAA controls consolidates compliance into a single hardened environment and simplifies operations.
decisions.options_considered: Implementing privacy and HIPAA controls separately outside the FedRAMP environment versus layering them onto the FedRAMP CoCounsel platform.

decisions.title: Use product-level templates for privacy controls
decisions.description: For each privacy control, control templates will be maintained at the product level (one template per control per product) rather than a single shared template across products.
decisions.rationale: A single shared template approach, as used for FedRAMP, would be too time‑consuming for the Port Authority program timeline; product‑level templates provide flexibility while allowing reuse where possible.
decisions.options_considered: A single control template per control shared across products (FedRAMP-style) versus separate control templates per product for each privacy control.

decisions.title: Rely on CIAM FedRAMP for authentication
decisions.description: CIAM FedRAMP will be used as the authentication system. HighQ and Contract Express will reuse all FedRAMP systems, including the CIAM FedRAMP solution.
decisions.rationale: Reusing the existing CIAM FedRAMP solution leverages an already FedRAMP-audited component, reduces additional security work, and maintains consistency across products.
decisions.options_considered: Using CIAM FedRAMP for authentication versus deploying a separate or local account authentication solution for Port Authority.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Decision 0018 regarding local account support; dependency 0024 regarding CIAM requirements gathering.

decisions.title: Exclude CoCounsel integration from June Port Authority deliverable
decisions.description: CoCounsel integration is not required for the June Port Authority deliverable. CoCounsel will instead deliver with FedRAMP in Q3 2026.
decisions.rationale: Deferring CoCounsel integration to Q3 aligns its delivery with FedRAMP and reduces scope and risk for the June Port Authority milestone.
decisions.options_considered: Including CoCounsel integration in the June Port Authority deliverable versus deferring it to align with FedRAMP in Q3 2026.
decisions.dependencies_linked: CoCounsel FedRAMP authorization dependency (0014) and broader CoCounsel HIPAA/privacy schedule decisions (0038, 0062).

decisions.title: Define critical HighQ features for June 30 Port Authority deliverable
decisions.description: For the June 30 Port Authority deliverable, the critical HighQ features are iSheets, Rule Builder, and Contract Express (document automation).
decisions.rationale: Focusing on iSheets, Rule Builder, and Contract Express ensures the HighQ government environment meets the core contractual requirements by the June 30 deadline.
decisions.options_considered: Various possible HighQ feature sets, including broader or narrower subsets, for the government version.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Dependencies on HighQ environment build and Contract Express integration; estimation exercises referenced in decisions 0027 and 0028.

decisions.title: Schedule HighQ Office Plug‑In for Q3 2026, not June deadline
decisions.description: The HighQ Office Plug‑In will be delivered as part of the Q3 2026 version and does not have an end‑of‑June deadline for the Port Authority project.
decisions.rationale: The Office Plug‑In is not critical to the June 30 Port Authority deliverable and can be deferred to reduce near‑term scope and risk.
decisions.options_considered: Delivering the HighQ Office Plug‑In by June 30 versus deferring it to Q3 2026.
decisions.dependencies_linked: HighQ Q3 2026 release planning and engineering capacity.

decisions.title: Do not support local accounts; rely on CIAM FedRAMP federated SSO
decisions.description: The Port Authority will use CIAM FedRAMP, which supports only federated SSO. Local username/password authentication will not be supported. No additional security work is required for the CIAM team for Port Authority because the CIAM solution has already passed FedRAMP audit. Some privacy controls may be implemented in CIAM FedRAMP in the second half of 2026 after FedRAMP ATO, subject to scope definition.
decisions.rationale: The CIAM FedRAMP solution was consciously designed for federated SSO only and has already passed FedRAMP audit; maintaining this model avoids additional work and preserves the FedRAMP boundary integrity.
decisions.options_considered: Supporting local account authentication for Port Authority versus requiring onboarding via federated SSO through CIAM FedRAMP.
decisions.dependencies_linked: CIAM FedRAMP solution and FedRAMP privacy controls scoping with James Pena and Jenna Perrin.

decisions.title: Move HighQ to Azure GovCloud
decisions.description: HighQ will be moved to Azure GovCloud for the government version.
decisions.rationale: Hosting HighQ in Azure GovCloud aligns the product with FedRAMP and government customer requirements and is consistent with decisions made for other products in the program.
decisions.options_considered: Retaining HighQ in commercial Azure versus moving to Azure GovCloud.
decisions.dependencies_linked: HighQ environment build dependency (0060) and FedRAMP/HIPAA-related decisions such as 0040 and 0052.

decisions.title: Keep separate commercial and government systems for HighQ and Contract Express
decisions.description: There will be two systems for each application: one commercial system, which remains as it is today, and a separate government system maintained independently from the commercial version.
decisions.rationale: Separating commercial and government systems simplifies compliance and operational boundaries for FedRAMP/HIPAA and Port Authority requirements.
decisions.options_considered: Maintaining a single unified system for both commercial and government use versus running separate commercial and government systems.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Azure GovCloud hosting decisions (0008, 0011) for HighQ and Contract Express and FedRAMP Moderate planning (0026).

decisions.title: Defer FedRAMP Moderate independent assessment for HighQ and Contract Express
decisions.description: HighQ and Contract Express will implement the technical work needed to achieve FedRAMP Moderate level security by June 30, 2026, to meet Port Authority requirements, but an independent third‑party FedRAMP Moderate assessment will only be performed later when they formally pursue FedRAMP Moderate authorization.
decisions.rationale: Port Authority requires a FedRAMP‑equivalent security posture but does not require an immediate formal FedRAMP Moderate assessment; deferring the assessment reduces near‑term cost and schedule pressure while still delivering the necessary technical controls.
decisions.options_considered: Completing a full independent FedRAMP Moderate assessment by June 30 versus implementing the technical controls by June 30 and deferring the formal assessment.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Security control implementation for HighQ and Contract Express and future FedRAMP PMO involvement for templates (0029).

decisions.title: Decide on subset of features for government HighQ
decisions.description: It was agreed that, following estimation exercises targeted for February 6, 2026, a decision would be made regarding whether the government version of HighQ will deliver a subset of features and, if so, which features will be included or excluded.
decisions.rationale: Understanding the effort and constraints first via estimation allows an informed decision on which HighQ features can be delivered in the government environment by the required timelines.
decisions.options_considered: Delivering the full HighQ feature set for government versus delivering a subset of features tailored to Port Authority needs and resource constraints.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Estimation exercises for HighQ; follow‑on action to share list with April Jones.

decisions.title: Decide on subset of features for government Contract Express
decisions.description: It was agreed that, following estimation exercises targeted for February 6, 2026, a decision would be made regarding whether the government version of Contract Express will deliver a subset of features and, if so, which features will be included or excluded.
decisions.rationale: Estimation results are needed before committing to a specific subset of Contract Express features for the government environment.
decisions.options_considered: Delivering the full Contract Express feature set for government versus delivering a subset of features tailored to Port Authority requirements and capacity.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Estimation exercises for Contract Express; follow‑on action to share list with April Jones.

decisions.title: Do not complete control templates for each security control prior to FedRAMP certification
decisions.description: The team will not complete a control template for each security control as part of the Port Authority program. When HighQ and Contract Express pursue FedRAMP certification, the FedRAMP PMO will own the control templates.
decisions.rationale: Deferring control template creation reduces workload and focuses the program on implementing necessary controls rather than duplicating FedRAMP PMO responsibilities.
decisions.options_considered: Creating control templates for each security control during the Port Authority program versus relying on the FedRAMP PMO to own templates during formal certification.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Security control implementation for HighQ and Contract Express; future FedRAMP PMO engagement.

decisions.title: Run Contract Express as a separate service, not hosted inside HighQ
decisions.description: Contract Express will not be hosted or run inside HighQ; it will operate as an independent system even in the government environment.
decisions.rationale: Separating Contract Express reduces architectural coupling and simplifies security and operational boundaries, especially under FedRAMP and Port Authority constraints.
decisions.options_considered: Hosting/embedding Contract Express inside HighQ versus running Contract Express as a standalone service.
decisions.dependencies_linked: HighQ–Contract Express integration patterns and environment design.

decisions.title: Exclude HIPAA compliance for WL and PL at launch
decisions.description: HIPAA compliance is not in scope for Port Authority for Westlaw (WL) and Practical Law (PL) at launch because customers cannot upload information into these products unless additional upload capabilities are added later.
decisions.rationale: Since no PHI will be uploaded, WL and PL do not need HIPAA compliance for the initial Port Authority scope, reducing unnecessary work.
decisions.options_considered: Including WL and PL in scope for HIPAA compliance versus excluding them due to lack of PHI upload capabilities.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Product feature set for WL/PL; any future features enabling data upload could change scope.

decisions.title: Remove CoCounsel data migration tool from Port Authority scope
decisions.description: The CoCounsel data migration tool is removed from the Port Authority scope. Port Authority users will not require migration of previously uploaded documents; they can re‑import items as needed since they will retain access to the commercial instance.
decisions.rationale: Accounts have confirmed that migration of uploaded data from the commercial to the FedRAMP environment is not required, so removing this work reduces scope and complexity without impacting user outcomes.
decisions.options_considered: Including a CoCounsel document upload migration tool in scope versus relying on users to re‑import documents from the existing commercial instance.
decisions.dependencies_linked: CoCounsel FedRAMP deployment and user access to the commercial CoCounsel environment.

decisions.title: Scope product integrations for CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add‑in (HighQ focus only)
decisions.description: For the CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add‑in, HighQ is the only required product integration for the Port Authority deliverable. CoCounsel and Legal Tracker integrations will be disabled and should not be available.
decisions.rationale: Limiting integrations to HighQ minimizes scope, reduces security and compliance complexity, and focuses on the required integration for Port Authority.
decisions.options_considered: Enabling multiple product integrations (HighQ, CoCounsel, Legal Tracker) in the Outlook Add‑in versus restricting the integration to HighQ only for the Port Authority deployment.
decisions.dependencies_linked: CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add‑in architecture and HighQ FedRAMP/HIPAA environment.

decisions.title: Set delivery date for Outlook CoCounsel Web Add‑in (HighQ integration) to Q3 2026
decisions.description: The Outlook CoCounsel Web Add‑in, with HighQ integration only, is required by the Q3 go‑live and is not required for June 30, 2026, as it does not impact data ingestion.
decisions.rationale: Deferring the Outlook Add‑in to Q3 avoids overloading the June 30 milestone with non‑critical functionality that does not affect data ingestion or compliance.
decisions.options_considered: Delivering the Outlook CoCounsel Web Add‑in by June 30 versus delivering it for the Q3 go‑live.
decisions.dependencies_linked: HighQ Q3 go‑live timeline and CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add‑in development.

decisions.title: Defer CoCounsel privacy control delivery for Port Authority to 2027 (superseded by later decision)
decisions.description: The CoCounsel privacy control delivery for Port Authority will be delayed until 2027, alleviating 2026 funding constraints while still meeting customer contractual needs. FedRAMP and HIPAA work will continue as originally planned. CoCounsel estimates for this deferred work will be included in the 2027 EPC funding asks.
decisions.rationale: Deferring privacy controls to 2027 reduces 2026 funding pressure while preserving the ability to meet overall contractual obligations by extending the delivery timeline.
decisions.options_considered: Delivering CoCounsel privacy controls in 2026 versus deferring their delivery to 2027 while continuing FedRAMP and HIPAA work.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Later decision 0062, which updates the CoCounsel HIPAA and privacy control delivery timeline; CoCounsel FedRAMP and HIPAA remediation schedules.

decisions.title: Set CoCounsel HIPAA remediation and privacy control implementation timeline to Q1/Q2 2027 (later updated)
decisions.description: With the delay in CoCounsel privacy control delivery, it was decided that CoCounsel would have until Q1/Q2 2027 to deliver, with the expectation that HighQ is FedRAMP certified for integration by then and CoCounsel privacy controls are in place at integration time.
decisions.rationale: Aligning CoCounsel privacy control implementation with HighQ’s FedRAMP certification and integration schedule provides a realistic timeframe and consistent security posture.
decisions.options_considered: Completing CoCounsel work in 2026 versus extending delivery into Q1/Q2 2027.
decisions.dependencies_linked: HighQ FedRAMP certification schedule; CoCounsel HIPAA and privacy control implementation; later updated by decision 0062.

decisions.title: Clarify that TDE/TFE is not a Port Authority contractual requirement for HighQ
decisions.description: Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) and Transparent File Encryption (TFE) are not Port Authority contractual requirements for HighQ. They are being pursued to meet HIPAA expectations and Thomson Reuters’ internal “reasonable and appropriate” risk posture. Port Authority requirements are satisfied as long as encryption is FIPS 140‑2 validated and data at rest and in transit are protected.
decisions.rationale: Separating contractual requirements from internal and HIPAA expectations clarifies priorities and ensures Port Authority obligations are met without mandating TDE/TFE for contract compliance.
decisions.options_considered: Treating TDE/TFE as mandatory for Port Authority contractual compliance versus treating them as internal/HIPAA‑driven enhancements while still meeting Port Authority encryption requirements via FIPS‑validated encryption.
decisions.dependencies_linked: HighQ encryption implementation decisions and HIPAA compliance planning; cryptography dependency 0051.

decisions.title: WL FedRAMP does not require HIPAA compliance at launch
decisions.description: For the WL FedRAMP environment, no PHI will be uploaded by the client; therefore, HIPAA compliance is not required at launch.
decisions.rationale: Since WL FedRAMP will not process PHI at launch, pursuing HIPAA compliance would be unnecessary for the initial release, conserving resources.
decisions.options_considered: Making WL FedRAMP HIPAA compliant for launch versus omitting HIPAA compliance due to absence of PHI uploads.
decisions.dependencies_linked: WL FedRAMP feature set and data ingestion capabilities.

decisions.title: Use Privacy SharePoint as system of record for privacy control documentation
decisions.description: The authoritative copy of privacy control documentation will be stored on the Privacy SharePoint page. While this is the system of record, teams may continue to store architecture documents, ADO artifacts, and other related documentation in their usual internal repositories.
decisions.rationale: Centralizing privacy control documentation in a dedicated SharePoint repository improves governance and traceability while allowing teams to maintain supporting artifacts where they normally work.
decisions.options_considered: Using multiple distributed repositories with no single system of record versus designating the Privacy SharePoint page as the authoritative source for privacy control documentation.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Privacy workstreams across CoCounsel, HighQ, Contract Express, and Outlook Add‑in.

decisions.title: Reuse HighQ hosting model for IAM/CoCounsel in Azure Gov for Outlook Add‑in
decisions.description: For the CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add‑in on HighQ, the group agreed to reuse the HighQ hosting model for IAM/CoCounsel in Azure Gov to maintain consistency, minimize scope changes, and meet project timelines. Improvements may be considered after the Port Authority project.
decisions.rationale: Reusing the existing HighQ hosting model reduces complexity, avoids new architectural risk, and supports meeting aggressive timelines.
decisions.options_considered: Designing a new hosting model for IAM/CoCounsel in Azure Gov versus reusing the established HighQ hosting model.
decisions.dependencies_linked: CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add‑in architecture and HighQ Azure Gov environment.

decisions.title: Leverage existing HighQ standards and controls for IAM/CoCounsel deployment
decisions.description: The group agreed to leverage existing HighQ standards and controls for deployment, logging, and compliance for IAM/CoCounsel in order to align with FedRAMP/HIPAA requirements and reduce additional engineering effort.
decisions.rationale: Using proven HighQ standards reduces engineering workload and ensures consistency with FedRAMP/HIPAA practices already in place.
decisions.options_considered: Creating new deployment and logging standards for IAM/CoCounsel versus reusing HighQ’s existing standards and controls.
decisions.dependencies_linked: CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add‑in deployment pipeline and compliance controls.

decisions.title: Exclude OpenAI/AI components from government Outlook Add‑in architecture
decisions.description: OpenAI/AI components will be excluded from the current CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add‑in architecture for government compliance; only HighQ and IAM microservices will be deployed.
decisions.rationale: Excluding AI components reduces compliance and security complexity and ensures a cleaner FedRAMP/HIPAA boundary for the initial government deployment.
decisions.options_considered: Including OpenAI/AI components in the government Outlook Add‑in architecture versus limiting the deployment to HighQ and IAM microservices.
decisions.dependencies_linked: CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add‑in architecture and FedRAMP/HIPAA scope.

decisions.title: Confirm thomsonreuters.com as the valid domain for public-facing URLs
decisions.description: The group confirmed that thomsonreuters.com will be used as the valid domain for public‑facing URLs, as required for DNSSEC and FedRAMP compliance.
decisions.rationale: Using thomsonreuters.com ensures alignment with DNSSEC and FedRAMP requirements and avoids complications with alternative domains.
decisions.options_considered: Using alternative domains versus standardizing on thomsonreuters.com for public‑facing URLs.
decisions.dependencies_linked: DNS configuration, FedRAMP compliance, and Outlook Add‑in public endpoint design.

decisions.title: Defer some HighQ application-level encryption work to post-June 30 and log risk in Protecht
decisions.description: The tech team proposed a layered encryption solution with proper access controls for HighQ, which the Privacy team accepted as sufficient for now. A formal risk entry will be logged in Protecht after April 7. Additional application-level work to further protect index and temporary files is acknowledged but intentionally deferred until after June 30, 2026, and will be tracked as a separate item.
decisions.rationale: The accepted layered encryption solution meets near‑term needs, allowing the June 30 milestone to be met while deferring more complex application-level work to a later phase.
decisions.options_considered: Implementing full application‑level protections for index and temp files before June 30 versus adopting a layered encryption approach now and deferring additional protections.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Cryptography dependency 0051; HighQ HIPAA and FedRAMP compliance work; Protecht risk tracking.

decisions.title: Do not adopt Plexus for HighQ and related projects at this time
decisions.description: The group decided not to adopt Plexus for HighQ at this time due to its lack of mature Azure cloud offerings and an associated budget ask that HighQ could not commit to. Plexus may be reconsidered in the future, but not while HighQ is simultaneously executing HIPAA/FedRAMP environment work and the DC exit project.
decisions.rationale: Introducing Plexus now would increase complexity and cost during a period when HighQ is already engaged in two major projects, offering insufficient benefit relative to the risk.
decisions.options_considered: Adopting Plexus for relevant security or compliance functions versus continuing with existing tools and approaches.
decisions.dependencies_linked: HighQ HIPAA/FedRAMP environment project and DC exit project timelines.

decisions.title: Set CoCounsel HIPAA and privacy control implementation delivery to Q3 2026
decisions.description: CoCounsel HIPAA remediation and privacy control implementation will be delivered in Q3 2026. This decision was made in a meeting with Paul, Bill, and Maria on April 29 and communicated during the Weekly Sync on April 30.
decisions.rationale: Establishing a Q3 2026 delivery date aligns CoCounsel’s HIPAA and privacy work with overall program planning and revises earlier assumptions that had pushed some work into 2027.
decisions.options_considered: Delivering CoCounsel HIPAA and privacy controls in 2027 versus bringing delivery forward into Q3 2026.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Earlier decisions 0038 and 0039 regarding CoCounsel privacy control deferral; CoCounsel FedRAMP and HighQ FedRAMP integration timelines.

## Executive Summary

**Signature Standalone (209356) – M&A Project Updates: No changes to previous updates**

**A. Scope:** Integrate Development, QA, Staging, Hotfix, and Production environments into the TR Azure Cloud platform.

**B. RAG Status:** GREEN  
Because non-production environments for Signature Standalone have been integrated into TR Azure ahead of the scheduled Q1 2026 deadline.

**C. Metrics:** Azure Non-Production Cloud integration (Dev, QA, Staging and Bugfix) is 50% complete. The team expects to complete integration of the remaining production environment by September 30, 2026.

**D. Key Successes:** In March 2026, the Landing Zone team inflated PTB accounts, enabling successful cloud integration across Dev, QA, and Hotfix environments. All milestones were achieved within the timelines agreed upon with Leadership.

**E. Risks/Dependencies:** None identified at this time.

**F. Next Action Items:** The project team will conduct architecture discussions and seek diagram approval during the ATP leadership call, prior to submitting the PTO request.

## Milestones

-   Complete Dev, QA, and STG environment testing and sign-off in TR Azure by 31 Mar 2026.
    
-   Complete the non-production Disaster Recovery exercise by 15 Jun 2026.
    
-   Begin production environment integration plannings for Signature Standalone in the Thomson Reuters Azure tenant by 15 Jun 2026.
    
-   Complete migration of Signature Standalone production environment and critical production data into the Thomson Reuters Azure tenant by 30 Sep 2026.

risks.description: Unresolved issues in the Snyk scanning process may continue to block or delay security scans for SafeSend One, Signature Standalone (SIGSA), and TTC Standalone codebases. If the scanning problems persist, the project teams may be unable to complete required security checks in time to meet non-production and production cloud integration timelines.
risks.impact_description: If the Snyk scanning issue is not resolved promptly, security scans for three critical projects (SafeSend One, Signature Standalone, and TTC Standalone) may not be completed on time. This would delay sign-offs and cloud integration activities for SIGSA 3x environments, push back the start of production cloud integration planning, and jeopardize the overall delivery timelines for these products.
risks.mitigation: ISRM-Platforms-Security-Dev (Efstathios) and Sachin are working together to resolve the Snyk scanning issue. If the issue is still not resolved into early the following week (after Feb 25), the project team and management will consider approving and proceeding with a manual intervention process to complete the required checks for SIGSA 3x environments cloud integration. This manual process is expected to take 1–2 days and would allow production cloud integration planning to begin on time.
