latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Customer Ticket Journey is delivering a standardized, end-to-end ticket journey by integrating Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Azure DevOps via Boomi so customer issues can be traced across systems with clear ownership, consistent handoffs, and unified reporting. This matters because it reduces escalation friction, improves time-to-resolution and customer communications, and avoids incremental connector/licensing costs by retiring legacy integrations such as Pagero Exalate.

June 30 remains on track for the Pagero MVP, delivering a 1:1 Exalate replacement (Salesforce ↔ ADO) and enabling Exalate renewal cancellation.  Focus has shifted to defining Phase 2/3 future-state capabilities (enhanced Salesforce–ADO/ServiceNow integration, AI-assisted matching and summarization, and UI/mapping enhancements), with timing to be confirmed following sizing by the newly dedicated Salesforce integration team.  Rollout of additional products (IDT, HighQ, GSTOIT) is paused pending the finalized Phase 2/3 plan.

Overall status is GREEN trending Amber, pending leadership-approval on delivery plan for Phase 2 and Phase 3. Pagero is still on track for 30 Jun 2026.

## Milestones

-   Achieve Pagero Salesforce–ADO agent-ready MVP go-live by 30 Jun 2026.
    
-   Complete HighQ and Indirect Tax Salesforce–ADO agent go-lives by 11 Jul 2026.
    
-   Deliver the initial Salesforce → ServiceNow integration to the target environment by 24 Aug 2026.
    
-   Complete GSTOIT Salesforce–ADO agent go-live by 19 Oct 2026.
    
-   Conclude the Customer Ticket Journey program and transition to steady-state operations by 31 Dec 2026.

risks.title: GSTOIT production cutover colliding with GST tax peak season
risks.description: Business stakeholders highlighted that GSTOIT has a tax peak season beginning around August 15 and intensifying into early September, during which support volumes and ADO ticket creation are very high. If the GST/GSTOIT integration is deployed to production close to or during this window, agents may have to learn and adopt new flows while handling peak volumes, increasing operational risk.
risks.impact_description: If the GSTOIT integration goes live near the Aug 15–mid-September tax peak, support agents will have to adapt to new Salesforce–ADO flows while handling very high ticket volumes. This could lead to confusion, slower handling times, mis‑escalations, and reduced willingness to use the new integration. Customer experience and SLA performance during peak could degrade, and the team might choose to delay or roll back the integration, wasting preparation effort.
risks.mitigation: Plan GST/GSTOIT integration so that the technical build and testing can complete ahead of tax peak, but schedule production cutover either well before Aug 15 or after the peak window. Use the existing Power Automate–based integration during peak if necessary. As part of the upcoming GSTOIT mapping session with ADO and GST teams, explicitly define a production blackout window around Aug 15–mid‑September and incorporate it into the release plan. Per the May 6, 2026 sponsor status report, GSTOIT agent go‑live is now explicitly targeted for October 19 to ensure no disruption to Fall Peak Tax Season, aligning production cutover after the peak window.
risks.source_file_name: Weekly Sponsor Touch Base - Customer Ticket Journey.docx

risks.title: Incomplete validation of Area Path routing in non‑production ADO environments
risks.description: ADO does not support full Dev/QA/Prod parity for Area Paths, and the team decided not to duplicate full production Area Path trees into non‑prod. Only a small set of sample Area Paths will be created in the TR Sandbox project for Boomi routing tests, leaving many production combinations untested.
risks.impact_description: If Area Path routing behaves differently in production than in the limited Sandbox tests, some Salesforce cases may be routed to incorrect ADO teams or Area Paths after go‑live. This could cause mis‑assignments, slower triage, and uneven workload distribution, affecting the quality and timeliness of defect handling in the MVP.
risks.mitigation: Create a small, representative set of sample Area Paths in the TR Sandbox project and use them to validate Boomi routing logic. Accept reduced fidelity testing as a calculated risk for the MVP and plan to update production mappings carefully to minimize discrepancies.
risks.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

risks.title: Service principal (SPN) strategy across environments may increase cost or operational overhead
risks.description: There was uncertainty about how many ADO service principals Boomi should use for non‑prod and prod. Using too many SPNs can increase connector costs and operational complexity; using too few may complicate security and access management.
risks.impact_description: If the SPN strategy is not optimized, the team may incur unnecessary connector licensing costs or create operational overhead managing multiple service accounts, potentially straining budgets and administration for the MVP.
risks.mitigation: Confirm a strategy that uses two service principals—one for non‑prod/TR Sandbox and one for production—to balance cost and operational complexity while maintaining appropriate separation.
risks.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

risks.title: Fallback Area Path behavior defaulting to root when mapping fails
risks.description: If Area Path mapping fails during ADO work item creation, work items will land in the root Area Path. The team has not yet formally confirmed that this fallback behavior is acceptable for MVP operations.
risks.impact_description: If Area Path mapping failures send work items to the root Area Path without clear ownership, items may be misrouted or overlooked. This would impair triage, delay issue resolution, and undermine reporting accuracy for the MVP.
risks.mitigation: Confirm acceptance (or rejection) of the default‑to‑root fallback behavior for MVP operations. If not acceptable, adjust routing or introduce monitoring and reassignment processes for root Area Path items.
risks.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

risks.title: Increased scope for GST (GSTOIT and GST must be delivered together)
risks.description: The GST scope must include both GST and GSTOIT together, and the business has confirmed they both need to go together. GST development work is in a different ADO org (tr tax project = TaxTrade).
risks.impact_description: If the combined GST and GSTOIT scope is not properly planned and integrated across the separate ADO org, it may increase complexity and effort for the GST portion of the MVP. This could cause delays or force scope adjustments for GST in the Q2 delivery window.
risks.mitigation: Meet with GST teams to walk through the current setup, document the proposal for integration, and validate expectations with stakeholders. Use that walkthrough to refine the integration approach for the TaxTrade ADO project.
risks.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

risks.title: ServiceNow access and field definition gap
risks.description: Baseline mapping for ServiceNow cannot be completed because the standardized ServiceNow fields and access for analysis are not yet available.
risks.impact_description: If ServiceNow field definitions and access are not provided, the team cannot complete Salesforce‑to‑ServiceNow mappings. This will delay ServiceNow integration work planned for later phases and could postpone post‑MVP expansion of the customer ticket journey to include service management workflows.
risks.mitigation: Provide Mike Polk with a list of standardized ServiceNow fields and ensure access via the ServiceNow delivery team. Leverage existing ServiceNow request RITM0097299 to cover the work and support baseline mapping.
risks.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

risks.title: Potential gap in ticket synchronization capabilities between Salesforce, ServiceNow, and ADO
risks.description: Exalate subscription may expire prior to the go-live of the replacement solution (including the Boomi integration layer), resulting in a potential gap in ticket synchronization capabilities between Salesforce, ServiceNow, and ADO
risks.impact_description: This could lead to disruption in end-to-end ticket traceability, delays in issue handling, and increased manual effort for teams, impacting overall workflow efficiency and alignment to the Customer Ticket Journey objectives.
risks.mitigation: Confirm alignment between the Exalate subscription end date and the Boomi integration go-live timeline, and initiate an extension or interim coverage if a gap is identified. In parallel, establish and communicate a fallback process and execute a defined cutover plan to ensure uninterrupted ticket synchronization.

risks.title: ServiceNow readiness for Q3 may lag behind Salesforce–ADO MVP
risks.description: The June 30 MVP focuses on Salesforce–ADO integration, but overall program health depends on ServiceNow readiness for a later phase (targeted around Q3). ServiceNow field definitions, design, and implementation are still pending.
risks.impact_description: If ServiceNow is not ready in Q3, the program will continue to lack full coverage of the customer ticket journey across Service Management workflows. This delays benefits such as unified incident handling and full end‑to‑end traceability and may require additional planning cycles and stakeholder re‑engagement.
risks.mitigation: Plan and track ServiceNow readiness as a follow‑on phase after the Salesforce–ADO MVP. Continue work on ServiceNow field definitions, access, and integration design so that Q3 delivery can proceed without reintroducing earlier blockers.
risks.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

risks.title: Scope creep from over‑synchronization
risks.description: There is a risk that teams will attempt to synchronize too much data between Salesforce, ServiceNow, and ADO rather than focusing on controlled, intentional integrations.
risks.impact_description: If over‑synchronization occurs, integration complexity and operational load will increase, jeopardizing the Q2 MVP timeline. It may also create unnecessary data replication, increase security and compliance exposure, and make support of the integration more difficult.
risks.mitigation: Do not push every update across systems. Agree on controlled, intentional data exchanges and use external links to source systems for detailed record views instead of full data synchronization.
risks.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

risks.title: No agreed High‑Level Design (HLD) and phase‑1 scope
risks.description: A formal High‑Level Design and clearly defined phase‑1 (Q2 MVP) scope are not yet fully agreed across Salesforce, Boomi, ADO, and ServiceNow architects.
risks.impact_description: Without an agreed HLD and phase‑1 scope, teams may implement inconsistent integration patterns, over‑synchronize data, or work to different assumptions about systems, instances, and use cases. This threatens the ability to deliver a coherent, supportable Q2 MVP and may cause rework, scope creep, or missed June 30 timelines.
risks.mitigation: Develop a High‑Level Design that shows Boomi orchestration, defines phased delivery with clear phase‑1 scope, aligns Salesforce, Boomi, ADO, and ServiceNow architects, and provides explicit guidance to limit data exchanges to agreed key events while using links instead of full synchronization for detailed records.
risks.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

risks.title: Customer Support developer resource capacity
risks.description: Concerns were raised that Customer Support developer capacity might be insufficient to drive key Salesforce integration priorities in parallel for the Q2 MVP.
risks.impact_description: If Customer Support developers are not available, Salesforce changes needed for intake fields, case linking, and integration triggers could be delayed, putting the Q2 MVP schedule at risk.
risks.mitigation: Validate developer resource capacity and secure commitment to support the Salesforce integration work for the Q2 MVP.
risks.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

risks.title: Initial misunderstanding of total integration count
risks.description: Early in planning, the team believed there were approximately 11+ integrations required, which overestimated effort and created timeline concerns.
risks.impact_description: If the integration count remained overestimated, it would have led to unrealistic expectations, inflated scope, and perceived infeasibility of delivering a Q2 MVP.
risks.mitigation: Clarify MVP scope to focus on Salesforce ↔ ADO bidirectional integration only and reduce the perceived number of integrations. Align on ~3 core interfaces for the MVP.
risks.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

risks.title: Dependency on availability of ADO architects and business analysts
risks.description: Requirements finalization and mapping reviews depend on the timely participation of ADO architects and BAs, whose availability is uncertain.
risks.impact_description: If ADO architects and BAs are not available for mapping review sessions, ADO constraints and work item requirements may not be fully understood, causing design gaps, integration rework, and potential delays to Sprint 9/10 and the Q2 MVP.
risks.mitigation: Identify named ADO architects and BAs and ensure their attendance at mapping review sessions to finalize requirements and constraints.
risks.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

risks.title: Business process readiness and handoffs not defined alongside technical MVP
risks.description: Successful June 30 MVP delivery depends not only on technical Salesforce–ADO integration but also on clear end‑to‑end business processes, including handoffs, SLAs, ownership, and customer communication across Support and Engineering. These processes are not yet fully defined and owned.
risks.impact_description: If business processes, roles, and SLAs are not defined and operationalized by the time the technical MVP goes live, teams may struggle with ownership, escalation paths, and customer communication, resulting in inconsistent execution, degraded customer experience, and limited realized value from the integration.
risks.mitigation: Align MVP definition to include process outcomes, not just integration. Use Action A28 to ensure end‑to‑end business processes, handoffs, SLAs, and ownership are clearly defined, aligned, and approved to operate alongside the June 30 technical MVP.
risks.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

risks.title: Boomi capacity constraints for Q2 MVP
risks.description: Boomi integration teams are fully committed to the Pagero integration for Sprints 9–10 and have limited capacity to take on additional scope for other products during the same period.
risks.impact_description: If Boomi capacity is exceeded or additional scope is added, the team may not complete the Salesforce–ADO integrations for Pagero, HighQ, Indirect Tax, and GST by June 30. This would delay the MVP, potentially incur licensing extension costs (e.g., Pagero Exalate renewal), and reduce leadership confidence in delivery.
risks.mitigation: Maintain a tightly controlled MVP scope limited to Salesforce ↔ ADO via Boomi. Secure leadership support to enforce scope discipline and acknowledge Boomi capacity limits. Reallocate resources and improve productivity within the Boomi team to cover all four MVP products without adding scope.
risks.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

risks.title: Cardinality complexity for one‑to‑many and many‑to‑many relationships
risks.description: The integrations must support real‑world one‑to‑many and many‑to‑many relationships between Salesforce cases, ServiceNow incidents/problems, and Azure DevOps work items. Incorrect handling of cardinality would break traceability and reporting for the unified customer ticket journey.
risks.impact_description: If cardinality is not handled correctly, multiple Salesforce cases may not be properly linked to shared ServiceNow incidents or ADO work items. This would lead to broken traceability, inaccurate impact roll‑ups, inconsistent reporting, and confusion over ownership during escalations, undermining the Q2 MVP value.
risks.mitigation: Explicitly account for cardinality rules in the BRD requirements, backlog items, and integration design. Use the BRD as the baseline artifact to ensure all implementation work considers one‑to‑many and many‑to‑many scenarios and avoid assuming one‑to‑one relationships during integration design.
risks.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

risks.title: Failure to complete Salesforce–ADO mapping reviews and MVP validation by April 17
risks.description: The Q2 MVP depends on completing all Salesforce–ADO mapping reviews and final MVP validation by April 17 to enable Boomi intake for Sprint 9. Any delay in this validation threatens the June go‑live.
risks.impact_description: If mapping reviews and MVP validation slip past April 17, Boomi cannot start Sprint 9 on time, compressing schedules and increasing the likelihood that the June 30 MVP cannot be met. This could affect delivery for Pagero, HighQ, IDT, and GST and may lead to contract extension costs.
risks.mitigation: Treat April 17 as a hard deadline, schedule and complete mapping review sessions, and obtain explicit MVP validation. Use the Unified CX tracker to ensure all MVP requirements and mappings are captured and assigned owners.
risks.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

risks.title: Unclear ADO dev/test environment strategy may block Boomi development
risks.description: The Boomi team requires a clear, unblockable ADO environment strategy (e.g., using a TR Sandbox org vs. a single dev project). Lack of clarity on dev/test environment usage could impede integration development and testing.
risks.impact_description: If the ADO dev/test environment strategy remains unclear, Boomi development and testing may be delayed or blocked, slowing progress toward the June 30 MVP and risking defects slipping into production due to inadequate testing.
risks.mitigation: Define and confirm the dev/test environment strategy, including creation of a new ADO project in the TR Sandbox org, configuration of required work item types, and assignment of service principals. Communicate this plan to the Boomi team so they can proceed with development and testing.
risks.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

risks.title: Mappings not reviewed and validated by April 17
risks.description: Salesforce–ADO mappings for Pagero, HighQ, Indirect Tax, and GST must be reviewed and validated by mid‑April to enable Boomi Sprint 9 intake and Q2 MVP delivery, but this review may not be completed on time.
risks.impact_description: If mappings are not reviewed and validated by April 17, Boomi will be unable to start Sprint 9 work as planned. This would threaten the June 30 Q2 MVP delivery for the four in‑scope products and could push integration completion into later sprints.
risks.mitigation: Schedule and execute dedicated working sessions with Salesforce, Boomi, and ADO teams to review mappings. Use existing Pagero mappings as a baseline and confirm readiness for Sprint 9 start.
risks.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

risks.title: Change‑management‑driven validation and business go‑live may significantly lag technical MVP
risks.description: Technical MVP for Salesforce–ADO (and later ServiceNow) is on track, but validation testing and business go‑live are being planned as part of a separate CSS change‑management process led by Darren Thurin’s team. Current indications are that this process could add roughly two months between technical readiness and agent rollout, with unclear ownership of validation and limited early exposure of flows to stakeholders.
risks.impact_description: If validation and business go‑live remain owned exclusively by the CSS change‑management team with a long lead time, the tool may be technically ready by June 30 but not in use by agents until much later. This would delay realization of MVP value, compress the window before critical business periods (e.g., tax peak season for GSTOIT), and increase the chance of late discovery of usability or process issues because sponsors and agents would see end‑to‑end flows only at the end of the change‑management cycle.
risks.mitigation: Work with CSS change‑management (Darren Thurin) and Salesforce leadership (including Mike Polk) to clarify ownership of validation testing and right‑size the change‑management approach. Introduce early demo days and simple end‑to‑end flows (e.g., a basic Salesforce‑to‑engineering escalation) so sponsors and agent representatives can review UX and process well before formal go‑live. Align on a concrete business go‑live date per product that keeps rollout comfortably ahead of critical periods such as GSTOIT tax peak season, and adjust the plan if the change‑management duration cannot be shortened.
risks.source_file_name: Weekly Sponsor Touch Base - Customer Ticket Journey.docx

risks.title: Data quality gaps in manual cross‑referencing
risks.description: Current manual cross‑referencing between Salesforce, ServiceNow, Azure DevOps and other systems lacks reliable identifiers and source data (such as source system IDs and URLs). Without a consistent common data model and clean cross‑reference data, tickets cannot be reliably linked across systems for the Q2 MVP integrations.
risks.impact_description: If data quality gaps persist, Boomi integrations will not be able to reliably connect Salesforce cases with downstream ServiceNow and ADO tickets, breaking the unified ticket journey. This would compromise traceability, reporting accuracy, and customer communications for the Q2 MVP and could require rework of integration logic after go‑live.
risks.mitigation: Establish a common data model and consistent payload definition so tickets can be reliably connected across systems. Capture both ticket identifiers and source/origin information (system plus URL) going forward. Use the Power BI dashboard to expose current data quality gaps and inform design decisions.
risks.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

risks.mitigation: Work with CSS change‑management (Darren Thurin) and Salesforce leadership (including Mike Polk) to clarify ownership of validation testing and right‑size the change‑management approach. Introduce early demo days and simple end‑to‑end flows (e.g., a basic Salesforce‑to‑engineering escalation) so sponsors and agent representatives can review UX and process well before formal go‑live. assumptions.title: June 30 SalesforceADO MVP delivery is achievable if scope and timelines remain fixed
assumptions.description: The program plans to deliver a June 30 MVP of the Boomibased SalesforceADO integration for Pagero, with HighQ and Indirect Tax (IDT) targeted for agent golive on July 11 and GSTOIT targeted for October 19, on the assumption that scope discipline is maintained and no additional interfaces are added beyond the revised, leadershipapproved MVP baseline.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The integration team confirmed the feasibility of delivering the revised MVP planPagero agent golive by June 30, HighQ and IDT by July 11, and GSTOIT by October 19within existing capacity, provided that MVP scope remains limited to Salesforce  ADO integrations and ServiceNow is deferred to later sprints. This reset MVP definition and timeline were formally approved by leadership (LT) in early May.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The April 21 WSR had already indicated reaffirmed confidence in a June 30 MVP, and the May 6, 2026 sponsor status report documented the leadershipapproved reset MVP scope. The May 20, 2026 WSR further states that the June 30 MVP remains on track for Salesforce  ADO integration for Pagero, with no new delivery risks identified and change/operational readiness advancing, which reinforces the validity of this assumption provided scope remains controlled.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If progress tracking shows that any of the planned dates (June 30, July 11, October 19) are at risk, reprioritize scope by product (e.g., preserving Pagero timelines even if other products slip), adjust golive sequencing, or formally rebaseline dates with leadership approval while clearly communicating any impact on contract, licensing, or peakseason constraints.
assumptions.validation_method: Ongoing sprint tracking, RAID monitoring, and formal readiness reviews aligned to the specific golive dates: late June for Pagero, early July for HighQ/IDT, and October for GSTOIT. Status will be reviewed in weekly WSRs and biweekly demo sessions.

assumptions.title: Each system remains the system of record for its domain
assumptions.description: Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Azure DevOps will each remain the authoritative system of record for their respective domains: Salesforce for customer support case ownership and communication, ServiceNow for internal service operations and change/incident/problem processes, and Azure DevOps for engineering work execution and code linkage.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The existing tools and operational processes are already organized around Salesforce for support, ServiceNow for service management, and ADO for engineering. Replacing or re‑platforming these systems is out of scope for the current initiative, so the project assumes they remain domain systems of record.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The BRD explicitly states that purpose‑built systems remain in place and that full replacement of any system is out of scope. Existing enterprise practices already treat Salesforce, ServiceNow, and ADO as systems of record for their domains, and no conflicting initiatives have been documented in the project materials.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If a system of record is changed or replaced, initiate a dedicated re‑architecture effort to adjust integration patterns, update mappings, and revise the BRD before proceeding with further rollout.
assumptions.validation_method: Architecture and governance reviews confirming no planned replacement of Salesforce, ServiceNow, or ADO within the project timeframe.

validation_owner.name: Architecture working group (Salesforce, ServiceNow, ADO, Boomi architects)

assumptions.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

assumptions.title: Integration supports regulated environments with least privilege and auditability
assumptions.description: The integration will be designed to support regulated environments, including appropriate PII handling, audit logs, and least‑privilege access for all integration components.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Customer support data includes PII and may be subject to regulatory and compliance requirements. The project must operate within existing security and compliance frameworks.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The BRD includes detailed security and privacy NFRs (NFR‑001 to NFR‑005) that are standard practice in the organization. Security teams are recognized stakeholders, making it reasonable to assume the integration can be designed to comply with existing regulatory obligations.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If any regulatory or security requirement cannot be met, constrain integration scope (e.g., reduce fields shared, disable attachments) or introduce compensating controls such as additional redaction, logging, or access restrictions before going live.
assumptions.validation_method: Security architecture review, NFR validation, and potentially internal compliance or audit sign‑off prior to production go‑live.
assumptions.source_file_name: Business Requirements Document (BRD) - Unified Customer Experience - Case Management Integration.docx

assumptions.title: Near‑real‑time updates for key state changes with eventual consistency for non‑critical fields
assumptions.description: The integration will deliver near‑real‑time synchronization for critical state changes (e.g., status updates, severity changes) while allowing eventual consistency for non‑critical fields.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The project aims to improve visibility and responsiveness for customers and internal teams without over‑engineering the integration or overloading systems with frequent updates.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The NFRs specify near‑real‑time sync for critical state changes and require guaranteed delivery and monitoring. Boomi has already established basic connectivity and service frameworks, and event‑driven patterns are standard for such integrations, making this assumption reasonable though still to be validated under load.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If near‑real‑time performance cannot be consistently achieved, adjust SLAs and customer messaging to reflect realistic update intervals, prioritize the most critical events for faster processing, or introduce additional infrastructure (e.g., queues, scaling) to improve latency.
assumptions.validation_method: Performance and integration testing in non‑prod environments, measuring end‑to‑end latency for key state changes from Salesforce to ADO (and later ServiceNow) under typical loads.

assumptions.title: Production Area Path routing will behave consistently with tested Sandbox mappings
assumptions.description: For the MVP, only a limited, representative set of Area Paths will be created in the TR Sandbox ADO project to validate Boomi routing logic. The team assumes that once production mappings are updated, routing behavior in production will be consistent with what is observed in Sandbox tests.
assumptions.rationale_basis: ADO environment limitations and the non‑scalable nature of duplicating full Area Path trees into non‑prod make comprehensive end‑to‑end testing infeasible. The team must rely on representative samples.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The April 22 mapping meeting explicitly accepted testing with sample Area Paths and treating incomplete end‑to‑end validation as an acceptable calculated risk for the MVP. This indicates conscious reliance on configuration parity between Sandbox and production.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If discrepancies are discovered post‑go‑live, prioritize correcting Area Path mappings and reassign misrouted work items. Consider adding monitoring to detect items landing in unexpected Area Paths and define a temporary triage process to quickly redirect them.
assumptions.validation_method: Compare and verify production Area Path configurations against the tested Sandbox mappings during deployment; perform targeted smoke tests in production with controlled cases after go‑live.

assumptions.title: Core integration flows will operate synchronously between Salesforce, Boomi, and downstream systems
assumptions.description: The team is assuming that key integration calls between Salesforce, Boomi, and ServiceNow/ADO will operate synchronously (request/response), with immediate confirmations when records are created or updated across systems, rather than relying primarily on asynchronous fire-and-forget patterns.
assumptions.rationale_basis: During the April 30 touch-base, when asked whether the integrations would be synchronous or asynchronous, Neha indicated that she believed the flows "should be synchronous" but needed to confirm. John Evora also reasoned that Boomi contacts ServiceNow and vice versa with immediate confirmations in current patterns.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Boomi and ServiceNow already use synchronous integrations for many use cases, and there was consensus in the meeting that synchronous behaviour is expected for the new flows. However, Neha explicitly noted the need to validate this, so the assumption has not yet been fully confirmed in the detailed design.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If some or all flows must be asynchronous, update the integration design to include robust queuing, retries, and reconciliation jobs, adjust monitoring requirements to track asynchronous processing health, and communicate to business stakeholders any changes in expected response times or user experience.
assumptions.validation_method: Technical design and build reviews by the Boomi team and platform engineers (Salesforce, ServiceNow, ADO) to confirm whether each integration path is synchronous or asynchronous and to document the chosen pattern.
assumptions.source_file_name: Touch Base _ Customer Ticket Journey _ SF_SN_ADO Integration .docx

assumptions.title: Salesforce agents will have sufficient ADO access to manage attachments directly without Boomi
assumptions.description: The team is considering a revised attachment-handling approach where Salesforce agents use the ADO URL stored on the Salesforce case to log into Azure DevOps and upload required attachments directly to the ADO work item. In this model, Boomi would not need to handle attachment links or binaries; instead, ADO users would request attachments via comments, and Salesforce agents would respond by logging into ADO and adding files. This assumes that relevant Salesforce agents (including contractors where applicable) can be granted at least minimal ADO access across in-scope products such as Pagero and Indirect Tax (IDT).
assumptions.rationale_basis: During the May 5 Boomi Delivery Touch Base, Siddella Shashendara proposed avoiding Boomi involvement in attachment handling by letting Salesforce agents log into ADO using the case URL and upload files directly when ADO users request them in comments. This approach would simplify Boomi integration logic and align with existing decisions to avoid binary attachment transfer during the MVP (URL-only handling). It relies on agents having sufficient ADO access to perform this action.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Current security and access practices already allow some Salesforce agents (particularly internal employees) to access ADO for linked work items, and Mike Polk indicated that agents normally have ADO access. However, Daniel Tillmann noted that there is no established pattern today for granting all contractors ADO access, and he needs to coordinate with Loveneet and project admins. This makes the assumption plausible but not yet validated, particularly for contractor-heavy support teams.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If validation shows that not all required agents can be given appropriate ADO access, the project will retain or expand the Boomi-based attachment handling pattern: ADO users will request attachments via comments, and Boomi will post Salesforce-hosted attachment URLs as comments back to ADO, avoiding binary transfer while ensuring attachments are reachable even when agents lack direct ADO access. For products or teams where ADO access cannot be standardized, the integration design will explicitly document that Boomi (rather than agents) is responsible for propagating attachment links.
assumptions.validation_method:
1) ADO platform leads (Loveneet Saini and Daniel Tillmann) will review current and planned ADO permission patterns for Salesforce agents, including contractors, and determine whether a standard minimal-access profile can be offered.
2) Salesforce leadership (Mike Polk and Siddella Shashendara) will confirm which agent populations (employees vs contractors, per brand) require ADO access for attachment handling.
3) Based on these findings, the team will explicitly decide whether to adopt the agent-direct attachment approach or retain Boomi-based URL handling for some or all products.
assumptions.source_file_name: May 5_Twice weekly - Boomi Delivery Touch Base.docx

issues.title: Unplanned change management and validation phase may delay business go-live beyond June 30
issues.description: A recent discovery from discussions with the Salesforce team indicates that validation testing and change management activities were not fully accounted for in the original delivery plan. While the Salesforce–ADO integration is expected to be technically functional by June 30, CSS change management (led by Darren Thurin’s team) anticipates additional validation and rollout steps that could delay actual agent/business go-live by up to two months beyond the MVP date.
issues.impact_assessment: The project’s June 30 MVP has been framed as delivering a functional Salesforce–ADO integration. However, the newly surfaced expectation that CSS change management will run a separate validation and rollout process—potentially taking several weeks—means agents may not actually use the new integration until significantly after June 30. This undermines stakeholder expectations of a Q2 operational MVP, compresses runway before critical business periods (e.g., GSTOIT tax peak around August 15), and may delay value realization and lessons learned needed for the subsequent ServiceNow phase. The lack of clarity on who owns validation testing and why the change management window is so long also creates confusion and misalignment across teams.
issues.dependencies_affecting: CSS change management processes (Darren Thurin’s team); Salesforce development readiness; dependency 'End-to-end business process readiness for June 30 MVP'; tax-peak constraints for GST/GSTOIT operations.
issues.resolution: To be defined. Likely actions include: (1) clarifying validation testing ownership between Salesforce delivery and CSS change management; (2) developing a joint validation plan anchored to existing use cases with shorter, iterative feedback cycles; and (3) aligning on a realistic but time-bounded change management window that supports early agent exposure (e.g., pilot groups) while avoiding peak business periods.
issues.source_file_name: Weekly Sponsor Touch Base - Customer Ticket Journey.docx

issues.title: MVP definition misaligned with business go-live expectations
issues.description: Leadership recently learned that the June 30 MVP definition focuses on having a technically viable Salesforce–ADO integration (tool built and able to pass data) without guaranteeing readiness for business go-live and agent usage by that date. Additional Salesforce testing, validation, and change management work were not fully accounted for in the original MVP definition.
issues.impact_assessment: If the MVP delivers only a technically functional integration by June 30 without completed Salesforce testing, validation, and change management, business stakeholders may consider the MVP a failure, even if the integration is built. This misalignment could erode sponsor confidence, complicate communications to agents and developers, and force unplanned work or schedule changes to achieve a true business go-live. It may also impact dependent products (Pagero, HighQ, Indirect Tax, GSTOIT) that expect integrated operations aligned to specific sprint and release dates.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Dependency: Salesforce development readiness for MVP completion; Assumption: June 30 Salesforce–ADO MVP delivery is achievable if scope and timelines remain fixed.
issues.resolution: Clarify and, if necessary, update the formal MVP definition to distinguish between technical completion and business go-live, and evaluate whether Salesforce development and change management timelines can be pulled in to reduce the gap. Align sponsors (including Pat Meuers and Mike Krause) on realistic go-live timing per product.
issues.source_file_name: Touch Base _ Customer Ticket Journey _ SF_SN_ADO Integration .docx

dependencies.title: GST/GSTOIT integration deployment must avoid August 15 tax peak
dependencies.description: The deployment of the GST/GSTOIT Salesforce–ADO integration must not occur near the August 15 GSTOIT tax peak period. The integration can be built and tested on schedule, but production cutover needs to be planned either sufficiently before peak or held until after it to avoid operational disruption during a period of very high ticket volume.
dependencies.dependent_on: GST/GSTOIT Salesforce–Boomi–ADO integration build and deployment schedule
dependencies.consumer: GST/GSTOIT Customer Support and Engineering operations during tax peak
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If the GST/GSTOIT integration go-live is pushed too close to or into the August 15 tax peak window, support agents and engineering teams will be forced to adopt a new integration flow while handling very high incident volumes. This increases the risk of operational issues, misrouted escalations, and degraded customer experience during a critical period. Conversely, if the go-live is deferred until after peak without clear planning, GST/GSTOIT will continue to rely on the interim Power Automate solution longer than expected.
dependencies.mitigation: Proceed with building and testing the GST/GSTOIT integration according to the existing Boomi and Salesforce timelines, but plan to hold production enablement if the projected cutover would fall near the August 15 peak. Consider re‑sequencing product rollout (e.g., prioritizing GST/GSTOIT ahead of HighQ if feasible) or scheduling the GST/GSTOIT cutover well before August, and maintain the interim Power Automate solution until after peak if needed.

decisions.rationale: GSTOIT experiences a significant tax peak starting around August 15, with high volumes of ADO tickets. latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

**No changes to milestones or features are being reported this week, as reporting follows a biweekly cadence aligned to the ADO sprint schedule.**

 **Overview Summary (06.08)**  
The team reviewed progress across AI Developer Tools cost management, DORA metrics coverage, and key platform integrations. A primary focus was on controlling Light LLM spend, which has increased significantly, with next steps centered on sharing detailed usage data, driving migration to [Cloud.ai](http://Cloud.ai), and improving cost accountability across engineering teams. Leaders also discussed gaps in adoption reporting and dashboard accuracy, with actions underway to correct API/data issues and improve visibility into tool usage and DORA coverage.

The team also covered progress on technical integrations, including secure ADO-to-Port connectivity, ServiceNow and DataDog integration work, and support for GitHub-to-Linear issues impacting the easy team. Overall, the discussion emphasized stronger data accuracy, improved reporting transparency, tighter cost governance, and targeted follow-up actions across teams.

**New Milestones & Process Update Summary (06.08)**  
We are currently refining the milestone plan to align with current delivery plans. This includes breaking the developer flow effort into multiple deliverables and advancing additional workstreams such as integrations and operational readiness to provide clearer visibility into execution priorities and progress. Aligned project leadership on a refined DevOps-IDP milestone governance approach to improve reporting accuracy, accountability, and stakeholder visibility.

DORA Metrics MVP dashboards for the top 12 revenue-generating product lines were delivered on 31 Mar 2026, initially covering approximately 25% of those products in production. IDP adoption has grown from 25 users at the end of Q1 2026 (2.5% of the ~1,000-user target) to 475 users as of 26 May 2026 (47.5% of the target), with Q2 OKR tracking in progress to sustain this trajectory.

Overall status is Green, driven by accelerated IDP adoption relative to the 2026 1,000-seat target while key Q1 and Q2 delivery milestones remain on plan.

## Path to Green

We are mitigating the risk of losing the lead engineer by backfilling the role and executing a structured knowledge-transfer plan by 30 Jun 2026, while tracking Port product dependencies such as scoped RBAC delivery through the risk register.

## Milestones

-   Complete Developer Flow Unblocked Q2 and End-to-End Delivery Visibility Q2 capabilities in the IDP by 30 Jun 2026.
    
-   Complete the Q2 Define and Operationalize OKR Metrics milestone, including NPS and adoption tracking, by 30 Jun 2026.
    
-   Deliver Team-Owned Self-Service Automation and Reliability Visible Before Incidents capabilities by 30 Sep 2026.
    
-   Deliver Security & Governance Without Friction and the Q4 Define and Operationalize OKR Metrics milestone by 31 Dec 2026.
    
-   Complete overall DevOps Automation / IDP program closeout by 31 Dec 2026.

## **Executive Summary**

**Scope:** GST Modernization is migrating tax batch, file system, database, and application services from AMS to AWS/Linux with upgraded Windows Server and CI/CD infrastructure. The initiative targets $40K annual cloud savings through platform modernization while stabilizing critical tax platforms and aligning with TR cloud standards.

**Current Status - AMBER** because Phase 1B batch services delayed 147 days from 30 Jan to 26 Jun 2026 due to SQL contention and GST Batch transfer defects requiring rollback. Phase 2A FSx storage migration runs 32 days late while BRMS/LAFI/Tax Return Live/Validation Services track 31 days ahead, deferring $9K monthly savings realization to late June.

**Key outcomes delivered:**  
• Phase 2B1 UAT completed - Delivered 05 Jun 2026 ahead of schedule; production cutover targeting 12 Jun; BRMS/Lafi/Tax Return Live/Validation Services migration ready.  
• Phase 1B Batch Services (GST Batch, ELF Batch, FS Batch) have been re-baselined - Regression/scale testing scheduled week of 08 Jun; GST/ELF/FSC Batch services prepared; 26 Jun 2026 completion targeted.  
• FSx modernization advancing - Lower-environment migrations underway; TechOps capacity prioritization remains a risk; maintaining 30 Jun 2026 production cutover target.  
• Windows-to-Linux roadmap developing with Tax Return Live API and RS Browser API Core underway - OTW application services architecture defined; resource planning underway; 30 Oct 2026 completion target maintained.

**Active RAID items:**  
• I1 — Issue: Phase 1B Batch Services delayed to 26 Jun 2026 deferring $9K monthly savings. Mitigation: Complete regression/scale testing; re-baseline SAT/UAT dates.

## Executive Summary

Project Aether is delivering AI agents across core infrastructure services so Platform Engineering can offer AI-powered orchestration, landing zone, database patching, network DNS, and security architecture review capabilities. This matters because it reduces manual effort, improves service speed and reliability, and enables clear measurement of usage, cost savings, and hours saved for internal stakeholders.

Four milestones are in progress and three are planned, with current work focused on maturing the DB Patching Agent, expanding Landing Zone capabilities, and preparing Investigator and FedRAMP-supporting agents.

Overall status is Green, driven by successful delivery of the foundational agents while the main remaining risk is subscription uptake for the DB Patching Agent.

To keep the project Green, we are engaging product teams to clarify and schedule the additional DB Patching Agent features needed to support their subscription decisions, targeting alignment with the 30 Sep 2026 enhancement milestones.

## Executive Summary

Enterprise Strategy for Cloud Containerization is defining and implementing an enterprise-wide containerization strategy, including GCP migration, to enable governed and scalable container adoption through strategy-as-code, portfolio-driven prioritization, and self-service enablement. This will standardize how applications move to containers, improve platform reliability, and accelerate modernization across the portfolio.

Two of two significant GCP platform risks have been resolved by their 31 May 2026 target closure date, keeping the platform path clear for upcoming pilot application onboarding. Current delivery work is focused on progressing the container strategy documentation toward stakeholder sign-off while preparing for the first GCP pilot and subsequent self-service and roadmap activities.

Overall status is Green, driven by the resolution of GCP Landing Zone and CICD readiness risks ahead of pilot onboarding activities.

## Path to Green

The primary focus is on LZ readiness and completion of the Plexus cluster build to support onboarding of the Constellation application. Work is in progress to resolve the open issue regarding ownership of application onboarding templates and to agree on a formal RACI. 

## Milestones

-   Complete container strategy documentation review and have the final version ready by 31 Aug 2026.
    
-   Onboard the first pilot GCP application to the established strategy and container platform by 31 Jul 2026.
    
-   Enable and validate the self-service model for container usage through pilots with a continuous feedback loop by 31 Dec 2026.
    
-   Create the application roadmap aligned with GCP Project Ferrari (GTM) roadmaps by 2027-03-31.
    
-   Complete the Enterprise Strategy for Cloud Containerization program and transition to steady-state by 31 Dec 2026.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

TMS Re-Platform is delivering a unified, modern territory and quota management solution by replacing the legacy TMS with Varicent Sales Planning and Salesforce Enterprise Territory Management, creating a single system of record for territories, quotas, and account assignments. This matters because it reduces manual effort, improves data integrity across Sales, Finance, Commercial Operations, and commissions, and enables more agile planning cycles.

Key financial and contracting milestones are complete, with overall program funding approved on 25 Mar 2026 and both the Varicent license and the ~$800k fixed-price implementation SOW executed by 10 Apr 2026 against a $4.1M three-year budget. Launch 0 for U.S. Corporates remains within its planned 01 Mar 2026 to 31 Dec 2026 execution window with no recorded schedule variance, and Launch 0/1 are funded while three later launches remain planned but unfunded.

Overall status is Green, driven by completion of the core funding and contractual decisions that secure Varicent licensing and implementation capacity for Launch 0 and Launch 1.

## Path to Green

With overall status Green, the focus is on mitigating the highest-impact RAID item by completing ECM and Data & Analytics readiness assessments early, so that a single, high-quality customer and prospect data source is in place before the U.S. Corporates parallel run.

## Milestones

- Execute the overall TMS Re-Platform program within the planned window from 2026-01-01 to 2027-08-31.  
- Complete Launch 0 internal parallel run capability for U.S. Corporates, including a 1–3 month full parallel run with acceptable alignment between legacy TMS and new platform outputs, by 31 Dec 2026.  
- Finalize the Discovery-phase and Design-exit funding model, including refined assumptions and any EPC 2027 acceleration asks, by 15 Jun 2026.  
- Establish the funding path for Sales Operations contractor backfill and secure incremental funding approvals for Launch 2, Launch 3, and subsequent segment/geography launches by 30 Jun 2026.  
- Deliver full production rollout for Big 3 U.S. & Canada (Launch 1) and subsequent funded phases and transition to steady-state operations by 31 Aug 2027.

risks.title: Unfunded future phases (Launch 2, Launch 3, subsequent launches) may not proceed as planned
risks.description: Launch 2 (AEM segment), Launch 3 (Latam), and subsequent segment/geography launches are explicitly noted as 'not currently funded'. The roadmap assumes additional funding will be secured later. If additional funding is not approved, later phases of the TMS Replatform may be delayed, descoped, or cancelled.
risks.impact_description: If funding for Launch 2, Launch 3, and subsequent phases is not approved, the organization may be left with a partially replatformed landscape where only Big 3 / Corporates segments are on Varicent and Salesforce ETM while other segments remain on legacy TMS or disparate solutions. This fragmentation would limit global standardization, reduce the expected enterprise benefits (data governance, analytics maturity, and process standardization), require maintaining multiple systems and processes, and increase operational complexity and cost. It may also undermine long‑term Commercial Systems and GTM transformation objectives.

raised_by.name: Project charter authors (Finance and Commercial Engineering)

mitigation_plan_owner.name: Finance lead (Alice Bryan) and Commercial Engineering program leadership

risks.mitigation: Develop detailed phase‑specific business cases and benefit profiles for Launch 2, Launch 3, and subsequent launches, using results from Launch 0/1 parallel runs and value realization. Incorporate these into EPC 2027 and subsequent funding cycles early to avoid gaps. Define a clear minimum viable roadmap and prioritization so that, if partial funding is approved, the highest value segments are addressed first. Maintain transparent communication with SteerCo on funding dependencies and timing.
risks.source_file_name: Varicent Territory & Quota Planning thru SF-ETM - Project Charter_V1.0.docx

risks.title: ECM and Data & Analytics readiness as single customer and prospect source of truth
risks.description: The target architecture assumes that ECM (Enterprise Customer Master) functions as the single system of record for customer and prospect accounts, with Enterprise Data & Analytics providing normalized and governed data to Varicent and Salesforce ETM. There is a risk that ECM and related data platforms may not be fully ready, aligned, or integrated in time to support initial launches.
risks.impact_description: If ECM and D&A platforms cannot reliably provide a single, clean, and timely source of customer and prospect account data, Varicent and Salesforce ETM will receive inconsistent or incomplete account identifiers, hierarchies, and attributes. This will lead to data misalignment across Varicent, Salesforce, commissions, and reporting systems, causing territory assignment errors, compensation discrepancies, poor seller experience, and increased manual reconciliation effort. It could undermine the core success criteria of establishing a single system of record and trusted downstream consumption.

raised_by.name: Business Architecture and Commercial Engineering (as described in the charter)

mitigation_plan_owner.name: ECM product owner and TMS Replatform data architect

risks.mitigation: Conduct an ECM and D&A readiness assessment early in the Discovery phase, identify gaps in account coverage, data quality, and integration latency, and prioritize remediation activities. Define clear data contracts and SLAs between ECM/D&A and Varicent/Salesforce ETM. Use the Corporates parallel run to validate ECM‑sourced data quality and alignment, and implement corrective data governance actions before broader rollout. Escalate any material data quality or coverage gaps to SteerCo for prioritization.
risks.source_file_name: Varicent Territory & Quota Planning thru SF-ETM - Project Charter_V1.0.docx

risks.title: Salesforce ETM integration partner not yet contracted or funded
risks.description: The project plans to use a systems integration partner (TCS or Deloitte) to implement Salesforce Enterprise Territory Management (ETM) and integrate it with Varicent, but no statement of work has been executed and the estimated $225K cost is not yet approved. If contracting and funding are delayed or not approved, Salesforce ETM capabilities may not be available in time for Launch 0/1, impacting the target architecture and seller experience.
risks.impact_description: If an ETM integration partner is not engaged and funded in time, ETM configuration and integration with Varicent could slip beyond the planned launches. This would delay rules-based territory assignment in Salesforce, degrade seller experience, force continued manual or legacy approaches to account‑territory assignment, and potentially require rework of downstream reporting and forecasting plans. Launch 0 and Launch 1 may have to proceed without intended ETM capabilities, reducing the business value of the replatform and creating additional operational risk and manual workarounds.

raised_by.name: Commercial Engineering (as documented in the project charter)

mitigation_plan_owner.name: Commercial Engineering program manager for TMS Replatform

risks.mitigation: Finalize scope for Salesforce ETM implementation, confirm preferred SI partner (TCS or Deloitte), and progress SOW development through IT Sourcing and Finance approval. Secure budget approval for the estimated $225K as part of EPC or other funding processes. Sequence ETM work to align with Varicent implementation milestones so that core ETM capability is available for Launch 0/1. If funding is delayed, prepare a contingency plan using minimal internal configuration and limited ETM scope to support the first launches.
risks.source_file_name: Varicent Territory & Quota Planning thru SF-ETM - Project Charter_V1.0.docx

risks.title: Unresolved data migration approach from legacy TMS to Varicent
risks.description: The scope notes that design and execution of data migration from legacy TMS into Varicent is still 'decision pending' and depends on Varicent Discovery findings. There is a risk that data migration decisions may be delayed, complex, or more resource‑intensive than expected, impacting the timeline and quality of the parallel run and cutover.
risks.impact_description: If data migration strategy, scope, and tooling are not defined and executed in time, there may be insufficient historical territory and quota data available in Varicent for parallel run comparisons. This would limit the ability to validate outputs against legacy TMS, delay cutover decisions, and potentially force a more conservative rollout. Poorly planned migration could also introduce data quality issues that propagate into Salesforce and commissions systems, increasing operational risk and manual correction effort.

raised_by.name: Commercial Engineering and Varicent implementation team

mitigation_plan_owner.name: Data migration lead within Commercial Engineering / Varicent SI

risks.mitigation: Complete Varicent Discovery with a specific focus on data migration scenarios (scope of history, transformation rules, and tooling). Define a migration strategy and detailed plan early in Design, including mapping from legacy TMS data structures to Varicent, and conduct pilot migrations for U.S. Corporates. Build automated validation scripts to compare legacy and new outputs during parallel runs. Secure appropriate resources (data engineers and business SMEs) to support migration and validation.
risks.source_file_name: Varicent Territory & Quota Planning thru SF-ETM - Project Charter_V1.0.docx

risks.title: Parallel run discrepancies between legacy TMS and Varicent + Salesforce ETM outputs
risks.description: The proposed architecture requires a full 1–3 month parallel run to achieve 100% confidence in the new solution, including capturing a full historical repository of rep‑territory‑account alignment. There is a risk that significant discrepancies will be found between legacy TMS outputs and the new platform during the parallel run.
risks.impact_description: If substantial or unexplained differences between legacy TMS and Varicent + Salesforce ETM outputs are discovered during the parallel run, cutover decisions for U.S. Corporates (Launch 0/1) may be delayed. This could push planned go‑live dates beyond territory and quota planning cycles, reduce stakeholder confidence in the new system, and require additional analysis, configuration changes, and re‑testing. Extended dual‑run periods would also increase operational overhead and may complicate compensation processing and reporting.

raised_by.name: Commercial Engineering / Business Architecture (as stated in the proposed architecture)

mitigation_plan_owner.name: Testing and validation lead for TMS Replatform

risks.mitigation: Define detailed parallel run test plans, including specific metrics and tolerances for acceptable variance between legacy and new outputs. Engage business SMEs from Sales, Finance, and Commercial Excellence to interpret differences and agree on expected vs. unexpected variances. Implement iterative defect triage and remediation cycles during the parallel run, and ensure sufficient time is built into the plan for configuration adjustments before formal cutover. Communicate clear entry and exit criteria for parallel run success to SteerCo.

assumptions.title: ECM will serve as the single system of record for customer and prospect accounts
assumptions.description: The architecture assumes that ECM (Enterprise Customer Master) is the authoritative source for customer and prospect accounts used in territory planning, providing the identifiers, hierarchies, segmentation, and attributes consumed by Varicent and Salesforce.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The charter explicitly states that ECM is required to function as the single system of record for customer and prospect accounts used in territory planning, aligning with the broader CPSP Enterprise Design.
assumptions.validity_explanation: ECM is an existing enterprise platform with defined ownership and governance, and is already integrated with multiple systems. However, its ability to handle all required prospect and customer scenarios for territory planning must be confirmed, especially for segments and regions beyond the current footprint.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If ECM cannot fully support all needed scenarios initially, introduce interim data enrichment or bridging solutions (e.g., supplemental data feeds, temporary reference tables) and limit early rollout scope to segments where ECM coverage is adequate, while prioritizing ECM enhancements for subsequent phases.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm ECM coverage, data quality, and integration readiness through Discovery and integration design; run data validation during the Corporates parallel run to ensure ECM‑sourced data supports required use cases.
assumptions.source_file_name: Varicent Territory & Quota Planning thru SF-ETM - Project Charter_V1.0.docx

assumptions.title: ECM will manage prospect accounts for territory assignment
assumptions.description: The proposed architecture assumes that prospect accounts will be managed within ECM, enabling consistent prospect coverage and territory assignment rules within Varicent and Salesforce ETM.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The architecture section states that 'ECM will manage Prospect Accounts to support Territory assignment', indicating a design decision that prospect data will be centralized rather than maintained in separate systems.
assumptions.validity_explanation: There is alignment in design artifacts that ECM will handle prospects, and ECM already manages customer hierarchies. However, prospect handling may require new processes, data feeds, and governance, which have not yet been fully implemented.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If ECM prospect management is delayed, limit initial rollout to customer accounts only and use temporary prospect lists managed in Salesforce or Varicent with clear governance; schedule ECM enhancements as part of later phases before expanding to additional segments.
assumptions.validation_method: Assess ECM’s current and planned capabilities for prospect management during Discovery, including data model, ingestion processes, and integration with Salesforce; validate through test data and pilot segments during parallel run.

validation_owner.name: ECM product owner and TMS Replatform data architect

assumptions.source_file_name: Varicent Territory & Quota Planning thru SF-ETM - Project Charter_V1.0.docx

assumptions.title: Salesforce accounts will be aligned 1:1 with ECM accounts for planning and commissions
assumptions.description: The design assumes that ECM and Salesforce will share a single, aligned account model for Sales Planning, Territory Planning, and Commissions, consistent with the CPSP Enterprise Design.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The proposed architecture states that 'ECM / Salesforce Account is single account for Sales Planning & Territory Planning & Commissions (aligned to SAP S/4Hana CPSP Enterprise Design)'.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Strategic direction and architecture documents support this alignment, and some of the synchronization mechanisms may already be in place. However, legacy data, regional variations, or custom objects could still cause misalignment that needs to be addressed.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If 1:1 alignment cannot be achieved immediately, define explicit mapping and reconciliation rules in integration layers (e.g., D&A or middleware) and limit early go‑live scope to accounts where alignment is assured. Plan remediation and cleanup of misaligned accounts as a dedicated workstream.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm account synchronization rules and mappings between ECM and Salesforce during integration design; run reconciliations on sample data sets during parallel runs to verify 1:1 mapping and hierarchy consistency.

validation_owner.name: Salesforce CRM architect with ECM product owner

assumptions.source_file_name: Varicent Territory & Quota Planning thru SF-ETM - Project Charter_V1.0.docx

assumptions.title: Account-territory assignment will be performed in Salesforce Enterprise Territory Management (ETM)
assumptions.description: The solution assumes that account‑territory assignments, including territory hierarchy, will be managed in Salesforce ETM to improve seller experience, with Varicent providing planning outputs that feed ETM.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The proposed architecture explicitly states that 'Account-Territory assignment will be done in Salesforce (Enterprise Territory Management – ETM)' and that ETM will include the territory hierarchy.
assumptions.validity_explanation: ETM is already proven at other organizations and is designed for this purpose, but local customizations, data volume, or complexity of territory rules at TR may require careful configuration and performance validation.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If ETM cannot support all desired assignment scenarios initially, implement a limited ETM configuration focusing on core regions and simpler rules, while retaining some assignment logic in Varicent or interim processes. Plan a phased expansion of ETM capabilities as constraints are resolved.
assumptions.validation_method: Design and prototype ETM configuration during Discovery and Design; validate that ETM can represent required territory hierarchies and rules and can consume outputs from Varicent. Confirm through UAT with pilot users.
assumptions.source_file_name: Varicent Territory & Quota Planning thru SF-ETM - Project Charter_V1.0.docx

assumptions.title: A full 1–3 month parallel run will be completed before cutover
assumptions.description: The project assumes that a full parallel run of 1–3 months will be executed, comparing legacy TMS and Varicent + Salesforce ETM outputs and capturing a historical repository of rep‑territory‑account alignment data before cutover.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The proposed architecture notes that 'A full parallel run for 1-3 months is required to ensure 100% confidence in solution' and calls for capturing a full historical repository.
assumptions.validity_explanation: SteerCo and program leadership understand the risk of cutting over without a parallel run and have built it into the architecture and high‑level plan. However, schedule pressure or funding constraints could lead to attempts to compress or bypass this step.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If time or funding constraints threaten the full 1–3 month parallel run, prioritize a minimum acceptable duration and scope (e.g., full planning cycle for Corporates) and adjust launch dates accordingly rather than cutting the parallel run below agreed thresholds.
assumptions.validation_method: Track and approve a detailed parallel run plan via SteerCo, including defined start/end dates, scope, and acceptance criteria. Confirm execution via documented test results and sign‑off from Sales, Finance, and Commissions teams.
assumptions.source_file_name: Varicent Territory & Quota Planning thru SF-ETM - Project Charter_V1.0.docx

assumptions.title: Varicent Sales Planning and implementation SOW funding will remain available as planned
assumptions.description: The project assumes that the approved Varicent Sales Planning software license and the fixed‑price implementation SOW (approximately $800K) will remain funded through the CPSP program and not be reduced or reallocated during the project timeline.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Funding approvals have been documented in RAIDs for license and SOW funding, with the SOW funded via CPSP and specific Capex/Opex splits over 2026 and 2027.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Contracts are already signed and funding lines established, making it unlikely that funding will be withdrawn without a deliberate leadership decision. However, enterprise reprioritization or budget cuts could still impact available funds.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If program-level budget pressures emerge, prepare alternative phasing or scope options that protect critical Launch 0/1 deliverables while deferring less critical features or later launches, and present these options to SteerCo for decision.
assumptions.validation_method: Monitor CPSP program budget and Varicent contract payment schedules; confirm continued funding availability during regular financial reviews and SteerCo updates.
assumptions.source_file_name: Varicent Territory & Quota Planning thru SF-ETM - Project Charter_V1.0.docx

assumptions.title: Software savings will offset Varicent license funding over 2026–2028
assumptions.description: One of the initial funding assumptions is that Varicent license costs will be offset by achieving software savings between Commercial Excellence and Commercial Engineering over 2026, 2027, and 2028.

owner.name: Commercial Engineering and Commercial Excellence leadership

assumptions.rationale_basis: The funding assumptions explicitly state a caveat that license funding will be offset by achieving software savings in the relevant organizations over a multi‑year period.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The potential for savings exists through consolidation and retirement of legacy systems, but exact timing and amounts depend on successful rollout and decommissioning decisions that are still future events.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If savings lag, explore renegotiation of Varicent license terms at renewal, adjust user volumes or tiers where possible, and identify alternative cost reductions in adjacent tooling or operations to maintain budget neutrality.
assumptions.validation_method: Track decommissioning of legacy systems and associated cost savings and compare against Varicent license costs in financial reviews over 2026–2028.
assumptions.source_file_name: Varicent Territory & Quota Planning thru SF-ETM - Project Charter_V1.0.docx

entities.name: Local User Migration
entities.okrs:
Completing the OnePass local user migrations. 
Enabling AI, API and Partnership Growth / ONESOURCE - CIAM Migration.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

**Scope:** Local User Migration delivers the transition of all local legacy identity provider users and tenants to Thomson Reuters Account, providing one secure login across TR products. This matters because it reduces credential complexity, strengthens access security, and enables a more seamless cross-product customer experience.

**Current Status:**

Overall status is AMBER, driven by basic authentication remediation blockers preventing CIAM migration eligibility for a significant proportion of ONESOURCE tenants (up to 60% of tenants).

-   100% of all SafeSend local users migrated to CIAM
    
-   98% of all OnePass local user accounts have been migrated to CIAM against a 100% target by 31 Dec 2026.
    
-   1% of all local ONESOURCE users migrated to date; migration pace is blocker-dependent with full eligibility expected after the July 2026 remediation.
    

## Path to Green

The path to green focuses on clearing the basic authentication remediation being complete by all outstanding ONESOURCE products and the ONESOURCE team implementing the OData connector by 31 Jul 2026 so that currently blocked tenants can enter migration waves.

## Milestones

-   30 Jun 2026 – ONESOURCE: mandatory migration for all unblocked MFA tenants (37), ~560 internal tenants and ~6,700 low usage/inactive tenants.  
    
-   31 Jul 2026 – Data Query, OSA, OTP, OCT legacy, OCT NG –(EMEA) and TAXONE have basic auth remediation or OData connector implementation complete
    
-   31 Dec 2026 – OnePass: 100% local user accounts migrated
    
-   31 Dec 2027 – ONESOURCE: 100% local user tenants migrated

risks.title: ONESOURCE products who leverage OData connections are unable to have users who license the product migrate
risks.description: There is no solution to migrate OData connectors to CIAM yet, putting the migration of customers using them at risk.
risks.impact_description: Customers using ONESOURCE products that rely on OData connections cannot migrate to CIAM until a compatible solution is available, delaying CIAM migration for those tenants and constraining the overall migration timeline.
risks.mitigation: ONESOURCE team to complete a POC and implement the approved pattern; CIAM team to accept the SAML assertions required for OData-based connections. POC has been completed and implementation work is in progress, targeting a June 2026 timeline for OData migration enablement.

milestones.name: Migrate 100% of all ONESOURCE MFA (who are not blocked by basic auth) tenants to CIAM
Migrate 100% of all local ONESOURCE users to CIAM

risks.title: Scaling migration execution and coordination across customer-facing teams
risks.description: As the program enters large-scale migration (non-SSO and non-basic auth tenants), scaling execution across the customer base may be constrained by the need for stronger coordination among account managers, support teams, marketing, and other customer-facing organizations.
risks.impact_description: If coordination across account managers, support, marketing, and customer-facing organizations is insufficient, migration velocity may lag, leading to slower-than-planned adoption of CIAM, extended reliance on legacy authentication, and potential slippage of migration milestones.
risks.mitigation: Continue conducting and expanding one-on-one migration sessions led by Prajyoth and Eduardo; CIAM SSO team to schedule further sessions directly with account managers; improve customer guidance and readiness materials (Pendo guides, communications) to support coordinated outreach.

risks.title: Customer readiness for API user migration timelines
risks.description: API user migration work is funded and in development with the API Guild team (development targeted for Q4 2026 and migrations starting Q1 2027), but there is a concern that customers may not be ready to adopt the new API authentication timelines.
risks.impact_description: If customers are not ready when API migration capabilities become available (Q4 2026–Q1 2027), adoption of CIAM-based API authentication may be delayed, extending reliance on legacy authentication and leaving API users misaligned with the broader CIAM migration strategy.
risks.mitigation: Continue progressing API Guild development work funded by CIAM; plan customer readiness activities (communications, guidance, and timelines) ahead of Q1 2027 to prepare API customers for migration and align expectations with the new capabilities.

risks.title: ONESOURCE Migration: Basic Auth Remediation of some ONESOURCE products blocking CIAM migration
risks.description:
Some of the product teams with basic auth scenarios are either blocked or have remediation timelines going well into Q2 2026. Other products are experiencing delays with the required remediation. This blocks the migration effort given that the customers who subscribe to these products will not be able to move to CIAM. This impacts 45% tenants in AMER, 80% in EMEA and 90% in APAC.
Products that need to be remediated: OCT legacy, OCT NG (EMEA), OIA CoCounsel, OIT Data Import AddIn, OIT Automation test suite, OSR, OSR Desktop, TAXONE
risks.impact_description: Users who license impacted products (e.g., OCT legacy/OCT NG, OIA CoCounsel, OIT Data Import AddIn, OIT Automation test suite, OSR/OSR Desktop, TAXONE) are unable to migrate to CIAM, blocking CIAM adoption for 45% of tenants in AMER, 80% in EMEA, and 90% in APAC and sustaining Amber status for the ONESOURCE-CIAM migration program.
risks.mitigation: Following up with product teams and making them commit to a timeline. ONESOURCE platform to provide support to product teams in adopting solutions to remediate basic auth. Teams with slipped remediation (e.g., OCT and OSR) are being actively tracked, with sign-offs chased for items listed as May 2026 (such as OIT and CoCounsel).
