latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

SSO Migration is consolidating more than 5,500 legacy SSO connections from products such as OnePass, OneSource, Checkpoint, Materia, and SurePrep into the Thomson Reuters Account (TRA) CIAM platform to improve security, simplify customer access, and create a scalable identity foundation. The program also establishes a dedicated SSO Onboarding team and standardized migration processes so all new SSO customers are onboarded directly to CIAM rather than legacy IDPs.

Progress against migration targets is significantly behind plan, with only 0.37% of targeted legacy SSO connections migrated as of 29 May 2026 versus a 33% completion objective by 30 Aug 2026 and 65% by 31 Dec 2026. Outreach effectiveness is improving, with response rates increasing to around 48% of contacted customers (up from 15–20% in earlier weeks) and only four customers, about 0.7% of communications, raising concerns after email template changes.

Overall status is RED, driven by extremely low completed-migration throughput (0.37%) versus the planned 33% milestone for 30 Aug 2026 despite recent gains in customer engagement.

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on converting improved engagement into completed migrations by completing the reprioritization and projection exercise by 30 Jun 2026, increasing vetted outreach volume toward 400–600 emails per month, and resolving Ping Federate configuration performance issues by 30 Jun 2026 so technical setup does not bottleneck cutovers. In parallel, the team will deliver the per-connection CIAM migration feature by 31 Aug 2026 and formalize HighQ as a separate, product-led workstream so 2026–2027 program targets reflect realistic, segment-specific migration capacity.

## Milestones

- Complete CIAM migration reprioritization and projection exercise by 30 Jun 2026.  
- Migrate the first batch of Confirmation customers to CIAM via the agreed workaround by 15 Jun 2026.  
- Enable the per-connection (multi-connection) CIAM migration feature for customer use by 31 Aug 2026.  
- Achieve 33% of targeted SSO migrations by 2026-08-30.  
- Reach 65% of targeted SSO migrations by 31 Dec 2026 and finalize all remaining legacy SSO customer migrations by 2027-06-30.

risks.mitigation: Develop and execute a proactive customer communication strategy and work with each customer’s account manager to negotiate acceptable migration windows and emphasize the importance and benefits of migrating to TRA SSO.

risks.title: 65% 2026 CIAM migration target (including OnePass) may not be achievable with current customer engagement and outreach capacity
risks.description: There is a significant risk that the program will not achieve the 2026 objective of migrating 65% of legacy SSO connections to CIAM and completing the OnePass SSO migration. Current customer response rates remain extremely low (reported as below 0.5% progress in executive reporting), the outreach vetting process is slow due to difficulty identifying the correct CSM/Account Specialist for each account, and communications volume, while increasing, is still only in the hundreds of emails per month. Leadership is questioning whether the 65% + full OnePass target is realistic even under the optimistic assumption that 100% of customers agree to migrate, given constraints on team capacity, customer engagement, and sequencing across products (OnePass, SafeSend, OneSource, Legal Tracker, etc.).
risks.impact_description:
If the 65% migration target and full OnePass completion cannot be achieved by the end of 2026:
- The program will miss its primary OKR/metric communicated to CIO leadership and executives, undermining confidence in the SSO Migration plan.
- OnePass customers (especially large/complex GLF/MLF customers) may remain on legacy IDPs longer than planned, increasing operational overhead and extending support for legacy SSO.
- Co Counsel/Co Counsel Next adoption may be negatively impacted if key customers are not on CIAM, or timelines for those customers must be adjusted.
- The project may require formal re-baselining of scope and timelines, with potential downstream impact on the final June 2027 completion target.
- Additional unplanned escalation and governance effort will be needed to explain and manage missed targets with senior leadership.
risks.mitigation:
1) Near-term re-planning and projections:
- Conduct a 1–2 week exercise (by late May 2026) to build realistic projections by segment and product (OnePass, SafeSend, OneSource, Legal products, etc.) based on actual response rates and capacity.
- Identify which products and customer segments can realistically be migrated by end of 2026 and to what percentage, including specific expectations for OnePass vs other products.
- Re-evaluate projections again in mid-July 2026 after a new feature (allowing customers to migrate without bringing all products at once) is available, to see if that accelerates legal product migrations.

2) Increase and improve customer outreach:
- Increase the volume of vetted customer communications (targeting ~350–400 emails per month in the near term, growing to 500–600 per month as processes stabilize).
- Strengthen the language in initial and follow-up emails (including clearer end-of-life messaging for legacy IDPs and a more urgent but polite tone). Raul Bauza has already updated first and second email templates.
- Send more messages and follow up sooner and more often with customers, leveraging the new templates.

3) Improve vetting and account ownership processes:
- Continue work by Eduardo Cuevas, Hassan, and Adrian to reconcile CSM/account owner information from multiple systems and vet customer contacts so outreach goes to the right person.
- Maintain the practice of engaging CSMs/Account Specialists prior to outreach to ensure correct contacts and to support escalations.

4) Re-sequence and prioritize segments:
- Revisit prioritization of segments and products, seeking opportunities to compensate for slow or complex OnePass migrations by accelerating migrations in other products (e.g., SafeSend, OneSource) while still honoring previously communicated commitments to noisy/priority customers (e.g., GLF and MLF).

5) Governance and metric alignment:
- Use the late-May and mid-July projections to determine whether the 65% + full OnePass metric remains realistic; if not, prepare a proposal for adjusted OKRs and timelines for executive review.

risks.title: Hybrid TR Account / legacy SSO states from partial federation may create long-term security and technical debt issues
risks.description: To accelerate meeting migration targets, the team is considering a "partial federation" / multi-connection approach where customers are migrated off OnePass for specific legal or OneSource products, while other Thomson Reuters Account (TRA/CIAM) products for the same customer remain on local (non-federated) credentials. In this model, a single customer can be left in a hybrid state for an extended period (some users/products federated, others not). During the May 29, 2026 weekly status meeting, Peter Grigoriou and Jeff Olson noted that many customers may be comfortable remaining in this hybrid state, while Harvarinder Batth expressed concern that once such configurations are in place they may persist "for the next 10 or 20 years," effectively becoming long-lived technical debt and potentially creating security gaps if customers assume all access is federated and centrally controlled.
risks.impact_description:
If hybrid partial-federation states become widespread and long-lived:
- Customers may assume all Thomson Reuters applications are protected by SSO and their IdP deprovisioning, while in reality some products remain on local credentials, increasing the risk that offboarded users retain access to certain TR products.
- Security and compliance posture could be weakened, especially for regulated clients, if account lifecycle management is inconsistent across products.
- CIAM and SSO teams will carry significant long-term technical debt, requiring ongoing BAU projects to "clean up" and fully federate customers long after the formal SSO Migration program end date.
- Future funding and capacity will be required to complete these full-federation cleanups, competing with new feature work and potentially impacting Vinay's and other leaders' budgets.
- Confusion in internal and executive reporting may arise if migrations are counted as "complete" at the connection level while customers remain only partially federated in practice.

raised_by.name: Grigoriou, Peter (TR Technology) and Olson, Jeff (TR Technology), with concerns strongly voiced by Batth, Harvarinder S. (Operations & Technology)

risks.mitigation:
1) Define a clear policy for hybrid states:
- Document under what conditions partial federation / multi-connection configurations are acceptable as an interim measure and for how long.
- Ensure customers are explicitly informed of the implications of remaining partially federated (e.g., some products still using local accounts) and acknowledge this risk.

2) Track hybrid configurations as first-class objects:
- Extend CIAM/SSO tracking (e.g., migration spreadsheets and dashboards) to flag customers in hybrid states, including which products are federated and which are not.
- Treat hybrid customers as not fully "done" from a CIAM perspective, even if specific federated connections are counted toward the program’s migration metrics.

3) Plan a follow-on clean-up program:
- Assign the CIAM team to own a phased plan to move hybrid customers to fully federated states over time, potentially as BAU once the main SSO Migration program ends.
- Estimate effort and seek funding approval from leadership (e.g., Vinay, Marc) for this remediation work to avoid perpetual technical debt.

4) Limit use of hybrid patterns where feasible:
- Prioritize full-federation for new customers and for high-risk / high-value clients, using the hybrid approach primarily as a tactical tool to unblock specific migrations (e.g., legal products) where necessary.

5) Governance and reporting:
- Align executive reporting so that both connection-level migration counts and the number of customers still in hybrid states are visible, avoiding a false sense of completion while significant technical debt remains.

risks.title: Delay in SAP product team implementing CIAM-only onboarding for new accounts may expand OnePass footprint and create rework
risks.description: For Co Counsel customers interested in Anthropic MCP and related AI features, the long-term plan is that all new accounts will be created as CIAM-only by default, regardless of sales channel. Sales leaders (Kristine and Marie) agree with this direction, but the SAP product team (owned by Kyle in the Amy Hutsell group) has not yet committed to delivering the required feature to stop creating new OnePass accounts. In the interim (next ~1.5 months), new accounts continue to be created on OnePass, requiring manual migration before MCP can be enabled and adding operational overhead and noise. Although the OnePass team is planning to deliver an API in mid-June that SAP can leverage, SAP’s implementation timing remains uncertain.
risks.impact_description:
If the SAP product team does not implement CIAM-only onboarding for new accounts by end of Q2 2026:
- New Co Counsel Legal and related customers will continue to be provisioned on OnePass, increasing the number of accounts that must later be migrated to CIAM.
- Operational overhead will grow as support and CIAM teams must first onboard customers onto OnePass and then subsequently migrate them, instead of onboarding directly to CIAM.
- Inbound Anthropic MCP demand will generate more one-off migration requests that must be manually handled via the current intake process, increasing noise and delay.
- The OnePass legacy footprint will expand instead of contract, complicating achievement of 2026 and 2027 CIAM migration targets.
- Leadership priorities (including Andrew’s focus on MCP success) may be harder to meet if the underlying onboarding pipeline continues to create new legacy accounts.
risks.mitigation:
1) Drive OnePass API delivery:
- Ensure the OnePass team delivers the required API for CIAM-only onboarding to non-production over the coming weekend and to production in their bi-monthly release targeted for June 15, 2026.

2) Engage SAP product management:
- Work with Hassan to provide SAP product management (Kyle and the Amy Hutsell group) with clear requirements and technical details for consuming the new OnePass API.
- Use the current MCP-related operational pain and Andrew’s strategic priority for MCP/AI features as leverage to prioritize this feature on SAP’s roadmap and seek an explicit commitment date.

3) Escalate if necessary:
- If SAP does not commit to a near-term implementation date, escalate through Jason and, if needed, to Raghu/Andrew to reinforce the importance of stopping new OnePass account creation for MCP-related products.

4) Monitor net-new account creation:
- Track the number of new Co Counsel-related accounts created on OnePass each week and quantify the additional migration and support effort required.
- Use this data to reinforce the case for expedited SAP implementation.

5) Temporary guardrails:
- Where feasible, have sales and support teams manually steer new high-priority MCP customers toward CIAM onboarding paths, even before the SAP feature is live, to limit growth of the OnePass footprint in critical segments.

risks.title: Ping Federate performance and UI limitations may delay SSO configuration and CIAM migrations
risks.description: Ping Federate is exhibiting performance and UI issues when handling large numbers of configured URLs and connections. Pages listing thousands of customer URLs are taking a very long time to load and intermittently timing out, which in turn causes errors and delays when the customer SSO team attempts to configure new CIAM SSO connections or modify existing ones. These issues are affecting not only CIAM migration work but any customer SSO configuration activity that relies on Ping, and are causing setup cycles to take significantly longer than expected. Although a workaround exists and some remediation work is planned (including a change being deployed the night of June 5, 2026), there is a risk that these problems persist or recur, creating ongoing friction and delay in enabling SSO for CIAM migrations.
risks.impact_description:
If Ping Federate performance and UI limitations continue to cause timeouts and errors when configuring SSO connections:
- The CIAM/customer SSO team will require more calendar time and manual retries to configure each new connection, reducing throughput and increasing lead times for customer migrations.
- Customers may experience delays in getting their SSO configurations set up and tested, extending the overall migration cycle beyond the targeted 30-day window discussed with customers and leadership.
- Planned migration waves (especially for OnePass, legal products, and OneSource) may slip, putting additional pressure on the team to meet the 65% 2026 CIAM migration target.
- Broader customer SSO work (not only CIAM-related) may be hindered, potentially impacting other programs that rely on timely SSO setup.
- Confidence in the mediation/native architecture and in CIAM as a stable platform could be undermined if these operational issues are perceived as persistent platform instability.
risks.mitigation:
1) Work directly with Ping support:
- Maintain and escalate existing tickets with Ping Federate support to diagnose the root cause of UI timeouts and performance degradation when listing large numbers of URLs.
- Collaborate on configuration or product-level changes (e.g., paging, limits, UI optimization) to ensure administrative actions remain performant even at current and projected scale.

2) Implement interim technical workarounds:
- Apply the change planned for the night of June 5, 2026 to reduce the probability of timeouts in the short term.
- Where possible, avoid navigating high-volume UI views and instead rely on more targeted configuration paths or APIs.

3) Protect customer migrations from impact:
- Prioritize Ping-related work that directly unblocks in-flight CIAM customer migrations.
- Communicate realistic configuration timelines to the CIAM migration team so customer-facing expectations (e.g., “within 2–3 days after metadata URL is received”) remain credible.

4) Monitor and validate improvements:
- Track configuration lead times and error rates before and after Ping changes to confirm the issue is improving.
- If issues persist beyond June, prepare a contingency plan (e.g., additional tooling, scripting, or capacity) to avoid Ping becoming a sustained bottleneck for SSO setup.

5) Governance and reporting:
- Highlight Ping-related constraints in the weekly migration process efficiency workstream so leadership understands how much of cycle time is controlled by external platform behavior versus internal process.

risks.title: Anthropic MCP migration intake handled by single SME may create capacity bottleneck and weekend coverage gaps
risks.description: Anthropic MCP-related migration requests for Co Counsel Legal/Next are currently funneled through a single intake process that is being manually reviewed and actioned primarily by Harvarinder Batth. Requests arrive via a new form and require checking whether accounts are SSO or local, obtaining customer approval to migrate to CIAM, and then handing off to Kim for inclusion in nightly migration waves. There is no weekend/holiday coverage in place yet, and Harv is considering checking requests hourly or every two hours. Leadership explicitly called out that Harv is a potential single point of failure and that early in the process there could be 72-hour windows (e.g., long weekends) where customers receive no response. This could undermine the opportunity to capitalize on strong inbound demand from Anthropic MCP users who are "fish wanting to jump into the boat."
risks.impact_description:
If MCP migration intake remains dependent on a single SME with no backup and ad-hoc review cadence:
- Customers requesting Anthropic MCP enablement may experience multi-day delays in getting migration approvals and instructions, especially over weekends/holidays.
- Co Counsel support teams will continue to send ad-hoc emails to Harv, increasing noise and confusion about status.
- The program may miss a key opportunity to demonstrate fast, customer-friendly CIAM migrations for highly interested customers, weakening one of the few strong demand levers for CIAM.
- Leadership perception (including Andrew and Jason) of the CIAM/SSO team’s operational readiness for AI-related features may be negatively impacted.
- As MCP-related features expand beyond the initial small-firm cohort into larger SSO customers, the bottleneck could scale into broader delays and customer dissatisfaction.
risks.mitigation:
1) Define and document a clear internal MCP migration intake process, including steps to:
- Verify whether the requesting account is SSO or local.
- Contact the customer to obtain approval to migrate to TR Account (CIAM).
- Provide the customer with migration steps and MCP enablement instructions.
- Hand off approved account numbers to Kim by an agreed daily cutoff time for inclusion in nightly migration waves.

2) Distribute load across multiple team members:
- Have Harv, Hassan, Nick, and potentially Shannon share responsibility for reviewing form submissions in time-boxed slots (e.g., Harv at 9:00, Hassan at 10:00, Nick at 11:00, etc.) to avoid a single point of failure.
- Ensure that at least one backup reviewer is identified for long weekends/holidays so that requests do not sit unreviewed for 72 hours.

3) Set and communicate SLAs and cutoffs:
- Establish and communicate a clear daily cutoff time (e.g., 15:00) by which vetted account lists must be sent to Kim so she can compile and process them before end of day.
- Communicate to Co Counsel support and other stakeholders that requests received after the cutoff will be processed the next business day.

4) Train and onboard additional reviewers:
- Harv to record a walkthrough of processing the next few MCP requests and share written steps/process with Nick and others so they can take over reviews when Harv is unavailable.

5) Monitor early volume and adjust staffing:
- Track request volume and response times in the first few weeks; if inbound demand grows faster than expected, adjust reviewer coverage and consider involving Ops once supporting tools (e.g., Greg’s tool to identify SSO vs non-SSO) are available.

risks.title: HighQ product team deprioritization may leave ~700 legacy HighQ SSO connections unmigrated within CIAM program timelines
risks.description: During the June 5, 2026 status meeting, Harvarinder Batth and Eduardo Cuevas reported that the HighQ product team does not currently prioritize migrating their legacy SSO customers to CIAM. HighQ is not on OnePass and has approximately 600–700 legacy SSO connections that would need to be moved to TR Account (CIAM). The HighQ team is in the middle of two other migrations, faces resource constraints, and has recently encountered issues when migrating customers to CIAM/SSO, leading them to pause proactive outreach. They indicated that they intend to perform further analysis and only plan to restart planning at the end of Q3 2026, with no firm migration deadline or schedule. There is a risk that HighQ migrations slip beyond the life of the central SSO migration team or are indefinitely delayed, leaving a large block of connections on legacy SSO and undermining CIAM migration objectives.
risks.impact_description:
If the HighQ product team continues to deprioritize CIAM migrations and does not commit to a concrete timeline:
- Approximately 600–700 HighQ legacy SSO connections may remain on legacy IDPs beyond 2026–2027, directly reducing the proportion of connections migrated to CIAM and making the 65% (and eventual 100%) migration objectives harder or impossible to achieve.
- The central CIAM/SSO migration team may disband or significantly shrink before HighQ is ready, forcing HighQ to run a separate, ad hoc migration program without the benefit of shared tooling, templates, and experience.
- Customers using HighQ in combination with other TR products (e.g., Legal Tracker or other legal products) may remain in fragmented or hybrid identity states longer than planned, with inconsistent SSO experiences and potential security/compliance gaps.
- Leadership may need to re-baseline migration KPIs and communicate that a large, named product family (HighQ) will complete after the main SSO Migration program, increasing scrutiny and governance overhead.
- Future funding may be required to support a separate HighQ migration initiative, competing with other priorities and increasing total program cost.
risks.mitigation:
1) Clarify ownership and scope:
- Decide formally whether HighQ migrations are part of the central SSO Migration program scope or a separate product-led stream, and document this in program governance.

2) Engage HighQ leadership:
- Schedule a leadership-level discussion with the HighQ product director and key stakeholders (including Hassan and Marc) to review expectations, enterprise CIAM objectives, and the consequences of an open-ended delay.
- Seek a commitment from HighQ to a concrete analysis completion date (end of Q3 2026) and a draft migration plan with target start/end dates.

3) Set program constraints and expectations:
- Communicate clearly that central migration team support is expected to taper by end of 2026; if HighQ defers beyond that, they may need to run migrations predominantly with their own resources, with CSS/central team only providing connection-level support.
- Establish a notional deadline (e.g., Q4 2026 / Q1 2027) by which HighQ migrations should be substantially complete, subject to leadership approval.

4) Prepare for re-inclusion in the program:
- Temporarily exclude HighQ connections from the core 5,700-connection total used for CIAM program metrics, while tracking them separately as a distinct HighQ workstream.
- Maintain periodic check-ins with HighQ so their analysis and planning can feed back into the main program if they are ready sooner than expected.

5) Governance and escalation:
- Escalate to CIO/platform leadership if HighQ does not produce a credible plan by end of Q3 2026, including options such as mandated timelines or additional shared resources.

risks.title: Client Communication Approach May Negatively Impact SSO Migration Adoption and Timeline
risks.description: Client-facing communications for the SSO migration program are currently perceived as overly aggressive, unclear, and not aligned with premium client engagement standards. Feedback indicates issues with tone, short response timelines, time zone mismatches, and lack of coordination with local account teams. This may lead to confusion, reduced trust, and delayed client responses.
risks.impact_description:
Delayed onboarding / migration scheduling
Reduced client satisfaction (especially Premium Care accounts)
Potential reputational impact to TR (white-glove experience expectations not met)
Increased operational overhead due to escalations and rework
Risk of inconsistent messaging across regions
risks.mitigation:
Refine email templates:

Adjust tone to focus on benefits and partnership
Remove high-risk wording (e.g., “not optional”, “disruption”)

Targeted follow-up actions for large / strategic customers (June 5, 2026 status meeting):
- Monitor customer feedback on the updated templates; to date, only four customers (~0.7% of communications) have raised concerns, mostly large or strategic accounts.
- For large / sensitive customers (e.g., GLLF and UK strategic accounts), consider slightly modified wording and/or bespoke communications led by their CSMs to avoid misinterpretation of subject lines and deadlines (e.g., clarifying that dates refer to response deadlines, not hard migration cutover dates).
- Continue using the strengthened templates for the broader customer base given the materially improved response rate (~48% of contacted customers have now responded, versus ~15–20% in earlier weeks).
- Work with Hassan and Tom to better tag UK strategic accounts (e.g., via the SMGE/SAML categorization field) so they can be handled with appropriate white-glove communications and excluded from generic email waves when necessary.

assumptions.title: Average time from customer engagement to migration completion is approximately 30–45 days
assumptions.description: Current migration projections assume that, once a customer has engaged (i.e., replied to outreach and started working with the SSO team), the end-to-end cycle to complete their migration is roughly one month. In the May 29, 2026 status meeting, Harvarinder Batth explained that the projection model assumes engaged customers are migrated within 30 days, but acknowledged this may actually be closer to 45 days or longer on average due to customer internal processes (coordinating IT resources, security reviews, data clean-up, user communication) and TR-side process gaps. This assumption underpins the monthly throughput estimates derived from the 84 currently engaged customers and future outreach plans.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The projection spreadsheet discussed by Harvarinder uses engagement rates (e.g., 25% in the first month, 15% in the second, then 10% thereafter) combined with an assumed 30-day cycle time from engagement to completion. This yields an upper-bound estimate of ~2,700–2,800 migrated connections in 2026 once adjusted for the corrected total connection count. The team needs a working estimate of cycle time to convert engagement numbers (e.g., current 84 engaged customers) into migration throughput for planning and for re-baselining the 2026 targets.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Current evidence is limited and mixed: some smaller customers can migrate quickly, but larger or more complex customers (e.g., GLLF) face extended internal coordination, security review, and data clean-up requirements, as highlighted by both Peter Grigoriou and Harvarinder. The team is still refining processes and expects efficiency gains by late June, but until more data is collected, the true average cycle time remains uncertain.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency:
If analysis shows that the average cycle time is materially longer than 30–45 days:
- Update the projection model with the new empirically-derived cycle times and re-baseline the 2026 migration targets, communicating changes to leadership.
- Explore process and tooling changes to shorten cycle time (e.g., multi-connection support to decouple legal product migrations from broader TRA SSO changes, better customer-facing tools for data clean-up).
- Consider additional capacity (e.g., expanding Capgemini team) to handle more migrations in parallel.
- Further prioritize segments and products where shorter cycle times are achievable to maximize progress against revised targets.
assumptions.validation_method:
1) Track the 84 currently engaged customers through to completion, recording the date of first engagement, date of TRA SSO setup, and date of final migration for each.
2) Calculate the average and distribution (e.g., median, 75th percentile) of cycle times across this cohort by the end of June 2026.
3) Repeat the analysis monthly (July, August) to see whether process improvements shorten the average.
4) Use these empirical cycle times to update the projection model and re-baseline migration targets and throughput assumptions.

assumptions.title: 65% of legacy SSO connections can be migrated to CIAM by end of 2026 by de-emphasizing complex OnePass customers and compensating with other products
assumptions.description: The program is proceeding under the assumption that the 65% migration target for 2026 can still be achieved even if some large/complex OnePass customers (e.g., GLF/MLF) are not fully migrated by year-end, by accelerating migrations in other products and segments such as SafeSend, OneSource, and other legal products. The idea is that these products may be able to move faster and partially compensate for delayed or incomplete OnePass migrations, potentially resulting in a mix where OnePass is not 100% complete but overall CIAM migration still reaches approximately 65%.
assumptions.rationale_basis: In the meeting, Harvarinder stated he still has confidence that 65% can be achieved, but not including full OnePass completion, and suggested compensating by pushing more migrations through other products (e.g., SafeSend with ~300 connections, OneSource, other products) that may be more willing to move faster based on different communication approaches.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Current leadership sentiment acknowledges that the original plan likely overestimated customer response rates and did not fully account for non-responsive customers. However, there is some evidence that other products (e.g., SafeSend, OneSource) may be easier to move and a new feature is expected to unlock faster partial migrations for legal products starting in Q3. Because these levers are not yet fully validated and rely on customer behavior, confidence is moderate rather than high.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency:
If analysis in late May and July shows that the 65% target cannot be met even with compensating migrations:
- Prepare a revised set of OKRs/metrics for executive approval, potentially reducing the 2026 percentage, decoupling OnePass completion from the 65% metric, or shifting some scope into 2027.
- Further re-sequence segments, focusing on highest-priority customers (e.g., GLF/MLF and Co Counsel Next candidates) even if overall percentage remains lower.
- Consider additional measures to improve customer engagement (e.g., stronger end-of-life enforcement, more aggressive escalation, or alternative outreach channels) to raise migration throughput.
assumptions.validation_method:
1) A 1–2 week projection exercise across segments and products to quantify realistic 2026 migration volumes.
2) A follow-up re-evaluation in mid-July 2026 after the new "partial migration" feature is available and early adoption data is observed.
3) Comparison of actual monthly migration throughput versus the projections to confirm whether compensating migrations are materializing.
assumptions.source_file_name: Sync on CIAM Migration timeline and metrics.docx

assumptions.title: Customer outreach volume can scale to approximately 400–600 vetted migration emails per month
assumptions.description: Planning assumptions for the SSO Migration program currently presuppose that the team can ramp and sustain a significantly higher volume of vetted customer communications, reaching roughly 350–400 emails per month in the near term and 500–600 per month in subsequent months, as data processes and account ownership identification improve.
assumptions.rationale_basis: In the meeting, Harvarinder and Eduardo noted that March outreach volume was around 100 emails, April around 200+, and that in the last week alone they sent approximately 80–90 emails. They discussed a trajectory where May might reach ~400 emails, June ~500, and subsequent months 500–600, assuming vetting and data processes are streamlined.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The team is already trending upward from ~100 to 200+ emails per month and has recently sent ~80–90 emails in a single week, indicating that a few hundred emails per month are feasible. However, vetting bottlenecks (e.g., identifying correct CSM/Account Specialist contacts across multiple systems) and limited data access still constrain growth, so sustained 500–600 emails per month is plausible but not yet proven.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency:
If outreach volume cannot reach or sustain 400–600 vetted emails per month:
- Prioritize outreach to highest-impact segments and customers (e.g., GLF/MLF, Co Counsel Next prospects, upcoming migration waves) rather than broad coverage.
- Seek additional data analysis and operations support to increase vetting throughput (e.g., temporary staffing, automation, better dashboards).
- Explore alternative outreach and escalation mechanisms (e.g., leveraging sales/CSM campaigns, webinars, or account reviews) that do not rely solely on direct emails.
- Re-calculate migration throughput and adjust 2026 targets accordingly, escalating to leadership if capacity remains a hard constraint.
assumptions.validation_method: Monitor monthly counts of vetted initial and follow-up outreach emails sent and compare them against the 400–600 per month target; correlate outreach volume with available vetted customer lists and vetting throughput to determine whether capacity and processes can sustain the planned scale.
assumptions.source_file_name: Sync on CIAM Migration timeline and metrics.docx

assumptions.title: Co Counsel Next enablement can proceed without requiring CIAM migration as a strict prerequisite for existing Co Counsel Legal customers
assumptions.description: The CIAM/SSO migration and Co Counsel Next product enablement plans are being discussed under the assumption that existing Co Counsel Legal customers can begin using Co Counsel Next without first being migrated to CIAM. The rationale is that these customers already have access and can be given a feature flag to enable Co Counsel Next, avoiding additional friction and delays from making CIAM migration a prerequisite.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Harvarinder explained that existing Co Counsel Legal customers already have access and that Co Counsel Next is effectively a new feature/skin enabled via a feature flag. Requiring CIAM migration as a prerequisite for these customers may introduce significant data clean-up and friction, potentially slowing time to market. There is active discussion with leadership (e.g., Marc) about whether CIAM should remain a prerequisite for these customers.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The current design indicates that Co Counsel Next can be enabled as a feature within the existing product, and leadership believes that many customers already have access with their current registration keys. However, there are concerns about customer friction, data clean-up, and perception of past access issues. Until more evidence is gathered, confidence remains moderate.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency:
If it is determined that CIAM migration must be a prerequisite for Co Counsel Next for existing Co Counsel Legal customers:
- Re-sequence the CIAM migration plan to prioritize co-counsel-related customers ahead of other segments.
- Coordinate carefully with Co Counsel Next go-to-market plans to minimize delays and communicate clearly with affected customers.
- Provide additional resources for data clean-up and migration support for these customers to shorten the prerequisite migration phase.
- Reassess CIAM migration capacity and timelines to ensure that prioritizing these customers does not critically undermine overall migration targets.
assumptions.validation_method: Ongoing product and architecture review between CIAM leadership and Co Counsel Next product leadership (including Marc and Hassan) to determine whether enabling Co Counsel Next without CIAM introduces unacceptable risk or experience issues; evaluation of early customer experiences and support incidents for customers enabled on Co Counsel Next without prior CIAM migration.
assumptions.source_file_name: Sync on CIAM Migration timeline and metrics.docx

issues.title: Ping Federate UI performance issues delaying SSO connection setup
issues.description: Ping Federate is experiencing UI performance and timeout issues when loading pages with large numbers of configured URLs for customers, causing delays and intermittent errors during SSO connection setup. Administrators sometimes receive errors and must retry actions, slowing down configuration of CIAM/SSO connections for new and migrating customers.
issues.impact_assessment: The Ping Federate UI performance issue is directly slowing down the configuration of SSO connections required for CIAM migrations and for any new customer SSO setups. Administrators are encountering timeouts and errors when loading pages that list thousands of URLs, forcing retries and extending the time required to create or modify connections. This reduces throughput on the technical setup stage and may create a backlog, even when customers provide metadata URLs promptly. The issue affects all customers whose SSO connections must be configured via the affected Ping Federate instances, not just CIAM migration customers, and therefore has a broad operational impact.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Ping Federate platform performance; CIAM customer SSO configuration team; all CIAM/SSO migrations requiring new or updated connections.
issues.resolution: Work with Ping support and internal administrators to identify and remediate the root cause of the UI performance bottleneck (e.g., optimizing how large URL lists are rendered, adjusting timeouts, or restructuring configuration views). Implement interim workarounds discussed in the June 5, 2026 meeting during a planned maintenance window to keep configuration work moving while a permanent fix is developed.

issues.title: Low customer response rate continues to impact CIAM migration progress
issues.description: Customer response to CIAM migration outreach remains below the level required to support the planned migration from legacy IDPs to TR Account (CIAM), though some improvements are being observed as outreach is accelerated and templates are strengthened.
issues.impact_assessment: The persistently low response rate continues to constrain the CIAM migration funnel. Even with increased outreach volume, insufficient customer replies make it difficult to schedule migrations and demonstrate progress against the 65% 2026 migration target. However, recent actions — including stronger first, second, and third emails and escalations via CSMs — are starting to show incremental improvements in responses, which may mitigate impact if sustained.
issues.dependencies_affecting: SSO Onboarding team’s outreach capacity; Customer Success Managers and Account Specialists for escalations; shared mailbox and tracking spreadsheet data quality.
issues.resolution: Increase the volume and cadence of outreach emails (currently ~80–90 per week), use updated first, second, and third email templates with stronger 'polite urgency' and clearer legacy IDP end-of-life messaging, send a third email for non-responders, and escalate to Customer Success Managers/Account Specialists when there is no response after the third email. Eduardo will also reconcile the shared mailbox with the tracking spreadsheet by May 20, 2026 to ensure response data is accurate.

issues.title: Difficulty Identifying Account Specialist / CSM Ownership for Customer Accounts
issues.description:
The project team is facing significant challenges identifying the appropriate Account Specialist (ASM) or Customer Success Manager (CSM) for each customer account requiring SSO migration follow-up and escalation.

The required account ownership information is spread across multiple systems and is not aggregated or centralized. Many of these systems support only specific customer segments, such as Corporates, Legal, and Tax, or sometimes only a single product area, such as Legal Tracker. As a result, the team is unable to easily determine the correct ASM or CSM contact for each account.

This has created a highly manual and time-consuming process, requiring the team to review accounts one by one and coordinate with multiple teams and data analysis resources to locate the correct account owner.
issues.impact_assessment:
The lack of centralized ASM/CSM ownership data is slowing down the escalation process for non-responsive customers and may delay customer engagement, migration scheduling, and overall execution of the SSO migration from the legacy IDP to TR Account (CIAM).

It also increases the operational burden on the project team and supporting teams, creating inefficiencies and risk of inconsistent or delayed follow-up.
issues.resolution:
To address this issue, the project team recommends the following actions:

Engage data owners and business segment teams:
Partner with representatives from Corporates, Legal, Tax, and product-specific teams to identify the authoritative sources for ASM/CSM ownership data.

Create a consolidated account ownership tracker:
Build a centralized working file or dashboard that aggregates ASM/CSM information from available systems and maps each customer account to the appropriate owner.

Assign data analysis support:
Secure dedicated support from data analysis experts to help extract, reconcile, and validate account ownership data across the different systems.

Define a repeatable lookup process:
Establish a standard process for identifying ASM/CSM ownership for each account, including clear escalation paths when ownership is missing, outdated, or conflicting.

Prioritize high-risk / non-responsive customers:
Focus initial ownership mapping efforts on customers who have not responded to migration communications or who are part of upcoming migration waves.

Identify long-term data governance needs:
Escalate the lack of centralized account ownership data as a broader operational gap and recommend a long-term solution for maintaining a single, reliable source of account ownership information.

dependencies.title: SAP CIAM-only account creation feature depends on OnePass API delivery by June 15, 2026
dependencies.description: The ability for SAP-based sales/account workflows to create new customer accounts as CIAM-only (without first provisioning them on OnePass) depends on the OnePass team delivering a new API. The OnePass team plans to deploy this API to non-production over an upcoming weekend and to production as part of their bi-monthly release on June 15, 2026. Until this is delivered, new accounts continue to be created on OnePass, creating additional operational overhead and requiring later migration.
dependencies.dependent_on: OnePass team delivery of the new CIAM onboarding API to production by June 15, 2026
dependencies.consumer: SAP sales and account provisioning workflows for new OnePass/Co Counsel Legal customers; CIAM/SSO Migration program seeking to onboard all new SSO customers directly to CIAM.
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If the OnePass API is not delivered to production by June 15, 2026, new accounts will continue to be created on OnePass rather than as CIAM-only, increasing operational noise and costs, requiring additional manual migrations later, and potentially complicating Anthropic MCP and other AI connector enablement for new customers.
dependencies.mitigation: Use the current manual process and intake form for Anthropic MCP and similar requests to migrate affected accounts to CIAM as needed; escalate priority of the API on the OnePass/SAP product management roadmap through Hassan and Harvarinder, emphasizing the operational burden of continuing to provision new customers on OnePass.

dependencies.title: Per-connection (multi-connection) CIAM migration feature delivery
dependencies.description: The CIAM migration program’s ability to migrate customers on a per-connection basis (allowing specific products, such as legal products, to move to CIAM without migrating all products at once) depends on delivery of a new per-connection (multi-connection) feature by the CIAM development team. This feature is currently expected to be available around mid-July 2026, after an initial June release and additional stabilization.
dependencies.dependent_on: CIAM development team delivery and stabilization of the per-connection (multi-connection) CIAM migration feature in production
dependencies.consumer: CIAM/SSO migration process efficiency workstream and legal/OnePass product migrations seeking to decouple specific products from full-customer migrations
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If the per-connection feature is delayed beyond mid-July 2026, the migration team will need to continue treating customers as all-or-nothing migrations, limiting flexibility to accelerate specific product migrations (e.g., legal products, OneSource) where customers are ready. This could extend cycle times, reduce migration throughput, and constrain the ability to achieve adjusted 2026 migration targets by compensating with faster-moving segments.
dependencies.mitigation: Continue refining the current end-to-end migration process so it remains workable without the per-connection feature; prioritize customers and products that can still proceed under the existing all-or-nothing model; and closely track development progress so process and communication changes can be implemented quickly once the feature is available.

decisions.title: Adopt multi-pronged strategy to improve CIAM migration outreach effectiveness
decisions.description: Leadership agreed that the CIAM migration program will simultaneously pursue four key strategies to improve customer engagement and migration progress: (1) send outreach emails to more customers (increasing volume), (2) follow up sooner and more frequently with non-responsive customers, (3) strengthen the language and tone of communications, including clearer legacy IDP end-of-life messaging to create urgency, and (4) re-segment and re-sequence migration priorities across products and customer segments to compensate for early slowness and adjust for low response rates.
decisions.rationale: Executive leadership has been concerned that reported metrics show poor progress and that initial plans were overly optimistic about customer response rates. A coordinated, multi-pronged approach is needed to increase engagement, accelerate migrations, and credibly demonstrate a 'path to green' while managing expectations about the 65% target and OnePass completion.
decisions.options_considered: Continue current outreach pace and messaging without change; focus solely on increasing email volume; focus solely on escalation through CSMs; defer changes until more data is available.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Issue: Low customer response rate to CIAM migration outreach; Issue: Difficulty identifying Account Specialist / CSM ownership for customer accounts.

decisions.title: Conduct two-stage reevaluation of 65% CIAM migration target and OnePass completion
decisions.description: The team will conduct a two-stage reevaluation of the 65% CIAM migration target and OnePass completion goal. First, a 1–2 week exercise (by late May 2026) will produce realistic projections based on current response data, segment-by-segment analysis, and reprioritization of products (including potential compensation from Safesend, OneSource and other products if large/complex OnePass customers lag). Second, in mid-July 2026, the team will reevaluate the plan again using data from the new feature that allows customers to migrate without all products moving at once, assessing whether overall completion can reach approximately 90–95% of the original target.
decisions.rationale: Progress to date and very low response rates indicate the original plan may not be realistic, especially for large and complex OnePass customers. Leadership needs a more evidence-based assessment of whether the 65% target is achievable and what trade-offs (e.g., compensating with other products) are required, while also considering new feature capabilities that may accelerate legal product migrations later in the year.
decisions.options_considered: Maintain the 65% and full OnePass completion goals without reevaluation; immediately reduce targets based on early pessimism; delay any reconsideration until much later in 2026.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Issue: Low customer response rate to CIAM migration outreach; CIAM migration OKRs and executive reporting commitments.

decisions.title: Define three CIAM migration workstreams with named leads
decisions.description: The CIAM migration program will be structured around three explicit workstreams: (1) outreach readiness (data preparation and account vetting) led by Batth, Harvarinder S. (Operations & Technology), Halta, Hassan (Operations & Technology), and Cuevas, Eduardo (TR Technology); (2) customer engagement and response rate improvement led by Cuevas, Eduardo (TR Technology); and (3) migration process efficiency led by Grigoriou, Peter (TR Technology). These workstreams will be tracked in the weekly status deck.
decisions.rationale: Discussion highlighted three major bottlenecks to achieving CIAM migration targets: readiness of vetted outreach lists, low customer response rates, and slow/complex migration execution. Formalizing these as workstreams with named leads and weekly tracking creates accountability and visibility into progress on each dimension.
decisions.options_considered: Continue treating these activities as implicit tasks without explicit workstreams or leads; focus only on customer engagement without separately tracking outreach readiness and process efficiency.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Risk: 65% 2026 CIAM migration target (including OnePass) may not be achievable with current customer engagement and outreach capacity; Issue: Low customer response rate continues to impact CIAM migration progress.

decisions.title: Schedule leadership review of updated CIAM migration plan for May 26, 2026
decisions.description: Leadership agreed to reconvene the week of May 26, 2026 (day after Memorial Day) for a follow-up meeting to review the results of the realistic projection and reprioritization exercise, updated outreach metrics, and any proposed adjustments to the 65% migration and OnePass completion targets.
decisions.rationale: Executive stakeholders (including Vinay, Jeff, and others) are requesting clearer evidence of a realistic 'path to green'. A fixed follow-up date ensures the leadership group reviews concrete data and projections rather than relying on early, incomplete observations from the first few weeks of the full team being in place.
decisions.options_considered: Delay follow-up until more data accumulates later in the summer; hold ad-hoc discussions without a scheduled checkpoint; provide updates only via written status reports.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Action: Run two-week realistic migration projection and reprioritization exercise; executive reporting for CIO critical projects.

decisions.title: All new SSO customers must be onboarded on CIAM
decisions.description: Reaffirmation that all new customers requiring SSO will be onboarded directly onto CIAM (TR Account), rather than using legacy IDPs, to reduce future friction, improve customer experience (including for Co Counsel and Co Counsel Next), and avoid expanding the legacy footprint.
decisions.rationale: Ensuring all new SSO customers use CIAM reduces operational risk, aligns with CIAM modernization goals, and simplifies future migrations and feature adoption (e.g., Co Counsel Next). It also helps manage perceived access issues by standardizing on CIAM for new deployments.
decisions.options_considered: Allow some new customers to continue using legacy IDPs temporarily; defer CIAM requirement for new Co Counsel Next customers; treat CIAM adoption for new customers as optional.
decisions.dependencies_linked: CIAM platform readiness and feature set; Co Counsel Legal and Co Counsel Next rollout plans.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Enterprise Identity and Entitlement is delivering a shared identity and entitlement model for CoCounsel Next, including ethical wall enforcement, CIAM-native identity, and Auth0 FGA-based authorization, to support seamless and compliant cross-product access. This matters because fragmented, product-specific entitlements are slowing onboarding and degrading admin experience

One of four defined delivery milestones is complete, so 25% of the current milestone set has been achieved. The “Post-login Requirements for CoCounsel Next” milestone has slipped by 35 days from the original 08 May 2026 plan to the latest 12 Jun 2026 estimate, and several high-impact risks and issues remain open, blocking reliable GA estimation.

Overall status is Amber, driven primarily by unresolved blocking architectural decisions that prevent build from starting and put the 22 Aug 2026 GA date at risk.

## Path to Green

The path to Green is to complete post-login entitlement requirements by 12 Jun 2026, close the overdue architecture and enterprise data model issues, and drive decisions on CIAM enforcement, FGA identity, admin tool placement, and FGA store structure so engineering can begin build and GA planning can move from blocked to committed.

## Milestones

-   Complete the “Current state assessment process for CoCounsel Next” across reg keys, Prism GUIDs, SAP WRP, TFMS, CIAM, OnePass, SSP, and Auth0 FGA by 08 May 2026.
    
-   Finalise “Post-login Requirements for CoCounsel Next” and close the 35-day variance against the original 08 May 2026 plan by 12 Jun 2026.
    
-   Enable “CoCounsel Next Pilots” for a defined cohort of customers by 31 Jul 2026.
    
-   Enable “CoCounsel Next GA” for all US customers by 22 Aug 2026.
    
-   Complete the Enterprise Identity and Entitlement program and transition to steady-state operations by 31 Dec 2026.

risks.title: GA planning blocked: August timeline at risk, crawl scope undefined, requirements incomplete
risks.description: General availability planning for August is blocked because engineering cannot estimate or commit without (1) a clearly defined October crawl scope and (2) complete tiered requirements that cover pre-login flows, commercial touchpoints, and agentic AI. These inputs are missing, leaving uncertainty in scope and effort.
risks.impact_description: If crawl scope and full requirements remain undefined, engineering will be unable to provide reliable estimates or commitments. This may delay the August GA date, cause scope gaps, and increase the likelihood of rework or missed functionality, particularly in pre-login, commercial, and agentic AI areas.
risks.mitigation: Product team to provide clear requirements .Patrick Wagstrom produces a complete requirements document, including pre-login, commercial touchpoints, and agentic AI,

risks.title: Ethical walls — agentic AI poses breach risk if permissions not enforced correctly
risks.description: Agentic AI can traverse large volumes of content and generate derived artefacts that may unintentionally combine restricted sources. Ethical walls must be enforced based on the content accessed during generation, not just on the appearance of the output. Derived content must inherit permissions from its sources, and admin privileges must not grant agents broader content access.
risks.impact_description: If ethical wall enforcement is not correctly designed and implemented, agents may access or combine restricted content, potentially breaching client confidentiality and legal or regulatory constraints. This could cause serious compliance incidents, reputational damage, and require costly remediation or rollback of AI capabilities.
risks.mitigation: Design an ethical wall enforcement model covering: file-level vs workspace-level inheritance, integration with DMS/intake tools such as iManage and Intapp Walls, and clear scoping of agent identity and permissions so that derived content inherits source permissions and admin privileges do not expand agent content access.

risks.title: Multiple blocking architectural decisions unresolved (identity, admin tool, FGA, CIAM)
risks.description: Four interdependent architectural decisions remain unresolved and are blocking the start of build: (1) where the admin tool will be hosted, (2) how CIAM enforcement will operate, (3) which user identity (Prism GUID vs EUID) will be used by Auth0 FGA, and (4) how the FGA store will be structured. Until these are decided, downstream design and implementation cannot progress.
risks.impact_description: If these architectural decisions are not resolved quickly, the engineering team cannot start build work. This will delay delivery of the GA scope, compress testing timelines, and may force rushed or suboptimal architecture choices that increase technical debt and rework later.
risks.mitigation: Escalate to secure agreement and assignment of the correct owners for each architectural block/module (admin tool placement, CIAM enforcement model, FGA identity, and FGA store structure) and drive decisions to unblock build.

risks.title: Admin portal is the largest GA body of work — no owner, no backlog, no funding
risks.description: The admin entitlement portal has been identified as the largest single body of work required for GA, but it currently has no confirmed owning team, no committed backlog, and no allocated funding. Building this as a net-new capability for the August release is not feasible without an immediate decision on ownership and resourcing.
risks.impact_description: If an owning team, backlog, and funding are not established promptly, the admin portal will not be delivered in time for GA. This will leave entitlements administration incomplete, impact operational readiness, and may delay GA or require manual workarounds that are risky and hard to scale.
risks.mitigation: Escalate through a core group session in the week commencing 28 April to decide admin tool placement and assign an owning team. Anthony Rokis must make the decision. No build will start until ownership is confirmed, ensuring accountability and resourcing.

assumptions.title: SAP WRP = source of truth for entitlement/billing. Auth0 FGA = runtime authorization layer only
assumptions.description: For GA, SAP WRP remains the system of record for entitlements and billing. Auth0 FGA is used only as a runtime authorization layer via a dual-write model, where admin actions update both SAP and FGA in parallel. Auth0 FGA is not intended to replace SAP as the master system.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Existing SAP WRP processes and data structures already support entitlements and billing, and replacing them before GA would be too risky and complex.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The project relies on established SAP WRP capabilities for entitlements and billing, with Auth0 FGA introduced only as a runtime evaluation engine. This lowers implementation risk by avoiding wholesale replacement of SAP before GA while enabling fine-grained authorization via a dual-write pattern.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If SAP WRP cannot be the source of truth or dual-write proves unworkable, define an alternative master (e.g., a dedicated entitlement store) and adjust integration patterns, accepting schedule or scope changes as needed.
assumptions.validation_method: Communicate and confirm this constraint with all affected teams and validate the dual-write implementation approach with the SAP/WRP team.

assumptions.title: Phase 1 only in scope for GA — minimum change, existing infrastructure preserved
assumptions.description: For GA, only Phase 1 is in scope: enabling CoCounsel Next, obfuscating registration keys, and implementing EUID-linked FGA. Subsequent phases (2A, 2B, and 3), which include billing evolution and full registration key retirement, are explicitly deferred beyond GA.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Limiting GA to Phase 1 reduces risk and keeps changes to a manageable level, allowing delivery on the August timeline while preserving existing infrastructure.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The GA plan is structured around a phased delivery where Phase 1 provides the minimum necessary capability. Leadership has already aligned on this approach, making it a realistic and enforceable constraint if communicated effectively.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If pressure mounts to include Phase 2/3 items, de-scope or defer non-essential work, renegotiate timelines, or secure additional resources to avoid undermining GA quality.
assumptions.validation_method: Communicate the Phase 1 scope boundary to all workstreams and monitor plans and backlogs to ensure Phase 2/3 items are not added to GA.

assumptions.title: CoCounsel owns FGA. Commercial/platform teams own system integrations
assumptions.description: The CoCounsel product team is assumed to own the fine-grained authorization (FGA) layer itself, while commercial and platform teams (SAP, TFMS, Prism, Order Capture) own their respective system integrations with FGA.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Clear ownership boundaries reduce overlap, confusion, and duplicated authorization logic across teams.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Assigning FGA ownership to the product that directly uses it (CoCounsel) and delegating integration responsibilities to system owners is a standard pattern that fits existing organizational structures, making the assumption realistic.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If ownership disputes arise or responsibilities are unclear, escalate to program leadership to clarify ownership and update documentation and backlogs accordingly.
assumptions.validation_method: Document ownership boundaries and validate them with all involved teams to ensure shared understanding.

assumptions.title: CIAM-native is the target. Prism GUID = interim FGA identity until CIAM migration completes
assumptions.description: The long-term target is CIAM-native identity using EUID for FGA. Until the OnePass-to-CIAM migration completes (by end of 2026), Prism GUID will be used as the interim identifier for FGA. The current beta OnePass login is a temporary solution.
assumptions.rationale_basis: CIAM is the strategic identity platform, but migration is in progress, requiring an interim identity approach for FGA.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The assumption balances strategic direction (CIAM/EUID) with current technical realities (Prism GUID and OnePass), allowing FGA to be implemented now while remaining compatible with the future identity model.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If CIAM migration is delayed or Prism GUID proves unsuitable, extend the interim model, introduce additional mapping layers, or adjust timelines for CIAM-native rollout.
assumptions.validation_method: Design FGA with a clear migration path to EUID and confirm the Prism GUID interim model with Vassil and identity architecture teams.

assumptions.title: TFMS = user-to-customer master. Fine-grained access control is product-side, not commercial
assumptions.description: CIAM is assumed to be the identity master (EUID). TFMS is assumed to be the master for user-to-customer entitlement/assignment for access-based products. Content sets, folders, and workspaces are assumed to be handled by product-side logic after login, not by commercial systems.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Separating identity, commercial entitlements, and product-level content control clarifies responsibilities and reduces complexity in integration design.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Assigning TFMS to manage user-to-customer entitlements while leaving fine-grained content control to products leverages existing system strengths and aligns with known responsibilities, making this a reasonable and efficient assumption.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If TFMS cannot reliably act as the user-to-customer master, identify an alternative system or data store and adjust provisioning flows and data models accordingly, accepting potential schedule impact.
assumptions.validation_method: Document this split clearly in data flow and sequence diagrams and validate it with Dheeraj and relevant architecture stakeholders.

issues.title: Architecture diagram outdated for entitlements program
issues.description: The current architecture reference is an outdated informal diagram by Rick Dauk that does not reflect Auth0 FGA, CIAM, SAP WRP dual-write, or the proposed admin tool. All design discussions rely on this inaccurate baseline.
issues.impact_assessment: Using an inaccurate architecture baseline for discussions risks misaligned design decisions, incorrect integration assumptions, and rework across Auth0 FGA, CIAM, SAP WRP dual-write, and the admin tool. Integration and implementation planning is compromised until an authoritative diagram exists.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Architecture sessions and downstream design decisions for entitlements, including integrations between CIAM, SAP, WRP, and the admin portal.
issues.resolution: Produce an updated authoritative architecture diagram that incorporates Auth0 FGA, CIAM, SAP WRP dual-write, and the proposed admin tool, and present it at the next architecture session.

issues.title: Enterprise data model for organization, tenant, subscription, and user IDs unresolved
issues.description: The relationships between organization ID, subscription ID, and user ID across CIAM, Prism, SAP, and TFMS are not documented, and ownership of the future enterprise subscription store is unclear. This gap blocks final architecture and engineering estimation.
issues.impact_assessment: Without a defined data model and ownership for organization, tenant, subscription, and user IDs, the final architecture cannot be completed and engineering cannot provide reliable estimates, risking delays and misaligned implementations.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Final architecture decisions, engineering estimation, CIAM, Prism, SAP, TFMS, and enterprise subscription store design.
issues.resolution: Have CIAM and Enterprise Data teams define and document the data model for organization, tenant, subscription, and user IDs across CIAM, Prism, SAP, and TFMS, and clarify ownership of the enterprise subscription store by coordinating with enterprise data architects.

## Executive Summary

Enterprise AI is delivering shared AI platforms and tooling, including the LLM Orchestrator, observability, and compliant deployment patterns, so product teams can adopt AI at scale with security, governance, and cost efficiency. These capabilities reduce friction for LLM-powered features, improve developer productivity, and support regulatory requirements such as FedRAMP and the EU AI Act.

To date, 45% of project targets have been achieved against a plan running through 30 Dec 2026. LLM Orchestrator adoption has reached 88% of enterprise LLM token consumption versus a 90% 2026 target, supported by 22 product teams onboarded and completion of foundational training, observability (Braintrust), and web grounding tool onboarding.

Overall status is Green, driven by strong LLM Orchestrator adoption at 88% of LLM token volume against the 90% 2026 target.

## Path to Green

The top risk is delay in FedRAMP certification for the LLM Orchestrator due to periodic approval lags for tool access, which is being mitigated through rigorous follow up with approvers and escalation to close by 17 Jun 2026.

## Milestones

- Achieve 90% LLM token consumption via the LLM Orchestrator and complete scale-up onboarding by 23 Dec 2026.
- Complete FedRAMP production deployment of the LLM Orchestrator in AWS GovCloud by 30 Jul 2026.
- Complete the SLM Acceleration POC, validating the feasibility and economics of small language models, by 31 Jul 2026.
- Implement AI digital signature capabilities for EU AI Act Code of Practice compliance across targeted TR products by 23 Dec 2026.
- Achieve overall project completion as per the current scope by 30 Dec 2026.

## Executive Summary

Transform FinOps is delivering modernized cloud financial operations on TRUCCR, including AI-powered assistance, deeper cost visibility, and integrated finance and revenue data, so teams can make better cost efficiency and investment decisions. The initiative matters because it reduces cloud waste, improves forecasting, and strengthens product-level unit economics for engineering, finance, and leadership.

To date, 2 of 5 defined milestones have been completed by their 27 Feb 2026 targets, with the remaining 3 milestones in progress and holding zero start and end variance against plan. The program is tracking to its 18 Dec 2026 end date with foundational capabilities such as role-based security and revenue reporting already delivered.

Overall status is Green, driven by on-plan execution of all active milestones and early completion of key TRUCCR revenue and security enhancements.

## Path to Green

The team is monitoring dependencies highlight critical AI/LLM initiatives including:

-   AI/LLM Cost Ingestion (Thomson) — The key focus is onboarding teams to the TR AI Gateway; Enterprise AI team holding biweekly stakeholder meeting to drive urgency. A revised timeline or scoped-down deliverable may need to be considered given the first production use case isn't expected until September. Ongoing weekly series scheduled with key stakeholders. 
    
-   Anthropic/OpenAI — Efforts to map workspaces to appropriate owners to support chargeback, in parallel kick off meeting with key stakeholders to confirm path forward for AI Dev Tool chargeback (June 5th).
    
-   TRUCCR Bot — One month ahead of schedule, production release of our AI-powered FinOps Assistant to align with user queries on cloud usage & spend with TRUCCR & AWS source data.
    

## Milestones

-   AI/LLM Cost Ingestion — Thomson | On Track | Q3
    
-   AI/LLM Cost Ingestion — Anthropic/OpenAI | On Track | June 30th
    
-   Strategic Initiatives: 
    
    -   Cloud Expense Forecasting & Variance Analysis | On Track | June 30th
        
    -   Revenue Forecast Integration | On Track | September 4th

## Executive Summary

Optimize TR Estate is delivering mature FinOps practices, intelligent automation, and multi‑cloud tooling so the TR technology estate runs at lower cost, with better financial control and sustainability. The program matters because it turns cloud spend into a managed investment by improving visibility, discipline, and waste reduction across CIO platforms.

Progress to date includes ARM64 adoption at 56.14% against a 57% Q2 target (up from 54.96% in March) on a path to 80% year-end, alongside completion of strategic and tactical efforts such as the Datadog Cost Optimization dashboard, AAWARE automation alignment, FinOps Office Hours reboot, and publication of FinOps Best Practices.

Overall status is Green, driven by strong delivery of foundational optimization tooling and ARM64 migration momentum.

## Path to Green

The primary mitigation focus is maintaining visibility on the cloud savings pipeline through 2026, ensuring ARM64 adoption with continued alignment with Platform Engineering CSAs to drive engagement with Product Engineering teams and promoting strategic cost savings tools such as AAWARE, BUCC and Datadog insights.

Task the CCE team with identifying and updating all in-flight and potential savings, including ideas under review, blocked items, and estimated savings. Progress Red Lever analysis by validating and vetting identified platform-level optimisation opportunities that can benefit multiple product pillars, and clean and normalise Red Lever data for SteerCo visibility. Include DR cost-optimisation by actively reviewing Tier 2/3/4 environments to identify downgrade or shutdown opportunities.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Time Base Integration is migrating all Time Base on-premises and cloud workloads into Thomson Reuters–owned cloud accounts so that operations continue in fully governed TR environments after the Australian office closure. The end state is that all Time Base applications, data, and work management run in TR AWS and supporting TR platforms.

Phase 1 migration from on-premises to Time Base AWS and office closure completed on schedule by 31 Mar 2026, and the Time Base BU AWS account has been onboarded into the TR AWS Organization within the revised timeframe. Foundational TR non-prod architecture was baselined on 31 May 2026, with TR non-prod environment build, DevOps pipeline standardization, and the new TR Google Cloud calendar project all in progress toward planned completion by 30 Jun 2026.

Overall status is Green, driven by on-schedule completion of Phase 1 and core TR non-prod architecture, with remaining risk centered on Time Base resource constraints as Phase 2 build and migration activities ramp up.

## Path to Green

For this Green project, the primary mitigation is the open Resource Availability risk, which is being managed by surfacing slippage early in weekly status calls so that scope, sequencing, or support from TR teams can be adjusted before key milestones are impacted.

## Milestones

- Complete TR Cloud Non-Prod Environment Build and set up the TR Google Cloud project for Time Base calendar integration by 30 Jun 2026.
- Complete DevOps Pipelines Migration and Standardization for PIT and Time Base, including CI/CD templates and non-prod deployments, by 30 Jun 2026.
- Complete PROD Preparation and Permit-to-Operate planning, including PROD account strategy and high-level migration plan, by 31 Dec 2026.
- Complete TR PROD Infrastructure Build and Account Readiness and PROD Environment Testing and Validation by 31 Dec 2026.
- Execute Production Cutover Execution and BU Account Closure by 31 Dec 2026, completing the Time Base Integration program.
