latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

**A. Scope:** Migrate all 60 legacy servers supporting the UFile Online Application in Montreal Data Center, as they will soon be out of vendor support.

**B.** **Metrics:** 100% of the App migration to AMS Cloud will be fully completed by Sept 30, 2026. Subsequently, all decommissioning and shutdown activities will be completed by December 30, 2026.

**C. Change in Migration Strategy: AMS Cloud:** On April 8, 2026, leadership approved migrating UFile Online from Montreal Data Center to AMS Cloud instead of Azure. This change supports service continuity and modernization.

· **Key Reasons:** (1) AMS migration expertise enables immediate start. (2) AMS Cloud simplifies transition for business and operations teams.

**D. Executive Summary of Recent Dependencies/ Blockers:**

**1. New Blocker Identified:** AMS currently supports the 2019 pattern but not the 2022 pattern.  
DBA Architects (John Tracy/Debopriya) provided guidance during the recent planning call. Based on their input, an intake request was submitted to Asif Haliyal (Data Services). Asif's team is now assessing the required development and migration efforts, including testing and validation. Estimated completion in 1–2 weeks (by June 8).

· **Contingency Plan:** If the Data Services team is delayed in delivering the 2022 SQL pattern (post 8th June), the project team will proceed with the SQL 2019 pattern for the Development environment.

2. **Architecture Design Milestone**: The deadline (May 20) for the Architecture Design planning milestone has passed. CSA’s are currently focused on critical requirements, including the architecture diagram (network topology, IAM roles, IIS permissions, database migrations, and connected environments) necessary for PCI DSS compliance review.

**E. Project Current Developments/ Progress:**

1) **Update: Development Environment Provisioning**  
The Cloud Implementation Team has initiated work on provisioning the Development environment. AMS resources are being created as planned, with the following components completed across all three environments (Dev, Int, QA):

·       KMS, Security Groups (SGs) and IAM

2) **Project Timeline Update (Milestone 1):**

· **Migration Window:** The optimal timeframe for migrating UFile Online data aligns with the Montreal Data Center Colo exit deadline for Milestone 1. Both the data migration and application migration are scheduled to be completed by September 2026.

· **Detailed Environment Plan:** Prasanna and BU leadership have mapped out the migration timeline across five environments (Dev/CI, Int/Demo, QA/QED, EPS/Pre-prod, and Production). The target for completing all migrations is September 18, 2026.

· **Communication:** **This timeline has been shared with the Project Sponsor, Kevin Dorle, as well as CSA representatives Gordon and Monica. Next the same will be shared with Project team on 2nd June 2026 in a weekly call and set the expectations as “Non-Negotiable”**

· **Contingency:** Should unforeseen technical challenges delay the September 18 deadline, the contingency plan is to complete the migration by early to mid-October 2026.

F. **Current RAG Status:** Amber trending to Green: Montreal RAG currently Amber due to a number of unknown outcomes, which could impact site being closed by end 2026 (please see below)

## Path to Green

Project teams are actively engaging in multiple follow-up iteration calls

1) The team has identified the key issues or blockers that could delay the project.

2) There is a defined path to resolve these blockers, and the team feels confident about executing it.

3) Despite the risks/Blockers, the project plan still shows it is feasible to meet the September/October 8th deadlines, which are critical for operational requirements.

4) COLO Exit Deadline: From the broader perspective of the Montreal COLO exit project, the ultimate deadline is the end of the year. However, operational constraints (e.g., seasonal factors and the client migration window) mean the production migration must happen much earlier, ideally before September/October.

5) Contingency Planning: Even if challenges arise, there is a backup plan to extend the migration into October, which provides an additional layer of confidence

risks.title: Lack of clarity in ownership for infrastructure and application setup tasks
risks.description: There is confusion about who is responsible for tasks such as server configuration, load balancing, application setup, SQL connection setup, TLS certificates, and network configuration in the AMS migration.
risks.impact_description: If ownership for these tasks remains unclear, critical activities may be delayed or missed, leading to misconfigured infrastructure, security weaknesses, failed connectivity, and delays in testing and go-live. This can significantly impact the migration schedule and stability of the application post-cutover.
risks.mitigation: Refine and communicate the RACI matrix specifically for server configuration, load balancing, application setup, SQL connectivity, TLS certificates, and network configuration. Ensure each task has a clearly assigned owner and that dependencies are documented in runbooks and migration plans.

risks.title: Ambiguity in roles and responsibilities for AMS migration (RACI)
risks.description: There is or was ambiguity in roles and responsibilities among team members during the AMS migration from the Montreal data center, which can cause overlapping efforts, missed tasks, and unclear accountability across the migration workstreams.
risks.impact_description: If role and responsibility ambiguity reoccurs, tasks may be duplicated or left incomplete, decision-making could be delayed, accountability for critical actions may be unclear, and confusion and inefficiencies could increase overall project risk, potentially impacting the migration timeline and service continuity.
risks.mitigation: Conduct a RACI workshop to clearly define and document roles and responsibilities for all migration tasks and communicate them to the stakeholders.

risks.title: Resource constraints in service management and lack of DevOps/cloud expertise
risks.description: The service management team is already heavily loaded with other initiatives such as Hyper-V migration, and product engineering lacks DevOps and cloud engineering expertise required for AMS migration.
risks.impact_description: If resource constraints and skill gaps are not addressed, key migration tasks may be delayed, executed with errors, or deprioritized. This increases the likelihood of schedule slippage, quality issues, and operational instability post-migration.
risks.mitigation: Secure additional hands-on resources with relevant DevOps and cloud skills to support the migration. Rebalance workload across service management and product engineering, and clearly prioritize AMS-related work to ensure critical tasks receive adequate attention.

risks.title: PCI DSS compliance risk for AMS production environment
risks.description: Meeting PCI DSS and other compliance requirements for a hardened, secure, documented, and certified production environment may be challenging without dedicated resources and specialized expertise.
risks.impact_description: Failure to achieve PCI DSS-compliant production infrastructure could result in non-compliance with regulatory and corporate standards, potential audit findings, restrictions on processing payment-related or sensitive data, and delays in go-live or the need to re-architect environments post-migration.
risks.mitigation: Engage the ISRM team early and integrate security and compliance activities throughout the migration. Ensure dedicated security resources review architecture, configurations, and documentation, and that a formal compliance assessment is completed before production cutover.

risks.title: Ownership gap for application configuration in new AMS environment
risks.description: While infrastructure and data migration tasks have assigned owners in platform engineering and service management, there is no clear owner for configuring and securing the application in the new AMS environment. Product engineering and service management teams lack expertise in application configuration in cloud-native infrastructure.
risks.impact_description: Without a clear owner for application configuration, critical tasks such as configuring application settings, securing endpoints, and aligning configurations with compliance requirements may be delayed or overlooked. This can jeopardize the migration timeline, create security and compliance gaps, and delay production readiness.
risks.mitigation:
Current challenge at this stage is finalizing setup documentation and validation. The business unit requires a sandbox environment to proceed with rebuild and re-engineering activities. 
•	Next Action: Gordon/Monica is currently working to define the initial build requirements for the sandbox and to identify the relevant Platform Engineering team to assist BU with Application installation.

risks.title: Change in migration strategy from Azure to AMS may impact project completion timeline
risks.description: The decision to change the migration strategy from Azure to AMS for UFile Online introduces uncertainty and may impact the overall Montreal DC Exit project completion timeline (targeted around September 2026).
risks.impact_description: The change in strategy could cause setbacks in project timelines and deliverables, delays in task execution due to unclear ownership, increased risk of errors and inefficiencies during the migration, and miscommunication among stakeholders regarding responsibilities, ultimately threatening the September 2026 completion target.
risks.mitigation: A RACI review session will be held to realign roles and responsibilities in accordance with the updated AMS migration strategy. Subsequently, dedicated sessions will be conducted to establish milestones and timelines for each phase, as well as to identify and address early-stage challenges and risks.

risks.title: AMS currently supports the 2019 pattern and not the 2022 pattern
risks.description:
1.	SQL Version Compatibility Risk:
•	Current non-production environments are running SQL 2022, but AWS (AMS) only supports SQL 2019.
•	Per Elsa, downgrading databases from SQL 2022 to SQL 2019 is not feasible, creating a significant migration blocker.
•	If this compatibility issue is not resolved, it could delay migration, increase project complexity, or lead to unsupported production environments.
risks.impact_description:
DBA Architects (John Tracy/Debopriya) provided guidance during the recent planning call. Based on their input, an intake request was submitted to Asif Haliyal (Data Services). Asif's team is now assessing the required development and migration efforts, including testing and validation. Estimated completion in 1–2 weeks (by June 8).
•	Contingency Plan: If the Data Services team is delayed in delivering the 2022 SQL pattern (post 8th June), the project team will proceed with the SQL 2019 pattern for the Development environment.
risks.mitigation: Asif's Data Services team has begun work on the intake request and is currently assessing the development and migration efforts needed, including testing, building, and validation. ETA 2-3 weeks

risks.title: Environmental ambiguity between non-production and production in file management space
risks.description: There is ambiguity between non-production and production environments in the file management space, including shared file systems and mixed-use environments, which makes it unclear how to manage, migrate, and control files across environments.
risks.impact_description: If this ambiguity persists, file migration activities may be misconfigured or mis-scoped, production data might be exposed in non-production contexts, or critical files could be missed during migration. This may cause service disruptions, compliance issues, or require rework and could delay cutover and acceptance for AMS migration.
risks.mitigation: Clarify and document the environment classification and usage for all file shares, especially where production and non-production systems share infrastructure. Define clear responsibilities for file migration across dev, non-prod, and prod, including how real-time replication will be managed for production migrations, and track this ambiguity as a formal RAID item until resolved.

dependencies.title: Upgrading production SQL Server instances from version 2012 to a supported version is a mandatory prerequisite for migrating to Windows Server 2022 and the cloud environment to ensure compatibility and mitigate risks.
dependencies.description: The migration to Windows Server 2022 and the cloud environment is critically dependent on upgrading the current production SQL Server instances from version 2012 to a supported version (SQL Server 2017 or later). Microsoft does not support SQL Server 2012 on Windows Server 2022, making these upgrades a mandatory preparatory step to ensure compatibility and avoid risks during the migration process. Production systems, including SQL 5, SQL 6, SQL 1, and SQL 2, must be upgraded prior to the migration, as well as the remaining pre-production reporting server.
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: A delay in the AMS migration scheduled for September 2026 will impact the overall project timeline, resulting in a subsequent delay of the final major milestone—the Dilapidation and Data Center Shutdown activities planned for Q4 2026.
dependencies.mitigation:
Mitigation Plan: Separate Upgrade Phase: Perform SQL Server upgrades as a distinct preparatory phase before the cloud migration to minimize risks and ensure compatibility with Windows Server 2022.
Documented Timeline: Create a detailed schedule and timeline for SQL Server upgrades, allocating sufficient time for planning, execution, and validation of the upgraded systems.
Risk Mitigation: Include contingency plans in the migration documentation to address potential issues during the upgrade and migration process.
Alignment on Timing: Collaborate across teams to align the timing and processes for upgrades and migration, ensuring a smooth transition to the cloud environment.
Ownership Assignment: Designate responsible team members to oversee the upgrade process, document the migration plan, and ensure accountability for meeting deadlines and addressing concerns.
Validation and Testing: Thoroughly test upgraded SQL Server instances in the pre-production environment to ensure stability and performance before implementing changes in production systems.

dependencies.title: Critical Architecture Design Milestone Drives Montreal DC Exit Success
dependencies.description:
The Architecture Design milestone is a key planning phase in the Montreal DC Exit project. It involves defining and documenting the technical architecture required to support the migration process, as well as ensuring compliance with security and operational standards. The milestone includes the following critical requirements:

Network Topology: Creating a detailed diagram of the network architecture to ensure connectivity and security during and after the migration process.
IAM Roles: Defining Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles to ensure proper permissions and secure access control for users and systems.
IIS Permissions: Establishing permissions for Internet Information Services (IIS) to support secure hosting and application functionality.
Database Migrations: Planning and documenting the movement of databases to new environments while maintaining data integrity and security.
Connected Environments: Ensuring that all interconnected systems and environments are properly accounted for and integrated in the new architecture.

The milestone deadline of May 20 has passed, and CSA (Cloud Solutions Architects, including @Toxtli and Monica/@Aitchison, Gordon) are currently focusing on these critical requirements. These efforts are essential for Rob's PCI DSS compliance review, which ensures the migration aligns with strict security standards for handling sensitive payment card data.
dependencies.dependent_on: BU Compliance Checklist
dependencies.impact_if_delayed:
Compliance Assurance: The architecture design directly impacts the ability to meet PCI DSS requirements. Failure to address critical requirements could delay the compliance review and potentially compromise the security of sensitive data.

Operational Continuity: A well-designed architecture ensures seamless migration with minimal disruption to systems and services. Poor planning could lead to outages, data loss, or performance degradation.

Risk Mitigation: Proper documentation and planning reduce risks associated with the migration, including security vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and integration challenges.

Project Timeline: Delays in completing the architecture design milestone could push back subsequent phases of the Montreal DC Exit, impacting the overall timeline and deliverables.

Stakeholder Confidence: Completing the milestone on time and meeting critical requirements builds confidence among stakeholders (e.g., Rob, CSA team, and
dependencies.mitigation: CSA ( @Toxtli, Monica/ @Aitchison, Gordon) are currently focused on critical requirements, including the architecture diagram (network topology, IAM roles, IIS permissions, database migrations, and connected environments) necessary for Rob’s PCI DSS compliance review.

entities.name: FedRAMP - CIAM Product Onboarding
entities.okrs:
Objective 1: Enable FedRAMP compliant customer access through a scalable CIAM foundation
Key Results
•	KR1: Deploy and operate a federation only Azure B2C CIAM solution approved for use within the FedRAMP authorization boundary. 
•	KR2: Establish standardized CIAM onboarding patterns and runbooks to support continued FedRAMP product adoption beyond the initial priority set. 
Objective 2: Complete CIAM onboarding for all priority FedRAMP products by June 30, 2026
Key Results
•	KR3: Onboard 100% of identified priority products in Non Prod to the FedRAMP CIAM solution. 
•	KR4: Onboard 100% of identified priority products in Prod by June 30, 2026, with no CIAM driven delays to authorization or customer readiness.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

FedRAMP – CIAM Product Onboarding is delivering a FedRAMP-compliant customer identity and access management foundation on federation-only Azure B2C to support secure onboarding of priority products in Non-Prod and Prod. This enables compliant, scalable access for U.S. government and regulated customers and provides a reusable pattern for future FedRAMP product adoption across Thomson Reuters.

As of 15 May 2026, 10 of 11 priority products are onboarded to CIAM in Non-Prod (91%) and 9 of 11 in Prod (82%), driving overall onboarding completeness of 86% against a 100% target by 30 Jun 2026. Key delivery milestones, including Non-Prod onboarding completion on 30 May 2026 and Prod onboarding completion on 30 Jun 2026, remain reported as tracking to plan, while the Azure B2C resiliency proof of concept is in progress toward a 19 Jun 2026 target.

Overall status is Green, driven by remaining Non-Prod and Prod onboarding and the Azure B2C resiliency proof of concept all tracking to their 30 Jun 2026 and 19 Jun 2026 target dates with no reported schedule variance.

## Path to Green

The top risk is Azure B2C outage recovery and disaster recovery, which is being mitigated by completing the resiliency proof of concept by 19 Jun 2026 and incorporating Microsoft resiliency guidance so that FedRAMP CIAM no longer relies on an unmitigated single point of failure.

## Milestones

- Complete onboarding of all 11 priority products in the Non-Prod environment by 30 May 2026, up from 10 of 11 products (91%) as of 15 May 2026.  
- Complete onboarding of all 11 priority products in the Prod environment and finish overall CIAM FedRAMP product onboarding delivery by 30 Jun 2026, up from 9 of 11 products (82%) and 86% overall completeness as of 15 May 2026.  
- Complete the Azure B2C resiliency proof of concept for outage recovery and disaster recovery by 19 Jun 2026.  
- Resolve SSP non-prod integration issues and restore SSP integration status to Complete by 30 Jun 2026.  
- Formally close the FedRAMP – CIAM Product Onboarding project, including documentation and handover, by 30 Jun 2026.

risks.title: Business reaction risk to revised customer-ready timeline
risks.description: The business may react negatively to the revised customer-ready timeline for FedRAMP CIAM onboarding.
risks.impact_description: If business stakeholders react poorly to the revised customer-ready timeline, it could create pressure to compress scope or timelines, drive unplanned work, or erode confidence in the FedRAMP CIAM program.
risks.mitigation: Communicate clearly that migrations are expected to start right after 3PAO audit approval (targeted for end of January), and share the team’s ETA of February 24, 2026 with Westlaw/Practical Law and other stakeholders, ensuring concerns are addressed proactively. Per the RAID log entry dated 2025-11-20, the team met with the Westlaw/Practical Law team on 2025-11-18, communicated the 2026-02-24 ETA, and received no negative reaction; stakeholders indicated that selling FedRAMP for those products would likely start around Q3.

risks.title: Risk of not completing onboarding by February 24
risks.description: There are significant risks to meeting the customer onboarding timeline (February 24) due to unforeseen engineering challenges, resource allocation issues, and the need for updated estimates.
risks.impact_description: If onboarding is not completed by February 24, customer onboarding will be delayed, potentially impacting commercial commitments, audit readiness, and the broader FedRAMP rollout schedule.
risks.mitigation: Review and refine scope and estimates, then mitigate by potentially reducing scope for the customer-ready timeline and ensuring the risk is visible at the program level. Communicate the mitigation plan and updated dates to stakeholders and plug the risk into the appropriate program-level tracker. The RAID log documents follow-up actions including Harvarinder finalizing a mitigation plan involving scope reduction and Alyssa ensuring the risk was tracked at the program level; the risk has since been closed with implementation of the agreed mitigation.

risks.title: LTS database migration risk
risks.description: LTS database migration work may not complete on time, impacting users and CIAM FedRAMP readiness.
risks.impact_description: If the LTS database migration does not complete successfully and on time (for both Non-Prod and Prod), related CIAM integrations and dependent services may be unavailable or unstable, delaying onboarding, increasing operational risk, and potentially impacting audit readiness.
risks.mitigation: Complete LTS database migration for Non-Prod and Prod, track progress and blockers via the dev team group chat, and provide regular updates. According to the RAID log, Non-Prod migration completed first, remaining blockers for Prod were resolved, and the overall LTS database migration was completed by 2026-02-26.

risks.title: Risk of not being customer ready by January 31 due to story sizing and outstanding requirements
risks.description: Based on the sizing of stories and some outstanding requirements, it is very likely that the program will not be customer ready by January 31 for FedRAMP CIAM onboarding.
risks.impact_description: If customer-ready status is not achieved by January 31, customer onboarding timelines will slip, potentially impacting commitments made to stakeholders and compressing time available for testing, audit preparation, and operational readiness.
risks.mitigation: Refine user stories, solidify estimates, and communicate revised dates (moving the customer-ready target to February 28) to stakeholders so expectations and downstream plans can be adjusted. Per the RAID log, refinement of stories was completed and the new ETA of 2025-02-28 was communicated on 2025-10-06.

risks.title: Impact from onboarding new FTE resources replacing contractors
risks.description: Moving from contractors to FTEs may impact CIAM FedRAMP delivery as new resources are onboarded.
risks.impact_description: If onboarding of new FTE resources is slower than expected or they require extended ramp-up time, velocity on CIAM FedRAMP engineering work could drop, impacting delivery timelines and quality.
risks.mitigation: Onboard new resources onto the Kappa/Iota teams, actively monitor the impact, and adjust assignments as needed. Per the RAID log, the risk level was reduced from Medium to Low, hiring and releasing were in progress, and one additional resource hire was being monitored as of early January; ongoing monitoring ultimately supported closure of the risk.

risks.title: Non-prod Plexus cluster readiness may miss September 15 deadline
risks.description: If the non-prod Plexus cluster is not fully operational by September 15, the program is likely to miss the January 31 customer-ready milestone for FedRAMP CIAM onboarding.
risks.impact_description: Missing the September 15 readiness date for the non-prod Plexus cluster would delay downstream SRE and product onboarding work, putting the January 31 customer-ready milestone at risk and potentially delaying overall FedRAMP CIAM onboarding timelines.
risks.mitigation: Fix the connectivity issue and get the non-prod Plexus cluster fully functional, working with Plexus, Tech M, and Landing Zone teams to debug API endpoint access from commercial Zscaler to use1. This work was executed without stopping SRE progress, and the non-prod cluster was completed on September 22.

risks.title: Permit to Operate (PtO) may not be obtained before key resource vacation
risks.description: If the Permit to Operate is not obtained before Chris goes on vacation, the CIAM FedRAMP timeline may be impacted.
risks.impact_description: Failure to obtain PtO before a key engineering resource’s vacation could delay environment readiness and associated onboarding tasks, potentially impacting critical milestones for FedRAMP CIAM delivery.
risks.mitigation: Finalize the CIAM FedRAMP architecture, ensure the low environment is functional, and obtain ISRM approval in time to secure the Permit to Operate (PtO) before the vacation period. According to the RAID log, the PtO for Production was completed by the 2025-11-07 due date, eliminating the risk prior to the vacation window.

risks.title: Westlaw / Practical Law reg key validator certificate and connectivity issue
risks.description: After fixing a firewall product issue, requests from CIAM to Westlaw and Practical Law began failing because their reg key validator domains were not added to TLS certificates, creating a blocking dependency on those teams to update their certificates and resolve SSL errors.
risks.impact_description: If Westlaw and Practical Law do not update their certificates and resolve reg key validator connectivity issues, CIAM FedRAMP integrations that rely on these validators will continue to experience SSL failures, blocking testing and production use, and delaying onboarding timelines for Westlaw, Practical Law, and related CLEAR flows.
risks.mitigation: Coordinate with Westlaw, Practical Law, and CLEAR teams to update certificates with required reg key validator domains and resolve connectivity issues, track progress via the FedRAMP Weekly CIAM Connect chat, and test across QED and Prod. Per the RAID log updates, the Westlaw and Practical Law certificate issues were resolved in Production first (with QED following), CLEAR deployments were coordinated, and by mid-April Chris confirmed that the WL/PL reg key validator issue was complete, allowing the risk to be closed.

risks.title: SAP / Audit account usage for internal testing

risks.impact_description: If the SAP audit account cannot be reused for internal testing, or if the decision and process are delayed, testing activities that depend on this account could be blocked or slowed, impacting schedule for validating CIAM FedRAMP scenarios that rely on SAP access.
risks.mitigation: Check with broader program management whether the audit account can be repurposed for internal testing and identify the appropriate contact(s) to assist with approvals and configuration. Adjust testing plans depending on the outcome.

risks.title: CLEAR reg key validator connectivity and availability
risks.description: CLEAR reg key validator endpoints are required for CIAM FedRAMP lower environment work, but connectivity and behavior are still being validated, with issues on CIAM’s side and dependencies on CLEAR deployments.
risks.impact_description: If CLEAR’s reg key validator endpoints are not fully functional and validated in lower and production environments, CIAM cannot reliably call these endpoints, blocking or delaying CLEAR-related onboarding flows and impacting the ability to meet CIAM FedRAMP onboarding timelines involving CLEAR.
risks.mitigation: Coordinate with CLEAR to confirm reg key validator availability in QA and Prod, test and resolve connectivity issues from CIAM, and address concerns raised by CLEAR (e.g., via Doug). Track progress with regular follow-ups, especially around February–April (including confirming Prod deployment and subsequent testing).

risks.title: Outage Recovery / Disaster Recovery strategy for Azure B2C single point of failure
risks.description: Current FedRAMP CIAM architecture has a single point of failure in Azure B2C, with no fully validated fallback during major Azure or AWS outages. An outage on October 29 highlighted limitations, and resolution depends on Microsoft guidance and an internal resiliency proof of concept focused on outage recovery and disaster recovery for Azure B2C.
risks.impact_description: If a major Azure or AWS outage occurs before a robust outage recovery / DR strategy is implemented and validated for Azure B2C, CIAM services for FedRAMP products could become unavailable, causing authentication failures for government and regulated customers, jeopardizing SLAs, damaging stakeholder confidence, and potentially impacting FedRAMP compliance posture.

risk_owner.name: Christopher Yip, Mohith Sai Krishna Katakam, and Tom Murphy

risks.mitigation: Work with Microsoft to obtain clear resiliency guidance and root cause information for past outages; evaluate Azure Front Door and related components as potential single points of failure; pursue an exception request (e.g., application gateway with B2C) where appropriate; and execute an internal resiliency proof-of-concept focused on outage recovery and DR. As of the sprint starting 2026-05-20, outage recovery work is in active development, with Devarshi leading execution and engineering support provided (including targeted support from Christopher to address dev questions). The plan is to complete the internal Azure B2C resiliency proof of concept by end May / early June so that the FedRAMP CIAM architecture no longer relies on an unmitigated single point of failure.

assumptions.title: No incremental commercial funding; costs managed within approved EPC allocation
assumptions.description: The CIAM FedRAMP Product Onboarding project assumes that required funding will be covered by TR Technology EPC funding for FY 2026, and that no incremental commercial funding will be needed, with all costs managed within the approved EPC allocation.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The Charter specifies that funding comes from TR Technology EPC funding (FY 2026) and explicitly states that no incremental commercial funding is assumed, with costs to be managed within the approved EPC allocation.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Current planning indicates that the EPC allocation covers all known project components (engineering, compliance, infrastructure, onboarding, audit, remediation). There are no stated requirements for commercial funding at this time, and scope is being managed within the approved budget envelope.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If EPC funding proves insufficient, raise an escalation through governance to either: (1) request incremental funding, or (2) reduce or phase scope (e.g., defer lower-priority product integrations or non-critical enhancements) to stay within the approved budget.
assumptions.validation_method: Ongoing comparison of actual and forecast project costs against the approved EPC budget, with finance and program reviews to confirm sufficiency of the allocation.

assumptions.title: Onboarding tracking will focus on product onboarding, not customer onboarding
assumptions.description: The project assumes that tracking and reporting for CIAM FedRAMP onboarding will focus on product onboarding only (Non-Prod and Prod), not customer onboarding, unless explicitly requested for initial customers.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The Charter states that Harv and Alyssa agreed to track product onboarding only (not customer onboarding) unless explicitly requested for initial customers, and that Harv will align with Liat to ensure stakeholder consensus.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The agreement between program management leads and key product stakeholders is documented in the Charter, and current scope and milestones are framed around product onboarding completion. No conflicting requirements for customer onboarding tracking have been documented yet.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If stakeholders request broader tracking to include customer onboarding, formalize a scope and reporting change: define additional metrics, timelines, and owners for customer onboarding, and adjust the project plan and resourcing accordingly rather than treating these items as implicit obligations.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm in governance and stakeholder meetings (including with Liat and product stakeholders) that reporting continues to be based on product onboarding, and document any exceptions where customer onboarding tracking is explicitly requested.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

FedRAMP – CoCounsel is extending Thomson Reuters’ existing FedRAMP Moderate authorization to onboard CoCounsel into compliant PreProd and Prod environments in East and West regions. This enables secure, audited use of CoCounsel by U.S. government and regulated customers, unlocking access to regulated markets while maintaining continuous FedRAMP compliance.

Core platform delivery is substantially complete, with 4 of 4 FedRAMP CoCounsel environments built and validated (100% completion, 16 days ahead of plan) and 5 of 5 key integrations (Plexus, Cumulus, Cloudflare, DNSSEC, LLM provisioning) delivered as of 19 Dec 2025. Audit readiness is partially complete, with ServiceNow GovCloud inventory coverage at roughly 50% against a 100% target and the ServiceNow Integration & 3PAO Audit milestone slipping from a 30 May 2026 plan to a latest estimate of 05 Jun 2026.

Overall status is AMBER, driven by incomplete and unstable ServiceNow GovCloud discovery and inventory integration that is limiting audit-ready evidence for the 3PAO and FedRAMP authorization.

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on completing and stabilizing ServiceNow GovCloud discovery and CMDB integration by driving vendor working sessions to resolve AWS GovCloud asset discovery and tagging, then regenerating and validating full inventory evidence for the 3PAO audit. Until automated discovery is reliable, the team will maintain a controlled manual inventory workaround so that audit artifacts can be finalized without further delaying authorization.

## Milestones

- Complete Project Kickoff and establish governance by 31 Mar 2025.
- Build and validate all FedRAMP CoCounsel non-production and production environments in East and West regions by 2025-11-30, achieving 4 of 4 environments live and validated by 14 Nov 2025.
- Complete Plexus, Cumulus, Cloudflare, LLM, and DNSSEC integrations across FedRAMP environments by 31 Dec 2025, with all 5 required integrations delivered by 19 Dec 2025.
- Complete ServiceNow GovCloud inventory integration and produce audit-ready evidence for the 3PAO audit by 2026-06-05.
- Achieve FedRAMP Moderate authorization extension for CoCounsel and complete project closure activities by 2026-06-30.

risks.title: IaC deployer feature gaps in Cumulus
risks.description: The Cumulus infrastructure-as-code (IaC) deployer lacked feature parity and was not in sync with current source code changes, forcing manual infrastructure provisioning.
risks.impact_description: If the IaC deployer remains incomplete, CoCounsel FedRAMP infrastructure will have to be provisioned manually or via ad hoc scripts, which increases risk of configuration drift, security misconfigurations, and delays in environment creation.
risks.mitigation: Define the required IaC deployer capabilities for CoCounsel, implement missing features with support from the Cumulus/DOE team, and update pipelines so infrastructure can be provisioned consistently through Cumulus in GovCloud.

risks.title: Blue / Green deployer approval delays
risks.description: Cumulus blue/green deployments can fail if the "green" approval is delayed, causing deployment failures and requiring re-runs.
risks.impact_description: If blue/green deployments fail when approvals are delayed, production and pre-production releases for CoCounsel and related services could be slowed, result in additional manual effort to re-run pipelines, and increase the chance of deployment errors or missed release windows.
risks.mitigation: Identify and fix the blue/green deployer behavior so that delayed approvals do not cause deployment failures; deliver the fix via an updated Cumulus version and validate with CoCounsel pipelines before general use.

risks.title: Difficulty troubleshooting Cumulus installations due to incomplete logging
risks.description: Logging for Cumulus installations and pipeline creations with multiple assets can be lost or is hard to locate, making it difficult to troubleshoot failed installations.
risks.impact_description: If installation and pipeline logs remain hard to access or incomplete, teams may not be able to diagnose failed Cumulus deployments quickly, causing extended outage or delay in bringing CoCounsel pipelines online and increasing support overhead.
risks.mitigation: Work with the CICD team to improve log availability: adjust logging so installation and pipeline creation events are captured reliably, and provide solution guidance (including using single-asset installs where appropriate) so consumers can access logs needed for troubleshooting.

risks.title: Cumulus installation on Prod CI/CD account 386694349529
risks.description: Cumulus was not yet installed on the critical production CI/CD account (386694349529), blocking automated deployments for CoCounsel.
risks.impact_description: If Cumulus is not installed and available on the production CI/CD account, CoCounsel and related FedRAMP workloads cannot use the standard CPI/Cumulus deployment model, forcing manual deployments or ad hoc automation and increasing risk to release quality and timelines.
risks.mitigation: Plan and execute the installation of Cumulus on the Prod CI/CD account 386694349529, validate pipeline operation, and hand over to consuming teams for production use.

risks.title: Cumulus CPI inflation runs assets sequentially instead of in parallel
risks.description: The CPI inflation process runs multiple assets sequentially rather than in parallel, extending execution time by several minutes per run.
risks.impact_description: If CPI inflation continues to process assets sequentially, pipeline runs will be slower than expected, marginally increasing deployment lead time and reducing efficiency, though without directly blocking CoCounsel releases.
risks.mitigation: Review the CPI inflation design and either accept the sequential behavior as non-blocking or adjust the implementation; agree with stakeholders that no change is required if the added time is acceptable.

risks.title: Helm deployer feature gaps in Cumulus
risks.description: The Cumulus Helm deployer lacked feature parity and was not in sync with current source code changes, requiring services to be deployed manually and halting some Cumulus adoption.
risks.impact_description: If the Helm deployer does not support the required features and current source patterns, CoCounsel services that depend on Helm charts cannot be deployed through Cumulus pipelines, leading to manual deployments, higher operational risk, and slower delivery.
risks.mitigation: Have Chetan’s engineering team work with the Cumulus/DOE team to define required Helm deployer capabilities, implement missing features, and remove blockers so Helm-based services can be deployed via Cumulus in GovCloud.

risks.title: Cumulus UI dashboard Lambda failure on null deployment status
risks.description: The Cumulus UI dashboard Lambda fails when a deployment record has a null status message, causing the dashboard to error and preventing blue/green deployment approvals via the UI.
risks.impact_description: If the dashboard Lambda continues to fail on null status values, teams cannot reliably use the Cumulus UI for blue/green deployment approvals, which may force manual workarounds and delay releases for CoCounsel FedRAMP environments.
risks.mitigation: Fix the dashboard Lambda to safely handle deployments with null status messages, release the updated Cumulus UI version, and verify that blue/green approvals work without error for GovCloud pipelines.

risks.title: Incorrect GovCloud pipeline links in Cumulus UI dashboard
risks.description: GovCloud pipeline links shown in the Cumulus UI dashboard used the wrong host, requiring users to manually navigate to the correct pipelines.
risks.impact_description: If GovCloud pipeline links remain incorrect, it is harder for teams to navigate from the dashboard to the underlying pipelines, slowing troubleshooting and increasing friction in managing CoCounsel FedRAMP deployments.
risks.mitigation: Update the Cumulus UI dashboard to generate correct GovCloud pipeline URLs and release the fix (v1.32.1) to all relevant environments.

risks.title: Cumulus multi-region support blocker
risks.description: A Cumulus defect blocked correct operation of multi-region pipelines needed for CoCounsel and related workloads.
risks.impact_description: If the Cumulus multi-region blocker is not fixed, CoCounsel may be unable to use a single Cumulus-based pattern to deploy to multiple GovCloud regions (e.g., East and West), leading to duplicated effort, inconsistent deployments, and higher operational risk.
risks.mitigation: Implement and validate a Cumulus fix for the multi-region blocker and roll it out to GovCloud environments used by CoCounsel, confirming that multi-region pipelines behave correctly.

risks.title: Cloudflare ingress blocked by Cumulus deployspec for Terraform
risks.description: The cumulus-deployspec-cloudflare (Terraform) implementation blocked creation of required public ingress (incoming calls) for CoCounsel and CARI services.
risks.impact_description: If the Cloudflare deployspec for Terraform cannot provision the necessary public ingress, CoCounsel and CARI services may not be reachable via Cloudflare in the FedRAMP environment, delaying go-live and creating security and availability risks.
risks.mitigation: Work through Engagement 454277 to debug and fix the Cloudflare Terraform deployer so it can successfully create required Cloudflare resources and public ingress; validate with CoCounsel pipelines before closing.

risks.title: EKS deployer feature gaps in Cumulus
risks.description: The Cumulus EKS deployer lacked feature parity with source code changes, forcing manual deployment of EKS-based services and temporarily halting some Cumulus usage.
risks.impact_description: If the EKS deployer remains incomplete, CoCounsel services running on EKS in GovCloud cannot rely on Cumulus pipelines for deployment, increasing the need for manual steps and risking deployment errors or delays.
risks.mitigation: Have Chetan’s engineering team, with DOE support, implement the required EKS deployer features, remove identified blockers, and validate deployments for CoCounsel EKS workloads in GovCloud.

risks.title: Terraform deployer feature gaps in Cumulus
risks.description: The Cumulus Terraform deployer lacked feature parity with current infrastructure definitions, requiring teams to automate Terraform deployments outside Cumulus (e.g., via GitHub Actions).
risks.impact_description: If the Terraform deployer is not brought up to feature parity, CoCounsel infrastructure deployments will continue to rely on external automation, leading to fragmented deployment tooling, more complex operations, and higher risk of misconfiguration.
risks.mitigation: Extend the Cumulus Terraform deployer to support the required Terraform workflows for CoCounsel, align it with current infrastructure code, and transition from ad hoc GitHub Actions automation back into Cumulus-managed deployments where appropriate.

risks.title: ServiceNow GovCloud setup and inventory integration stability
risks.description: Ongoing issues with the ServiceNow GovCloud setup, including asset discovery challenges, vendor engagement, and asset tagging; a manual workaround is currently in place. Discovery for FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts is still not functioning as expected, requiring repeated vendor cases and engineering access changes.
risks.impact_description: If ServiceNow GovCloud setup and inventory integration issues are not resolved, automated asset discovery and tagging will remain unreliable, forcing continued manual workarounds and risking incomplete or inaccurate inventory data needed to support FedRAMP operational monitoring and audit requirements for CoCounsel. This could create audit findings, delay audit readiness closure, and jeopardize the overall authorization and project-closure timeline.
risks.mitigation: Drive FedRAMP ServiceNow GovCloud discovery via workaround: maintain AWS GovCloud discovery, track vendor cases, enable access for ServiceNow engineers, run joint working sessions, and iteratively tune until assets are reliably discovered/tagged. Following the Apr 30 session, schedule a live troubleshooting call with ServiceNow (Marshall), AWS (Ervan), and internal engineering (Prudhvi Yaswanth Kolluru) to review logs, resolve sub‑account discovery gaps, and address CMDB issues in real time.

actions.title: Complete ServiceNow GovCloud inventory integration for FedRAMP CoCounsel
actions.description: Drive completion of the ServiceNow GovCloud setup and inventory integration required for FedRAMP audit readiness, coordinating with the vendor and internal engineers until the integration is fully working and evidence is available for auditors.

actions.title: Schedule joint troubleshooting call with ServiceNow vendor, AWS (Ervan), and internal ServiceNow/FedRAMP teams
actions.description: Schedule a joint troubleshooting meeting for FedRAMP ServiceNow GovCloud discovery involving ServiceNow vendor engineer Marshall, AWS team representative Ervan, the internal ServiceNow core team, and project stakeholders to review discovery logs and understand why discovery is only occurring at the master account level and not at sub-account level.

assumptions.title: Most Westlake FedRAMP work is reusable for CoCounsel FedRAMP environments
assumptions.description: Project planning assumes that most of the work delivered for the Westlake FedRAMP implementation can be leveraged to onboard CoCounsel into the FedRAMP environment, with only some new components required.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The project is described as an extension of the broader FedRAMP program that has been running for almost two years, and the charter explicitly states that most of the work delivered for Westlake is expected to be leveraged.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The broader FedRAMP program has already implemented compliant infrastructure, controls, and patterns for Westlake within the same authorization boundary. Because CoCounsel is being added to this existing boundary and environment, it is reasonable to expect that networking, security controls, monitoring, and many platform components can be reused, needing only incremental extensions or configuration changes rather than net‑new designs.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If reuse proves limited, re‑baseline the implementation plan and budget to include additional engineering work, prioritize critical capabilities necessary for FedRAMP readiness, and potentially phase lower‑priority features into subsequent change packets.
assumptions.validation_method: Architecture and design reviews comparing Westlake components to CoCounsel requirements; detailed gap analysis and implementation planning.

validation_owner.name: Lead solution architect for FedRAMP CoCounsel

assumptions.title: Allocated $1M capital budget is sufficient for FedRAMP CoCounsel build work
assumptions.description: The project assumes that the $1 million capital budget allocated by finance will be sufficient to cover platform, engineering, and science work required to onboard CoCounsel into the FedRAMP environment, despite the originally assumed May start no longer being feasible.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Rough estimates for FTEs and contractors are around $750K, which is well within the allocated $1M capital budget, providing apparent headroom for variation.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The charter cites an initial estimate of $750K for FTEs and contractors versus a $1M allocation, creating a 25%+ buffer for unanticipated needs. While the May start date is no longer feasible, the underlying scope and complexity are not indicated to have substantially changed, so it is reasonable to assume the total capital requirement will remain within the approved envelope, at least until more detailed plans suggest otherwise.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If forecasts indicate the capital budget will be exceeded, prepare a change request and business justification for additional funds, or adjust scope and phasing to keep critical FedRAMP readiness work within the existing budget while deferring non‑essential features to a later packet.
assumptions.validation_method: Refined bottom‑up estimation and periodic re‑forecasting of engineering and contractor effort against actuals, reviewed with finance.

validation_owner.name: Project manager / finance partner for FedRAMP CoCounsel

assumptions.title: FedRAMP cadence and lessons learned from Packet #1 will reduce delivery and audit risk for CoCounsel
assumptions.description: Project planning assumes that aligning execution sequencing with the established FedRAMP cadence and leveraging lessons learned from Packet #1 will materially reduce delivery and audit risk for the CoCounsel FedRAMP extension.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The charter explicitly states that execution sequencing aligns with the established FedRAMP cadence and leverages lessons learned from Packet #1 to reduce delivery and audit risk.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Having already executed FedRAMP work and a prior change packet, the team understands the expectations of 3PAO auditors and the FedRAMP PMO, common pitfalls, and realistic lead times. Using this lived experience to drive the CoCounsel schedule, scope sequencing, and artifact preparation should, in principle, lower the likelihood and severity of surprises, provided the regulatory context and core architecture remain similar.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If execution or audit activities show similar levels of risk or findings as earlier packets, adjust the plan by adding intermediate readiness assessments, dedicating additional compliance and security resources, and re‑sequencing or de‑scoping lower‑priority items to protect critical authorization milestones.
assumptions.validation_method: Retrospectives and planning sessions mapping Packet #1 outcomes and issues to the CoCounsel plan; early checkpoints during execution and pre‑audit readiness reviews to confirm reduced issues compared to earlier packets.

assumptions.title: ServiceNow GovCloud discovery configuration proven on one AWS GovCloud account will be reusable for all FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts
assumptions.description: Planning assumes that once the ServiceNow cloud discovery process for FedRAMP AWS GovCloud is successfully configured and validated on one AWS GovCloud account, the same configuration and process can be cascaded to the remaining FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts without requiring materially different patterns per account.
assumptions.rationale_basis: During the April 30, 2026 "FedRAMP SNOW - Cloud Discovery - GovCloud" meeting, the team stated that they will only cascade the configuration to remaining FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts after seeing a successful discovery scenario for one account, implying an expectation that the discovery pattern is reusable across accounts.
assumptions.validity_explanation: All FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts are being onboarded into the same ServiceNow GovCloud instance using common discovery patterns. The primary current issue is with discovery not reaching child/sub-account levels on the first account; once this routing and pattern issue is understood and resolved collaboratively with ServiceNow and AWS, the underlying mechanism should function similarly for other accounts in the same environment, making reuse reasonable but not yet proven.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If reuse proves unreliable and each FedRAMP AWS GovCloud account requires unique discovery adjustments, replan the work to include per-account configuration and testing, prioritize accounts that are in scope for near-term FedRAMP audit, and consider temporary supplemental approaches (e.g., scripted exports or manual CMDB updates) for lower-priority accounts until discovery patterns are stabilized.
assumptions.validation_method: First achieve a fully successful discovery run (including child/sub-account coverage) on the initial FedRAMP AWS GovCloud account, then apply the same configuration to additional FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts and compare discovery results and logs to confirm that configuration is reusable without per-account customization.

dependencies.title: ServiceNow GovCloud inventory integration for asset discovery and tagging
dependencies.description: Completion and stabilization of the ServiceNow GovCloud inventory integration, including reliable asset discovery and tagging for FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts, is required to provide accurate configuration and asset data for FedRAMP operational monitoring and audit of CoCounsel.
dependencies.dependent_on: ServiceNow vendor engineering support and internal ServiceNow platform engineers
dependencies.consumer: FedRAMP CoCounsel audit readiness and ServiceNow Integration & 3PAO Audit milestone
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If the ServiceNow GovCloud inventory integration is not fully working by the audit readiness target, automated asset discovery and tagging for FedRAMP CoCounsel environments will remain unreliable, forcing continued manual workarounds and risking incomplete or inaccurate inventory data for 3PAO and FedRAMP PMO audit reviews.
dependencies.mitigation: Maintain a manual inventory workaround while coordinating with ServiceNow vendor engineers via support cases and working sessions; grant required table access to engineers; iterate on configuration based on test results until GovCloud asset discovery and tagging are stable.

dependencies.title: Production monitoring verification dependent on CoCounsel production deployment
dependencies.description: Verification of production monitoring for CoCounsel in Prod East and Prod West is dependent on the CoCounsel team deploying services into the FedRAMP production environments so that monitoring, alerts, and dashboards can be exercised and evidence collected for continuous monitoring.
dependencies.dependent_on: CoCounsel production deployments in AWS GovCloud Prod East and Prod West
dependencies.consumer: FedRAMP CoCounsel continuous monitoring evidence and Audit Readiness milestone
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If CoCounsel production deployments or monitoring verification are delayed, the project may lack sufficient production monitoring evidence for FedRAMP continuous monitoring, potentially delaying final authorization and project closure.
dependencies.mitigation: Coordinate deployment and monitoring verification windows between the CoCounsel engineering team and SRE/Service Management; if necessary, use targeted test deployments and synthetic traffic in production to generate monitoring events and evidence ahead of full customer rollout.

decisions.title: Use GitHub Actions as temporary CI/CD solution for Cloudflare deployments until Cumulus is ready
decisions.description: Adopt GitHub Actions, authenticated to AWS via OpenID Connect or access/secret keys, as a temporary CI/CD mechanism for Cloudflare-related infrastructure (including updating Cloudflare API tokens and deploying Cloudflare resources) while Cumulus deployer features are being completed and stabilized for GovCloud.
decisions.rationale: To keep CoCounsel FedRAMP delivery on track and avoid blocking Cloudflare work on unresolved Cumulus deployer and CPI issues, the team needed a short-term CI/CD approach that could be implemented quickly and independently of Cumulus releases.
decisions.options_considered: 1) Pause Cloudflare deployments until Cumulus deployers were fully feature-complete and stable; 2) Build an alternative CI/CD solution using GitHub Actions with temporary Cloudflare API token configuration; 3) Attempt manual Cloudflare configuration without automation.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

LatAm Top of Funnel Migration is delivering a unified Salesforce platform for the LatAm sales organization, leveraging Lightning and AI to improve sales efficiency, data integrity, leadership visibility, and customer engagement across the end-to-end lifecycle. This migration will consolidate fragmented sales tools into a single enterprise-aligned platform for future growth.

Steering Committee governance and cadence are 100% defined, while 70% of migration phasing options are confirmed against a 100% target by 14 Jun 2026. Key scope and wave decisions for Chile, Brazil, Peru, and Mexico were taken between 26 May 2026 and 29 May 2026, locking the initial Chile wave for an October 2026 go-live.

Overall status is Green, driven by early confirmation of Chile as the first October 2026 go-live wave, which anchors scope and schedule.

## Path to Green

The primary mitigation focus is on data readiness and ECM capacity, with targeted profiling, dependency management, and ECM resourcing actions completing by 12 Jun 2026 to protect the Q3–Q4 build and migration window.

## Milestones

- Scope, Migration Option and Governance Confirmed by 14 Jun 2026, increasing migration phasing confirmation from 70% to 100%.
- Architecture and High-Level Design (Top-of-Funnel) Approved by 05 Jul 2026, providing an agreed target-state architecture and account/data model baseline.
- Data Readiness and Prerequisites Complete and Build and Configuration Complete by 25 Sep 2026 and 22 Sep 2026 respectively, enabling safe progression to migration and testing.
- Data Migration and End-to-End Validation Complete with UAT Signed Off by 10 Oct 2026, supporting LATAM Business Go-Live for the Chile wave on 14 Oct 2026.
- Program closure and transition to steady-state support by 30 Nov 2026.

risks.title: Technology / Systems - Account & Data Model Misalignment (S2E vs GSI / ECM)
risks.description: LATAM S2E account hierarchy differs from GSI/ECM (gold account vs SSD/location model). Incorrect mapping may lead to duplicate accounts, orphaned records, and inconsistent reporting.
risks.impact_description: Poor data integrity, reduced user confidence, increased remediation effort post go‑live, long‑term technical debt.
risks.mitigation: Confirm target account hierarchy for LATAM; validate ECM segmentation and SSD usage; agree migration mapping rules before HLD sign‑off.

risks.title: Operations / Business Process - Service & Back‑Office Dependency on S2E
risks.description: Service, renewals, and back‑office processes remain dependent on S2E. Moving sales/opportunities to GSI without service alignment introduces duplicate records and swivel‑chair processes.
risks.impact_description: Operational inefficiency, degraded seller and service experience, continued dependency on legacy systems.
risks.mitigation: Explicitly confirm service future‑state (remain in S2E vs phased move); document interim operating model and risks for leadership decision.

risks.title: Cost / Budget - Dual Licensing Exposure
risks.description: If quoting, renewals, or service remain in S2E while sales moves to GSI, users may require dual licenses. LATAM leadership has indicated no appetite for additional licensing cost.
risks.impact_description: Potential budget impact due to having ~150+ dual licenses.
risks.mitigation: Working with central sourcing team to transfer S2E to GSI licenses through SELA.

risks.title: Technology / Systems - High Data Duplication & Salesforce Storage Risk
risks.description: LATAM data volumes are large. Partial migration options may significantly increase duplicate accounts/contacts in Salesforce, which is already close to storage limits.
risks.impact_description: Increased Salesforce storage cost, performance degradation, data governance issues.
risks.mitigation: Quantify duplication under each migration option; confirm storage headroom; include storage impacts in option comparison deck.

risks.title: LatAm - productivity tools
risks.description: 2026 scheduled agreed at Steer Co for full data migration for Chile. October 2026 includes productivity tools - risk of timeline slippage to be managed
risks.mitigation: Chile scope and design to be signed off by Steer Co Jun 5. All enabling functions and relevant workstreams to confirm owners and delivery plans following kick off meeting in June

assumptions.title: Scope - Re‑use of Existing S2E Translations
assumptions.description: Assumes existing Spanish/Portuguese translations in S2E can be reused, with only new/custom GSI fields requiring translation.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Validation Needed: Inventory of reusable vs net‑new custom fields.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Risk if Invalid: Increased cost and extended change timeline.

assumptions.title: Schedule / Timeline - Q3 Feasibility for Top‑of‑Funnel Migration
assumptions.description: Assumes prerequisites (territory alignment, ECM hierarchy, translations, limited data scope) can be completed in parallel and on time.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Validation Needed: Architecture commitment to HLD timing; prerequisite readiness confirmation.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Risk if Invalid: Delivery likely shifts to Q4 or later.

issues.title: Scope Ambiguity — North LATAM Inclusion
issues.description: Conflicting views during discovery on whether North LATAM was in scope for the migration.
issues.impact_assessment: Early planning confusion and rework.
issues.resolution: Scope clarified and confirmed as in scope via leadership alignment.

issues.title: Schedule / Timeline - LATAM Data Readiness Not Validated
issues.description: Last comprehensive LATAM data quality assessment is ~3 years old; current readiness for migration is unvalidated.
issues.impact_assessment: Increased risk of defects, rework, and timeline slippage during UAT and cutover.
issues.resolution: Perform targeted data profiling and readiness assessment for in‑scope objects; feed findings into HLD and migration plan.

issues.title: D&A capacity constraints
issues.description:
Severe ECM tech capacity constraints as:
1.	there are a few high-priority projects that need to be fully resourced – Customer Data program, CPSP etc.
2.	there are multiple programs that drive resource requirements without appropriate funding and planned outside of normal cycles.
issues.impact_assessment:
Migrating the customers/contacts is critical for this project's success. 
Sales, marketing and service teams depend on this data to be migrated and sync'ed to GSI. 
They will not be able to process any sales activity in GSI until we get this data correctly.
Without ECM and ECX ingestion, we cannot easily (if at all) identify matching GSI accounts and contacts, with the following impacts:
- duplicates will be created in GSI
- accounts and contacts that would otherwise be matched will have to be included in profiling and data clean-up activities
issues.resolution:
ECM capacity Constraint is partially mitigated as most accounts already exist in ECM and contacts are available via WRP/S2E.
ECM is not blocking us from starting — but it is still critical for finishing the full migration.

dependencies.title: Schedule / Timeline - Territory Alignment to GSI
dependencies.description: LATAM seller territories must be aligned to GSI (via TMS or approved upload method) before any migration option proceeds.
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Migration cannot start without resolved territory alignment.

dependencies.title: Technology / Systems - ECM Hierarchy & Segmentation Readiness
dependencies.description: ECM hierarchy and segmentation must be confirmed and loaded prior to migration to avoid remapping and duplication later.
dependencies.dependent_on: ECM, Master Data Team
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Incorrect hierarchy impacts data model, reporting, and service workflows.

dependencies.title: Quality - Custom Field Translation (Spanish & Portuguese)
dependencies.description: All LATAM‑required GSI custom fields must be translated; standard Salesforce translations are insufficient.
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Poor usability and adoption if untranslated.

decisions.rationale: For Legal it will be mandatory to migrate together (they are on both S2E and SGD). Dominio (exclusively SGD) can be migrated afterwards.

decisions.rationale:

## Executive Summary

Project Ochre is delivering full technology separation of the RAMS, BRS, and CV Mail product lines from Thomson Reuters so the buyer can operate independently while meeting all Transition Services Agreement (TSA) obligations. Scope includes multi‑stage cloud migrations, domain and DNS transfer, Salesforce and O365 migrations, data retention, device collection, and access revocation for 18 employees and 1 contractor.  

Cloud Migration Phase 1 from colocation to TR AWS is 100% complete for BRS and cvMail (BRS cutover on 09 Mar 2026, cvMail on 24 Mar 2026), and Cloud Migration Phase 2 from TR AWS to NewCo is 8.4% complete against a 29 Jun 2026 plan. O365/SharePoint/OneDrive historical data migration is 60% complete toward the 29 Jun 2026 cutover, the data retention workstream is about 80% progressed toward its current 04 Sep 2026 target, and employee leaver activities are approximately 93% complete ahead of the 30 Oct 2026 project end date.  

Overall status is Green, driven by the on‑schedule completion of Phase 1 cloud migrations and solid progress across Phase 2, O365, and data retention activities within TSA‑aligned timelines.  

## Path to Green

Top risk is that Cloud Migration Phase 2 could extend beyond earlier TSA expectations, so we are locking in NewCo infrastructure readiness dates and cutover windows to meet the 29 Jun 2026 milestone, with TSA amendment options held as contingency only.  

## Milestones

- Complete Cloud Migration Phase 2 from TR AWS to NewCo cloud for BRS, cvMail, and RAMS by 29 Jun 2026, increasing Phase 2 completion from today’s 8.4% to 100%.  
- Finish M365/SharePoint/OneDrive migration cutover, validation, and cleanup by 29 Jun 2026, moving the O365 migration from 60% to full completion.  
- Execute TR cloud decommissioning and revoke TR access for divested users between 29 Jun 2026 and 17 Jul 2026, including decommissioning by 10 Jul 2026 and access revocation by 17 Jul 2026.  
- Close the data retention workstream, including execution and validation of seven‑year retention actions, by 04 Sep 2026.  
- Complete the overall Project Ochre technology and separation program by 30 Oct 2026.

risks.title: Dependency on Vendor for Cloud and DNS Migration Timelines (BRS- New Co, the BRS team lacked sufficient bandwidth and specialized skillsets to perform this work internally)
risks.description: DNS hosting migration cannot be started before completing domain ownership transfer for bigredsky.com, cvmailuk.com, and cvmail.com.au.
risks.impact_description: If domain ownership transfer is delayed, DNS hosting migration to NewCo name servers will also be delayed. This could postpone DNS-related changes, including email and application routing, potentially affecting service availability and alignment with cloud migration timelines.
risks.mitigation: Ensure domain ownership transfers complete on schedule and prepare DNS migration plans, including record exports/imports and testing, so hosting migration can be executed quickly once ownership is transferred.

risks.title: TSA amendment approval and timelines realignment
risks.description: Cloud Migration Phase 2 for the Ochre divestiture (TR AWS to NewCo cloud for BRS, CV Mail, and RAMS) may extend beyond the May 31 TSA deadline if Phase 1 cloud migration or NewCo cloud/DNS readiness is delayed.
risks.impact_description: If Phase 2 cloud migration is not completed by May 31, 2026, the project may miss the TSA end-date for technology separation. This would impact the ability to fully transition BRS, CV Mail, and RAMS to NewCo infrastructure, potentially requiring an extension of the TSA, additional infrastructure and support costs for Thomson Reuters, and a delay in decommissioning TR cloud resources and revoking access for divested employees.
risks.mitigation: 1) Danny to confirm the NewCo infrastructure setup timelines and dependent timelines for Cloud Migration Phase 2. 2) Explore options to create cloud services in the new company before regular use, if cost is lower than extending the TSA. 3) Ensure CICD pipelines are created before cloud services are built; involve DevOps (Chandresh Sutthar and Vijay Reddy) to support pipeline setup and address technical challenges, and estimate pipeline creation timelines.

assumptions.title: Phase 1 cloud migration completes in time to enable Phase 2 and dependent work
assumptions.description: Assumption that Phase 1 cloud migration (Colo to TR AWS Cloud for BRS and CV Mail) will complete on the planned dates (e.g., BRS by 2026-03-09 and CV Mail by 2026-03-24), enabling Phase 2 cloud migration, domain transfer, DNS hosting migration, and other downstream activities.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The HL Milestones show Phase 1 migrations for BRS and CV Mail as largely complete with specific cutover dates, and dependencies such as Phase 2 cloud migration and domain/DNS activities are scheduled assuming Phase 1 will be finished by early March 2026.
assumptions.validity_explanation: As of the latest updates, BRS AWS migration tasks are all marked Complete with a final cutover date of March 9, 2026. CV Mail AWS migration, including QA/Staging and Prod execution, is also reported as Complete with revised dates accepted. These completed tasks demonstrate that the assumption that Phase 1 would be delivered in early March has largely held true, making it a valid basis for planning subsequent work.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If any remaining Phase 1 activities slip, adjust Phase 2 schedule and prioritize critical workloads for earlier migration. Consider parallelizing some preparation for Phase 2 (e.g., CICD pipeline base structure, inventory and design work) so that the impact of minor Phase 1 delays on overall TSA timelines is minimized.
assumptions.validation_method: Track completion status of Phase 1 tasks in the HL Milestones (BRS AWS and CVMail AWS lines) and confirm Go-Live dates with the cloud migration team.

assumptions.title: ADO migration will be completed before Phase 2 cloud migration
assumptions.description: Assumption that migration of data from TR ADO to BRS ADO will be completed before Phase 2 cloud migration due to financial and other dependencies.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The RAIDD log lists a dependency that ADO migration should be completed before Phase 2 cloud migration because of financial dependencies. Project planning schedules ADO migration during April–May 2026, ahead of the overall Phase 2 completion date of June 29, 2026.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The ADO migration work item is scheduled for 2026-04-01 to 2026-05-29, with ownership assigned and TechM involved from the TR side. However, there are notes that vendor contract timing and start date are still to be confirmed, meaning the assumption is reasonable but not yet fully validated.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If ADO migration cannot be completed before Phase 2, defer non‑critical ADO-related scope from Phase 2 or implement temporary read‑only access to TR ADO for the buyer until migration completes. Re-sequence Phase 2 cutovers to prioritize environments that are less dependent on historical ADO data.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm ADO migration start and completion dates against the HL Milestones and verify that required data (e.g., development ticket history) is present and usable in BRS ADO before Phase 2 cutovers.

assumptions.title: Domain transfer must complete before DNS hosting migration and O365/email migrations
assumptions.description: Assumption that ownership transfer of key domains (e.g., bigredsky.com, cvmailuk.com, cvmail.com.au, cvmail.net) can be completed before DNS hosting migration and before Office 365 / email migrations that depend on the new DNS setup.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Project notes describe domain ownership transfer as a prerequisite for DNS hosting migration and subsequent O365 migrations. The HL Milestones show detailed steps for domain transfers (Phase 1) followed by a separate Phase 2 DNS hosting migration, and O365 migrations are noted as dependent on domain/email setup.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Multiple domain transfer tasks are already marked Complete, including bigredsky.com.au, bigredsky.au, cvmail.au, and cvmail.net. A combined task to transfer bigredsky.com, cvmailuk.com, and cvmail.com.au is scheduled through 2026-04-10 with active follow‑up reported. Given this progress and clear sequencing, it is reasonable to assume remaining transfers will complete ahead of DNS and O365 work.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If any critical domain transfer is delayed, delay dependent DNS hosting migration and email migrations for that domain while proceeding with unaffected domains. Implement temporary mail forwarding or aliases using existing TR infrastructure during the TSA to maintain service continuity until ownership transfer is complete.
assumptions.validation_method: Track completion of each domain transfer task in the HL Milestones and confirm registrar ownership change plus internal DNS updates before proceeding to Phase 2 DNS hosting migration and O365 cutovers.

assumptions.title: Office 365, SharePoint, and OneDrive migrations will complete successfully within TSA timelines
assumptions.description: Assumption that migration of user email (M365), SharePoint, and OneDrive data to the buyer’s environment can be completed using the chosen tools and vendor within the TSA period, after domain and email setup are finished.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Planning notes describe O365 migration as typically straightforward and handled by the O365 migration team, with a defined migration tool (AvePoint Fly) and third‑party provider (Troppus). Detailed phases (pre‑migration setup, identity/object mapping, pre‑stage and delta migration, cutover, validation and cleanup) are already scheduled.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The project has an agreed migration tool (AvePoint Fly), a migration vendor (Troppus), and documented progress showing completion of early phases and substantial work on pre‑stage/delta migration. However, Phase 4 (cutover) and Phase 5 (validation/cleanup) are not yet started and are tied to broader milestone readiness, so while the approach is sound, there remains schedule and coordination risk.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If migration appears unlikely to complete by TSA end, prioritize critical user mailboxes and high‑value SharePoint/OneDrive content for early cutover, extend O365 migration windows where possible, and if necessary arrange temporary continued TR access for a subset of users or data until final validation is complete.
assumptions.validation_method: Monitor execution and completion of each migration phase in the HL Milestones and obtain confirmation from Neel and the buyer’s IT that all required mailboxes and data have been successfully migrated and validated.

assumptions.title: NewCo will have cloud and DNS infrastructure ready in time for Phase 2 migration and DNS hosting cutover
assumptions.description: Assumption that the buyer (NewCo) will set up the necessary cloud environments and DNS infrastructure (including name servers and any Cloudflare/CloudFront integration) in time to support Phase 2 TR AWS to NewCo cloud migration and DNS hosting migration within planned dates.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The Phase 2 cloud migration plan and DNS hosting migration plan both rely on NewCo having its own cloud infrastructure and DNS servers ready. Notes state that DNS hosting migration cannot start until Phase 2 cloud migration infrastructure is in place and that NewCo must set up DNS servers and related records.
assumptions.validity_explanation: While project notes indicate Danny is actively engaged in planning and that NewCo is moving forward with other technical capabilities, there is also explicit feedback that Phase 2 may not meet a May 31 date due to infrastructure readiness concerns. This suggests partial progress but not yet confirmed readiness, making the assumption plausible but not secure.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If NewCo infrastructure is not ready, pursue: (1) temporary extension of TR hosting for critical workloads; (2) phased migration where components can move to any ready NewCo environments while others remain on TR; and (3) revisiting TSA scope/costs to cover extended hosting and support until NewCo is fully ready.
assumptions.validation_method: Obtain firm dates and readiness confirmation from Danny and NewCo technical leads (e.g., Vish, Parvathi) for cloud environment availability and DNS/server configuration, and verify with test deployments and DNS record changes prior to production cutover.
