latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

SafeSend One is integrating the SafeSend product into Thomson Reuters’ enterprise commercial and technology platforms, standardizing lead-to-cash, customer identity, and digital self-service so new sales run on scalable and compliant systems. This reduces reliance on legacy platforms while supporting growth and maintaining operational stability.

Front Office high-level design has been completed for 15 of 15 applications, delivered on 16 Jan 2026 against a 15 Jan 2026 plan, enabling downstream build and UAT. Lead-to-cash UAT for all workstreams is running from 25 May 2026 to 11 Jun 2026, ahead of the 20 Jun 2026 tech release that underpins the 13 Jul 2026 CS&S go-live and the 27 Jul 2026 New Sales go-live, which will deliver approximately 70% of the SafeSend scope.

Overall status is AMBER, driven by unresolved MDM integration issues that risk the 20 Jun 2026 tech release and could compress downstream testing and go-live readiness.

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on closing MDM integration gaps through a dedicated MDM and SafeSend working group, locking committed delivery dates and short-term workarounds so the 20 Jun 2026 tech release and July go-lives are protected, while simultaneously expediting resolution of the Informatica connectivity issue and tightening CS&S UAT scheduling and capacity planning.

## Milestones

- Complete Lead-to-Cash UAT for all workstreams by 11 Jun 2026.  
- Deliver the SSOne Market/Sales/Support/SSP tech code release by 20 Jun 2026.  
- Go live for SafeSend One CS&S production on 13 Jul 2026.  
- Go live for New Sales on the CPSP strategic commercial stack by 27 Jul 2026, which will account for approximately 70% of the SafeSend One scope.  
- Achieve overall project completion for SafeSend One by 15 Dec 2026.

risks.title: Stripe delivery plan not aligned with SafeSend target delivery
risks.description: The current Stripe project plan is not aligned with the SafeSend target delivery date, with Stripe delivering at the same time SafeSend aims to deliver. This overlap is likely to evolve into an unmet dependency.
risks.impact_description: If Stripe is not ready or integrated when SafeSend needs payment processing, SafeSend could face a critical dependency gap for payments, risking launch delays or requiring unplanned workarounds and impacting customer billing and payment experiences.
risks.mitigation: SafeSend will continue to use Paymetric for payments until a migration plan to Stripe is in place and executed by the Payment Unification team.

risks.title: Semarchy migration delay potentially impacting April 2026 lead‑to‑cash UAT
risks.description: Semarchy migration is supposed to complete by Q1 2026. If this project stalls or ‘sits’, it could impact the April 2026 lead‑to‑cash UAT schedule due to required environment downtime.
risks.impact_description: If Semarchy migration does not complete as planned, required environment outages or incomplete data migration could prevent or delay lead‑to‑cash UAT in April 2026, which may push back defect resolution, integration testing, and overall SafeSend launch readiness.
risks.mitigation: MDM team has proposed running EPM and Semarchy in parallel so that necessary capabilities remain available while migration completes and required downtime is minimized or scheduled to reduce impact on UAT.

risks.title: Flash migration delays tying up key CS&S resources and impacting SafeSend launch
risks.description: Completion of the Flash migration, which is required for CS&S, may be delayed. This could tie up key resources and cause a four‑week slip in SafeSend’s business launch and complicate UAT scheduling. If Flash is not delivered before mid‑July, its go‑live may be postponed to the following year.
risks.impact_description: If Flash migration slips past the planned timeframe, CS&S resources needed for SafeSend could remain focused on Flash, delaying SafeSend’s business launch by up to four weeks, impacting the planned July 2026 deployment and potentially deferring related benefits.
risks.mitigation: Close tracking of the Flash program to identify and address schedule risks early and coordinate resource allocation with SafeSend needs.

risks.title: Loss of key architect (Andy) for ECM/ECX high‑level design

risks.impact_description: If the HLD is delayed due to lack of architectural capacity, design sign‑off will slip, delaying the start of development and potentially affecting downstream integration, testing, and SafeSend’s overall delivery timeline.
risks.mitigation: Identify and onboard replacement or additional architectural capacity to complete the ECM/ECX HLD within the planned timeframe, and adjust plans or scope as needed to reflect available resources.

risks.mitigation: Onboard the required Informatica resource and commence scoping work as soon as they join the project.

risks.impact_description: As EPM jobs are not running, cutover files are not getting processed and impacting UAT testing timeline

risks.title: MDM Integration Delays Impacting SafeSend One Timeline
risks.description: Ongoing Master Data Management (MDM) integration issues are causing delays in data synchronization required for SafeSend One. Dependencies on MDM readiness for customer, product, and entitlement data remain unresolved, creating a risk to planned milestones and downstream integrations.
risks.impact_description: Continued MDM integration issues may delay SafeSend One system integration testing and go‑live readiness due to incomplete or unreliable master data feeds. Prolonged delays could impact dependent integrations, compress downstream testing timelines, and increase the risk of schedule slippage and rework close to go‑live.
risks.mitigation:
Establish a dedicated MDM + SafeSend integration working group with weekly checkpoints
Confirm committed delivery dates for required MDM objects and interfaces
Identify and approve short‑term workarounds (e.g., interim data loads or controlled fallbacks)
Engaged PE as well for a temporary work around as file drop from SafeSend is not straight forward

1. Centralized UAT Window Alignment
2. Early Dependency & Conflict Identification

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

ETS Service Desk Automation is integrating ServiceNow, Now Assist, Virtual Agent, and Amazon Connect into core Service Management and ETS workflows to automate common requests, chat, and voice interactions. This will reduce manual tickets, improve agent efficiency, and enable AI-driven self-service for employees across chat, Teams, and IVR.

Core platform capabilities are in place, with the Now Assist platform and Virtual Agent enabled and live since 17 Mar 2026, and the delegated Service Desk knowledge base migrated to production Service Desk, internal SME review on KB article clean up is delayed and the timelines extended to 30th June. The key external dependency on ServiceNow licensing and Now Assist enablement for the new instance was resolved on 03 Jun 2026.

Automation Delivered  
Starter/Leaver ticket closure — Live in production; 700+ tickets closed via automation in May alone.  
BitLocker key retrieval- Delivered; activation pending chat go-live.  
Mac Key Vault retrieval - Ready; go-live gated on the June ServiceNow upgrade. GAM automation is live  we have 750 tickets deflected. Pasword less we are partnering with IAM team for extended pilot start Start of Q3 , which is will bring the volume down, Lastly, discussions with sourcing started for RFP

Overall status is Amber trending Green, driven by a path forward with Co Pilot integration in place of Now Assist, with the remaining Amazon Connect CTI URL issue contained to the post–08 Jun 2026 window and not yet impacting the 2026-09-30 rollout milestones.

## Path to Green

Chat Experience - Now Assist chat is not meeting the desired user experience due to LLM limitations within the platform. We are evaluating alternatives- to replace Now Assist’s native  LLM within SNOW or  use  Microsoft Copilot integration as front end for chat. We are working with TR SNOW and vendor to explore both options and plan for POC in June

## Milestones

-   Delegated Service Desk knowledge base migration to production by service desk(HCL) is completed on 30 May 2026, internal KB clean up delayed and extended the timeline from 30th May to 30th Jun.
    
-   Agent Chat platform readiness to replace Vayusphere will complete by 19 Jun 2026, enabling the extended CIO pilot and downstream enterprise rollout activities.
    
-   MIM Transition to SNOW for DL and shared mailbox management will complete foundation work by 30 Jun 2026.
    
-   Copilot Integration Testing for live agent transfer and transcript sharing will complete by 15 Aug 2026.
    
-   Automations for VDI, and M365 and the phased Pilot and Enterprise Rollout of Now Assist plus Agent Chat will complete by 30 Sep 2026, with the overall ETS Service Desk Automation program completing by 24 Apr 2027.

risks.title: Agent chat interaction visibility model may not support desired multi-agent access
risks.description: Jakub requested investigating whether the same interaction conversation can be available to multiple agents at once, which is not the default behavior of Advanced Work Assignment (AWA). Current understanding is that supervisors/managers can join ongoing interactions, but it is unclear whether the system can be configured so different agents can pick up the same interaction, or if timing parameters (e.g., 1-minute search interval) must be adjusted instead.
risks.impact_description: If ServiceNow and AWA cannot be configured to support the desired level of multi-agent access to a single interaction, or if timing parameters for agent search are not tuned, agent collaboration workflows may be constrained. This could limit the ability for multiple agents to assist on complex cases, slow handoffs, and impact response times. Alternatively, aggressive parameter changes (e.g., very short search windows) without careful testing could destabilize routing behavior.
risks.mitigation: 1) Investigate ServiceNow and Advanced Work Assignment documentation and configuration options to confirm whether an interaction can be surfaced to multiple agents concurrently and under what conditions (e.g., supervisor join vs re-queueing). 2) Evaluate alternative approaches such as adjusting the default 1-minute agent search window to shorter intervals (e.g., 10–15 seconds) and enabling supervisor join capabilities for complex cases. 3) Prototype the desired behavior in DEV/QA and review with Jakub to confirm it meets operational needs. 4) If true multi-agent access is not feasible, document the chosen interaction handling model and ensure HCL is trained on expected behavior and escalation paths.

Establish a Backward‑Planned Service Desk Roadmap (2026–2027)

Backward‑plan a multi‑year Service Desk delivery roadmap starting from:

December 2027 VC outcomes, and
HCL renegotiation decision date as a hard commercial milestone.


Decompose the roadmap into quarterly milestones for:

Automation & deflection (e.g., Virtual Agent, Now Assist, self‑service)
Operating model evolution (insource vs vendor-delivered)
Capability build (process maturity, tooling, workforce readiness)
Define explicit decision gates aligned to the HCL contract timeline:

Gate 1: Proof points on automation/deflection and productivity gains
Gate 2: Comparative insource vs vendor cost/service scenarios
Gate 3: Final sourcing recommendation (renegotiate vs insource vs hybrid)


Each gate must have:

Entry/exit criteria
Data requirements (metrics, benchmarks, pilot outcomes)
Accountable owners

risks.title: Agent chat access/role configuration for HCL testers not fully working
risks.description: Some HCL users (e.g., Kandibanda Rakesh, Sri Lakshmi and others) cannot see or use the agent chat widget despite being added to the "Nava pilot users" / HCL groups with required roles. Causes appear related to legacy membership in HCL service desk groups and/or roles not propagating correctly from groups to users. If unresolved, HCL agents will not be able to perform hands-on testing of agent chat end-to-end.
risks.impact_description: If agent chat access and role issues for HCL testers are not fully resolved, HCL will be unable to explore agent chat hands-on "without any issues" as required. risks.title: Agent capacity and presence configuration may overload or mis-route chats
risks.description: Advanced Work Assignment (AWA) agent presence and capacity settings are not yet properly configured. Many agents appear as "available" indefinitely (even after being inactive for long periods), and default capacities (e.g., number of parallel chats per agent) are effectively unset or inconsistent. This can cause the system to treat long-inactive agents as available capacity and over-assign chats beyond reasonable limits.
risks.impact_description: If agent presence and capacity configurations remain unoptimized, chats may be routed to agents who are actually offline or no longer on shift, leading to long customer wait times and abandoned chats. Agents who are online can be overloaded with too many concurrent chats, impacting quality and agent experience. Misrouted or stuck chats will undermine confidence in the new agent chat solution and may force manual interventions, slowing adoption and putting service KPIs at risk.
risks.mitigation: 1) Define standard capacity limits per agent (e.g., 5 concurrent chats/incidents as discussed) and configure these limits consistently across all pilot agents. 2) Investigate whether there is an out-of-the-box or script-based mechanism to automatically mark agents offline after a defined period of inactivity or after logout; if available, implement and test it. 3) Review historical presence data (e.g., agents still showing available after weeks) to validate that the new configuration works as expected. 4) Coordinate with Gandikota, Srinu to deploy configuration changes across DEV/QA and PROD environments to keep them aligned. 5) Monitor queue utilization and agent feedback during the pilot to refine capacity and presence thresholds before broader rollout.

risks.title: Conversational greeting and fallback workflow may miss 2026-05-07 commitment
risks.description: The team committed to having a more natural, conversational virtual agent greeting, closing, and fallback experience ready by 2026-05-07, based on feedback from leaders (including Marc) that the current Now Assist chat lacks greetings, closing messages, validation, and ticket number sharing. During the 2026-05-05 SNOWNAWA working session, Shariq highlighted that there has been "no meaningful progress" on these conversational workflows, ownership is unclear (who raises the story, what Ashima and developers are working from), and admin access to edit templates is constrained. Although predefined templates and out-of-the-box system topics exist, they are not yet configured to meet the desired experience. If these items are not implemented and tested rapidly, the team may miss the 2026-05-07 target it has "given ourselves" for fixing the greetings and related chat behaviors.
risks.impact_description: If the conversational greeting, closing, and fallback workflows are not implemented and validated by 2026-05-07, the virtual agent experience will remain non-conversational (no personalized greeting, no clear closing, weak error/fallback handling, inconsistent ticket number communication). This will directly contradict commitments made to Marc and other stakeholders, undermine confidence in Now Assist as a polished product, and may delay further pilot or rollout activities that assume a baseline conversational experience. It also increases the likelihood of additional rework after leadership feedback, consuming scarce developer and SME time during an already compressed window.
risks.mitigation:
1) Capture a concrete story with clear description and acceptance criteria for the conversational workflow (greeting, closing, error handling, and fallback messages), as discussed by Vinay and Shariq, using the existing "virtual agent" story template format.
2) Shariq, Mayank, and Prithwiraj will meet immediately after the 2026-05-05 team meeting to define the exact greeting and fallback prompts, including personalization (e.g., "Hey, <name>, how can I help you?"), and provide these to Vinay the same day.
3) Ensure appropriate admin access is granted (e.g., to Mayank or another designated admin) to edit or duplicate the greeting templates and system topics in the sandbox environment.
4) Ashima has scheduled a focused working session for the next day with Srinivasan, Vinay, and others to prioritize and implement the greeting and fallback changes, treating this as a working session rather than relying on daily, asynchronous feedback.
5) Run internal "beta" testing by Shariq, Mayank, and Prithwiraj on the updated experience before requesting Marc and other leaders to retest, iterating quickly on any issues identified in the session.
6) Track progress against the 2026-05-07 target explicitly and escalate immediately if development or access constraints threaten that date.
7) As of the 2026-05-07 Service Desk AI automation sync, the team has progressed two of the seven documented conversational topics (initial greeting scenario and handover flow) but Mayank reported test failures in key scenarios (e.g., user enters a problem statement directly without "hi" and receives no greeting or empathy message; handover confirmation flow not yet implemented). Additional UX requirements were agreed, including an empathy-style acknowledgement that references the user’s name where technically feasible, replacing drop-down topic selection with visible options for top topics, and capturing all feedback and status in a centralized Excel tracker that Ashima will create. Daily 9 PM IST standups will be used to track completion of the remaining topics and retesting.

risks.title: Copilot live agent handoff and transcript sharing may not meet requirements
risks.description: The team is pivoting to Microsoft 365 Copilot as the interim conversational front end, but the live agent transfer capability from Copilot into ServiceNow Agent Chat has not yet been implemented or tested. Mayank and Shariq emphasized that for a good user experience, the entire Copilot conversation (or at least a useful summary) must be handed over to the ServiceNow live agent so that the agent can see the history and context. Today, the live agent functionality sits fully on the ServiceNow side, and it is unclear whether Copilot can reliably pass conversation history into the ServiceNow interaction/incident or whether an additional topic/API must be built specifically for live agent transfer. Until this is designed and validated, there is a risk that the handoff will be incomplete or fail altogether.
risks.impact_description: If Copilot cannot reliably transfer conversation history to ServiceNow during live agent handoff, agents will receive chats without prior context, forcing customers to repeat information and degrading the user experience. This will undermine the key requirement that the handoff from Copilot to the service desk be seamless, may increase handle times, and could reduce trust in the new Copilot-based channel. It may also require rework of the Copilot design or additional custom integration between Copilot and ServiceNow, delaying rollout and potentially impacting call/deflection targets.
risks.mitigation:
1) Design and implement a specific live agent transfer flow for Copilot that captures the user conversation (or a summary) and passes it into the ServiceNow interaction/incident as part of the handoff.
2) Use lower environments (Dev1) to prototype this behavior, ensuring the ServiceNow live agent sees the full context.
3) Coordinate between Mayank (Copilot design) and the ServiceNow team (Prastuti and Vinay) to determine whether this can be achieved without custom APIs, or if a limited API-based integration is required only for live agent transfer.
4) Execute end-to-end tests of Copilot conversations that escalate to live agents, validating that agents can see transcript/summary content and that no data is lost.
5) Document any limitations (e.g., only summaries, not full transcripts) and incorporate them into the pros/cons comparison table that Shariq will prepare for leadership review.

risks.title: Dynamic language translation capability may be lost when moving from Now Assist to Copilot
risks.description: Jakub and Shariq highlighted that the current dynamic language translation feature (used in Agent Chat to support non-English users while routing to English-speaking agents) relies on Now Assist capabilities. As the team pivots to Copilot as the front-end conversational agent, it is unclear whether equivalent dynamic translation will be available or how it will be implemented. Prastuti confirmed that Now Assist is required for the current AI-based real-time translation. If an alternative solution is not put in place, the project could lose the ability to offshore non-English traffic to the main support center while still providing localized experiences to users.
risks.impact_description: If dynamic translation cannot be provided in the Copilot-based solution, non-English language support may be constrained. TR might be unable to route non-English interactions efficiently to centralized English-speaking support teams while maintaining a localized user experience. This would reduce potential savings from offshoring non-English languages to the main support center in India, limit call/chat deflection for non-English users, and weaken the business case that assumes multi-language support via AI translation.
risks.mitigation:
1) Inventory the current dynamic translation implementation with Now Assist and document exactly which components (LLM, configuration) provide real-time translation in Agent Chat.
2) Assess Copilot capabilities for dynamic translation in the context of the planned Teams-based Copilot agent, including whether Copilot can translate user inputs and agent responses in real time.
3) Engage ServiceNow and Microsoft contacts to understand supported patterns where Copilot and ServiceNow Agent Chat can jointly provide translation, or whether Now Assist must remain in the path for translation only.
4) Prototype one or two non-English flows end-to-end with Copilot as the entry point and ServiceNow Agent Chat as the backend, validating that translation works for both directions.
5) If equivalent translation cannot be achieved, update the options/pros-cons table (that Shariq and Mayank will prepare) to reflect this limitation and escalate to Marc and AD for a decision on whether to retain Now Assist for translation, adopt an alternative LLM, or accept reduced multi-language capability in the near term.

risks.title: Copilot-based solution may not preserve interaction linkage and history in ServiceNow
risks.description: Prastuti raised concern that, with Now Assist, conversational data is attached to the ServiceNow interaction and carried forward to incidents, enabling AWA-based features such as routing users back to the same agent within a time window. She noted that, with Copilot, TR will likely not store Copilot conversations as Virtual Agent conversations in ServiceNow by default. It is uncertain whether Copilot conversations will be linked to interaction/incident records in a way that preserves history and supports existing AWA capabilities (e.g., context-aware routing).
risks.impact_description: If Copilot conversations are not stored and linked to ServiceNow interaction and incident records, agents will lose access to historical conversational data associated with a case, and AWA will be unable to use this history for routing (e.g., trying to route repeat contacts back to the same agent within three days). This reduces the effectiveness of Agent Chat, complicates follow-up interactions, and may degrade the service desk experience compared to the current Now Assist-based approach.
risks.mitigation:
1) Define a data model for capturing Copilot conversations or summaries in ServiceNow, ensuring that they are attached to interaction and/or incident records similarly to Now Assist conversations.
2) Evaluate mechanisms (e.g., MCP server configuration, service account access) to write summaries or transcripts from Copilot into ServiceNow tables without violating security or compliance constraints.
3) Test repeat-contact scenarios (e.g., user contacts service desk multiple times within three days) to verify whether AWA can leverage this stored history and whether any existing features (such as routing to the same agent) continue to work.
4) If full parity with Now Assist is not feasible, document the reduced capability and include it in the options comparison that will be presented to leadership, so that any gaps are explicitly accepted or mitigated via process changes.

risks.title: Amazon Connect CTI URL misconfiguration may delay IVR demo and cutover
risks.description: During the May 11, 2026 Service Desk AI automation sync, Jakub and Saket reported an issue with the URL used by the Amazon Connect CTI integration: it currently opens an incident record populated with user details instead of an interaction record, whereas the desired behavior is to start from an interaction record. This misconfiguration is blocking completion of CTI testing and prevents scheduling the previously agreed Amazon Connect demo session for Wednesday. Saket stated that once the correct URL is provided and CTI testing is successful, the team will need an additional 2–3 business days to confirm testing, followed by approximately 10–14 days for the telco/ISP to change the external IVR numbers and perform cutover, with old numbers running in parallel for 2–3 weeks. Until the URL issue is resolved, these downstream steps cannot begin, putting IVR cutover timelines at risk.

This, in turn, delays finalizing IVR cutover dates and communicating new numbers to Thomson Reuters users. Because the telco/ISP requires roughly 10–14 days to implement number changes and old numbers will run in parallel only for a limited period, any slip in resolving the URL issue can cascade into delays for Avaya-to-Amazon Connect cutover and subsequent integration of Amazon Connect with Now Assist / Agent Chat. This would slow realization of voice deflection benefits and could necessitate re-planning of 2026 IVR-related milestones.
risks.mitigation:
1) Identify and correct the CTI integration URL so that Amazon Connect opens an interaction record in ServiceNow instead of an incident record; Kiran and Bineesh to coordinate with the appropriate ServiceNow and telephony contacts (as referenced in the email chain including Ragesh).

4) After successful testing, agree and document IVR cutover dates, ensuring the ISP/telco has at least 10 days (ideally 2 weeks) to implement number changes and that old Avaya numbers run in parallel with new Amazon Connect numbers for 2–3 weeks.
5) Communicate new IVR numbers and cutover timelines to HCL and Thomson Reuters users well in advance, so downstream dependencies (e.g., integration into Agent Chat and Virtual Agent) can proceed.
6) Track progress and blockers in the existing Amazon Connect / CTI integration action items and escalate if URL resolution exceeds the 2–3 business day window.

risks.title: Agent chat dashboards and analytics requirements not yet defined
risks.description: HCL stakeholders requested dashboards to monitor agent chat performance (e.g., agent status, availability, queues in line). While the conversational analytics plugin can provide some out-of-the-box insights, custom dashboards must be built from scratch based on specific KPIs HCL wants to see. These KPIs and dashboard requirements have not yet been provided by HCL.
risks.impact_description: If agent chat dashboard and analytics requirements from HCL are not defined and implemented before broader rollout, TR and HCL will lack visibility into operational performance (e.g., agent availability, queue backlog, volumes). This can hinder proactive management of the service desk, make it harder to detect issues, and limit the ability to demonstrate value of the new agent chat solution to leadership.
risks.mitigation: 1) Request HCL to provide a prioritized list of desired KPIs and views for agent chat dashboards (e.g., agent status, availability per queue, queue lengths, interaction volumes). 2) Enable the conversational analytics plugin to leverage available out-of-the-box dashboards where helpful. 3) Design and build custom dashboards from scratch in ServiceNow based on the agreed KPIs, ensuring they align with AWA data structures. 4) Review prototype dashboards with HCL (e.g., Nitin, Mehwish) and TR stakeholders (e.g., Jakub) to validate that they meet operational needs. 5) Iterate based on feedback and deploy dashboards to production aligned with the pilot timelines.
risks.source_file_name: Service Desk AI automation WF Daily Sync.docx

risks.title: HCL Vayusphere renewal decision may be misaligned with Agent Chat and Copilot timelines
risks.description: Jakub reminded the team that Vyas has a renewal with HCL this month and that HCL needs to know whether they should renew their existing Vayusphere chat solution. Kiran noted that Agent Chat as a Vayusphere replacement is "almost 95% done" and IVR work is also ongoing, while Shariq said they need a one-page view of options and impacts before deciding. If the Copilot and Agent Chat strategy is not clarified in time, HCL may either renew Vayusphere unnecessarily or face a gap without a supported chat solution.
risks.impact_description: If the decision on HCL's Vayusphere renewal is not aligned with the readiness of ServiceNow Agent Chat and the Copilot front end, HCL may renew Vayusphere and incur additional costs for a legacy solution while also investing in the new stack, reducing savings and complicating operations. Alternatively, if they do not renew and Agent Chat/Copilot are not yet production-ready, the service desk may experience a disruption in chat support, impacting user experience and potentially increasing call volumes.
risks.mitigation:
1) Prepare the one-page options and pros/cons table that Shariq and Mayank discussed, explicitly covering: (a) continuing with Vayusphere, (b) moving fully to ServiceNow Agent Chat with Copilot, and (c) hybrid or phased options.
2) Use this summary to support a decision meeting with Marc, AD, and HCL leadership (including Vyas) ahead of the renewal deadline.
3) Clearly communicate to HCL the expected go-live readiness of Agent Chat (currently ~95% complete) and any dependencies on Copilot or IVR work so they can make an informed renewal decision.
4) If there is a risk of delay in Agent Chat/Copilot go-live, consider a short-term extension of Vayusphere as a contingency, rather than a full renewal, and incorporate this into the negotiation with HCL.
5) Update project timelines and financial models to reflect the chosen path and ensure the PMO tracker and RAAID log capture any residual risk.

assumptions.rationale_basis: During the May 11, 2026 sync, Kiran stated he was coordinating with ServiceNow (via John) to schedule working sessions from Tuesday to Friday to address conversational workflow issues. Ashima explicitly asked whether customization was feasible, and Vinay advised that high‑risk customization should only be considered after consulting ServiceNow. The team aligned on using these vendor sessions to work through the greeting behavior and related items.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The vendor sessions are being actively organized, with ownership by Kiran and clear participation from key technical and UX stakeholders (Vinay, Ashima, Mayank, Prithvi). However, the complexity of Now Assist / Virtual Agent internals and the explicit caution against customization mean there is some uncertainty about whether all blockers can be resolved within four sessions.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If the vendor sessions do not resolve all blockers by May 15, the team should (1) prioritize a minimum viable set of conversational changes for production (e.g., greeting and handover only), (2) schedule additional vendor sessions or escalate within ServiceNow for deeper support, and (3) update project milestones and the associated risk to reflect a revised delivery date.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm that four working sessions with ServiceNow are scheduled and held between Tuesday and Friday and that they produce concrete configuration or design decisions for each of the eight conversational feedback items, especially greeting behavior when users do not start with "hi".
assumptions.source_file_name: Service Desk AI automation WF  Sync (1).docx

assumptions.title: Developers will complete backup of update sets and documentation before Zurich upgrade clone
assumptions.description: It is assumed that developers (primarily Srinu and Prashanth, with any contributions from Prudhvi or Mayank) will export all relevant ServiceNow update sets and document configuration changes not captured in update sets before the Zurich upgrade clone from production to the dev environment, as discussed in the May 11, 2026 sync.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Vinay explained the need to take backups of update sets before Friday and to document configuration-only changes so they can be re-applied after the clone. Srinu confirmed on the call that he and Prashanth would "take care of those" and that they are aware some items require manual rework.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Srinu and Prashanth have prior experience managing update sets and clones, and they explicitly acknowledged ownership for backups and documentation on the call. However, time constraints and competing upgrade testing tasks introduce moderate risk that some items may be missed.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If, upon verification, some update sets or configuration steps were not backed up, the team should (1) immediately catalog what was lost, (2) allocate time for Srinu and Prashanth to re-implement those changes on the cloned dev instance, and (3) tighten the process for future upgrades by standardizing a backup checklist and sign-off step.
assumptions.validation_method: Verify by the end of Friday that (1) update sets containing recent conversational workflow and Agent Chat changes have been exported and stored, and (2) a document exists listing configuration-only changes that must be manually re-applied post-clone.
assumptions.source_file_name: Service Desk AI automation WF  Sync (1).docx

assumptions.title: Non-production development can continue during Zurich prod change freeze without impacting timelines
assumptions.description: The team assumes that the Zurich production change freeze does not prevent ongoing development and testing in non-production environments (Dev1 and QA) for virtual agent conversational workflows and Agent Chat, and that only promotions to production are restricted until after the upgrade window.
assumptions.rationale_basis: During the May 11, 2026 sync, Vinay clarified that although there is a dev freeze period for production (May 8 to June 8), developers can continue to work on changes in Dev1 and QA, with only production deployments blocked until after the change freeze. Kiran explicitly sought confirmation that this would not stop their work, and Vinay confirmed it would not.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The assumption is grounded in standard ServiceNow upgrade procedures and explicit statements from the platform lead, but final enforcement depends on broader change management policy, which may impose additional constraints.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If non-prod development is restricted, the team should (1) adjust timelines for conversational workflow and Agent Chat changes, (2) explore using a separate sandbox or lower environment not subject to the freeze, and (3) communicate revised delivery dates and risks to stakeholders, updating the RAAID log accordingly.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm with the ServiceNow upgrade/change management team that Dev1 and QA can be used for ongoing development and testing during the Zurich prod change freeze, and monitor whether any unexpected restrictions or repeated clones impact their usability.
assumptions.source_file_name: Service Desk AI automation WF  Sync (1).docx

issues.title: ServiceNow license renewal and Now Assist license mapping blocking AI capabilities on new instance
issues.description: ServiceNow license renewal and license mapping between the legacy and new instances are preventing Now Assist and related AI capabilities from being enabled on the new ServiceNow instance. The license team has confirmed that licenses are still effectively tied to the legacy instance, causing the Now Assist mapping on the new instance to be disconnected. As a result, ongoing work on Agent Chat enhancements, Amazon Connect CTI URL fixes, and other Now Assist/virtual agent features is currently on hold until the renewal discussion is resolved and licenses are properly applied to the new instance.
issues.impact_assessment: The unresolved ServiceNow license renewal and license mapping issue directly blocks enabling Now Assist/AI capabilities on the new ServiceNow instance. This has halted progress on Agent Chat gap analysis, Amazon Connect CTI URL enhancements, and broader Now Assist work (including Teams integration and password reset use cases). Until the licensing issue is resolved, the team cannot fully use out-of-the-box Now Assist capabilities or proceed with certain ServiceNow working sessions, which risks delaying multiple SD Automation milestones and pushing out planned go-lives for chat and IVR capabilities.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Agent Chat gap analysis and enhancements; Amazon Connect CTI URL fix and IVR migration; Now Assist / virtual agent development and testing; planned ServiceNow working sessions on password reset via Teams integration.
issues.resolution: Work with the AD licensing team and the ServiceNow account manager to finalize the renewal and ensure Now Assist licenses are correctly mapped to the new instance. Request that the account manager expedite re-enablement of Now Assist capabilities on the new instance even while broader renewal negotiations continue, so that ongoing AI/virtual agent work can resume. Once licenses are corrected, re-enable Now Assist on the new instance and validate that AI capabilities (including virtual agent and Teams integration) function as expected.

issues.resolution: Validate that group roles from the NAVA pilot group are correctly applied to affected users by checking sys_user_role mappings and scheduled jobs; adjust group membership (remove/re-add users) as needed. decisions.title: No customization of interaction record for Amazon Connect CTI; use out-of-the-box interaction view
decisions.description: For the Amazon Connect–ServiceNow CTI integration, the interaction record opened for agents must remain the out-of-the-box interaction view (showing user details, recent tasks/interactions, and assigned assets). TR and HCL agreed that no new fields or layout customizations will be implemented on this interaction record as part of the CTI URL change; the focus is solely on providing a URL that opens the standard interaction record instead of an incident.
decisions.rationale: ServiceNow vendor (John) recommended using out-of-the-box CTI capabilities and the Amazon Connect connector rather than building custom APIs or customized interaction forms. Keeping the interaction record standard reduces maintenance, avoids high-risk customizations, and ensures future compatibility, while still meeting HCLs requirement to see user details and related records when a call is received.
decisions.options_considered: 1) Customize the interaction record (new fields/layout changes) to meet HCLs expectations; 2) Use the out-of-the-box interaction record and only adjust the CTI URL to open it; 3) Redesign the integration using the ServiceNow Amazon Connect connector and new flows in a future phase.

decisions.title: Prioritize minimal-change CTI URL fix for Amazon Connect migration and defer connector-based redesign
decisions.description: For the immediate Avaya-to-Amazon Connect migration, TR and HCL will prioritize a minimal-change solution that adjusts the existing CTI URL so it opens an interaction record (instead of an incident) using current architecture, rather than redesigning the integration around the ServiceNow Amazon Connect connector. A connector-based redesign and proof of concept (POC) may be pursued later once the basic migration is stable and time/resources permit.
decisions.rationale: HCL reported that almost all technical and UAT activities for the Amazon Connect migration are complete, with only the URL landing page behavior pending. ServiceNow vendor guidance and internal review indicated that re-architecting around the Amazon Connect connector would require additional time, effort, and POC work, which the team cannot afford before go-live. A minimal-change CTI URL fix enables timely migration while keeping open the option to adopt the connector later.
decisions.options_considered: 1) Redesign the integration using the ServiceNow Amazon Connect connector and perform a POC in sandbox before go-live; 2) Adjust the existing CTI URL and parameters to open an interaction record instead of an incident, keeping the current architecture; 3) Continue with the current incident-landing behavior and accept the UX gap.

decisions.rationale: Now Assists LLM and conversational experience were assessed as not good enough for end users, and ServiceNow indicated that Employee Works is the longer-term answer. Copilot testing shows promising results, requires no Now Assist dependency, and can be integrated with ServiceNow while licensing and Employee Works negotiations proceed in parallel.
decisions.options_considered: 1) Continue investing in Now Assist conversational workflows; 2) Pause Now Assist and move directly to Employee Works when available; 3) Adopt M365 Copilot as the interim conversational AI integrated with ServiceNow, while treating Employee Works as a future phase; 4) Replace Now Assists LLM with a different LLM while keeping the ServiceNow front end.

decisions.rationale: Waiting for Employee Works licensing and implementation would introduce significant schedule risk and delay user experience improvements, while Copilot can fill the gap now. decisions.options_considered: 1) Hold SD Automation milestones until Now Assist vs Employee Works licensing strategy is finalized; 2) Proceed with Copilot and treat licensing strategy as a non-blocking, parallel track; 3) Stop all AI work until Employee Works is ready and licensed.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

AI Reimagine Other Pillar Point Solutions is delivering AI-driven automation across ETS, ISRM, and CIO Strategy & Operations to reduce Service Desk demand, embed automated vulnerability scanning, and streamline PMO and Customer Trust workflows. This matters because it shifts effort from routine execution to exception management, unlocking efficiency and improving security and governance outcomes.

To date, PMO Partner has completed CIO rollout with 100% project adoption as of 26 May 2026, in line with its planned end date. Remaining workstreams are progressing to plan, with ETS Discovery targeting completion by 30 Jun 2026, ETS Service Desk automation rollout by 30 Sep 2026, and ISRM InfoSec point solutions sustaining delivery through 31 Dec 2026.

Overall status is Green, driven by the on-plan completion of the CIO-wide PMO Partner rollout and adoption.

## Path to Green

The primary mitigation focus is on the ETS value creation risk, with a detailed review of Service Desk value cases and alternative software-driven VC opportunities targeted for completion by 30 Sep 2026, alongside formalising BAU support and SLAs for PMO Partner to address post-pilot capacity constraints by 30 Jul 2026.

## Milestones

- Complete PMO Partner CIO rollout and achieve 100% adoption for CIO projects by 26 May 2026.
- Complete ETS Discovery and benefits identification for the 2026 plan by 30 Jun 2026.
- Deliver ETS Service Desk Automation proof of value and enterprise rollout for Now Assist by 30 Sep 2026.
- Maintain continuous ISRM InfoSec point solution delivery and embedded automated vulnerability scanning across the estate through 31 Dec 2026.

risks.title: ETS VC Targets
risks.description: ServiceDesk case does not have a firm roadmap in place on how VC outcomes will be achieved in 2027 regarding HCL Insource/Renegotiation. Latest feedback from team was a revision of savings estimate to ~$1.5M annualized, down from $3M.
risks.impact_description: Lack of a defined roadmap for ServiceDesk case delivery introduces uncertainty in achieving 2027 VC outcomes tied to HCL insource/renegotiation, increasing risk to financial targets. The downward revision of estimated savings from $3M to ~$1.5M annualized further impacts expected value realization and may necessitate re-baselining of program benefits and stakeholder expectations.
risks.mitigation: ETS is committed to identifying VC opportunities through software solutions and is currently conducting a detailed review and analysis, targeted for completion by the end of Q3.

risks.title: PMOP: Post‑Pilot Support & Capacity Risk
risks.description: After Tiger Team rolls off, PMO Partner depends on existing AI Services capacity with no incremental resourcing, while simultaneously absorbing pilot bugs, MVP gaps, and fast‑follow features. This creates a risk of backlog stagnation and delayed fixes if PMO Partner competes with other EAIS priorities.

## Executive Summary

Service Health Remediation (SHA) is delivering remediation of 2026 SHA recommendations for priority products, covering performance, stability, security, observability, and technical debt. This matters because it reduces service health risks that could impact customer experience, business continuity, and regulatory or policy compliance.

The 2026 plan targets remediation of 187 high and critical recommendations across in-scope products by 31 Dec 2026, with work running from 02 Feb 2026 to 31 Dec 2026 and no schedule variance reported to date.

2026 Funding Allocation –

In April, OS Income Tax and Pagero submitted funding requests to accelerate remediation of critical and high-priority recommendations planned for 2026. These requests are currently on hold pending Finance’s review of other potential submissions.

Additionally, $70k in break-fix funding for Content Systems has been approved to address KeyCite Publishing stability issues following the AWS go-live earlier this year.

Overall status is Green, driven by scope and schedule remaining aligned to the 2026 plan and clear governance in place to treat unfunded recommendations as accepted business risk.

## Path to Green

The primary mitigation focus is on managing Product Engineering capacity risk by sequencing remediation realistically, prioritising high impact items, and escalating material constraints through SHA governance so that the 187 planned recommendations can be completed by 31 Dec 2026.

## Milestones

-   Commence 2026 service health remediation for in-scope products on 02 Feb 2026.
    
-   Complete remediation of 187 high and critical service health recommendations by 31 Dec 2026.
    
-   Mitigate the Product Engineering capacity risk in line with SHA governance expectations by 31 Dec 2026.

risks.mitigation: The SHA Governance team is working closely with Product teams to identify and address capacity issues as they arise, including prioritising remediation work, sequencing recommendations realistically, and escalating material capacity constraints through governance forums including additional funding

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

**No new updates are being reported this week, as milestone and feature updates are provided on a bi-weekly cadence aligned with the ADO sprint schedule and SteerCo. meeting.**

Diamond Lane has established its initial operating model and made tangible progress toward pilot readiness, but the program remains amber while key execution gaps are closed. Materia remains on track for initial policy-driven enablement by June 30, relying on the existing deployment circuit breaker for rollback. For Cocounsel Legal, major architectural and QA process constraints make MFE enablement a poor near-term pilot candidate, so focus is shifting to llmproxy as the better path to demonstrate value by the end of July. Initial assessment of Cocounsel Next has not surfaced major technical barriers and points to a timely opportunity to align Diamond Lane expectations with the team’s planned blue/green deployment evolution. In parallel, product expansion prioritization will continue through assessment of business-critical products with significant security vulnerability findings, while also targeting newer services where stronger deployment patterns can be shaped earlier.

## Path to Green

To reach green, the immediate priorities are to close DORA and observability gaps, kick off Cocounsel Legal llmproxy enablement work, finalize Materia deployment rules and trigger automation, and align with Cocounsel Next Engineering on a Diamond Lane enablement target achievable within Q3. Completing these items for the initial pilots will put Diamond Lane in a stronger position to support repeatable, lower-friction production releases.

## Milestones

-   Complete Diamond Lane CI criteria definition and formalization by 2026-06-30.
    
-   Finalize Diamond Lane participation contracts, change scorecard v1, and pipeline‑driven change automation for pilot products by 2026-06-30.
    
-   Complete automated rollback and resilience crawl/walk/run patterns for pilot products by 2026-06-30.
    
-   Establish the phased Diamond Lane KPI framework (including initial DORA‑based metrics) and feedback loops by 2026-12-31.
    
-   Complete expansion and enablement assets and crawl‑stage application onboarding to Diamond Lane, and transition to steady‑state operations by 2026-12-31.

risks.title: ServiceNow integration — automation ownership and readiness for Cocounsel Legal

(Owners: LSM CM + LSM RM + Cocounsel Legal SRE)
risks.impact_description: Delays in ServiceNow integration may block standardized change management workflows and delay delivery timelines.
risks.mitigation: Align with the ServiceNow core team on required templates and approvals; align with LSM CM, LSM RM, and Cocounsel Legal SRE on timelines to migrate and test standard change templates within pipeline.

risks.title: Materia DORA metric accuracy and trustworthiness (multi-repo lead time mapping)
risks.description: Lead-time metrics are correct for single repos but multi-repository services still have incomplete commit-to-deploy correlation (e.g., missing/ambiguous commit SHA mapping), which can skew DORA reporting in Port/IDP.  (Owners: Materia SRE + Materia Engineering)
risks.impact_description: Misleading readiness signals could drive incorrect gate decisions or erode stakeholder confidence, slowing adoption and scaling.
risks.mitigation: Run parallel validation against known deployments, document assumptions, and implement multi-source aggregation/custom hooks where needed; delay enforcement decisions until metrics pass validation criteria.

risks.title: Roadmap pressure to onboard additional products before pilot maturity
risks.description: Stakeholders are requesting additional app onboarding before the pilot has stabilized templates, validation criteria, and automation, creating pull to scale ahead of demonstrated repeatability.
risks.impact_description: Context switching and overcommitment could dilute focus, increase defects, and slow time-to-green for the core platform.
risks.mitigation: Communicate entry criteria for new apps, share a phased scaling plan (pilot → validate → template → expand), and provide periodic executive checkpoints on readiness metrics

risks.title: Cocounsel Legal MFE bundling + QA cycle limits Diamond Lane
risks.description: CoCounsel MFEs ship as bundled release sets with multi-day QA/code-freeze validation and heavy UI E2E testing; MFEs aren’t reliably independently releasable due to container/dependency coupling. Current Diamond Lane eligibilty evaluation design doesn't support bundles with multiple different release versions for each app.  (Owners: CoCounsel Legal Eng + QA/Release Mgmt)
risks.impact_description: Original scope of repos cannot be validated for release as a deployment bundle with current DL evaluation design or rearchitecting of software dependencies; threatens OKR timelines if enablement is defined as demonstrated deployment behavior change specifically for MFEs
risks.mitigation: Pursue Diamond Lane work on backend services (llmproxy) better suited for isolated release; Continue enhancement efforts for MFEs - formalize push-button secrets/config workflow; pursue incremental integration-test improvements to reduce manual QA dependencies.

risks.title: Cocounsel Legal DORA metric accuracy and trustworthiness (PORT extraction query and Cumulus logging)
risks.description: Port utilizes an extraction query to fetch Cumulus deployment logs in the Datadog Software Delivery account for DORA metric reporting. The extraction query does not pick up on "deployment-engine" and "simple_static_content_deployer" service types. (owners: Cumulus Dev + PORT Team)
risks.impact_description: Missing DORA metric reporting in PORT for MFEs.
risks.mitigation: Cumulus update to log "simple_static_content_deployer" service appropriately; Cocounsel Legal update cumulus version, update PORT extraction query to fetch "deployment-engine" and "simple_static_content_deployer" service types; Long term - adjust cumulus deployment logging to reduce conditions required in PORT extraction query.

risks.title: Automated rollback for Materia
risks.description: Materia has a single workflow that deploys all services in a rolling fashion as a release set and end to end tests that validates all services at once. This is partly due to a dependency on shared database schemas across services. Rolling back releases that contain db migrations after a deployment completes (without circuit breaker) requires significant development changes to deployment logic with implications to operational complexity.
risks.impact_description: Automating rollback post release for application only changes provides limited value above existing deployment circuit breaker capability and would execute against all services in a release set, not just ones facing issues.
risks.mitigation: Focus pilot on application only releases and rely on circuit breaker capabilities to stop unhealthy deployments in the near term; align with Materia engineering on plans for expanded feature flag use; ensure post-deployment validations page out on degraded customer experience.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

FedRAMP – Akkadia is deploying Akkadia as the secure content platform for CoCounsel Legal Research in AWS GovCloud, replacing S3 storage and enabling Tabular Analysis within the FedRAMP boundary. This matters because it aligns FedRAMP and commercial architectures, strengthens security and compliance, and unlocks advanced Legal Research capabilities for regulated government customers without disrupting the existing Moderate authorization.

Overall, the project is 49% complete toward the 01 Sep 2026 readiness target. GovCloud Dev/QA deployment is 53% complete against a 01 Jul 2026 plan and GovCloud UAT/Prod readiness is 44% complete against a 01 Sep 2026 plan, with architecture and scope alignment already 100% complete as of 13 May 2026.

Overall status is Green, driven by Akkadia GovCloud Dev/QA and UAT/Prod milestones tracking to plan with no schedule variance.

## Milestones

- Project Kick-Off was completed, with charter and governance confirmed, on 27 Mar 2026.
- Architecture and scope alignment for FedRAMP Akkadia, including container platform and infrastructure-as-code decisions, was finalized on 13 May 2026.
- Achieve GovCloud Dev/QA readiness in US Gov East, with Akkadia deployed and core capabilities validated, by 01 Jul 2026.
- Complete GovCloud UAT/Prod readiness in US Gov East, including Legal Research data migration from S3 and production validation, and complete overall project delivery with FedRAMP SCR authorization and 3PAO audit by 01 Sep 2026.
- Formally close the FedRAMP – Akkadia project with governance sign off by 31 Mar 2027.

risks.title: GovCloud feature gaps may require Akkadia design adjustments
risks.description: Differences in AWS GovCloud feature availability versus commercial regions may require Akkadia design adjustments. If identified late or complex to resolve, these gaps could impact architecture timelines, delay environment readiness milestones, or limit parity with commercial CoCounsel.
risks.impact_description:
If critical Akkadia or supporting service features available in commercial AWS are limited or unavailable in GovCloud and require significant redesign:

Architecture validation may extend beyond plan, delaying Dev/QA readiness (1-Jul-2026).
Rework and retesting could push UAT/Prod readiness beyond September 2026.
Late SCR updates may drive documentation churn and review delays.
Full architectural parity with commercial CoCounsel may not be achieved, increasing long-term technical debt and operational complexity.

raised_by.name: FedRAMP - Akkadia Status report dated 2026-04-27 (Executive Summary)

risks.mitigation: Explicitly assess GovCloud feature differences during architecture validation by comparing commercial Akkadia patterns to GovCloud capabilities early, identifying required design changes, and incorporating them into technical designs before build-out advances. Use early security documentation and review cycles to ensure continued FedRAMP alignment.

risks.title: Akkadia as largest new FedRAMP risk surface in Packet #2
risks.description: As Akkadia is new to the FedRAMP boundary, late identification of FedRAMP security or architectural gaps for Akkadia could delay GovCloud milestones, slow SCR approval, increase 3PAO remediation cost, and risk continuity of the existing Moderate authorization.
risks.impact_description: Late findings could delay GovCloud Dev/QA and UAT/Prod milestones, slow or complicate FedRAMP Significant Change Request (SCR) approval, increase 3PAO findings and remediation scope, drive additional cost and resource demand, and put continuity of the existing FedRAMP Moderate authorization at risk.

raised_by.name: FedRAMP - Akkadia Status report dated 2026-04-27 (Executive Summary)

risks.mitigation: Apply early discovery and disciplined governance to Akkadia onboarding in GovCloud, validating security, architecture, and FedRAMP boundary alignment upfront. Reuse proven commercial Akkadia patterns—adapted for GovCloud as needed—and embed these checks into early architecture and security documentation to identify and resolve high‑impact gaps ahead of Dev/QA and UAT/Prod readiness.

Outcome: Confirm Terraform as the long‑term solution or identify residual gaps requiring Cumulus.

assumptions.title: Datadog GovCloud account creation will complete independently of infrastructure installation and not delay monitoring readiness
assumptions.description: The project assumes that creation of the required Datadog accounts for GovCloud can proceed as a standalone activity, independent of the Akkadia infrastructure installation in GovCloud, and that Gregory will complete the in-progress tickets without impacting the non-prod schedule.

owner.name: Gregory (Datadog / Monitoring owner referenced by John)

assumptions.rationale_basis: In the 2026-05-27 planning meeting, John clarified that Datadog account creation is standalone and does not depend on completion of the GovCloud infrastructure installation. He also noted that Gregory reported the Datadog-related tickets as "still in progress" and will update the team when finalized. Alyssa agreed to remove the (incorrect) dependency linkage.
assumptions.validity_explanation: John has direct confirmation from Gregory that account tickets are in progress, and he has explicitly corrected the project plan to remove an unnecessary dependency on infrastructure installation. However, completion timing and any unforeseen technical prerequisites for Datadog remain uncertain until accounts are live and integrated.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If Datadog account creation is delayed or blocked, escalate to Gregory’s management and platform/monitoring leadership, prioritize the tickets as critical for FedRAMP observability, and, if necessary, temporarily rely on alternative logging/monitoring (e.g., CloudWatch alone) while updating timelines for full Datadog integration and associated control evidence.
assumptions.validation_method: Track status of the Datadog account tickets with Gregory and confirm account availability and access; validate that Akkadia services in non-prod can successfully send metrics and logs to Datadog before non-prod completion.

assumptions.title: Clear cross-partition network limitations will not apply because Clear will not be used in a hosted or shared fashion
assumptions.description: During the 2026-05-29 FedRAMP Akkadia planning meeting, Kamaluddin Mohammed stated that for the "Rust partition / Clear" dependency (referenced as line 12 in the tracker), the Clear team confirmed they will not use Clear in a hosted or shared fashion. As a result, previously expected cross-partition network limitations for Clear are no longer applicable and the related blocker can be removed.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Earlier planning assumed potential cross-partition network limitations for Clear, creating a dependency and perceived blocker (tracked as line 12). In the 2026-05-29 meeting, Kamaluddin relayed that Clear confirmed they will not use a hosted or shared deployment, eliminating the cross-partition scenario and allowing the team to treat the item as complete.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Clear’s confirmed decision not to use a hosted or shared deployment directly removes the cross-partition use case that drove the original concern. Because this is a straightforward architectural choice under Clear’s control and was communicated through the platform owner, it significantly reduces the likelihood that cross-partition limitations will impact the project. However, as with any upstream system, there remains a small chance that Clear’s requirements could change in the future.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If Clear later requires a hosted/shared deployment, immediately re-open the dependency, re-assess cross-partition network limitations with Network/Platform teams, add the necessary design and implementation tasks back into the plan, and adjust schedule expectations to account for additional firewall and routing work.
assumptions.validation_method: Rely on Clear’s current deployment decision and periodically reconfirm with Clear stakeholders during architecture or dependency reviews to ensure they are not shifting to a hosted/shared model that would reintroduce cross-partition needs.

assumptions.title: Akkadia can be instantiated in AWS GovCloud and approved via a FedRAMP Significant Change Request while maintaining Moderate authorization
assumptions.description: The project assumes that Akkadia can be established from the ground up in AWS GovCloud and successfully approved as part of the existing FedRAMP system through a Significant Change Request, without requiring a new authorization or disrupting the current Moderate ATO.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The purpose statement explicitly states that Akkadia will be introduced into the FedRAMP boundary via a FedRAMP Significant Change Request to maintain continuity of the existing Moderate authorization.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The FedRAMP framework and the project’s existing Moderate authorization support the concept of managing substantial architecture changes through SCRs. However, the precise acceptability of introducing Akkadia via SCR depends on detailed boundary definitions, risk assessments, and agency acceptance, which have not yet been formally finalized for this change.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If the SCR path is not accepted or proves insufficient, prepare to adjust the authorization strategy (e.g., broader reassessment or incremental authorization), extend timelines, and potentially sequence Akkadia adoption in stages, while keeping a fallback path of continued S3 usage to avoid disruption to authorized services.
assumptions.validation_method: Engage early with Fortreum (3PAO) and the FedRAMP Program Office to confirm the SCR approach, boundary definition, and documentation expectations, and obtain formal acceptance of the SCR path as part of the FedRAMP process.

assumptions.title: All existing FedRAMP Legal Research data can be migrated from S3 to Akkadia with zero data loss
assumptions.description: The project assumes it can migrate all existing FedRAMP Legal Research data from the current Amazon S3 storage to Akkadia without any data loss, ensuring continuity of historical content and research results.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The purpose statement explicitly calls out migrating all existing FedRAMP Legal Research data with zero data loss as an objective of the project, indicating that planning and expectations are set on this outcome.
assumptions.validity_explanation: While zero data loss is technically challenging, careful design of migration procedures, robust backup and validation strategies, and repeated dress rehearsals can make it achievable. However, until real data migrations are successfully completed and validated, this remains an assumption rather than a proven fact.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If minor discrepancies or losses are detected, leverage backups and logs to restore affected data and, if needed, rerun portions of the migration. If significant issues arise, roll back to the S3-based solution temporarily while revising migration tooling and plans before attempting another cutover.
assumptions.validation_method: Execute test migrations and reconciliation in non‑production environments, perform checksums and record‑level comparisons, and validate functional search and retrieval across a representative dataset before production cutover.

assumptions.title: Service continuity for FedRAMP CoCounsel Legal Research will be maintained during Akkadia onboarding and data migration
assumptions.description: The initiative assumes that the introduction of Akkadia, Turbo backend integration, and data migration from S3 can be completed while maintaining service continuity for FedRAMP Legal Research users, with minimal disruption.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The purpose statement notes that the project is intentionally scoped to maintain service continuity while delivering new capabilities and completing the data migration.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The involvement of SRE, service management, and architecture roles in the stakeholder list indicates that operational impacts are being considered. Nonetheless, the exact behavior under production load and integration with Turbo and GovCloud infrastructure is not yet fully validated.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Plan for maintenance windows and communicate them to stakeholders, prepare a tested rollback path to the prior storage configuration, and ensure incident response playbooks are ready to handle any unexpected service degradation or outages during cutover.
assumptions.validation_method: Conduct non‑production failover and deployment tests, simulate cutover scenarios, and monitor performance and availability metrics during pilot or phased deployments before full production migration.

assumptions.title: The Akkadia-based FedRAMP architecture will provide a scalable foundation for future Legal Research enhancements
assumptions.description: The project assumes that by aligning the FedRAMP architecture with the commercial CoCounsel baseline through Akkadia, it will establish a scalable, extensible platform that supports future FedRAMP Legal Research enhancements beyond this initial scope.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The purpose statement describes the project as creating a scalable foundation for future FedRAMP Legal Research enhancements by aligning architecture with the commercial baseline and leveraging Akkadia’s platform capabilities.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Architectural alignment with a proven commercial baseline increases confidence that the FedRAMP implementation can support future enhancements. However, differences in compliance constraints, infrastructure (GovCloud), and agency requirements may introduce limitations that are not yet fully understood.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If scalability or extensibility limitations are discovered, plan targeted architectural refactoring, introduce supporting services or patterns that better accommodate future features, and adjust roadmap expectations for new FedRAMP Legal Research capabilities.
assumptions.validation_method: Review target architecture against anticipated future use cases, stress-test scalability of Akkadia in GovCloud, and compare patterns with the commercial implementation to confirm reusability and extensibility.

assumptions.title: Cloudflare will not be required for Akkadia because it is a backend-only service and failover will be handled via Route 53 or similar mechanisms
assumptions.description: The planning discussion on 2026-04-29 indicated a working assumption that Cloudflare is not needed for Akkadia, because Akkadia is a backend document storage service with no direct customer-facing front end. Both Ervan Setiawan and Peter France noted that Akkadia and Turbo are backend services, and Kamaluddin Mohammed confirmed that Akkadia currently relies on Route 53 for failover in commercial environments. While a Cloudflare line item is being kept open "for awareness" pending final design, the implicit assumption is that no additional Cloudflare work will be required specifically for Akkadia.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Initial FedRAMP Akkadia planning sessions concluded that Akkadia is not directly exposed to customers and already uses Route 53-based failover in commercial deployments. In the 2026-05-13 planning meeting, Kamaluddin Mohammed stated that the Cloudflare sizing item could be removed entirely, reinforcing the expectation that Cloudflare will not be needed for Akkadia.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Recent planning decisions (2026-05-13 meeting) removed the Cloudflare sizing task for Akkadia, with Kamaluddin Mohammed explicitly stating that the item can go away as not needed. Combined with existing Route 53-based patterns in commercial deployments, this substantially increases confidence that Cloudflare will not be required for Akkadia in FedRAMP.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If Cloudflare is later determined to be required for Akkadia, reintroduce Cloudflare tasks into the project plan, update architecture diagrams, coordinate sizing and configuration with Cloud Networking, and adjust timelines to cover any new work and FedRAMP evidence updates.
assumptions.validation_method: Finalize network and traffic management design for Akkadia, confirming that all relevant endpoints use Route 53 or similar mechanisms without Cloudflare. Obtain agreement from Cloud Networking and CoCounsel architecture that Cloudflare is not in the critical path.

assumptions.title: GovCloud CI/CD GitHub integration for Akkadia will be BAU reuse from previous project

During the 2026-04-29 meeting, Ervan Setiawan noted that the GovCloud GitHub integration task was copied from a previous project plan and "should be just BAU," with Kyle identified as the contact, and did not anticipate needing a dedicated meeting.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The CI/CD GitHub integration task for GovCloud was explicitly described as a copy from a previous project plan, and Ervan stated that it should be business-as-usual, implying that existing, proven patterns are expected to work without major changes.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Current evidence suggests that this is a straightforward reuse of established GovCloud CI/CD patterns, and specific contacts (Kyle) have already been identified. However, until actual Akkadia pipelines are created and validated in GovCloud, there remains some uncertainty about subtle differences in requirements or configurations.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If reuse of existing GovCloud GitHub CI/CD patterns is not possible, escalate early to establish a dedicated design and implementation workstream for Akkadia CI/CD, allocate additional engineering time, and adjust environment readiness dates accordingly. Ensure any new patterns are reviewed and approved by security/compliance before widespread use.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm with Kyle and Anders that existing GovCloud GitHub CI/CD patterns can be reused for Akkadia without significant changes, and validate that required repositories, pipelines, and permissions are configured and functional in a test deployment.
