This creates a misalignment between product support and central operations, reduces coverage on AIOps alerts, and further delays the ability to rely on Event Management and to cut over from Datadog-direct incidents.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Depends on ServiceNow role and access configuration managed by the ServiceNow platform team (e.g., Khanna, Prastuti) and on GCC onboarding processes; affects the Legal Tracker AIOps pilot, GCC readiness for future products, and the previously identified risk about teams losing visibility during cutover.

issues.title: AIOps-generated incident priorities are higher than corresponding alert priorities
issues.description: Incidents created by ServiceNow AIOps from group alerts are being assigned higher priorities (often P1) than expected based on the underlying alert severity and priority. Analysis of the 'create incident TR presets' subflow and related flow actions shows that incident impact and urgency are set to their highest values whenever the alert priority group or severity is 1 or 2, which forces the incident priority matrix to produce P1 incidents. In addition, the alert 'priority group' field is driven by an out-of-the-box priority score that may not align with Thomson Reuters expectations, and current event rules map Datadog monitor priority into alert severity but do not explicitly map priority into the alert priority group. As a result, Legal Tracker alerts with moderate priorities (e.g., P3) can still generate P1 incidents, causing misaligned incident priorities compared to direct Datadog-created incidents.
issues.impact_assessment: The mismatch between alert priority and AIOps-generated incident priority causes Legal Tracker incidents to be raised as P1 when the underlying monitor/alert priority is lower (e.g., P2 or P3). This over-escalation inflates the number of P1 incidents, drives unnecessary major incident engagement, and creates inconsistency between incidents created directly from Datadog and those created via AIOps. It undermines trust in the AIOps implementation, complicates incident reporting and metrics, and makes Legal Tracker and GCC reluctant to rely on AIOps-driven incidents until priority behavior is corrected.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Depends on ServiceNow vendor configuration of the 'create incident TR presets' subflow and priority score thresholds; relies on correct Datadog monitor priority values and current event rules that map Datadog priority into alert severity; interacts with the ServiceNow incident priority matrix and incident management practice settings.
issues.resolution:
Review and adjust the incident creation flow and priority mapping so that incident impact and urgency are derived appropriately from alert severity and priority group without systematically elevating incidents to P1. This includes: (1) analysing the 'create incident TR presets' subflow and its scripted flow actions to change logic that currently sets incident impact/urgency to 1 when alert priority group or severity is 1 or 2; (2) confirming how the alert 'priority group' field is populated from the out-of-the-box priority score and whether threshold properties should be tuned instead of custom code changes; and (3) ensuring event rules that map Datadog monitor priority to alert severity and priority group produce incident priorities aligned with TR's incident priority matrix. Proposed changes will be validated on sample Legal Tracker alerts and incidents before wider rollout.  
*Datadog priority and service directly being transferred to the incident

issues.title: Datadog P3 alerts mapped as critical severity in ServiceNow alerts for Legal Tracker
issues.description: In the ServiceNow production instance, Legal Tracker alerts coming from Datadog with monitor priority P3 are being mapped to critical severity on the ServiceNow alert records. As a result, incidents created from these alerts appear as P1, even though the underlying Datadog monitors are configured as P3. The problem appears to originate in the custom ServiceNow event field mapping rule "Datadog map alert priority to severity" not behaving as it did in dev, potentially due to rule ordering or execution context.
issues.impact_assessment: Because P3 Datadog alerts for Legal Tracker are being mapped to critical severity in ServiceNow, any incidents generated from these alerts are incorrectly created as P1. This mis-prioritization would cause an excessive number of P1 incidents, distort SLAs and reporting, and could trigger unnecessary major incident workflows and on-call paging. The team has therefore disabled automatic incident creation and set the incident-creation subflow to manual to avoid flooding operations with false P1s, which in turn delays full end-to-end testing and cutover to the AIOps event-first model.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Depends on the correct configuration and execution order of the ServiceNow event field mapping rule "Datadog map alert priority to severity" and on availability of representative Legal Tracker alerts from Datadog (including synthetics) for testing. Affects the ability to safely enable AIOps-driven incident creation for Legal Tracker without generating spurious P1 incidents.
issues.resolution:
Investigate and correct the ServiceNow event field mapping rule that converts Datadog alert_priority values (P1–P5) into ServiceNow alert severity. Specifically: (1) review the "Datadog map alert priority to severity" event field mapping script in production; (2) adjust the rule order so that it executes before other mapping rules (e.g., synthetic-related mappings at order 20/25); (3) rerun tests with known P3 Legal Tracker alerts (including synthetics) to confirm that alert severity is set correctly; and (4) only after the mapping is verified, re-enable automatic incident creation for Legal Tracker alerts, starting with manual creation from alerts and then switching back to automatic once behaviour is stable.
Refer to Issue#15

issues.title: Datadog to ServiceNow production OAuth authentication failures (401 errors)
issues.description: After pointing the Datadog webhook to the ServiceNow production instance, Datadog receives HTTP 401 responses when attempting to send events, indicating authentication/authorization failures.
issues.impact_assessment: Until authentication between Datadog and the ServiceNow production instance is working, no production events can be ingested for AIOps, blocking end‑to‑end testing of connectivity, plugin behaviour, and production cutover readiness.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Depends on correct OAuth credentials and roles in ServiceNow, Datadog auth method configuration, and potentially ServiceNow plugin health.
issues.resolution: Validate and correct the OAuth client configuration (token URL, client ID, client secret, scopes) and ServiceNow user permissions; if issues persist, escalate to Doug for deeper platform‑level troubleshooting.

dependencies.title: Datadog webhook configuration for Legal Tracker
dependencies.description: The AIOps implementation for Legal Tracker depends on Datadog’s webhook handler being correctly configured (URL, auth, payload, handler naming) to send events to the appropriate ServiceNow instance.
dependencies.dependent_on: Datadog webhook handler and auth methods managed by Rodriguez, Luis Jorge and Knaack, Gregory
dependencies.consumer: ServiceNow AIOps / Event Management for Legal Tracker
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If the webhook is not correctly configured and authenticated, ServiceNow will not receive production events and the AIOps solution cannot be validated or go live.
dependencies.mitigation: Route initial webhook traffic to dev while testing configurations; involve ServiceNow vendor (Doug) to troubleshoot OAuth/auth issues; fall back to existing direct Datadog→ServiceNow incident integration if needed.

dependencies.title: Datadog hygiene programme alignment with AIOps
dependencies.description: Successful scale-out of AIOps requires alignment between the Datadog hygiene programme (standard monitor configuration, tagging) and AIOps-specific needs (payload, severity/priority usage).
dependencies.dependent_on: GCC observability practice (Heymann, Damian) and platform engineering
dependencies.consumer: All future TR products to be onboarded to AIOps / event management
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If Datadog hygiene and AIOps standards are not aligned, future onboarding may be inconsistent, with some teams following conflicting standards, increasing rework and governance overhead.
dependencies.mitigation: Feed AIOps requirements discovered in Legal Tracker into Mikes hygiene programme and adjust standards iteratively; use onboarding checklists to enforce minimum requirements even before full alignment.

dependencies.title: FedRAMP governance approval and AIOps plugin enablement before ServiceNow clone
dependencies.description: AIOps integration for FedRAMP environments depends on completing FedRAMP governance documentation and enabling the required ServiceNow AIOps/Event Management plugins before the scheduled ServiceNow clone over the weekend so that configurations are cascaded to lower environments.
dependencies.dependent_on: FedRAMP governance/compliance review and ServiceNow AIOps plugin configuration managed by ROE, TIM and Kolluru, Prudhvi Yaswanth
dependencies.consumer: AIOps/Event Management implementation in FedRAMP-scoped ServiceNow environments
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If FedRAMP governance documentation is not completed and required AIOps plugins are not enabled before the clone, lower environments may not have the necessary configurations to support AIOps testing and validation in FedRAMP scope, potentially delaying compliance approval and rollout for those environments.
dependencies.mitigation: If the clone occurs before governance documentation or plugin enablement is complete, perform a follow-up configuration pass on lower environments post-clone, and coordinate a subsequent clone or targeted migration to propagate AIOps plugins and settings once FedRAMP approval is obtained.

dependencies.title: Enable AIOps/Event Management in FedRAMP ServiceNow instance
dependencies.description: AIOps/Event Management rollout for FedRAMP-hosted applications (including HighQ and other FedRAMP services) depends on enabling and configuring the same AIOps/Event Management modules and integrations in the FedRAMP ServiceNow environment as in the enterprise instance, while complying with FedRAMP-specific approval and compliance requirements.
dependencies.dependent_on: ServiceNow FedRAMP instance configuration, FedRAMP compliance approvals, and guidance from Vinay Kumar and FedRAMP representatives
dependencies.consumer: FedRAMP-hosted applications requiring AIOps/Event Management (e.g., HighQ and other FedRAMP services)
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If AIOps/Event Management is not enabled in the FedRAMP ServiceNow instance by the end of June 2026, FedRAMP applications will continue to generate unmanaged alert noise, delaying noise reduction and correlation benefits and creating divergence between enterprise and FedRAMP operational models, which could impact the onboarding roadmap through September.
dependencies.mitigation: Tim Roe and Vinay Kumar will continue coordinating FedRAMP governance approvals and plugin enablement; if end-of-June enablement proves infeasible, the team will (1) adjust the onboarding roadmap to deprioritize FedRAMP-hosted applications temporarily, and (2) plan a follow-on configuration and clone/migration cycle once FedRAMP approvals and technical changes are complete.

dependencies.title: Resolution of CI/service association behaviour by CMDB resource and ServiceNow consultant
dependencies.description: Legal Tracker AIOps alert management and incident routing depend on a CMDB resource (identified by John) and ServiceNow consultant Doug completing analysis and configuration changes to fix CIservice association behaviour so that impacted services populate correctly in AIOps-generated incidents.
dependencies.dependent_on: ServiceNow CMDB expert resource identified by John and Dougs configuration changes to CI/service association logic
dependencies.consumer: ServiceNow AIOps/Event Management implementation for Legal Tracker and future onboarded products
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If CI/service association behaviour is not corrected in a timely manner, impacted services will remain missing from AIOps-generated incidents, making alert categorization and routing difficult and preventing cutover from legacy Datadog-direct incident creation. This will delay full realization of AIOps benefits and may erode stakeholder confidence.
dependencies.mitigation: Talia Loch to schedule a follow-up session next week with the identified CMDB resource and Doug to review design options and agree next steps. In the interim, continue using the temporary approach of passing service and priority from Datadog while closely monitoring incident behaviour, and keep Legal Tracker stakeholders informed that cutover is dependent on this dependency being resolved.

dependencies.title: ServiceNow vendor configuration of event rules, responder rules, and mappings
dependencies.description: The project relies on the ServiceNow vendor (Doug and team) to define and adjust event rules, alert correlation, CI binding logic, and incident mapping logic in the dev instance and to prepare these for promotion to production.
dependencies.dependent_on: ServiceNow professional services team
dependencies.consumer: TR AIOps / Event Management implementation for Legal Tracker and future products
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If vendor rule and mapping work is delayed, the team cannot fully validate CI binding, incident creation behaviour, or implement advanced correlation and responder rules, potentially delaying go-live.
dependencies.mitigation: Use a minimal set of out-of-the-box rules plus three TR-specific rules for initial go-live; capture vendor changes in update sets for later refinement; maintain existing Datadog→ServiceNow incident integration as fallback.

dependencies.title: Establish monitoring governance practice and ownership for Legal Tracker event management
dependencies.description: Formal monitoring governance must be in place so Datadog and Azure Alerts remain the detection layer under a controlled, standardized configuration model. This includes standardized thresholds for infrastructure monitors (~20%), auditing and enforcement of classification standards, and clearly defined ownership of monitor configuration governance for Legal Tracker (and later other products) before and during AIOps rollout.

owner.name: Service Management / GCC monitoring governance lead (e.g., Heymann, Damian)

dependencies.dependent_on: Monitoring governance practice and owner (GCC / Platform Engineering) being defined and operational
dependencies.consumer: ServiceNow Event Management implementation for Legal Tracker
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Without a formal monitoring governance practice and owner, Legal Tracker monitors may continue to use inconsistent thresholds and classifications, leading to noisy or misclassified events entering ServiceNow. This will reduce the effectiveness of filtering, prioritization, and correlation, and could undermine confidence in the AIOps solution.
dependencies.mitigation: Proceed with Legal Tracker using interim governance based on existing Datadog hygiene standards while accelerating definition of a formal governance model. Use Legal Tracker as the pilot to refine governance artifacts (policies, review process, exception handling) and then institutionalize them via GCC and Platform Engineering.

dependencies.title: Select and implement integration mechanism for consolidating monitoring sources into ServiceNow
dependencies.description: To redirect events from Datadog and Azure Alerts into the ServiceNow event table, an integration mechanism must be selected and implemented (e.g., Lambda-based integration vs Service Graph Connector). Monitor inventory and integration design must support consolidation of Datadog, Azure Alerts, and cloud-native monitors into a single event ingestion path for Legal Tracker.
dependencies.dependent_on: Chosen integration mechanism (e.g., AWS Lambda integration, Service Graph Connector) and completed monitor inventory for Legal Tracker
dependencies.consumer: ServiceNow Event Management ingestion for Legal Tracker
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If an integration mechanism is not selected and implemented in time, Legal Tracker events from Datadog, Azure Alerts, and other cloud-native monitors cannot be redirected into the ServiceNow event table. This will block the architectural shift from direct-to-incident to event-first processing and delay all downstream capabilities (filtering, correlation, prioritization).
dependencies.mitigation: Use the simplest viable integration (e.g., existing Datadog webhook plus incremental Azure integration) as an MVP while evaluating Service Graph Connector or Lambda for longer-term standardization. Maintain the legacy Datadog→incident path as fallback until consolidated ingestion is proven.

dependencies.title: Define event taxonomy for informational, warning, and exception events
dependencies.description: An event taxonomy must be defined for Legal Tracker monitors to distinguish informational, warning, and exception events. This taxonomy is the basis for filtering, classification rules, and event prioritization in ServiceNow Event Management and will guide which events generate incidents versus being suppressed or treated as informational.

owner.name: Incident Management and AIOps design leads (e.g., Heymann, Damian; Rutherford, Chris)

dependencies.dependent_on: Agreement on Legal Tracker event taxonomy (informational vs warning vs exception) and documentation of how it maps to ServiceNow severity and incident policies
dependencies.consumer: Event filtering and prioritization configuration for Legal Tracker in ServiceNow
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Without a defined event taxonomy, filtering and prioritization rules cannot be consistently implemented. This will result in inconsistent suppression of informational events, potential creation of non-actionable incidents, and difficulty standardizing behaviour across monitors and products.
dependencies.mitigation: Draft an initial, directional taxonomy for Legal Tracker based on current incident practices and iterate during early AIOps usage. Use lessons learned to refine and formalize the taxonomy before broader rollout.

dependencies.title: Define incident creation policy for AIOps events
dependencies.description: An explicit incident creation policy must be defined for Legal Tracker to decide when correlated events should generate incidents versus remaining as events or being handled through auto-remediation. This governs whether every actionable event creates an incident or whether some remediation can occur under event records only.

owner.name: AD Al-Ghourabi (TR Technology) with input from Service Management leadership

dependencies.dependent_on: Agreement on incident creation criteria (e.g., only exceptions create incidents; some remediations handled at event level) and configuration of corresponding rules in ServiceNow
dependencies.consumer: ServiceNow Incident Management behaviour for AIOps-generated events in Legal Tracker
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If incident creation policy remains undefined, AIOps may either create too many incidents (replicating the 1:1 pattern) or too few (risking missed incidents). This uncertainty will delay tuning of incident rules and hinder safe cutover from the legacy Datadog incident path.
dependencies.mitigation: Define a provisional incident creation policy for Legal Tracker (e.g., incidents only for exception-level events and primary correlated groups) and validate during a controlled observation period, adjusting policy before applying it as a standard for other products.

dependencies.title: Define notification tiers for after-hours paging vs next-business-day alerts
dependencies.description: Notification tiering rules must be defined to determine what event or incident severities trigger after-hours pages versus next-business-day notifications for Legal Tracker. This is needed to reduce notification noise and align on-call behaviour with the new alert-centric AIOps model.

owner.name: Service Management / Incident Management leadership (e.g., Heymann, Damian)

dependencies.dependent_on: Agreed set of notification tiers mapping event/incident severity to after-hours paging vs next-business-day notification, and corresponding configuration in ServiceNow on-call and notification modules
dependencies.consumer: On-call paging and notification behaviour for Legal Tracker and future AIOps-onboarded products
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Without defined notification tiers, teams may continue to receive excessive after-hours pages for non-critical events or insufficient notifications for true exceptions. This undermines one of the key benefits of AIOps (notification reduction) and may cause resistance from on-call engineers.
dependencies.mitigation: Adopt an interim rule (e.g., only P1/P2 incidents from primary correlated alerts generate after-hours pages) based on current practice, then refine notification tiers once incident creation and prioritization behaviour is stable.

dependencies.title: Improve KB and runbook quality to enable phased automation and AI-assisted resolutions
dependencies.description: KB articles and runbooks must be improved for Legal Tracker so that incidents arriving with enriched context from correlated events can leverage reliable remediation content. This is a prerequisite for introducing automated remediation and AI-recommended resolutions in later phases of Event Management.

owner.name: Knowledge management and AIOps remediation lead (e.g., Doug – ServiceNow consultant – in partnership with GCC)

dependencies.dependent_on: Consolidated, high-quality KB articles and runbooks for top Legal Tracker incident scenarios, integrated with ServiceNow knowledge and Flow Designer
dependencies.consumer: Later-phase AIOps capabilities (automated remediation, Now Assist / LEAP suggestions) for Legal Tracker and other products
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If KB and runbook quality is not improved, later-phase AIOps capabilities such as AI-suggested resolutions and automated remediation workflows will be ineffective or inaccurate. This will limit MTTR improvements and delay realization of higher-stage value from the AIOps program.
dependencies.mitigation: Delay automation-focused capabilities for Legal Tracker until core ingestion, correlation, and incident behaviour are stable, while running a parallel workstream to uplift KB/runbook content for the most frequent incident types.

decisions.title: Use out-of-the-box ServiceNow AIOps incident priority calculation instead of custom impact/urgency event fields
decisions.description: The team will not persist custom impact and urgency fields on ServiceNow event records to mirror Datadog values. Instead, Datadog monitors will be configured with appropriate severity and priority, and ServiceNow will use its out‑of‑the‑box logic (including severity and alert type) to calculate incident impact and urgency.
decisions.rationale: Custom impact/urgency fields add complexity and diverge from the out‑of‑the‑box product design. Using ServiceNow’s standard AIOps logic simplifies maintenance and ensures consistency as the solution scales across products, even though it requires additional work to train teams on correct use of severity and priority in Datadog.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Introduce custom impact/urgency fields on events populated directly from Datadog and map them to incidents.
2) Stay out-of-the-box by configuring severity/priority in Datadog and relying on ServiceNow’s AIOps engine to derive impact/urgency for incidents.
3) Hybrid approach using both custom fields and AIOps calculations.
decisions.dependencies_linked: ServiceNow CI binding and incident creation behaviour; Datadog monitor configuration standards; removal of custom event fields added by Yash.

decisions.title: Legal Tracker AIOps to proceed using minimal rule set (out-of-the-box plus three TR rules)
decisions.description: For Legal Tracker go‑live, the team will rely primarily on out‑of‑the‑box ServiceNow event rules with a small set of three Thomson Reuters–specific rules, rather than waiting to design a comprehensive custom rule library.
decisions.rationale: Using a minimal rule set allows the team to start realizing AIOps value sooner and avoids over‑engineering for the first product. Additional rules can be added iteratively once real event data and behaviours are better understood.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Design extensive custom event and correlation rules for Legal Tracker before go‑live.
2) Use out-of-the-box rules only.
3) Use out-of-the-box rules plus a small number of TR-specific rules for initial go-live.
decisions.dependencies_linked: ServiceNow vendor rule configuration; Datadog payload contents; cutover planning for incidents.

decisions.title: Event forwarding from ServiceNow production to dev/QA is not a go-live blocker
decisions.description: The team agreed that ServiceNow event forwarding from production to lower environments (dev and QA) is helpful for testing but is not required for the initial Legal Tracker go‑live.
decisions.rationale: Forwarding allows consistent test data across environments, but its absence does not prevent AIOps from functioning in production. Delaying go‑live until forwarding is perfect would unnecessarily slow delivery.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Make event forwarding a prerequisite for go-live.
2) Treat forwarding as a post-go-live improvement while focusing on production connectivity and incident behaviour.
decisions.dependencies_linked: ServiceNow event forwarding configuration managed by Yash; Datadog webhook pointing to production.

decisions.title: Pilot parallel incident run in QA before enabling AIOps incidents in production
decisions.description: Before AIOps begins creating incidents in production for Legal Tracker, the team plans a time‑boxed parallel run in a QA environment where AIOps incidents can be compared to existing Datadog‑driven incidents, to assess completeness and volume reduction.
decisions.rationale: A QA parallel run allows the team to validate that AIOps does not miss important incidents and provides incident volume reduction, without risking production operations or confusing support teams with duplicates.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Immediately enable AIOps incident creation in production and disable Datadog incidents.
2) Run AIOps alerts only in production and compare manually.
3) Run AIOps incidents in QA for a short period while keeping production unchanged, then decide on production enablement.
decisions.dependencies_linked: QA environment setup; ability to mirror event data into QA; cutover plan for disabling Datadog incidents per product.

decisions.title: Define notification tiers for after-hours vs next-business-day alerts
decisions.description: The team must decide what severity levels and event types trigger after-hours paging versus next-business-day notification for Legal Tracker, based on correlated incidents and event severity.

decision_owner.name: Service Management / Incident Management leadership (e.g., Heymann, Damian)

decisions.rationale: Tiered notifications reduce alert fatigue by ensuring that teams are only paged for true service-impacting exceptions while less severe events are handled during business hours.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Only P1 (and possibly P2) incidents generated from primary correlated alerts trigger after-hours pages; others become next-business-day notifications.
2) Include some high-severity warnings in after-hours paging for specific services.
3) Maintain current incident-based paging behaviour initially and gradually introduce alert-driven paging tiers.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Incident creation policy, on-call configuration on the ServiceNow alert/incident tables, and Legal Tracker on-call agreements.

decisions.title: Timebox QA observation period for new AIOps product onboardings
decisions.description: For new products being onboarded to AIOps/Event Management (such as ONESOURCE GTM4 and SIAM), the QA observation period for running their monitors and alerts through ServiceNow will be timeboxed to no more than three to four weeks, with a target of one to two weeks, to avoid prolonged onboarding and encourage iterative movement towards production.
decisions.rationale: AD emphasized the need to avoid letting QA observation drag on, preferring short, iterative cycles so that teams can move to production quickly while still gaining sufficient insight into alert grouping and rule behaviour.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Run QA observation for an open-ended period until all issues are resolved.
2) Timebox QA observation to a maximum of three to four weeks with a target of one to two weeks before deciding on production onboarding.
3) Skip QA observation and onboard directly to production using enterprise rules.
decisions.dependencies_linked: AIOps onboarding plans for ONESOURCE GTM4 and SIAM; Legal Tracker lessons learned; QA data ingestion for GTM4 and SIAM.

decisions.title: Proceed with onboarding ONESOURCE GTM4 and SIAM in parallel with caution
decisions.description: The team will initiate AIOps/Event Management onboarding for both ONESOURCE GTM4 and SIAM in parallel, while closely monitoring the workload and alert volumes from GTM4 and leveraging QA observation to understand and manage the expected high volume of findings.
decisions.rationale: Both GTM4 and SIAM generate significant alert volume and their teams are ready to engage. Despite concerns about the effort required for GTM4, the group agreed that starting with both, with a cautious and timeboxed QA approach, provides maximum learning and impact.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Onboard only ONESOURCE GTM4 first, then onboard SIAM later.
2) Onboard only SIAM first.
3) Onboard both ONESOURCE GTM4 and SIAM in parallel, with a timeboxed QA observation period and readiness assessments.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Readiness assessments for GTM4 and SIAM monitors; Datadog webhooks and QA event flow; Legal Tracker feedback influencing configuration adjustments.

decisions.title: Prioritize AIOps capabilities in sequence: ingestion → correlation & prioritization → notification → root cause & resolutions
decisions.description: For Legal Tracker, capability rollout will follow a defined order: (1) Alert ingestion (event-first processing) as the foundation; (2) Intelligent correlation as the highest-value capability; (3) Event prioritization and notification reduction; and (4) later-phase root cause identification and AI-suggested resolutions once correlation and data volume are sufficient.
decisions.rationale: Sequencing capabilities ensures a stable foundation before introducing advanced features. Ingestion and correlation deliver the highest immediate value by breaking the 1:1 event-to-incident pattern, while notification reduction and advanced root cause/AI resolutions depend on stable correlation, prioritization, and sufficient historical data.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Implement all capabilities at once (ingestion, correlation, prioritization, notification, root cause, AI resolutions).
2) Focus only on ingestion and correlation for MVP and defer all other capabilities.
3) Implement capabilities in the chosen sequence: ingestion → correlation & prioritization → notification → root cause & resolutions.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Ingestion readiness (integration mechanism), correlation tuning, event taxonomy definition, KB/runbook quality, and sufficient historical incident data.

decisions.title: Adopt deterministic Datadog monitor priority as MVP incident priority for Legal Tracker
decisions.description: For the Legal Tracker MVP, ServiceNow’s out-of-the-box incident priority calculation has been disabled and Datadog monitor priority is passed deterministically through to the incident priority. This patch aligns incident priority with existing Legal Tracker practices while the team gains experience with AIOps and prepares to tune non-deterministic priority behaviour in lower environments.
decisions.rationale: Legal Tracker and GCC are accustomed to deterministic incident priority based directly on Datadog monitors. Early trials of AIOps-native, non-deterministic priority were perceived as too aggressive (e.g., raising priority after only two alerts). To avoid blocking the production MVP and to meet previously communicated timelines, the team agreed to a temporary deterministic configuration as an MVP, while planning a ‘laboratory’ effort in dev/QA to tune native AIOps scoring before reintroducing it.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Keep ServiceNow out-of-the-box non-deterministic incident priority (based on CI importance, blast radius, and alert state).
2) Temporarily disable AIOps-native priority and deterministically map Datadog monitor priority directly to incident priority for Legal Tracker.
3) Delay Legal Tracker MVP until non-deterministic behaviour is fully tuned and accepted by the product team.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Linked to risk 'Reliance on temporary customizations for incident priority and CI binding instead of AIOps-native behaviour' and dependency 'ServiceNow vendor configuration of event rules, responder rules, and mappings'; also interacts with future tuning sessions in dev/QA for non-deterministic priority.

decisions.title: Use incident data from new ServiceNow instance (January 2026 onward) without backfilling legacy instance data for initial AIOps onboarding prioritization
decisions.description: For the first round of AIOps onboarding prioritization, the team will rely on incident data extracted from the new ServiceNow instance (approximately January 2026 onward) combined with existing alert data, and will not pursue extracting or merging historical incident data from the legacy ServiceNow instance at this stage.
decisions.rationale: Paul Berry judged that five months of incident data from the new ServiceNow instance is sufficient to reveal patterns and identify candidate applications for the top 40 AIOps migration list. Fetching and merging legacy incident data would consume additional effort without materially improving the directional signals needed for round-one prioritization. Any anomalies (e.g., applications with high recent incidents but lower historical alert ranking) will themselves be useful signals to investigate rather than reasons to delay decisions.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Extract and merge legacy ServiceNow incident data with new-instance data to create a full-year, like-for-like incident view.
2) Limit analysis to incident data from the new ServiceNow instance (January 2026 onward) and compare with existing alert data for prioritization.
3) Restrict both alert and incident datasets to a common time window starting January 2026, requiring additional re-extraction but still avoiding legacy system queries.
decisions.dependencies_linked: AIOps product prioritization spreadsheet; action for Rodriguez, Luis Jorge to add incident data column from new ServiceNow instance.
decisions.source_file_name: AIOps Product Onboarding Reg Sync 30 Apr.docx

decisions.title: Define ingestion scope for Legal Tracker monitors entering ServiceNow
decisions.description: The team needs to decide whether all Legal Tracker monitors will send events into the ServiceNow event table from the outset, or whether AIOps will start with a defined subset of monitors and expand in later phases.

decision_owner.name: TR AIOps leadership (e.g., Rutherford, Chris; AD Al-Ghourabi)

decisions.rationale: Ingestion scope affects both risk and value. Including all monitors maximizes observability and correlation opportunities but may introduce noise and configuration risk; starting with a subset reduces initial complexity but may limit early value and require additional rollout planning.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Route all Legal Tracker monitors into ServiceNow from day one.
2) Start with a defined subset of monitors (e.g., infrastructure and critical synthetics) and expand in Phase 2.
3) Pilot with only specific regions or monitor types before full ingestion.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Event ingestion dependencies (integration mechanism, monitor inventory) and filtering/correlation configuration for Legal Tracker.

decisions.title: Define Legal Tracker event taxonomy for informational, warning, and exception events
decisions.description: The project must agree on what constitutes informational, warning, and exception events for Legal Tracker monitors. This taxonomy will drive filtering, suppression, and classification rules in ServiceNow Event Management.

decision_owner.name: Incident Management and AIOps design leads (e.g., Heymann, Damian; Rutherford, Chris)

decisions.rationale: A clear event taxonomy is necessary to consistently suppress non-actionable events, classify exceptions that should create incidents, and align monitor configurations with business impact expectations.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Adopt a simple three-level taxonomy (informational, warning, exception) aligned with current incident severity definitions.
2) Use a more granular taxonomy (e.g., multiple warning levels) for synthetics versus infrastructure.
3) Defer to existing Datadog priority levels and map them directly to ServiceNow severities with minimal new taxonomy definition.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Event prioritization configuration, monitor classification standards, and Datadog hygiene programme alignment.

decisions.title: Set incident creation policy for AIOps-correlated events
decisions.description: A decision is required on whether every actionable event should create an incident or whether some remediation can occur at the event level without incident records, based on correlation and classification outcomes.

decision_owner.name: AD Al-Ghourabi (TR Technology) with Service Management leadership

decisions.rationale: Incident creation policy determines the balance between visibility and noise. Creating incidents for all actionable events maintains legacy visibility but risks retaining the 1:1 event-to-incident pattern; restricting incidents to true exceptions reduces noise but requires strong confidence in correlation and remediation processes.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Every actionable event creates an incident.
2) Only exception-level events (as defined by the event taxonomy) create incidents; informational and warning events remain as events.
3) Some remediations are executed and recorded at the event level only, with incidents created only if remediation fails or service impact is detected.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Correlation rule tuning, event taxonomy definition, and incident management SLAs for Legal Tracker.

decisions.title: Prioritise maturing GCC coverage for existing products before onboarding additional applications
decisions.description: For GCC onboarding and AIOps adoption, the programme will first focus on making products already on GCC (such as Legal Tracker and other tier 1 services) fully onboarded and working correctly under the new event-first, AI Ops-enabled model before expanding aggressively to additional products. This includes stabilising Datadog monitor hygiene, CI/CMDB service associations, and routing rules so the formula is proven before scaling.
decisions.rationale: AD emphasised that continuing to add more products without a proven, repeatable formula for GCC + AIOps onboarding risks spreading issues across a larger footprint. Ensuring that current GCC products are correctly onboarded, with stable routing and service-mapping, will provide a reusable pattern and reduce operational risk when scaling to the broader portfolio.

2) Prioritise making products already on GCC (e.g., Legal Tracker) fully onboarded and stable before onboarding additional products.
3) Attempt to do both simultaneously by onboarding many new products while also stabilising existing ones.

latest_report.content:
## **Executive Summary**

**Scope:** Cobalt Modernization is migrating key Westlaw components to AWS including OpenSearch migration, S3-based document caching, and multi-phase .NET modernization for cloud services. The initiative targets $2.47M in 2026 cost savings through platform modernization and cloud optimization with $480K EPC capital investment.

**Current Status - AMBER** because development resourcing remains unresolved for Elastic Search to OpenSearch migration threatening 01 Oct 2026 deadline. Image, Report, and Doc modules have completed activating $1.39M savings (56% of goal), with Website Phase 2 re-planned to 30 Sep 2026 reducing expected savings by $274K.

**Key outcomes delivered:**  
• .NET Phase 0 completed - Delivered 27 Apr 2026 enabling $143K savings; Image/Report components fully migrated; approximately 6% of total goal achieved.  
• Phase 1 (Doc) completed - Doc instances decommissioned 04 Jun 2026; $1.25M run-rate savings activated; representing 51% of total savings goal.  
• Website phase re-planned - Analysis and delivery shifted to 30 Sep 2026 completion; phased approach confirmed; $274K savings reduction accepted.  
• Elastic Search migration constrained - Five instances requiring OpenSearch migration identified; architecture defined; 01 Oct 2026 target at risk without resources.  
• S3 Document Store phased - Novus Cloud application rollout planned; implementation approach revised; 20 Dec 2026 completion with $46K savings.

**Active RAID items:**  
• R1 — Risk: Development resource commitments pending for Elastic Search migration impacting October deadline. Mitigation: Secure formal commitments following 08 Jun leadership discussions; detail migration plan by 19 Jun 2026.  
• I1 — Issue: Website Phase 2 re-planned reducing 2026 savings by $274K. Mitigation: Complete analysis; execute phased delivery by 30 Sep 2026.

**Path to Green**  
Status returns to GREEN by securing formal development resource commitments with detailed migration and verification plan for all five Elastic Search instances by 19 Jun 2026 ensuring 01 Oct 2026 completion.

**Next Steps**  
• Secure Elastic Search resources - Obtain formal development commitments; detail migration plan; confirm instance priorities — by 19 Jun.  
• Progress Website modernization - Execute Westlaw Cobalt Cloud Services analysis; track against 30 Sep target — ongoing.  
• Complete S3 Document Store - Execute phased Novus Cloud rollout; enable $46K savings — by 20 Dec.  
• Monitor savings realization - Track $1.39M activated savings; validate run-rates; report actuals — monthly.  
• Update stakeholder alignment - Communicate re-planned timelines; confirm reduced savings profiles; maintain executive support — by 15 Jun.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Partnership Enablement is migrating Pagero and Thomson Reuters channel partners from legacy tools (Zift, Quickbase, PowerBI) to a unified strategic tech stack and PRM platform, enabling automated revenue-sharing, compliant consent management, and decommissioning of redundant systems. This matters because it consolidates partner data and workflows, reduces operational risk, and improves partner and sales experience across regions.

Zift retirement is at 90% Gantt progress toward the 30 Jun 2026 cut-off, with MVP channel partner consolidation and Pagero production data cut-over both completed on 31 May 2026. Channel Partner user migration is at 70% and Pagero channel partner data migration is at 50% against the 30 Jun 2026 target, while Partner Consent enablement is advancing with the GSI build at 50% and overall consent work at 25% completion.

Overall status is GREEN, driven by on-track decommissioning of Zift and associated migrations against the 30 Jun 2026 end date.

## Path to Green

Risk and dependency exposure is being managed by securing funding approvals for remaining Pagero roadmap items and formalising upstream system commitments (SAP, IFS, Boomi, ECX/ECM) through the Leadership Forum so integration and PRM feature timelines remain aligned.

## Milestones

- Complete Channel Partner migration to the strategic tech stack for Product/Software and Professional Services by 19 Jun 2026.
- Deliver Partner Consent Agreement production go-live by 20 Jun 2026.
- Finish Partner Consent data correction and SIT/UAT/regression testing by 30 Jun 2026.
- Finalise Pagero Channel Partner user migration, Pagero channel partner data migration, and Pagero Channel Partner PowerBI decommission by 30 Jun 2026.
- Decommission the Zift Partner Portal and close the Partnership Enablement program by 30 Jun 2026.

risks.impact_description: If the third-party delivery model for IFS work is not aligned with project needs, timelines for Partner Portal integration and PRM feature delivery may slip due to coordination challenges, slower turnaround on IFS-related changes, or misaligned priorities. This could delay feature releases, extend testing cycles, and potentially impact the overall migration schedule and business value realization.
risks.mitigation: Align with the third-party provider on Ways of Working, SLAs, and release cadence for IFS changes needed for Partner Portal and PRM. Establish clear coordination mechanisms, points of contact, and escalation paths prior to January 2026 to reduce disruptions to timelines and continuity.

risks.title: Dependency on upstream/downstream systems and teams for Partner Portal integrations

risks.impact_description: If upstream/downstream teams (Boomi, ECX/ECM, SAP, IFS, and related integration teams) are unavailable or cannot support required changes on schedule, key PRM features and Partner Portal integrations may be delayed. This could lead to slip in planned releases, extended testing windows, misaligned deployments across environments, and delayed realization of automation benefits for commissions, royalties, and discounts.
risks.mitigation: Identify all upstream/downstream teams and systems required for Partner Portal and PRM integrations. Secure their commitment via a shared roadmap and agreed timelines, schedule integration windows in advance, and establish governance and escalation mechanisms to address resource or scheduling conflicts early.

risks.title: Channel Partner (Limited to Pagero) data and MDM alignment risks
risks.description: SAP field length limits (Name/Address) are blocking some records due to a 35-character restriction, and there are currency/region mapping gaps awaiting IFS Sales inputs. There is a schedule risk if the SAP ECC production upgrade or IFS/SAP/MDM alignment slips. Any design changes required by MDM need to be managed through Change Control because IFS ownership is with a third party and any changes will require a new SOW. RAID log entry #2 under the Systems & Tools workstream further highlights the need for MDM architects’ alignment on the channel partner strategic solution design and a committed delivery timeline.
risks.impact_description: If MDM architects do not align on the design and delivery timeline, and SAP/IFS/MDM alignment is delayed, channel partner data migration from IFS to SAP/GSI could slip, blocking or delaying channel partner enablement for Pagero. Blocked records due to SAP field length limits and unresolved currency/region mappings would prevent accurate and complete partner data in the strategic stack, forcing extended reliance on legacy systems (IFS, PowerBI) and potentially delaying Zift retirement and downstream workstreams dependent on clean channel data.

risks.mitigation: IFS, SAP, and Partnership projects teams (including MDM architects) to agree on a unified design for channel partner strategic solution, address SAP field length constraints (e.g., truncation or alternative mapping), and close currency/region mapping gaps. risks.title: Pagero roadmap delivery depends on funding approval
risks.description: The P&A BAU roadmap note states that the roadmap is subject to change or pivot based on discovery and design recommendations from the technology team and depends on the funding request on Pagero. If funding is not approved or is reduced, planned Pagero integration and partner enablement activities may be delayed, descoped, or cancelled.
risks.impact_description: If Pagero funding is not approved, approved late, or reduced, workstreams related to Pagero integration (e.g., MVP Channel Partner (TR + Pagero) consolidation, Channel Partner PowerBI decommission, Channel Partner data migration, Zift retirement) may slip beyond 2026-06-30, be delivered in a reduced scope, or be cancelled. This would delay decommissioning of legacy tools such as Zift and PowerBI, extend reliance on legacy systems, and reduce the expected business benefits of unified partner data and streamlined partner enablement.
risks.mitigation: Coordinate with finance and program leadership to secure timely approval of the Pagero funding request, ensuring alignment between the technology team’s discovery/design recommendations and the budget ask. Prioritise critical Pagero-related work (e.g., core channel partner consolidation and decommission milestones) so that, if partial funding is granted, the highest-value items are delivered first. Prepare contingency scenarios (e.g., phased rollout, deferred non-critical features) in case funding is constrained.

assumptions.title: Pagero funding will be approved to execute the 2026 roadmap items
assumptions.description: The P&A BAU Program Roadmap 2026 explicitly notes that the roadmap is subject to change or pivot based on technology team discovery and design recommendations and depends on the funding request on Pagero. Planning for Pagero integration and partner enablement workstreams assumes that the requested funding will be approved.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The P&A BAU roadmap has been defined with specific Q1–Q4 activities for Pagero integration and partner enablement (e.g., MVP Channel Partner consolidation, Channel Partner PowerBI decommission, Zift retirement), and the roadmap note states that these plans depend on an outstanding funding request for Pagero.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The Pagero integration is positioned as a strategic integration within the Pagero acquisition program, increasing the likelihood that funding will be prioritised. However, the roadmap explicitly flags dependence on the Pagero funding request and acknowledges that discovery and design outcomes may change the plan, indicating that approval is not yet guaranteed.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If the funding request is not approved or is partially approved, re-prioritise the Pagero roadmap to focus on the highest-value deliverables (e.g., critical channel partner consolidation and decommissioning of high-risk legacy components) and adjust scope, phasing, or timelines accordingly. Consider deferring lower-priority enhancements to future budget cycles or aligning them with other funded initiatives.
assumptions.validation_method: Monitor and confirm formal funding approval decisions through program governance and finance processes, including steering committee updates and budget approvals.

objectives.description: Automate tiered revenue sharing and support royalty calculation (resell), referral fee payments, and channel discount logic in the Partner Portal, with system logic for pricing and royalty payments based on sales thresholds and discount conditions.
Ensure the Partner Portal system has capability to automate payment of commission, royalty, and discounts for partner-led transactions.
Enable seamless integration of IFS system with Partner Portal and GSI/Conga for PRM feature development.
Establish a controlled deployment flow for PRM features from Dev to QA to UAT to PROD with gate review at each stage.
Align all PRM-related environments and associated repositories with Thomson Reuters' security, compliance, and operational standards.
Maintain business continuity so the PRM system continues to operate as a key business system while feature development is underway without disrupting existing business workflows.
Ensure PRM system performance, reliability, and security meet or exceed Thomson Reuters standards after migration and feature deployment.
Improve stakeholder satisfaction by providing PRM business users and internal stakeholders with enhanced workflow automation and communication during and after migration.

Retire the legacy Quickbase USL and AEM instances by migrating all partner data and documents (including partnership agreements and addendums) to GSI and SharePoint, establishing a unified global partner data structure and eliminating regional data silos and Quickbase licensing costs.

Decommission the Zift Partner Portal by 2026-06-30 as part of the broader partner decommission workstream, ensuring all active Pagero and TR channel partners are migrated to the strategic stack and related reporting (e.g., PowerBI for Pagero) is retired.

Consolidate MVP Channel Partner (TR + Pagero) solutions onto the strategic platform by 2026-04-30, including completion of GSI and Conga design, MDM configuration, ETL development, and IFS-to-SAP migration for supported currencies.

Implement a Partner Consent agreement capability integrated with OneTrust to enable compliant partner marketing, with bi-directional consent tracking across Eloqua, the Partner Portal, and PAM-created entry points, supporting implicit, explicit, and double opt-in by geography.
Streamline partner opportunity roles by implementing a standardized set of four partner roles and associated partner taxonomy across opportunity processes.

Enable automated partner training access by implementing Docebo LMS auto provisioning so that partner users are provisioned automatically when accounts are created in GSI, eliminating manual tickets and multi-day onboarding delays.

Improve partner marketing and sales reporting by delivering systems and tools such as lead-to-opportunity conversion tracking dashboards, partner attribution and campaign visibility reporting, and differentiated product reporting at the material level.

Establish strategic business model capabilities for partners, including clickthrough agreements for fast partner activation, SAP notifications for partner material termination, system enablement for royalty payment logic, automated tiered revenue sharing, and embedded partner products and packages.

Deliver a Lead – Insight tab that provides TR Sales representatives with controlled visibility into partner activity on shared customers—without granting direct access to restricted Partner End Customer accounts—enabling better coordination, informed deal planning, and reduced friction between direct and partner‑led sales motions while remaining compliant with access and data‑privacy controls.

Implement a Save Deal Registration capability that allows partners to save and manage deal registrations in progress, improving the partner experience, safeguarding deal pipeline value, and enhancing data accuracy while maintaining current GSI workflows and approval processes.

Migrate the North LatAm Partner Portal to the GSI-based US Partner Portal with Seismic (marketing) integrations, providing centralized partner access aligned with the US partner experience and consistent enablement tooling across regions.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Pricing Engine is delivering a centralized PROS-based pricing capability for selected online Legal, Corporate, and Corporate Tax products, integrated with SAP, EPM, GSI, ECM/MDM, Conga, and Boomi so that Thomson Reuters can execute pricing decisions consistently and with clear systems of record. This enables faster pricing changes, reduced manual intervention, and improved pricing accuracy and compliance.

Foundational design is complete for Release 1 and Release 2, and Release 1 transactional data is approximately 95% available, with only three remaining optimization fields outstanding against a 100% target. However, about 40% of Boomi integration work is blocked by PROS REST API delays and RTPE reload, and 14 Release 1 user stories have spilled into the next sprint, increasing pressure on the 22 Jun 2026 SIT start and 14 Aug 2026 go-live.

Overall status is Red, driven by PROS REST API and RTPE readiness delays that are blocking Conga–Boomi–PROS integration and compressing SIT and UAT timelines for Release 1.

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on unblocking integration by reloading the corrected customer, product, and transaction dataset into PROS, stabilizing RTPE, and delivering near-final REST request and response payloads and endpoints by 28 May 2026 so Boomi can complete the Conga–Boomi–PROS flow and QA integration plan ahead of the 22 Jun 2026 SIT start. In parallel, sprint scope will be rebaselined to clear the 14 spilled Release 1 stories and high-risk dependencies (customer ID alignment, remaining transactional fields, dual-UAT provisioning, and Boomi performance SLAs), with explicit de-scope or timeline decisions escalated if these items threaten the 14 Aug 2026 Release 1 go-live.

## Milestones

- Complete Release 1 System Integration Testing (SIT) for pricing execution and optimization between 22 Jun 2026 and 17 Jul 2026.  
- Start and complete Release 1 User Acceptance Testing (UAT) for Small Law and Mid Law segments between 13 Jul 2026 and 30 Jul 2026.  
- Achieve Release 1 Go Live with production pricing execution and optimization capabilities on 14 Aug 2026.  
- Achieve Release 2 Go Live with price management and pricing analytics capabilities on 14 Sep 2026.  
- Complete overall program closure and transition to steady-state operations by 18 Sep 2026.

risks.title: Unclear PROS‑to‑EPM price publishing process may delay Release 2 price management readiness
risks.description: For products whose price lists are managed in EPM strategic stacks (e.g., Pagero), the end‑to‑end process for publishing PROS‑generated prices into EPM—including approvals, data structures, and automation boundaries—has not yet been fully defined. This clarity is required to support Release 2 price management capabilities.
risks.impact_description: If the PROS‑to‑EPM price publishing and governance process is not defined during Release 2 design, build activities may be delayed or require rework, resulting in extended manual price maintenance and delayed realization of centralized price management benefits.
risks.mitigation:
1. Conduct focused design sessions with the EPM strategic team to document current approval and price loading processes.
2. Define the future‑state PROS‑to‑EPM integration and approval model as part of Release 2 design.
3. Confirm which price management steps remain manual versus automated in Release 2.
4. Capture decisions in the Release 2 architecture and operating model documentation.

risks.title: Customer data source for pricing may not contain complete parent–child hierarchy
risks.description: The program is moving towards using GSI as the customer data source for pricing. However, there was uncertainty whether GSI contains the required parent–child customer relationships (e.g., global vs regional accounts) needed for pricing logic, and whether those relationships from ECM/D&B are properly propagated to GSI.
risks.impact_description: If GSI does not contain complete and correct parent–child customer hierarchy, the pricing engine may not be able to apply account‑hierarchy based pricing rules (e.g., global parent discounts rolling down to branches). This could lead to inaccurate pricing, rework to change the system of record to ECM, additional data mapping effort, and potential delays in design and implementation.
risks.mitigation: 1) Confirm with ECM and MDM architects (Sridhar, Kongot Sripriya) that parent–child relationships from ECM/D&B are pushed into GSI and where they are stored (e.g., Salesforce account parent fields, ultimate parent, domestic parent). 2) Have sales/MDM teams pull reports from GSI to verify those fields and the hierarchy quality. 3) Include the relevant hierarchy fields in the customer data mapping and spreadsheet so PROS can consume them. 4) If gaps are discovered, evaluate switching the pricing customer source to ECM and plan the additional mapping effort.

risks.title: Price list structure and pricing model design may not be agreed in time for Release 2 price management
risks.description: The program still needs to align on the number of price lists, their segmentation logic (e.g., by product line, business unit, or sub-business unit), and the pricing models/formulas that will be configured in PROS. Current discussions reference SAP granularity (customer group, material ID, sales org, UOM), but there is not yet consensus on how to partition price books in PROS or how many price lists will exist. Neetika highlighted this as one of the most important design decisions for price management that needs to be closed within about a week and before the April 17 design target.
risks.impact_description: If agreement on price list structures and pricing models is delayed, the Release 2 price management design cannot be finalized by the planned April 17 date. This will impact configuration of PROS price management, slow down related design sessions and KDD closures, and may delay subsequent build activities for price management. It also increases the risk of suboptimal performance (e.g., overly large price books) or later rework if list segmentation decisions are changed after configuration has started.
risks.mitigation: 1) Use the full extract of active materials that Rajat and Arshad are arranging to quantify variation across segments and product families and inform practical price list segmentation options. 2) Leverage SAP’s current granularity (customer group, material ID, sales org, UOM, scales) as a baseline and workshop with TR Commercial Excellence (Rajat, Arshad) and Deloitte to propose 2–3 concrete price list segmentation scenarios (e.g., by product line or business unit). 3) Hold focused design workshops over the next week to review these scenarios, evaluate performance implications in PROS, and converge on the final number and structure of price lists. 4) Document the agreed model and lock it into Release 2 design decisions so later changes go through formal change control.

risks.title: Pricing engine call latency due to Boomi processing and batch design
risks.description: End‑to‑end pricing and optimization calls from Conga through Boomi to PROS may exceed acceptable response times, particularly during high‑volume transactions. This risk exists because Boomi parallel processing and batching patterns are being implemented for this use case for the first time, PROS batch size limits and throughput are still being validated, and final performance SLAs have not yet been proven under realistic load conditions. There is also uncertainty whether additional Boomi infrastructure capacity or PROS license scaling will be required to meet target response times.
risks.impact_description: If pricing and optimization calls exceed agreed SLAs, sales users may experience increased latency during quote creation and repricing, degrading user experience and potentially slowing deal execution and approvals. Failure to meet acceptable performance thresholds could force late architectural or capacity changes (e.g., infrastructure scaling, batch size adjustments, licensing increases), introducing schedule risk to Release 1 Go Live and subsequent releases.
risks.mitigation:
1. Define and formally agree acceptable performance SLAs for Conga–Boomi–PROS pricing and optimization calls with business stakeholders.
2. Finalize and review detailed Boomi design (batching approach, parallelization strategy) in middleware architecture sessions.
3. Perform early performance validation with PROS to confirm supported batch sizes and throughput limits; validate scalability assumptions.
4. Develop a capacity and cost estimate for potential Boomi infrastructure or PROS license scaling, if required.
5. Align on a phased performance strategy where initial go‑live meets minimum acceptable SLAs, with planned optimization improvements post‑launch if needed.
6. Communicate performance expectations clearly to business stakeholders ahead of Release 1 Go Live and secure agreement.

risks.title: Fragmented intake requests may disrupt Release 1 design closure and SLA alignment
risks.description: New intake requests related to Pricing Engine Release 1 (e.g., SAP, EPM, data, integrations) may be submitted without explicit linkage to the original program‑level intake, causing the work to be treated as net‑new. This can reset SLA expectations, create prioritization misalignment, and introduce confusion around scope, ownership, and delivery timelines during Release 1 design activities.
risks.impact_description: If Release 1–related intakes are not consistently linked to the parent Pricing Engine program context, delivery teams may reprioritize or delay work based on perceived “new” requests. This can result in missed SLAs, design churn, governance escalations, and delays to Release 1 design closure.
risks.mitigation:
1. Enforce linkage of all Release 1–related intakes as child requests under the Pricing Engine program intake.
2. Explicitly tag new intakes as Release 1 or Release 2 to maintain scope clarity.
3. Coordinate with Commercial Excellence and data domain owners to ensure consistent intake references and SLA alignment.
4. Transition any new Release 1 scope after design freeze through formal change control.

risks.title: PROS REST API delay and server errors may block Release 1 and Release 2 integration timelines
risks.description: Server errors in RTPE (Real-Time Pricing Engine) calls were root-caused to product description/code mismatches and data quality issues in the TR extract. Although a corrected extract was delivered on 2026-05-26, PROS has not yet fully reloaded and validated RTPE. In parallel, delivery of the PROS REST API (final request/response mappings and endpoint) is delayed, with RAID 1281891 raised to track this. Boomi development is blocked on receiving the final API version and payloads, and Release 1 and Release 2 timelines are at risk until the PROS API is available and stable.
risks.mitigation:
1) PROS to reload the corrected product and transaction data extract delivered on 2026-05-26 and validate RTPE to eliminate server errors.
2) Deliver the final PROS REST API version (including request/response payload structures, field mappings, and E2E endpoint) by 2026-05-28 so Boomi can resume development.
3) Target ~90% completeness for request/response payload coverage by 2026-05-28 and finalize the QA integration plan by 2026-06-03.
4) Track RAID 1281891 in ADO with clear ownership and due date; escalate delays through Palani and program leadership as needed, as already initiated on 2026-05-27.
5) Sequence Boomi work so that currently unblocked tasks (e.g., generic integration scaffolding) progress while waiting for final payloads, reducing idle time and limiting further sprint spillover once the API is available.
risks.source_file_name: PROS Pricing Engine Program Technology Weekly Status Update (W22)_Rev0.3.pptx

risks.title: Integration layer complexity due to XML-only PROS output may delay EPM price ingestion and increase Boomi scope
risks.description: An Architecture Call confirmed that PROS can output only XML and that CSV exports cannot include approvals. The agreed PROS–EPM integration pattern is PROS → Middleware → EPM in CSV format, with Day-1 manual operations and Day-2 automation. To support this, middleware must now perform XML-to-CSV conversion and transform delta updates from PROS into full-snapshot CSV files for EPM. This expands the integration layer scope beyond the originally envisioned Boomi mapping work and introduces new design and build effort that is not yet fully estimated.
risks.mitigation:
1) Naresh to return with concrete options and effort estimates for XML-to-CSV conversion and delta-to-full-snapshot transformation in the middleware layer, informed by Architecture Call outcomes.
2) Select and baseline a single middleware design pattern for PROS→EPM (including error handling and approval-related data handling) by early June 2026.
3) Update Boomi and middleware backlogs to reflect the expanded scope, and adjust sprint planning so this work is prioritized ahead of Release 2 price management milestones.
4) Coordinate with EPM SMEs (Matt, Nick) to ensure the CSV format and snapshot approach align with EPM template field definitions and approval model requirements.
5) Monitor the impact of the expanded middleware scope on SAP and EDL integration timelines, and escalate to program leadership if additional resources are required to avoid delays.
risks.source_file_name: PROS Pricing Engine Program Technology Weekly Status Update (W22)_Rev0.3.pptx

risks.title: Delay in business validation of data mappings may impact Release 1 ETL and Go Live readiness
risks.description: Business validation of data mappings across key entities (customer, product, transactional quote/order data, and asset/contract data) is still in progress. While foundational design is complete, delayed validation of remaining attributes and business logic may slow ETL development, data loads into PROS, and integration testing required for Release 1 Go Live.
risks.impact_description: If business validation of data mappings is delayed, ETL development and data provisioning to PROS may be blocked or require rework. This could delay integration testing, UAT readiness, and ultimately Release 1 Go Live timelines.
risks.mitigation:
1. Continue focused mapping validation sessions with business stakeholders for high‑priority Release 1 attributes.
2. Enforce deadlines for business sign‑off on remaining mappings required for ETL completion.
3. Enable ETL and PROS teams to proceed using validated subsets of data while remaining mappings finalize.
4. Actively track unresolved mapping items as blockers to SIT/UAT readiness.

risks.title: Delay in receiving transactional order data extracts for price optimization design
risks.description: The team is unable to pull historical transactional/orders data from at least one source system and is also dependent on the MDM team to deliver a full extract of active materials and transactional variations across in-scope products. This data is required to understand how many variations exist (e.g., multiple UOM, banded vs fixed pricing) and to design how the price optimization engine and business rules will differentiate between models.
risks.impact_description: If complete transactional data extracts are not received in a timely manner, the team will be unable to: (1) design and validate the multi-UOM and pricing-method handling in the optimization engine; (2) confirm which attributes must be treated as drivers for optimization; and (3) finalize the business rule configuration for price optimization. This will delay Sprint 1 non-functional data setup, slow down price optimization design, and may force rework later if rules are based on incomplete patterns, potentially pushing out Release 1 optimization timelines.
risks.mitigation: 1) Work offline between TR Commercial Excellence (Arshad) and Deloitte (Neetika/Aditi) to resolve extraction blockers for the specific source that cannot currently provide orders data. 2) Continue coordinating with the MDM team to obtain a full, exhaustive extract of active materials and related transactional variations across in-scope products, and secure an explicit delivery timeline. 3) As soon as extracts are available, create a summary/segmentation view with Deloitte to identify key variation patterns and required optimization attributes in a joint working session. 4) If full-history extracts are delayed further, start with a representative subset of data for initial rule design, clearly marking assumptions and planning a validation pass once the complete extract is available.

risks.title: Adding Mid Law testing alongside Small Law in Release 1 may strain UAT scope and timelines
risks.description: Originally, Release 1 UAT was aligned to focus on Small Law. Recent discussions with business teams indicate that Mid Law also wants to start testing in parallel with Small Law, using largely overlapping use cases but with some Mid Law–specific scenarios (including approval dashboard requirements). Yogesh confirmed that Small Law and Mid Law testing can happen in parallel, with weekly working sessions (Tuesdays and Thursdays), but enablement timing for Mid Law in production is still to be decided by the pricing/business team. Anantha noted this as a change item that needs leadership awareness and sign‑off, and there is not yet a clear, documented plan for when Mid Law will be enabled relative to Small Law.
risks.impact_description: If Mid Law testing is added to Release 1 UAT without a clear plan and resourcing, (1) the UAT scope and workload will increase, potentially overloading business testers and UAT support teams; (2) additional Mid Law–specific use cases and approval dashboard requirements may extend test design and execution time; and (3) ambiguity around production enablement timings for Mid Law versus Small Law could cause confusion, misaligned expectations with leadership, and last‑minute replanning. Collectively, this could delay UAT completion or force de‑scoping of test coverage for one or both segments.
risks.mitigation: 1) Document a clear plan and grid for Release 1 testing and enablement, explicitly listing which segments (Small Law, Mid Law) will test which scenarios and when, and how their UAT sign‑off aligns to release timelines. 2) Socialize this plan with enterprise and technical leadership to obtain explicit sign‑off on including Mid Law in parallel UAT, along with any required resource adjustments. 3) Work with UAT support to identify Mid Law–specific use cases and required accounts/products early, and make sure they are ready before test execution ramps up. 4) Clarify and communicate the intended production enablement sequence (e.g., whether Mid Law goes live with Release 2 while still using the optimization engine in Release 1) to avoid last‑minute scope changes.
risks.source_file_name: Price Engine - Internal Weekly Meeting (Core Working Group).docx

risks.title: Data readiness risk: incomplete guidance and analytics data may delay next sprint stories
risks.description: As of Week 20, Release 1 optimization data is only partially complete: approximately 50 attributes have been shared with PROS and fees generation is still in progress. Analytics data needed for UDD dashboard charts (e.g., ACV%, discount%) is not yet fully available. This partial data set blocks certain next-sprint stories that depend on complete guidance and analytics inputs.

raised_by.name: PROS Pricing Engine Week 20 status report

risks.mitigation:
1) Complete delivery of the remaining three optimization-related fields (add-on and AI/non-AI classifications) by 2026-05-22 so that the full optimization attribute set can be loaded.
2) Run the first raw deal guidance iteration, using approximately 50 attributes, by 2026-05-22 and initiate business review of the outputs to identify any critical data gaps early.
3) Continue the daily data-mapping working sessions (including Phalguni and Praveen) to finalize analytics attributes; verify that the 26 shared analytics fields (16 overlapping with optimization and 10 net new) cover all UDD dashboard chart needs.
4) Sequence next-sprint stories so those dependent on final guidance and analytics data are scheduled after 2026-05-22, minimizing idle time and reducing the likelihood of additional spillover.

Per the W22 status (May 27, 2026), all requested data has now been confirmed as loaded and deal guidance generated, addressing the previously incomplete optimization and analytics data set.
risks.source_file_name: PROS Pricing Engine Program Weekly Status Update (W20)_RevG.pptx

risks.title: Sprint spillover risk: R1 and R2 stories may carry over and compress timelines
risks.description: Week 20 status indicates that for Release 1 (price optimization) approximately 4–6 stories are expected to spill over from Sprint 4, and for Release 2 (price management and analytics) approximately 7–8 stories are expected to spill over from Sprint 2. This cumulative spillover of around 12 stories may compress subsequent sprints and testing windows.

raised_by.name: PROS Pricing Engine Week 20 status report

risks.mitigation:
1) Quantify the exact spillover impact by 2026-05-19, including which specific R1 and R2 stories are at risk and their dependency relationships.
2) Reprioritize upcoming sprint backlogs to ensure that spillover stories tied to critical path milestones (e.g., SIT, UAT, go-live) are completed first.
3) Consider de-scoping or deferring lower-priority stories from the next sprint to maintain a realistic workload and avoid cumulative spillover.
4) Communicate any residual spillover and adjusted timelines to stakeholders so expectations are managed for SIT (2026-06-22), UAT (July), and the planned August/September go-live dates.
5) For W22 specifically, accommodate the 14 R1 Sprint 11 and 10 R2 Sprint 11 spillover stories into the next sprint, with mitigation options to be proposed and actioned by 2026-05-29, ensuring Boomi capacity is adjusted to reflect reduced story points taken in the current sprint due to dependency uncertainty.
