risks.title: Risk of exceeding PROS usage limits by onboarding all tenants
risks.description: Current direction was to onboard PROS for all tenants, but concerns were raised that if all tenants invoke PROS, the number of calls could quickly reach or exceed licensed or technically supported limits.
risks.impact_description: If all tenants begin calling PROS without usage controls, the program may exceed PROS transaction or license limits, resulting in throttling, failures, or unplanned license costs. This could force emergency restrictions or reconfiguration of integrations, delaying rollout and undermining business trust in the solution.
risks.mitigation: Revise onboarding strategy so that initially only the SCS tenant calls PROS. Defer enabling other tenants until actual usage is understood and performance and license impact are assessed. Inform Kumar of the revised direction and adjust tenant integration plans accordingly.

risks.title: Limits in SAP/EPM geographic granularity may constrain Release 2 pricing strategy
risks.description: The strategic pricing program has requested location‑specific list prices (e.g., state‑level pricing within a country). While PROS can model geography as a pricing dimension, it is not yet confirmed whether SAP and EPM master data and pricing models can support and operationalize this level of geographic granularity at scale. This clarification is required as part of Release 2 price management design.
risks.impact_description: If SAP and EPM cannot support the desired geographic pricing granularity, the end‑to‑end pricing stack may be unable to implement the requested location‑specific pricing strategy. This may require constraining geographic scope (e.g., region‑based pricing), introducing reference data workarounds, or adjusting business expectations for Release 2.
risks.mitigation:
1. Validate with PROS the supported geographic pricing dimensions.
2. Assess SAP and EPM master data structures and pricing models for their ability to support state‑ or location‑level pricing without excessive data growth.
3. Evaluate alternative design patterns (e.g., regional groupings, reference attributes) if state‑level pricing is not feasible.
4. Document supported geographic granularity and socialize constraints with strategic pricing stakeholders as part of Release 2 design.

risks.title: Key design decisions (KDDs) for price management and analytics may not be closed by April 17
risks.description: Design sessions for Release 2 price management and pricing analytics have started, but the team is still in the familiarization phase and there are multiple key design decisions (KDDs) outstanding. Neetika stated that these KDDs are being targeted to close by April 17, and additional workshops are being scheduled up to that date. Given the volume of open questions (including price list structures, analytics requirements, and dashboard/chart constraints), there is a risk that not all KDDs will be fully resolved in time.
risks.impact_description: If the KDDs for price management and analytics are not closed by April 17, the ‘Design Completion Release 2’ milestone will effectively slip, delaying downstream build work on price management workflows and analytics dashboards in PROS. This can compress or push out development and testing timelines for Release 2, impact Sprint planning, and reduce the time available for validating analytics KPIs and user experience constraints (e.g., PROS five-charts-per-tab limitation), thereby increasing the likelihood of usability issues or scope reductions later.
risks.mitigation: 1) Maintain and execute the workshop schedule through April 17 with clear agendas focused on closing specific KDDs (price list structures, pricing models, analytics KPIs, and dashboard layouts). 2) Request that business stakeholders (Rajat, Arshad, Jenny and others) pre-populate required inputs such as formulas, KPIs, and process flows ahead of design sessions, as Aditi is already coordinating. 3) Prioritize the most critical KDDs that directly impact build (e.g., price list design, core analytics metrics) and formally defer lower-priority design details to later sprints if necessary. 4) Track KDD closure in Scrum calls twice a week, escalating unresolved items to Naresh and program leadership for timely decisions.

risks.title: Dual‑UAT testing approach may increase effort and impact Release 1 test timelines
risks.description: Managing testing across two UAT environments may require duplicate execution of test scenarios, increasing effort and coordination complexity. This could delay UAT completion, introduce test coverage gaps, and negatively impact Release 1 Go‑Live readiness if not tightly planned and managed.
risks.impact_description: Managing testing across two UAT environments may require duplicate execution of test scenarios, increasing effort and coordination complexity. This could delay UAT completion, introduce test coverage gaps, and negatively impact Release 1 Go‑Live readiness if not tightly planned and managed.

Explicit scenario‑to‑environment mapping
Reuse strategies
Avoiding compression of testing

risks.title: JWT-only PROS–TR integration approach may be delayed or rejected by Architecture Review Board
risks.description: The connection between the PROS environment and Thomson Reuters (TR) environment is currently designed to use a JWT token–based integration from Boomi to PROS. PROS product team confirmed that JWT is the only supported option (no OAuth or other alternatives). The proposed JWT solution is working in initial trials, but it still requires formal approval from the architectural review board (IRS/architecture forum), where the Boomi architect will present the design. Until this approval is granted, the integration pattern remains at risk of change.
risks.impact_description:
If the architectural review board does not approve the JWT-only integration pattern, or if the approval is significantly delayed, the program may need to revise the integration approach between Boomi and PROS. This could 
(1) delay completion of integration build and testing, 
(2) introduce rework in Boomi and PROS configuration, 
(3) postpone UAT and production readiness of pricing calls, and 
(4) potentially require exception or security waivers that add governance overhead and slow down deployment.
risks.mitigation:
1) Prepare and submit a thorough design package for the JWT-based Boomi–PROS integration to the Architecture Review Board (IRS forum), including security considerations, token lifecycle management, and auditability. 
2) Ensure the Boomi architect clearly presents that JWT is the only option PROS supports at this time, so alternatives are not assumed. 
3) Engage with security and architecture stakeholders ahead of the formal review to pre‑empt concerns and adjust minor design elements without changing the core JWT approach. 
4) Define a fallback plan (e.g., temporary exception approval or controlled scope of use) if the board raises concerns but cannot offer an immediate alternative, to avoid blocking critical integration timelines.
risks.source_file_name: Price Engine - Internal Weekly Meeting (Core Working Group).docx

risks.title: Release 1 data extract delays increasing likelihood of late price optimization design and testing
risks.description: Week 18–19 status reports that Release 1 is trending Red due to incomplete data extracts required by PROS to progress sprint work, including pending derived attributes for optimization. This amplifies the existing concern that historical transactional/order data and related attributes will not be available in time to support price optimization design, rule configuration, and testing.
risks.impact_description: If complete transactional data extracts (including derived attributes) continue to be delayed, PROS will not be able to finalize multi-UoM and pricing model design, determine key optimization drivers, or validate rules against real patterns. This will delay completion of Sprint 4 optimization stories, push out raw guidance generation, and may force hurried or suboptimal configuration based on incomplete data, increasing the risk of defects and further schedule slippage for Release 1.
risks.mitigation:
1) Escalate the data extract delays through the Pricing Engine SteerCo, explicitly linking them to the Red status for Release 1 and Sprint 4 blockers.
2) Work with MDM and source-system teams to define a committed delivery date for the full transactional extract, including derived attributes, and treat it as a hard milestone.
3) In the interim, expand the existing partial extract used by PROS so that at least a representative subset of events and attributes is available for continued design work.
4) Re-sequence Sprint 4 stories where possible so teams can focus on non-data-dependent tasks (e.g., Boomi integration plumbing) while waiting for the full extract, minimizing idle time.
5) If the full extract cannot be delivered within the current sprint, update the Release 1 plan and communicate revised optimization readiness dates to stakeholders.

According to the Week 20 status update, Release 1 transactional data is now approximately 95% available, with only three remaining fields (add-on indicator and AI/non-AI classification) due by 2026-05-22. The first raw deal guidance iteration, using around 50 attributes, is also targeted for 2026-05-22, after which remaining data validation will be performed.

risks.title: Order Capture event‑type alignment may block Sprint 4 Release 1 optimization configuration
risks.description: Release 1 Sprint 4 depends on confirming the event-type model in Order Capture so that price optimization business rules can be correctly triggered and evaluated. As of the Week 18–19 status, event-type confirmation is described as the primary remaining gating item for Release 1 optimization outcomes. Until event types are finalized and aligned across Order Capture, Conga, Boomi, and PROS, the team cannot fully configure or validate optimization rules, risking further sprint spillover and delays in producing raw guidance.
risks.impact_description: If event-type alignment in Order Capture is not achieved in time, Sprint 4 optimization stories will slip, delaying generation of raw pricing guidance and end-to-end integration validation with Conga via Boomi. This would push out Release 1 optimization readiness, compress remaining development and testing windows, and could force de-scoping of optimization features or delay overall Release 1 go-live, impacting planned benefits for Small Law and Mid Law segments.
risks.mitigation:
1) Convene a focused working session with Order Capture, Conga, Boomi, and PROS design leads to finalize the event-type model and mapping required for optimization rules.
2) Document a single, agreed list of event types and their semantics (e.g., new sale, renewal, upsell) and how they will be derived in Order Capture and passed through to Boomi and PROS.
3) Update Sprint 4 stories and acceptance criteria to reflect the finalized event-type logic and ensure QA test cases explicitly cover each event type.
4) Track event-type closure as a gating KDD for Release 1; escalate to program leadership if agreement is not reached within the current sprint so scope or timeline adjustments can be decided.

risks.title: Unresolved PROS–SAP price list mechanism and analytics data granularity may cause Release 2 sprint spillover
risks.description: In Week 18–19 status, Release 2 is in Sprint 2 with development focused on analytics setup and sample data loads. Progress is constrained by unresolved integration and design questions, specifically the mechanism for sending price lists from PROS to SAP (e.g., XML vs CSV) and alignment on analytics data granularity. These open items gate completion of Sprint 2 stories and threaten to cause sprint spillover and delay downstream work, even though development capacity itself is not the bottleneck.
risks.impact_description: If the PROS–SAP price list mechanism and analytics data granularity are not decided promptly, Sprint 2 stories for Release 2 will spill over, delaying completion of analytics setup and integration work. This will shorten the time available for subsequent development and testing cycles, increase the risk that analytics dashboards and price management capabilities are not ready by the planned Release 2 dates, and may force scope reductions or rework if late decisions conflict with earlier implementation assumptions.
risks.mitigation:
1) Hold a dedicated integration design workshop with SAP functional/technical teams, PROS architects, and Deloitte to compare XML vs CSV options for PROS–SAP price list exchange and decide on a single, supported mechanism.
2) Document the chosen interface format (including schema, transport, and error-handling approach) and update Release 2 integration user stories and technical designs accordingly.
3) In parallel, define target analytics data granularity by aligning Commercial Excellence, MDM, and EPM stakeholders on required dimensions and aggregation levels for dashboards, using current Sprint 2 sample data as a reference.
4) Treat these items as top-priority KDDs for Release 2; track them explicitly in sprint ceremonies and escalate to program leadership if decisions are not made within the current sprint so scope, sequencing, or timelines can be adjusted.

Per the Week 20 status, a proof of concept is underway to test CSV output from PROS instead of XML for better scalability, with PROS price list format decisions due around 2026-05-20 and all remaining integration design items (including the PROS–SAP mechanism) due by 2026-05-27.

risks.description: Architecture forums have flagged parent–child pricing as a Release 1 risk. PROS-based custom tables to drive parent–child pricing were determined to be not feasible for Release 1, and the design decision for parent–child rules has been reopened. The only viable option for Release 1 is to rely on PROS’ native capabilities and a manual one-time load of parent–child relationships, with a more robust fix deferred to Release 2.

2) Document clear operational procedures for maintaining parent–child pricing behavior in Release 1, including when and how manual updates must be applied if hierarchies change.

risks.title: End-to-end pricing call performance SLA not yet agreed for Release 1
risks.description: The program does not yet have a confirmed performance model and SLA for pricing calls initiated from Conga and processed via Boomi to PROS. Boomi is implementing parallel processing with request splitting, but their current SLA is 2.5 seconds, and they cannot yet confirm expected processing time for the new pattern. Additional latency is expected due to multiple sequential calls (~3 × 300 ms), and it is unclear whether performance can be achieved without infrastructure or license cost increases. Business stakeholders have not yet agreed to the expected performance impact for initial releases.
risks.impact_description: Lack of clarity on Boomi and PROS performance and final SLA may result in slower-than-expected pricing calls for initial launches, affecting user experience and potentially delaying go-live if performance is unacceptable to business. Without a clear decision on either optimizing the integration pattern or investing in additional infrastructure and licenses, the architecture remains unsettled and business expectations cannot be managed. This uncertainty also complicates capacity planning (e.g., calling PROS from all tenants) and may force scope reductions such as limiting PROS onboarding to SCS initially.
risks.mitigation:
Potential resolutions under consideration include: 
(1) Boomi handling batching of pricing requests with optimized parallel processing; 
(2) PROS increasing batch size limits (from 10 to 40–50) to reduce the number of calls; and/or 
(3) upgrading Boomi infrastructure and licenses. 
Final resolution will require cost estimates, performance data, and business agreement on acceptable SLAs.
Agreement between Technology and Business on an acceptable Release 1 performance SLA, along with approval of any required infrastructure or licensing changes needed to meet that SLA.

Week 20 status confirms that manual end-to-end flow is working and integration design items (including field mapping and unique keys) are targeted for closure by 2026-05-27. However, performance SLAs remain to be validated once dynamic integration and guidance-driven calls are fully in place, so the risk remains open until those measurements and agreements are completed.

assumptions.title: Boomi–PROS integration will achieve approximately 1 second incremental latency for pricing calls
assumptions.description: Current understanding is that Boomi will make three sequential calls as part of the PROS pricing flow, each taking about 300 ms, leading to roughly one second additional time for a pricing request.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Boomi indicated that the new parallel processing and splitting design involves three call sequences and estimated 300 ms per call, while their current SLA is 2.5 seconds for other workloads.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Boomi’s existing SLA performance gives a reasonable baseline, but the pricing flow introduces parallel processing and batching that they are implementing for the first time. Until the detailed design is implemented and tested, the 1 second figure remains an engineering estimate rather than a measured fact.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If measured latency exceeds expectations, increase PROS batch sizes where possible, optimize Boomi flow design, and/or scale Boomi infrastructure or licenses; align with business stakeholders on any residual performance trade‑offs for the first launch.
assumptions.validation_method: Performance testing of the Boomi–PROS integration under expected load, comparing measured latency to the 1 second estimate.

assumptions.title: Only SCS tenant will initially call PROS to control transaction volumes
assumptions.description: The program will adjust its earlier direction of onboarding PROS across all tenants and instead initially enable PROS calls only for the SCS tenant to avoid quickly reaching transaction or license limits.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Palani observed that if PROS is called from all tenants from day one, the total number of calls could easily reach the licensed or supported limit, creating volume and cost issues.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Tenant enablement is governed by program decisions and integration configuration; as long as the team enforces the plan, only SCS will call PROS initially. The main uncertainty is later business pressure to enable additional tenants sooner.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If additional tenants must be onboarded earlier, re‑estimate expected transaction volumes, confirm PROS licensing and technical capacity, and phase tenant activation to stay within safe limits.
assumptions.validation_method: Review and confirmation of the tenant onboarding plan in architecture and environment strategy sessions, and checking integration configurations prior to go‑live.

assumptions.title: GSI will serve as the primary customer data source for pricing, with hierarchy supplied via ECM/D&B
assumptions.description: The solution is moving toward using GSI as the customer data source for the pricing engine. The assumption is that ECM maintains customer hierarchies (e.g., domestic parent, ultimate parent) sourced from D&B, and that these are pushed into GSI at the account level so they can be used for pricing.
assumptions.rationale_basis: GSI already contains most customer data, and program architects want a single primary source for pricing. ECM is known to hold legal hierarchies, and MDM/ECM architects indicated these are replicated into GSI.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Architectural confirmations suggest the necessary fields exist and are batch‑loaded, but hands‑on verification through reports and mapping exercises is still pending, so some uncertainty remains about coverage and quality.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If gaps are found, either add missing hierarchy attributes to GSI from ECM/D&B or switch the pricing customer source to ECM and update mappings and integration flows accordingly.
assumptions.validation_method: Data profiling and reporting on GSI customer records to confirm presence and quality of parent/ultimate parent fields, and cross‑checking against ECM for representative accounts.

assumptions.title: Using GSI product data as the source for Release 1 is acceptable despite future rework for Release 2
assumptions.description: For Release 1, the program will use GSI product data as the source for pricing because it provides a consolidated view, even though GSI is a point‑of‑sale system and not the master product data source. The team accepts that Release 2 will need to re‑point product sourcing to master data systems.
assumptions.rationale_basis: In EPM, product data is scattered across multiple objects and tables, requiring complex logic to assemble. GSI already consolidates sellable products, making it a simpler and faster source for Release 1.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Architects understand GSI’s nature as a POS system and deliberately accept that it provides adequate coverage for Release 1, while recognizing that it is not sustainable for price management in Release 2 and beyond.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If product gaps emerge before Release 1 go‑live, selectively integrate required product attributes directly from master data systems for the affected products; for Release 2, plan and resource the rework to source product data entirely from master schemas.
assumptions.validation_method: Validation of Release 1 scenarios using GSI‑sourced product data in test environments, and confirming coverage of required products for legal, corporate, and corporate tax online offerings.

assumptions.title: Four key entities (customer, product, quote/opportunity/line items, asset) are sufficient for initial pricing data scope
assumptions.description: The program is focusing data mapping on four critical entities: two master data entities (customer and product) and two transactional entities (a combined quote/opportunity/quote line item entity and an asset entity for existing contract data). The assumption is that these four entities cover the data required for Release 1 pricing and renewals.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Palani and Naresh explicitly framed these four entities as critical for pricing and renewals, and Abinash’s team has already performed substantial technical mapping on them.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The entities reflect standard pricing and renewal data needs. However, ongoing discussions about asset fields and renewals indicate that some details are still being clarified, so the scope may need refinement.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If new required entities or attributes are identified, extend the data mapping and ETL scope and adjust release plans or prioritize incremental delivery of additional data in later sprints or releases.
assumptions.validation_method: Review of detailed pricing and renewal use cases with business stakeholders to confirm that all required data elements are contained within these four entities.

assumptions.title: PROS can act as system of origin for prices for selected online products while SAP/EPM continue for others
assumptions.description: The program assumes that PROS will be the system of origin for prices for specific online products in legal, corporate, and corporate tax, while many other products (e.g., print products, existing SAP‑only products) will continue to be governed and maintained via current SAP/EPM processes. The systems will coexist.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Product scope discussions clarified that not all products—especially print SKUs—will be onboarded to PROS. Program objectives target online products in certain business lines first, with existing governance remaining for other products.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Current discussions explicitly limit the PROS scope to selected online products; however, other programs and stakeholders (e.g., CPSP, MLC) may push for broader coverage, which could challenge this assumption over time.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If scope expansion is requested, treat it as a new phase with separate planning, funding, and architecture work, rather than absorbing it into the current release; maintain clear boundaries on what PROS will own versus what remains with SAP/EPM.
assumptions.validation_method: Formal scope documentation and architectural decisions that list which products are in scope for PROS pricing, and confirmation with pricing, MDM, SAP, and EPM governance stakeholders.

assumptions.title: Customer data can be finalized and used to start PROS table creation ahead of full transactional data validation
assumptions.description: Abinash and Gayathri agreed that Deloitte can begin creating PROS tables and starting data extracts as soon as the customer entity mapping is finalized, even if product and transactional mappings and business validation are still in progress. The plan is to proceed entity-by-entity (starting with customer) so that Sprint 1 non-functional work on master data and dimension tables can begin without waiting for full transactional data sign-off.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Sprint 1 is focused on non-functional requirements and master/transactional data setup, but business validation of all entities is not yet complete and transactional mapping is complex. To keep PROS configuration and data model work moving, the team wants to leverage the relatively simpler and more stable customer mappings as an early starting point.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Discussions in the meeting show convergence that customer mappings are closer to being finalized, and both Abinash and Gayathri confirm they can unlock Deloitte’s PROS table creation by starting with customer. However, transactional data complexity and ongoing mapping workshops introduce some uncertainty about whether customer will remain untouched as other entities are refined, so confidence is moderate rather than high.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If significant changes to customer mappings are required after PROS table creation starts, implement controlled schema evolution: (1) capture deltas, (2) adjust PROS customer tables and ETL mappings in a dedicated hardening sprint, and (3) limit production of downstream artifacts (e.g., optimization configuration) that depend on the changed fields until tables are corrected. If customer cannot be finalized early, re-plan Sprint 1 to focus on other non-functional work (e.g., access, environment setup) while deferring data table creation to a later sprint.
assumptions.validation_method: 1) Achieve internal agreement on the customer mapping between TR Technology and Deloitte, and mark it as baselined for Sprint 1. 2) Monitor for change requests to customer attributes during ongoing business validation; if changes are minor and do not impact table structure, the assumption holds. 3) If material structural changes occur, log them and assess rework impact.

assumptions.title: Day-1 manual operations at Release 2 go-live will mirror the eventual automated solution without rework
assumptions.description: For Release 2, the integration roadmap adopts a two-phase approach: (1) Day-1 manual operations at Release 2 go-live in September 2026, where pricing-related steps are executed manually but designed to match the eventual automated solution; and (2) post-go-live automation via Boomi integration with PROS–EPM–SAP bi-directional synchronization targeted for November 2026. The assumption is that the Day-1 manual processes will be designed and executed in a way that closely mirrors the future automated integration flows, so that minimal or no process rework is required when automation is introduced.
assumptions.rationale_basis: To avoid delaying Release 2 until full automation is available, the program intends to start with manual operations that follow the same logical steps as the future Boomi-based integration. This allows business benefits from price management and analytics to start in September 2026 while integration work continues towards a November 2026 automation target.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The Week 20 integration roadmap explicitly states that Day-1 manual operations are designed to match the eventual automated solution, which indicates intentional alignment between process and integration design. However, ongoing changes to integration details (e.g., unique keys, price list formats) and external dependencies (EPM–Semarchy migration, SAP RPA decision) introduce some uncertainty about whether all manual steps will remain aligned without adjustment.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency:
If it becomes clear that Day-1 manual processes cannot fully mirror the automated solution, the team will:
1) Prioritize documenting gaps and planning a structured transition playbook for when automation is enabled;
2) Schedule change-management and training activities specifically focused on the shift from manual to automated operations; and
3) Consider phasing automation by process area to reduce disruption, rather than switching all processes at once.
assumptions.validation_method:
1) Document the Day-1 manual process flows and compare them explicitly with the target automated Boomi integration design.
2) Run walkthroughs or tabletop simulations involving both operations and integration teams to confirm that manual steps correspond one-to-one with future automated steps.
3) Revalidate alignment before enabling automation in November 2026.
assumptions.source_file_name: PROS Pricing Engine Program Weekly Status Update (W20)_RevG.pptx

issues.title: Release 1 development trending Red due to data and integration blockers
issues.description: Release 1 is trending Red because server errors and REST API delays on the PROS side, combined with earlier data extract issues, have constrained Sprint 11 development. Although TR Priority 1 and 2 data items have been resolved and a corrected extract (with unique IDs, add-on, AI/non-AI data) was delivered on May 26, 2026, PROS has not yet completed data reload and RTPE validation. Boomi has reduced story points this sprint due to uncertainty and dependency on PROS mappings and payloads, and 14 Release 1 stories have spilled over into the next sprint.
issues.impact_assessment: Despite significant progress on TR-side data readiness, Release 1 remains Red because PROS-side reload and API work have not caught up, leaving integration and optimization development partially blocked. The spillover of 14 Release 1 stories into the next sprint, along with Boomi’s reduced story points, reduces available buffer ahead of key milestones (Design Closure May 27, SIT start June 22). If PROS reload and API delivery slip further, SIT and UAT windows will be compressed, increasing the risk of defects and potentially jeopardizing the August 2026 go-live date.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Depends on resolution of the PROS REST API and endpoint issue (RAID 1281891), completion of Boomi integration design, and SAP/EPMS integration design closure. Affects SIT start on June 22, UAT in July, and Release 1 go-live in August.
issues.resolution: Complete the PROS data reload using the corrected extract, validate RTPE and generate deal guidance, finalize REST API request/response payloads, and rebaseline sprint scope to prioritize blocked integration stories. Incorporate mitigation options for handling spillover stories (e.g., backlog reprioritization, de-scope) by May 29, 2026, and update the integrated plan to protect SIT and go-live dates.
issues.source_file_name: PROS Pricing Engine Program Technology Weekly Status Update (W22)_Rev0.3.pptx

issues.title: Customer parent–child hierarchy source initially unclear for Pricing Engine
issues.description: At the start of the discussion, there was uncertainty about whether customer parent–child relationships (e.g., KPMG global vs. regional branches) are available in GSI or only in ECM. This hierarchy is critical for pricing scenarios requiring roll-ups to parent accounts. It was not clear if ECM/D&B-derived hierarchy data is pushed back into GSI and accessible for use in pricing.
issues.impact_assessment: If parent–child hierarchy data were not available in GSI, the program would need to either change the customer data source to ECM or implement additional integrations, potentially adding complexity and delaying data mapping and ETL design. Lack of hierarchy in the pricing engine would limit support for enterprise-level pricing decisions for large multi-entity customers.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Relies on ECM maintaining hierarchy based on D&B legal hierarchy and pushing it to GSI, daily batch updates from ECM to GSI, and ETL mappings from GSI (Account/SST) into EDL and onward to PROS.
issues.resolution: Kongot, Sripriya confirmed that customer hierarchy data from ECM is fed into GSI. In Salesforce/GSI, hierarchy is maintained at the account level using fields such as ultimate parent, domestic parent, and parent account. This information is updated via daily batch jobs. The team agreed that GSI can be used as the customer source while including these hierarchy fields. Abinash will include these fields in the mappings for Account and SST so PROS can consume the relationships.

issues.title: Unclear EPM strategic process for ingesting prices from PROS
issues.description: The process and approach for loading price lists from PROS into EPM (particularly for Pagero and strategic stack products such as Pagero and Shore Prep) is not clearly understood. Current EPM processes involve significant manual steps and multiple approvals, and there was no representation from EPM strategic or SAP teams in the prior call. The team needs to align on how PROS, as system of origin for certain price lists, will interface with EPM in both legacy and strategic contexts.
issues.impact_assessment: Without clarity on the EPM ingestion process for PROS-generated price lists, the program risks designing PROS price structures that are not consumable by EPM or require excessive manual work. This may undermine automation goals, cause operational friction for pricing and EPM teams, delay implementation for Pagero and other strategic products, and require rework of integration design.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Dependent on participation and input from EPM strategic team members (including Dorothy and Matthew), SAP team representation for legacy and S/4 stacks, and PROS design sessions on price management and environment strategy.
issues.resolution: Plan and conduct focused sessions with EPM strategic team, including Dorothy and Matthew, to understand EPM price structures, approval workflows, and current interfaces (particularly SAP-to-EPM). Use these insights to design PROS price structures and outbound integrations that align with both SAP and EPM schemas and processes, minimizing manual work.

issues.title: Complex dual-UAT testing setup for Pricing Engine may increase effort and delay timelines
issues.description: To work around inaccurate data in the existing UAT environment and the inability to fully refresh UAT before late September, the team will run two separate UAT environments in parallel: (1) a fully integrated UAT environment for end-to-end flows (ECM → GSI → SAP, etc.), and (2) a dedicated production-copy UAT environment connected only to PROS for price optimization testing, where orders cannot be submitted but carts and discounts can be exercised. Business testers (including Commercial Excellence) expressed that this dual-environment approach is complex, will require double testing, and is not ideal, increasing the risk of timeline slippage.
issues.impact_assessment: Running two UAT environments in parallel will force business and QA testers to repeat or coordinate tests across environments, increasing test planning and execution overhead. This additional complexity may slow down UAT cycles, strain testing resources, and push out Release 1 timelines for both pricing execution and optimization. Misalignment between test environments could also lead to defects being missed or discovered late if scenarios are not consistently replicated across both environments.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Provisioning of the dedicated production-copy UAT environment (including data copy through May release and integration to PROS Dev); deployment of Conga and related releases (May, June, July semis) into both environments; availability of business testers from Small Law, Mid Law, and other segments.
issues.resolution: Define a detailed dual-UAT testing plan that clearly documents which scenarios must be executed in the integrated UAT environment vs the dedicated production-copy environment for optimization, how data and configuration differences will be managed, and how to avoid unnecessary duplication. Socialize the plan with business testers and leadership, adjust test schedules and resourcing to accommodate extra effort, and monitor test progress closely to identify and mitigate schedule impact early.
issues.source_file_name: Price Engine - Internal Weekly Meeting (Core Working Group).docx

issues.title: End‑to‑end pricing call performance SLA not yet agreed for Release 1
issues.description: The program does not yet have a confirmed performance model and SLA for pricing calls initiated from Conga and processed via Boomi to PROS. Boomi is implementing parallel processing with request splitting, but their current SLA is 2.5 seconds, and they cannot yet confirm expected processing time for the new pattern. Additional latency is expected due to multiple sequential calls (~3 × 300 ms), and it is unclear whether performance can be achieved without infrastructure or license cost increases. Business stakeholders have not yet agreed to the expected performance impact for initial releases.
issues.impact_assessment: Lack of clarity on Boomi and PROS performance and final SLA may result in slower-than-expected pricing calls for initial launches, affecting user experience and potentially delaying go-live if performance is unacceptable to business. Without a clear decision on either optimizing the integration pattern or investing in additional infrastructure and licenses, the architecture remains unsettled and business expectations cannot be managed. This uncertainty also complicates capacity planning (e.g., calling PROS from all tenants) and may force scope reductions such as limiting PROS onboarding to SCS initially.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Depends on Boomi detailed design and batching approach (Raju’s design), PROS providing batch size performance numbers, Chopra, Neha’s Boomi infrastructure upgrade cost estimates, and guidance from Eric Fast on acceptable investment and performance trade-offs.
issues.resolution:
Potential resolutions under consideration include: 
(1) Boomi handling batching of pricing requests with optimized parallel processing; 
(2) PROS increasing batch size limits (from 10 to 40–50) to reduce the number of calls; and/or 
(3) upgrading Boomi infrastructure and licenses. 
Final resolution will require cost estimates, performance data, and business agreement on acceptable SLAs.
Agreement between Technology and Business on an acceptable Release 1 performance SLA, along with approval of any required infrastructure or licensing changes needed to meet that SLA.

issues.title: Release 1 development trending Red due to incomplete data extracts and pending attribute mappings
issues.description: Release 1 is currently in Sprint 4 and is trending Red because (1) attribute mappings are still incomplete and (2) PROS has not received a complete data extract, including derived attributes, required to progress optimization sprint work. Sprint capacity is being impacted by carryover items and active blockers, and the missing data and mappings are now directly constraining development and preventing generation of raw pricing guidance.
issues.impact_assessment: Because required attribute mappings and complete optimization data extracts (including derived attributes) are not yet available, Sprint 4 work on price optimization rules and end-to-end integration with Conga via Boomi is blocked or slowed. This is causing Release 1 to trend Red, with sprint capacity consumed by carryover work and unresolved blockers. If not resolved quickly, this will delay generation of raw pricing guidance, compress later testing cycles, and may push the Release 1 go-live beyond the current plan.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Depends on completion of data mappings that require business validation, delivery of full transactional and optimization data extracts (including derived attributes) to PROS, and confirmation of event-type definitions in Order Capture needed for business rule execution.
issues.resolution: Accelerate completion of attribute mappings and business validation, finalize and deliver the complete transactional/optimization data extract (including all required derived attributes) to PROS, and close remaining design dependencies such as event-type alignment in Order Capture. Once these data and design gaps are resolved, rebaseline Sprint 4 scope to focus on delivering raw guidance and stabilizing optimization outcomes.

issues.title: PROS REST API delays and endpoint errors blocking integration (RAID 1281891)
issues.description: PROS REST API response delivery and endpoint stability are delaying Release 1 and Release 2 pricing integration. Server errors were traced to product description/code mismatches in the initial data extract; TR delivered a corrected extract on May 26, 2026, but PROS must reload and validate the Real-Time Pricing Engine (RTPE). Until PROS provides stable REST endpoints and near-final request/response payloads, Boomi cannot proceed with mapping sheet completion, error handling design, or full integration development. RAID 1281891 has been logged in ADO to track this risk/issue, and escalation has occurred up to Palani as of May 27.
issues.impact_assessment: The PROS REST API delays and server errors are directly blocking approximately 40% of Boomi integration work and preventing validation of the Conga–Boomi–PROS pipeline in QA. Without stable API responses and confirmed request/response payloads, field mapping cannot be finalized, error scenarios cannot be tested, and end-to-end pricing calls cannot be exercised. This places Release 1 on the critical path, threatens the planned June 22 SIT start, and increases the likelihood of further sprint spillover and schedule slippage for the August 2026 Release 1 go-live and September 2026 Release 2 go-live.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Dependent on TR data corrections provided via Informatica (Mani, Abinash), PROS internal fixes for customer hierarchy and unique key implementation (Annie/Dallas, Carlos), and DLP/SFTP workarounds for Customer Dimension upload. Affects Boomi integration (Naga, Srinivas), Conga field mapping, SIT readiness, and Release 1/2 schedules.
issues.resolution: Reload the corrected customer, product, and transaction data into PROS; resolve server errors caused by product description/code mismatches; validate the RTPE with the corrected dataset; and deliver near-final REST API request and response payloads (including field names and structures) to Boomi by May 28, 2026. Once the API is stable and payloads are agreed, Boomi can proceed with integration development and QA testing.

dependencies.title: Provisioning of dedicated production-copy UAT environment for Price Optimization testing
dependencies.description: Price optimization testing for Release 1 depends on provisioning a new UAT environment that is a copy of production (containing customer and product data up to the May release) and integrated only with PROS Dev. This environment will exist alongside the existing integrated UAT, and will require deployment of Conga and related changes for multiple upcoming releases (May, June, July semis) before it can be used for business testing.
dependencies.dependent_on: Environment provisioning and data refresh teams to create the production-copy UAT environment; Conga and related application teams to deploy May/June/July semi releases into the new environment; PROS Dev integration configuration
dependencies.consumer: Commercial Excellence and business UAT testers for price optimization scenarios; Pricing Program Release 1 testing and go-live readiness
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If the production-copy UAT environment is not provisioned and fully configured in time, price optimization scenarios will either be tested with inaccurate data in the existing UAT or delayed. This may reduce the quality of optimization validation, increase the risk of production issues, and potentially delay Release 1 go-live if critical defects or configuration gaps are discovered late.
dependencies.mitigation: Finalize the environment plan and timeline jointly between Technology and Commercial Excellence, prioritize provisioning and deployment tasks (including Conga changes) for the new UAT, and communicate clear milestones to business testers. If environment creation slips, consider limiting initial optimization testing scope or temporarily using a subset of refreshed data within existing UAT while the full production-copy environment is completed.

dependencies.title: Finalize PROS–SAP price list exchange mechanism and middleware transformations
dependencies.description: Select and implement the technical mechanism and transformation pattern for exchanging price lists between PROS and SAP. An Architecture Call confirmed that PROS can output price lists only in XML format (which includes approvals), and CSV output cannot carry approvals. The middleware layer must therefore handle XML-to-CSV conversion and transform delta outputs from PROS into full-snapshot files consumable by EPM/SAP.
dependencies.dependent_on: Architecture and middleware teams (including Naresh and Boomi/integration engineers) to define and implement XML-to-CSV and delta-to-full-snapshot transformations, and SAP/EPM teams to accept the chosen mechanism.
dependencies.consumer: Release 2 PROS price management implementation and SAP/EPM price list ingestion processes
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If the PROS–SAP price list mechanism and associated XML-to-CSV/delta-to-snapshot transformations are not finalized and implemented in time, Release 2 Sprint 11 and subsequent sprints will experience additional spillover. Price lists may not be consumable by SAP/EPM with approvals, delaying price management, extending manual operations, and potentially pushing the September 2026 Release 2 go-live.
dependencies.mitigation: Use the Architecture Call outcome (XML-only from PROS) to lock in the middleware-based conversion approach. Naresh will provide concrete options and effort estimates for XML-to-CSV and delta-to-snapshot transformation. Prioritize design and implementation of these transformations in upcoming sprints, and validate end-to-end flows in QA before SIT. If delays persist, plan for Day-1 manual operations using XML outputs while automation is completed.

dependencies.title: Delivery of PROS request/response payloads and stable endpoint for Boomi integration
dependencies.description: Conga–Boomi–PROS integration depends on PROS providing a stable REST endpoint and near-final request/response payload definitions (including field names and mappings) so that Boomi can complete mapping sheets, error handling, and integration development for Release 1.
dependencies.dependent_on: PROS team (Abdul Rahiman and Deloitte PROS engineers) to finalize API naming, field mapping, and RTPE validation, and to deliver ~90% complete payload definitions by May 28, 2026.
dependencies.consumer: Boomi integration middleware (Naga, Srinivas), Conga order capture flows, and Release 1 SIT/UAT cycles
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If PROS does not deliver stable request/response payloads and a functioning endpoint by late May, Boomi will remain blocked from progressing beyond the initial two-field integration, delaying QA integration planning (targeted for June 3), compressing SIT starting June 22, and increasing risk to the August 2026 Release 1 go-live.
dependencies.mitigation: Continue escalation via RAID 1281891; prioritize PROS reload of corrected data and RTPE validation; deliver interim payload drafts if needed to unblock Boomi design; and adjust sprint scope so that Boomi focuses on non-payload-dependent tasks while waiting for final definitions.

dependencies.title: Finalize PROS–SAP price list exchange mechanism (XML vs CSV) for Release 2
dependencies.description: Release 2 depends on selecting and implementing a concrete technical mechanism for exchanging price lists between PROS and SAP (e.g., XML vs CSV). This decision and corresponding integration design remain open and are explicitly called out as a design item gating Sprint 2 story completion for price management.
dependencies.dependent_on: SAP functional/technical teams and PROS/Deloitte integration team to agree on format, interface pattern, and operational process for price list exchange (XML vs CSV)
dependencies.consumer: Release 2 PROS price management implementation and SAP price list ingestion processes
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If the PROS–SAP price list mechanism is not finalized promptly, Sprint 2 development for Release 2 price management will be blocked or forced to proceed on assumptions, increasing rework risk. This could cause sprint spillover, delay end-to-end testing of price list publication, and potentially push out Release 2 timelines.
dependencies.mitigation: Hold focused technical design sessions with SAP and PROS/Deloitte teams to compare XML vs CSV options, document pros/cons, and converge on a single supported approach. Once selected, lock the mechanism into integration design and update related user stories so development can proceed without further format changes.

decisions.title: Do not use Conga–PROS connector for current scope
decisions.description: The Conga connector will not be used for integrating Conga with PROS in the current Pricing Engine scope. Both Conga and PROS teams confirmed that the connector has significant functional gaps (including Proflux handling, bundle handling, sequential processing) and they cannot meet the program’s timeline. The connector team has effectively backed out for this phase.
decisions.rationale: The connector cannot meet required timelines and has multiple unresolved functional gaps, and both Conga and PROS confirmed they cannot deliver a viable solution in time. Continuing with the connector would put delivery at risk.
decisions.options_considered: 1) Proceed with Conga connector despite gaps; 2) Use alternative integration approach without connector (custom or Boomi-based); 3) Delay program until connector is ready. Option 2 was selected.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Impacts integration design for Conga–PROS, monthly governance with Conga to track connector roadmap, and performance expectations for non-connector approach.

decisions.title: Use GSI as product data source for Release 1
decisions.description: For Release 1, the product entity for the Pricing Engine will be sourced from GSI product data, as it is more consolidated than EPM and avoids reconstructing complex logic across multiple EPM objects. Product data will be taken from GSI via EDL.
decisions.rationale: GSI provides a more consolidated view of products, whereas EPM spreads product-related data across multiple objects and tables. Recreating GSI-like logic in EPM for pricing would add complexity. Using GSI allows a faster and more manageable Release 1.
decisions.options_considered: 1) Source product data from GSI; 2) Source product data directly from EPM master schema; 3) Use a hybrid approach. Option 1 was selected for Release 1.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Requires understanding that GSI is a point-of-sale system and only contains sellable materials with prices already published. For Release 2, product and price will need to be sourced from master data systems directly rather than from GSI.

decisions.title: Accept GSI limitations as product source for Release 1 with planned rework in Release 2
decisions.description: The team agreed that for Release 1 it is acceptable to use GSI as the product source despite it being a point-of-sale system that only receives products after master data and price are published. However, for Release 2, the solution must be refactored so that product data comes directly from master data systems, aligning with PROS as system of origin for price.
decisions.rationale: Using GSI enables Release 1 progress with a known, consolidated product view, while acknowledging that this is not suitable for long-term price management needs. A phased approach avoids blocking Release 1 while preserving a path to a more correct architecture in Release 2.
decisions.options_considered: 1) Block Release 1 until master-data-based product sourcing is available; 2) Use GSI for both releases; 3) Use GSI for Release 1 and move to master data in Release 2. Option 3 was selected.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Future dependency on master data systems and PROS integration to support product creation and price origination flows for Release 2.

decisions.title: Prioritize customer and product entities before transactional and asset entities for mapping
decisions.description: The data mapping work will prioritize completing customer and product entities first, followed by transactional entities (opportunity, quote, quote line item) and then the asset entity for contracting and renewal information.
decisions.rationale: Customer and product data are foundational master data entities required for the Pricing Engine, and their completion is necessary before transactional and asset mappings can be fully leveraged in ETL and PROS configuration.
decisions.options_considered: Various sequences of mapping (e.g., transactions first, assets first). The chosen sequence is: 1) customer, 2) product, 3) transactions, 4) assets.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Tied to dependency on business validation of mappings and ETL development sequencing.

decisions.title: Include Mid Law users in Release 1 testing alongside Small Law
decisions.description: Mid Law users will be included in Release 1 testing in parallel with the Small Law segment. This grouping was discussed and mutually agreed as a logical approach by Jesse/Pricing, Vittalrao, Yogesh, and P, Palaniappan in the latest SteerCo meeting, with formal documentation and approvals to follow from Eliane and Linki.
decisions.rationale: Testing Mid Law alongside Small Law leverages largely overlapping use cases and allows earlier validation of Mid Law-specific scenarios, while aligning with Pricing leaderships view that the segments form a logical grouping for Release 1 UAT.
decisions.options_considered: 1) Limit Release 1 testing to Small Law only; 2) Include Mid Law testing alongside Small Law in Release 1; 3) Defer all Mid Law testing to a later release. Option 2 was endorsed by Jesse, Vittalrao, Yogesh, and Palaniappan, pending formal approval by Eliane and Linki.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Linked to risk 'Adding Mid Law testing alongside Small Law in Release 1 may strain UAT scope and timelines' and to actions owned by Vittalrao, Yogesh to document and socialize the updated testing scope and enablement plan.

decisions.title: Scaled price list design – each scale as a separate price record
decisions.description: The program will model scaled price lists in PROS such that each scale (e.g., quantity or band) is represented as a separate price record. This design unblocks configuration of price lists and supports scalability for large lists.
decisions.rationale: Representing each scale as a separate price record simplifies configuration, aligns with PROS capabilities, and supports better performance and scalability for large price lists.
decisions.options_considered: 1) Represent scales within a single price record using internal structures; 2) Represent each scale as a separate price record. Option 2 was selected.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Linked to dependencies on price list scalability validation (50K+ price records) and EDL–SAP–PROS integration design for price list exchange format.
decisions.source_file_name: PROS Pricing Engine Program Weekly Status Update (W20)_RevG.pptx

decisions.title: Event type model for Order Capture for Release 1 price optimization
decisions.description: Most event types in Order Capture required for Release 1 price optimization (e.g., renewal, upsell) have been aligned, but mapping for "new sale / new customer" is still under investigation. Invalid price methods have been confirmed as not valid and will not be supported.
decisions.rationale: Aligning event types is necessary for PROS to interpret pricing events correctly; partial agreement allows progress while remaining gaps are addressed.
decisions.options_considered: 1) Delay all event-type decisions until full alignment is achieved; 2) Close alignment for known event types and continue investigating new sale/new customer mapping. Option 2 is currently being pursued.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Linked to dependency 'Event-type alignment in Order Capture for Release 1 optimization rules' and risk 'Order Capture event-type alignment may block Sprint 4 Release 1 optimization configuration'.
decisions.source_file_name: PROS Pricing Engine Program Weekly Status Update (W20)_RevG.pptx

decisions.title: Parent–child pricing rule implementation path for Release 1 and Release 2
decisions.description: The previously proposed PROS custom table approach for parent–child pricing is not feasible for Release 1. For Release 1, a workaround using a manual one-time load of parent–child pricing relationships will be used. A longer-term, fully supported solution will be designed and implemented in Release 2.
decisions.rationale: Technical constraints prevent implementing the desired parent–child pricing rule via PROS custom tables in Release 1. A manual one-time load allows critical use cases to be supported while deferring a robust solution to Release 2.
decisions.options_considered: 1) Proceed with PROS custom table despite limitations; 2) De-scope parent–child pricing from Release 1; 3) Use a manual one-time load in Release 1 and design a robust solution for Release 2. Option 3 was selected and the decision has been reopened for detailed design.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Impacts risks and dependencies related to parent–child pricing and customer hierarchy usage in PROS, and relies on customer ID alignment and hierarchy data availability.

objectives.description: Implement a centralized PROS pricing engine that provides scalable, governed, and integrated pricing execution across in‑scope products, customer segments, and channels.

Establish a repeatable, auditable, and extensible pricing operating model that clearly defines data ownership, integration patterns, and architectural guardrails across SAP, EPM, ECM/MDM, GSI, and PROS.
Reduce manual pricing work, operational inefficiencies, and time‑to‑market delays caused by fragmented pricing logic and data across systems.

Align business, data, and technology stakeholders on performance expectations, integration scope, and system roles (including the concept of PROS as system of origin) before scaling beyond initial releases.

entities.name: Software Cost Optimization
entities.okrs: 5.2 Software optimization

latest_report.content:
## **Executive Summary**

**Scope**  
Deliver software savings across the portfolio to meet the $10M financial target, comprised of $5M in AI Reinvestment, $2M in Innovation Reinvestment, and $3M in Net Savings. This includes reducing unplanned cost growth and ensuring AI and organic investments are governed and offset by realized savings. 

**Current Status: Amber**

Gross savings are tracking well at $12.6M forecasted ($12.3M in 2026, $0.3M in 2027+), with $6.0M realized to date against a $10M annual target. Additional gross savings opportunities forecasted to further strengthen the recovery path, include: MessageBird $.06M, Oracle Svenska AB DB $.04M and Intuit $.02M.

Net savings remain under pressure at ($5.1M) vs. a $3M target, driven by $7.8M in AI reinvestment, $0.5M in Innovation Fund reinvestment and $9.4M in unplanned organic growth.

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on closing the $8.1M net savings gap by accelerating in-flight savings initiatives and partnering closely with sourcing on strategic, multi-year renewals to maximize impact. At the same time, contain the $9.4M organic growth by strengthening monitoring, enforcing governance guardrails, and escalating unplanned cost increases more rapidly. Sustain progress by maturing Pillar Portfolio Reviews (Platform Engineering now, Commercial Engineering in Q3) and shifting to a dashboard-first insights model to improve speed, visibility, and scalability of analysis.

## Milestones

-   Achieve $1.5M in Q1 software cost savings by 31 Mar 2026.
    
-   Achieve $4.0M in Q2 software cost savings by 30 Jun 2026.
    
-   Achieve $6.0M in Q3 software cost savings by 30 Sep 2026.
    
-   Achieve $10.0M in Q4 software cost savings, including $3.0M net savings, by 31 Dec 2026.
    
-   Complete the Software Cost Optimization program and confirm total annualized savings of at least $10.0M by 31 Dec 2026.

issues.title: Organic Growth Outpacing Savings Forecasts
issues.description: Organic growth is outpacing savings forecasts, creating a significant net savings gap against target. Two emerging risks are contributing to this pressure: increased Cursor adoption is driving higher licensing and consumption costs beyond current forecasts, and SQL Server licensing is expected to increase at renewal, adding further unplanned cost growth to the portfolio.
issues.impact_assessment: Organic growth exceeding forecast is eroding planned savings, resulting in a material shortfall against savings targets. Cursor's rising adoption and SQL Server's anticipated license increase at renewal represent incremental cost pressures that, if unmitigated, will further widen the gap against savings targets.
issues.resolution: Close the net savings gap by accelerating execution of identified opportunities across the portfolio. Partner with Sourcing to prioritize strategic and multi-year renewals, maximizing value through volume, term, and vendor negotiation leverage. Proactively manage Cursor consumption growth through governance and demand controls. To mitigate SQL license cost increases, the team is actively pursuing optimization, licensing-rule-based exclusions, and an architecture review with HighQ to reduce consumption, lower exposure, and protect overall savings targets.

## Executive Summary

Pagero – S3NS Cloud Provider Build and Support is delivering a compliant S3NS cloud environment and CIO controls so Pagero can meet French e‑invoicing and e‑reporting mandates. This enables French buyers to receive mandated e‑invoices and reporting through S3NS by 01 Sep 2026.

To date, 8 of 9 defined milestones are complete, including all S3NS test, pre‑prod, and prod environments and the full CIO tool and control stack. Tool builds finished on 29 Apr 2026 against a 30 Jun 2026 plan, providing roughly two months of buffer to support ongoing testing and production onboarding.

Overall status is Green, driven by early completion of core environments and controls relative to the 01 Sep 2026 readiness target.

## Path to Green

The current top RAID item, the Memority eSSO implementation risk, is closed with ISRM providing a workaround to support S3NS testing while the eSSO solution build completes.

## Milestones

- Completed PTB and PTO Cloud Account Processes for Non Prod and Prod on 02 Mar 2026 and 03 Mar 2026 respectively.  
- Completed Pre-Prod and Prod S3NS environments for Pagero on 16 Oct 2025 and 27 Feb 2026.  
- Completed CIO tool builds and controls for S3NS on 29 Apr 2026, ahead of the planned 30 Jun 2026 date.  
- Complete PLE Support for production onboarding by 30 Sep 2026.  
- Achieve program closure with the S3NS platform ready to support the French e‑invoicing mandate by 01 Sep 2026.

entities.status: FedRAMP – CoCounsel Core is a cross-functional program to deploy CoCounsel and its dependent services (CARI, DU, platform services, CIAM, ServiceNow, observability, security tooling) into AWS GovCloud and align them with FedRAMP requirements under the Thomson Reuters Legal Research authorization. entities.okrs: FedRAMP Authorization of CoCounsel Core

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

FedRAMP – CoCounsel Core is building and operating CoCounsel and its dependent services in AWS GovCloud to meet FedRAMP requirements under the Thomson Reuters Legal Research authorization, enabling compliant delivery of AI‑powered legal capabilities to U.S. government and regulated customers. The program coordinates platform, security, observability, CIAM, ServiceNow, and service management capabilities to achieve FedRAMP authorization and a sustainable operational model.

The program is tracking four critical authorization milestones through 15 Jul 2026, with the only variance a 6‑day slip in the “ServiceNow Integration & 3PAO Audit Target” from 30 May 2026 to 05 Jun 2026. Despite the loss of five FedRAMP DevOps staff on 15 Apr 2026, replanning and backfill from the commercial CoCounsel team have preserved target dates for program audit readiness and TR Legal Research authorization on 30 Jun 2026 and CoCounsel Significant Change approval on 15 Jul 2026.

Overall status is Green, driven by all June 30 authorization and closure milestones remaining aligned to plan while resource and ServiceNow risks are actively mitigated.

## Path to Green

To mitigate the top RAID item of reduced FedRAMP DevOps capacity, the program is backfilling from the commercial CoCounsel team and completing backlog reprioritization by 30 Jun 2026 to protect CIAM, Disaster Recovery, production integration, and audit readiness milestones.

## Milestones

- Complete ServiceNow Integration and 3PAO Audit activities, including stable ServiceNow GovCloud inventory integration for FedRAMP CoCounsel, by 05 Jun 2026.  
- Achieve Program Audit Readiness for FedRAMP across all in-scope services and receive TR Legal Research FedRAMP authorization from the FedRAMP PMO government team by 30 Jun 2026.  
- Secure FedRAMP authorization and formal project closure for the FedRAMP – CoCounsel project by 30 Jun 2026.  
- Obtain federal agency FedRAMP Significant Change approval for CoCounsel under the TR Legal Research authorization by 15 Jul 2026.  
- Achieve full FedRAMP Authorization of CoCounsel Core for the program, completing all remaining activities, by 30 Sep 2026.

risks.title: IaC deployer feature gaps in Cumulus
risks.description: The Cumulus infrastructure-as-code (IaC) deployer lacked feature parity and was not in sync with current source code changes, forcing manual infrastructure provisioning.
risks.impact_description: If the IaC deployer remains incomplete, CoCounsel FedRAMP infrastructure will have to be provisioned manually or via ad hoc scripts, which increases risk of configuration drift, security misconfigurations, and delays in environment creation.
risks.mitigation: Define the required IaC deployer capabilities for CoCounsel, implement missing features with support from the Cumulus/DOE team, and update pipelines so infrastructure can be provisioned consistently through Cumulus in GovCloud.

risks.title: Blue / Green deployer approval delays
risks.description: Cumulus blue/green deployments can fail if the "green" approval is delayed, causing deployment failures and requiring re-runs.
risks.impact_description: If blue/green deployments fail when approvals are delayed, production and pre-production releases for CoCounsel and related services could be slowed, result in additional manual effort to re-run pipelines, and increase the chance of deployment errors or missed release windows.
risks.mitigation: Identify and fix the blue/green deployer behavior so that delayed approvals do not cause deployment failures; deliver the fix via an updated Cumulus version and validate with CoCounsel pipelines before general use.

risks.title: Difficulty troubleshooting Cumulus installations due to incomplete logging
risks.description: Logging for Cumulus installations and pipeline creations with multiple assets can be lost or is hard to locate, making it difficult to troubleshoot failed installations.
risks.impact_description: If installation and pipeline logs remain hard to access or incomplete, teams may not be able to diagnose failed Cumulus deployments quickly, causing extended outage or delay in bringing CoCounsel pipelines online and increasing support overhead.
risks.mitigation: Work with the CICD team to improve log availability: adjust logging so installation and pipeline creation events are captured reliably, and provide solution guidance (including using single-asset installs where appropriate) so consumers can access logs needed for troubleshooting.

risks.title: Cumulus installation on Prod CI/CD account 386694349529
risks.description: Cumulus was not yet installed on the critical production CI/CD account (386694349529), blocking automated deployments for CoCounsel.
risks.impact_description: If Cumulus is not installed and available on the production CI/CD account, CoCounsel and related FedRAMP workloads cannot use the standard CPI/Cumulus deployment model, forcing manual deployments or ad hoc automation and increasing risk to release quality and timelines.
risks.mitigation: Plan and execute the installation of Cumulus on the Prod CI/CD account 386694349529, validate pipeline operation, and hand over to consuming teams for production use.

risks.title: Cumulus CPI inflation runs assets sequentially instead of in parallel
risks.description: The CPI inflation process runs multiple assets sequentially rather than in parallel, extending execution time by several minutes per run.
risks.impact_description: If CPI inflation continues to process assets sequentially, pipeline runs will be slower than expected, marginally increasing deployment lead time and reducing efficiency, though without directly blocking CoCounsel releases.
risks.mitigation: Review the CPI inflation design and either accept the sequential behavior as non-blocking or adjust the implementation; agree with stakeholders that no change is required if the added time is acceptable.

risks.title: Helm deployer feature gaps in Cumulus
risks.description: The Cumulus Helm deployer lacked feature parity and was not in sync with current source code changes, requiring services to be deployed manually and halting some Cumulus adoption.
risks.impact_description: If the Helm deployer does not support the required features and current source patterns, CoCounsel services that depend on Helm charts cannot be deployed through Cumulus pipelines, leading to manual deployments, higher operational risk, and slower delivery.
risks.mitigation: Have Chetan’s engineering team work with the Cumulus/DOE team to define required Helm deployer capabilities, implement missing features, and remove blockers so Helm-based services can be deployed via Cumulus in GovCloud.

risks.title: Cumulus UI dashboard Lambda failure on null deployment status
risks.description: The Cumulus UI dashboard Lambda fails when a deployment record has a null status message, causing the dashboard to error and preventing blue/green deployment approvals via the UI.
risks.impact_description: If the dashboard Lambda continues to fail on null status values, teams cannot reliably use the Cumulus UI for blue/green deployment approvals, which may force manual workarounds and delay releases for CoCounsel FedRAMP environments.
risks.mitigation: Fix the dashboard Lambda to safely handle deployments with null status messages, release the updated Cumulus UI version, and verify that blue/green approvals work without error for GovCloud pipelines.

risks.title: Incorrect GovCloud pipeline links in Cumulus UI dashboard
risks.description: GovCloud pipeline links shown in the Cumulus UI dashboard used the wrong host, requiring users to manually navigate to the correct pipelines.
risks.impact_description: If GovCloud pipeline links remain incorrect, it is harder for teams to navigate from the dashboard to the underlying pipelines, slowing troubleshooting and increasing friction in managing CoCounsel FedRAMP deployments.
risks.mitigation: Update the Cumulus UI dashboard to generate correct GovCloud pipeline URLs and release the fix (v1.32.1) to all relevant environments.

risks.title: Cumulus multi-region support blocker
risks.description: A Cumulus defect blocked correct operation of multi-region pipelines needed for CoCounsel and related workloads.
risks.impact_description: If the Cumulus multi-region blocker is not fixed, CoCounsel may be unable to use a single Cumulus-based pattern to deploy to multiple GovCloud regions (e.g., East and West), leading to duplicated effort, inconsistent deployments, and higher operational risk.
risks.mitigation: Implement and validate a Cumulus fix for the multi-region blocker and roll it out to GovCloud environments used by CoCounsel, confirming that multi-region pipelines behave correctly.

risks.title: Cloudflare ingress blocked by Cumulus deployspec for Terraform
risks.description: The cumulus-deployspec-cloudflare (Terraform) implementation blocked creation of required public ingress (incoming calls) for CoCounsel and CARI services.
risks.impact_description: If the Cloudflare deployspec for Terraform cannot provision the necessary public ingress, CoCounsel and CARI services may not be reachable via Cloudflare in the FedRAMP environment, delaying go-live and creating security and availability risks.
risks.mitigation: Work through Engagement 454277 to debug and fix the Cloudflare Terraform deployer so it can successfully create required Cloudflare resources and public ingress; validate with CoCounsel pipelines before closing.

risks.title: EKS deployer feature gaps in Cumulus
risks.description: The Cumulus EKS deployer lacked feature parity with source code changes, forcing manual deployment of EKS-based services and temporarily halting some Cumulus usage.
risks.impact_description: If the EKS deployer remains incomplete, CoCounsel services running on EKS in GovCloud cannot rely on Cumulus pipelines for deployment, increasing the need for manual steps and risking deployment errors or delays.
risks.mitigation: Have Chetan’s engineering team, with DOE support, implement the required EKS deployer features, remove identified blockers, and validate deployments for CoCounsel EKS workloads in GovCloud.

risks.title: Terraform deployer feature gaps in Cumulus
risks.description: The Cumulus Terraform deployer lacked feature parity with current infrastructure definitions, requiring teams to automate Terraform deployments outside Cumulus (e.g., via GitHub Actions).
risks.impact_description: If the Terraform deployer is not brought up to feature parity, CoCounsel infrastructure deployments will continue to rely on external automation, leading to fragmented deployment tooling, more complex operations, and higher risk of misconfiguration.
risks.mitigation: Extend the Cumulus Terraform deployer to support the required Terraform workflows for CoCounsel, align it with current infrastructure code, and transition from ad hoc GitHub Actions automation back into Cumulus-managed deployments where appropriate.

risks.title: ServiceNow GovCloud setup and inventory integration stability
risks.description: Ongoing issues with the ServiceNow GovCloud setup, including asset discovery challenges, vendor engagement, and asset tagging; a manual workaround is currently in place. Discovery for FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts is still not functioning as expected, requiring repeated vendor cases and engineering access changes.
risks.impact_description: If ServiceNow GovCloud setup and inventory integration issues are not resolved, automated asset discovery and tagging will remain unreliable, forcing continued manual workarounds and risking incomplete or inaccurate inventory data needed to support FedRAMP operational monitoring and audit requirements for CoCounsel. This could create audit findings, delay audit readiness closure, and jeopardize the overall authorization and project-closure timeline.
risks.mitigation: Drive FedRAMP ServiceNow GovCloud discovery via workaround: maintain AWS GovCloud discovery, track vendor cases, enable access for ServiceNow engineers, run joint working sessions, and iteratively tune until assets are reliably discovered/tagged. Following the Apr 30 session, schedule a live troubleshooting call with ServiceNow (Marshall), AWS (Ervan), and internal engineering (Prudhvi Yaswanth Kolluru) to review logs, resolve sub‑account discovery gaps, and address CMDB issues in real time.

actions.title: Complete ServiceNow GovCloud inventory integration for FedRAMP CoCounsel
